He and the others ask Gyomei if something can be done to change this problem. Gyomei, having served Kagaya for the longest, since he was nineteen, only responds that he had been asking that same question for eight years, and Kagaya had always denied protection each time. He had insisted that the Hashira shouldn't be wasted on him, worrying them greatly. Shinobu adds that she had heard the Ubuyashikis had never had a bodyguard of any sort throughout their history. Sanemi hurries through the forest, towards the Ubuyashiki Mansion. As he catches sight of it, a massive explosion destroys the mountainside, to Sanemi's sheer horror. The explosion is noticed by the rest of the Hashira, horrifying them all; Tanjiro realizes the scent of blood and burning flesh is in the air. Caught in the center of the explosion, Muzan begins to regenerate as he curses Kagaya. In his final moments, with a smile of seemingly blissful unawareness, he has killed himself, his wife, and his two daughters Hinaki and Nichika present in the explosion. He knew he had laid a trap but could have never imagine one of this scale, as he thought to mix steel spikes as shrapnel to maximize its effectiveness and slow his healing as much as possible. Despite the trap, Muzan knows that Kagaya has something else planned, sensing that people, most likely the Hashira, must be close by all across the mountain. He thinks back to the Oyakata's final moments; the young man had managed to hide all his anger and bloodlust without Muzan ever noticing anything, something he begrudgingly commends him for. As Muzan tries to put his mind towards regenerating quicker, flesh seeds appear around him. They suddenly burst into giant black bramble branches. He realizes they must be someone's Blood Demon Art but is immobilized. However, the spikes don't harm him severely and Muzan believes he can simply absorb them to escape. Tamayo unexpectedly appears and stabs her hand through Muzan's stomach, who is angered at her sudden appearance and asks her reason. Tamayo mentions the flesh seeds belong to the man in Asakusa he turned into a demon. He realizes she must have hidden herself with another Blood Demon Art, using Yushiro's talisman. She tells Muzan the drug in her fist absorbed by him will turn demons back into humans. Muzan claims such an action is impossible but she states it became possible with someone's help. Muzan curses her stubbornness and makes the claim that her hatred of him is unjust, reminding her that she alone was responsible for the deaths of her family. She tearfully responds all she wanted was to survive her disease and see her children grow up. The Demon King mentions she had eaten other people after that and states she had fun doing so, viciously grabbing her head and stabbing her eye. Tamayo does not deny that she has killed and states that in order to atone for those deaths, she and Muzan will die together. She calls out to Gyomei, the first to arrive at the scene. With a single swing of his flail, he decapitates Muzan.

Chapter 139 is the one hundred and thirty-ninth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Kagaya Ubuyashiki is dead at the age of 23. The progression of his illness had eventually rendered him immobile and left him bedridden; until that day happened, Kagaya had visited the graves of the fallen Demon Slayer Corps member, never missing even a single day. Gyomei recalls the first time he met Kagaya, when the Oyakata was fourteen and he himself was eighteen; it has surprised Gyomei to know that someone of his character was younger than himself. At the time, Kagaya immediately knew that he had protected the children he was accused of killing, causing the former monk to bow in gratefulness; Gyomei remembers even back then, Kagaya spoke in a way that people wanted to hear, and his solemness remained till his last moments. During the last time he personally spoke with the Stone Hashira, Kagaya predicts that Muzan will come within five days, instructing Gyomei to kill him while he uses himself as bait. When asked about his certainty, Kagaya only responds it is just his instincts. It is revealed that the Ubuyashiki clan not only possessed their special calming voice, they had instinctual precognition that allowed them to see the future, using it to become wealthy and avoid crisis many times as a result. Kagaya knows the other Hashiras will not accept his decision of self-sacrifice, asking the Hashira he has known for the longest to carry out his last wish. Gyomei obliges, to the gratitude of Kagaya, who finally requests he does not let any of "his children" die. Gyomei manages to successfully behead Muzan, assisted by Tamayo keeping the demon still. As Kagaya had predicted, Muzan does not die and regenerates his head completely, which does not come as a surprise to Gyomei. He recalls his late leader's words that sunlight is the only way to kill the Demon King and he surmises from the sound of his healing that Muzan's regeneration surpasses that of any demon he has faced; even after the damage he had taken from the explosion, he remains extremely powerful. He nonetheless promises to restrain him till dawn. Muzan attempts to ensnare the Stone Hashira with Blood Demon Art: Black Blood, Brambles, but the attack is deflected when Gyomei performs Stone Breathing, Third Form: Stone Skin. Sanemi soon arrives and angrily asks what has become of Kagaya, to the relief of Gyomei, as do the rest of the Hashira, who all call out to Kagaya. Gyomei announces they are now facing Muzan Kibutsuji himself, to the shock of all the Hashira as none of them have ever directly encountered him. Tanjiro, the only one present who has personally faced him, angrily calls out to him. All the Hashira use their respective Breathing Styles in order to cut Muzan down: Muichiro uses Mist Breathing, Fourth Form: Shifting Flow Slash, Shinobu uses Insect Breathing, Butterfly Dance: Caprice, Obanai uses Serpent Breathing, First Form: Winding Serpent Slash, Mitsuri uses Love Breathing, Fifth Form: Swaying Love, Wildclaw, Giyu uses Water Breathing, Third Form: Flowing Dance, Sanemi uses Wind Breathing, Seventh Form: Gale, Sudden Gusts and Tanjiro attacks with Hinokami Kagura: Sunflower Thrust, but as they converge on the demon, Muzan only smiles with an eerie expression. Giant doors suddenly appear and slide open under the Demon Slayers, causing all of them to plummet into the Infinity Castle. Muzan mocks them for believing they had him cornered, declaring they will now fall into hell and that he will kill them all. Tanjiro responds back that the only one to go to hell will be Muzan and he promises to kill him. Muzan answers his challenge: "Then do it if you can! Tanjiro Kamado!!".

Chapter 14 is the fourteenth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. The newly transformed demon bites into his wife's shoulder, horrifying the crowd around them. Tanjiro runs at the demon and pulls him away from her, stuffing his hood into his mouth as a muzzle. Despite her concerns for him, Tanjiro orders her to put pressure on her bite. Muzan tells his frightened wife that it would be best to move away and they leave the situation. Seeing his target escaping, Tanjiro yells out Muzan's name and declares he will never let him get away. His wife becomes worried at his behavior but Muzan instead notices Tanjiro's earrings. As he declares that he will feel his sword on his neck, proclaiming he would never forgive him, the demon remembers when a Demon Slayer had him cornered, and that he too was wearing Tanjiro's earrings. The authorities arrive at the scene and order Tanjiro to release the man immediately, not knowing his demonic nature. Tanjiro pleads with them to either arrest the man or to not interfere, not wanting any harm to come to anyone else. The police ignore him and try to pull the boy off but Tanjiro desperately holds on, unwilling to let the demon go. A woman is seen engraving her nails into her arms causing her wounds to bleed. Tanjiro notices a shift in the scent of the environment and an illusionary pattern engulfs his vision. The police are blinding by the patterns and can no longer see Tanjiro. He goes on the defensive thinking that he is about to get attacked by another demon but is surprised when the woman comes forward accompanied by a boy. She reveals that she is as he had detected, a demon, and adds her intentions of wanting to help Tanjiro defeat Muzan. Elsewhere in Asakusa, Muzan claims to his wife and daughter that he has a meeting to attend to, and adds that he will ask the police about the "incident" earlier, easing his family's concern. As they ride away in a taxi, Muzan shortcuts through an alleyway but accidentally bumps a drunk man. He apologizes and walks away but the man holds onto him. Muzan again apologizes and claims he is in a hurry but the drunkard does not take kindly to Muzan's expensive clothes, before mocking his skin complexion and claiming he looks half-dead. Enraged, Muzan immediately kills the man with one swing of his arm and his lifeless body is slammed head first against a wall. The second larger man angrily approaches Muzan and demands an explanation for what happened to the other man, who he regards as his brother, and the woman accompanying the men cries out as she realizes he is dead. To her horror, she looks back to see that Muzan has killed the second man by kicking him in the air with such force that blood spews out from his mouth and rains down on her below. Muzan finally approaches the terrified woman and mocks her with a series of questions regarding his appearance. He touches her forehead and forcefully pierces her skull, injecting massive amounts of his blood into her, as he tells her that she will not be able to withstand the transformation and her cells will disintegrate one by one. The woman starts to scream but quickly transforms into a demon-like creature before dissolving into ash. At the snap of his fingers, two new individuals appear before Muzan, with him instructing them to kill the "demon hunter with the hanafuda earrings", alluding to Tanjiro.

Chapter 140 is the one hundred and fortieth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As he falls into the Infinity Castle, Tanjiro is confused by his surroundings; directions and gravity are mixed around and he wonders if the place is Muzan's Blood Demon Art. Knowing Tamayo will not be able to resist him for long, he resolves to take down Muzan as quickly as possible. He quickly sees the bottom of where he is falling and attempts to grab a ledge to save himself; though he fails, an arm successfully reaches him and pulls Tanjiro to safety, revealed to be Giyu. As he thanks his friend, a demon suddenly attempts to attack him, killed when he uses Water Breathing, First Form: Water Surface Slash. Doors open from behind Tanjiro and a large horde of demons converges on them. As Tanjiro uses Water Breathing, Sixth Form: Whirlpool, Giyu uses Fourth Form: Striking Tide; together, they slaughter all the attacking demons in rapid succession. Afterwards, an unnerved Tanjiro remarks that Giyu is incredible, quickly knowing what form he would use just from his slight movement and coordinating an attack that wouldn't accidentally hit him, as Giyu regards him with an unimpressed expression. The two make their way through the castle. Obanai lands down and is attacked by numerous demons, which he kills using Serpent Breathing, Fifth Form: Slithering Serpent; he demands they all stay away from Mitsuri, who is ecstatic to see him save her. When he asks if she is alright, Mitsuri can barely contain her joy when she answers, before they proceed through the Infinity Castle together. As Gyomei and Muichiro make their path, quickly cutting down any demon in their wake, Muichiro makes note of the sheer number of demons. Gyomei believes each demon is as powerful as a Lower Rank; the job of the numerous demons is to wear them down. When Muichiro asks for Kagaya's status, Gyomei only tells him he had met a dignified end. Knowing Kagaya would have never let a demon get close, he asks the Stone Hashira if he had used himself as bait, to which Gyomei confirms he had. Accepting he knew he did not have long to live, the Mist Hashira remembers when Kagaya had visited him as he lay in bed following a demon's attack, never leaving his side; he had also done the same to other members of the Corps. Muichiro becomes enraged that Muzan not only took his brother but their father figure, promising to make him suffer before killing him, a sentiment the equally angry Gyomei agrees with. Sitting by himself on a wooden platform, Sanemi laments his inability to save Kagaya; when a demon attacks him, he easily slashes it to pieces without looking. Numerous more appear and converge on him, but the tearful and furious Sanemi, grieving his master's death, demands they all come to him, promising to kill each one of them. Elsewhere, Inosuke makes his way through the castle, slaughtering any demon he encounters, which he sees as the perfect way to test his training. Genya makes his way through the endless halls, confused by his surroundings and wondering if everyone else and Sanemi is alright. Zenitsu, after hearing something in the distance, wonders if Muzan is close by, promising to never forgive him. Shinobu, after walking through a hallway, suddenly smells blood. She opens a door and sees a demon surrounded by numerous bloody corpses. Doma, upon noticing he has a visitor, remarks that Shinobu appears young and tasty, promising to thank Nakime for making his night.

Chapter 141 is the one hundred and forty-first chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Kanae Kocho lay dying in Shinobu's arms, she begs her younger sister to quit the Demon Slayer Corps. She knows she is trying too hard but believes that perhaps she too also wants to live a normal life and eventually grow old. Shinobu tearfully rejects her idea and answers she will never quit until she avenges her. She asks for what kind of demon it was who attacked her, adding that she could never live a normal life again with her death. Kanae answers the demon appears to have blood on his head; the memories of her sister's last moments in her mind as Doma greets her. Kanae describes Doma as always grinning and laughing, speaking with a calm and kind voice, evident when he introduces himself. One of his victims calls out to Shinobu for help. Doma chastises her for interrupting their meeting and swings at her, but Shinobu rushes forward and takes the woman in her arms, as Doma grows impressed with her speed and wonders if she is a Hashira. However, when she asks the woman if she is alright, she suddenly falls to pieces. Stunned by the gruesome scene she has just witnessed, Shinobu stares blankly as Doma tells her to leave the woman's body, promising to eat it later. She turns to face him as she remembers Kanae had said her killer wields a pair of sharp fans, just as Doma reveals his weapons. The demon introduces himself as the leader of the Eternal Paradise Faith; his role is to make with those faithful to him happy and that he will devour her without wasting anything. As Shinobu realizes Doma is the demon who killed Kanae, she retorts that the woman wasn't happy pleading for her life, only for Doma to answer that he did ""help" her; by killing her, she is no longer in pain or afraid. He believes because everyone fears death, it is his role to eat them, taking everything they were in him to "save"" them. Shinobu responds that his actions sicken her, surprising Doma with her harsh and prickly personality despite never meeting her before. He surmises something painful has happened to her and opens his ears for her to speak. The Insect Hashira answers what she feels isn't just painful; he has killed her sister, grabbing her haori and demanding he remember where he saw it. Doma realizes the haori belongs to his former opponent who uses Flower Breathing; he describes Kanae as kind and cute, adding that he regrets not being able to eat her, just as Shinobu attacks him without warning. Using Insect Breathing, Dance of the Bee Sting: True Flutter, she stabs Doma in his left eye. The Upper Rank compliments her since he was unable to stop the blow, as he retaliates with Blood Demon Art: Frozen Lotus. The extremely cold attack freezes part of her clothing and face, as Shinobu retreats and remarks that the air is so cold, it could freeze her lungs. Though he commends Shinobu for her speed, Doma calls her attack pathetic for not beheading him. Shinobu responds that she knows this but questions if he is aware about the use of poison. Suddenly, pain strikes Doma in the head and his skin begins to decay. Shinobu, about to find out if her poison can work on an Upper Rank, remembers Kanae and hopes she can succeed. Doma falls to his knees in severe pain and vomits blood, remarking that the poison is more powerful than the one she had used on Mount Natagumo, disappointing Shinobu to realize that demons do share their information, making poison a double-edged sword. At that moment, his coughing slows and he gets up to face her, revealing he had successfully decomposed the poison in his body, offering her a sarcastic apology. He makes note of the sound her sword made when she sheathed it and surmises it is where she changes the poison she uses. Doma becomes excited to face a user of poison and believes he can get used to the pain, asking if she has more planned for him. Shinobu, having anticipated he would survive her initial attack, draws her blade to face Upper Rank Two.

Chapter 142 is the one hundred and forty-second chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Doma recalls his past and his childhood. Born with rainbow colored eyes and white hair, he was believed to be special and connected to the gods. His parents, whom he considered dim-witted, arranged a cult with him at the head called the Eternal Paradise Faith; despite this, he never heard the gods' voice and simply played along. Worshippers flocked to Doma to repent their issues and problems in life, hoping for advice. However, even at a young age, the unemotional Doma found it annoying that adults had come to seek wisdom from a child. When they begged him to guide them to paradise, he cried, believing that paradise, the gods and Buddha were a fairy tale that never existed, confused why people wouldn't believe they were all destined to die and rot and pitying them for their inability to see reality. Doma believes he was born to make it his duty to make these people happy, by devouring them whole. After a fifth stab on his hand fails to hurt him, Doma quickly heals himself of Shinobu's poison, before asking if she is okay after noticing she is breathing heavily. Shinobu realizes the true strength of an Upper Rank, noting Doma's resistance and inability of poisons to work on him. He tells her that her lungs' cells are dying after accidentally breathing in his Blood Demon Art, now making it dangerous to breathe. She then decide to use multiple blows to poison him again. Using Insect Breathing, Dance of the Dragonfly: Compound Eye Hexagon, Shinobu rushes forward and stabs Doma six times. He remarks that the Insect Hashira might be the fastest one he has fought, but as she backs away, Shinobu bleeds profusely, realizes she herself was also slashed in return before she could notice. Doma taunts her as she collapses in pain, mentioning that she could have easily cut off his head with her immense speed but can't due to her small frame. As blood falls on her hands, she sees just how small they are. She remembers she never grew any taller, lamenting that she could have killed demons the usual way had she grown a bit more. Shinobu knows larger hands and legs meant more muscle and that it was a distinct advantage. She recalls Kanae also was unable to do so despite only being taller due to also having a dainty and thin frame, and remarks that Gyomei's strength puts others at ease when he fight. Shinobu remembers Kanae's last moments with her, telling herself she would likely lose to Doma. Kanae's spirit suddenly appears before the injured Shinobu, telling her to stand. Shinobu believes she can no longer after losing so much blood, and with her left lung damaged by Doma's attack, she cannot breath normally as well. Kanae declares that irrelevant and states she will win with the right resolve to kill him, no matter the sacrifice, noting she promised to her and to Kanao. Remembering their younger sister, Shinobu crouches down while Doma approaches her, noting the slashes he gave was only half-hearted, making it very painful for her. Kanae urges her younger sister to keep trying, causing her to stand up, surprising the Upper Rank. As she stares at Doma, Shinobu starts to cough blood, prompting Doma to laugh that the blood in her lungs is causing her to do so. Resolving to behead Shinobu to end her pain, he tells her to give up, claiming she is already beyond saving. Shinobu takes a stance, and using Insect Breathing, Dance of the Centipede: Hundred-Legged Zigzag, she speeds towards the Upper Rank and attacks him. Doma becomes shock at this feat, noting the destroyed bridge from the impact of her feet. He tries to slash her in response but is too slow, only manage to slice her cape. Shinobu crouches down and launches into the air, driving her sword through Doma's neck and forcing his body into the ceiling in one final thrust.

Chapter 143 is the one hundred and forty-third chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Shinobu remembers her childhood, once believing that happiness was an endless road throughout life. That belief was shattered when a demon entered her home and killed both her parents, leaving her and Kanae orphaned. They were saved however by Gyomei Himejima, who had arrived and quickly defeated the demon. Shinobu realized that though her happiness was forever destroyed, other people's weren't, and the sisters resolved to defeat demons and prevent other people from suffering the same fate as them. She and Kanae promised to each other to both become Demon Slayers to do so. The two believed that despite their weak strength, stopping one demon could save tens of people, and stopping an Upper Rank could save hundreds. It didn't matter that they could or could not, what matter was they had to try. Recalling the time when Tanjiro had asked if she was angry, she states she has been so for a long time, remembering her parents' death, her sister's death, and the deaths of all her Tsugukos before Kanao. She remembers Aoi, Sumi, Kiyo and Naho, how their families too were killed. Most of all, she is incensed at her poison's inability to hurt Doma. Her swords slips from Doma's neck, causing her to fall. Doma then uses his ice to catch her and pull Shinobu into a hug. With crocodile tears in his eyes, he mockingly congratulates her for making it thus far, while insulting her for being weaker and less talented that Kanae, to her fury. Doma acknowledges her foolishness at trying to kill him despite all the odds and calls it the thing that make humans so fleeting. As he decides she is finally worthy of being eaten by him, Doma asks for her final words; Shinobu only responds, "Go to hell". Kanao opens the door to the cult room and looks up to see Doma clutching her in the roof. Shinobu attempts to signal Kanao with her hand, but Doma notices it. As she watches, Doma breaks Shinobu's body in his arms, to Kanao's horror, killing her and causing her sword to fall from her hand. She desperately leaps upwards to use Flower Breathing, Fourth Form: Crimson Hanagoromo but misses when Doma escapes and lands onto the floor. The demon advises her not to attack him in the middle of absorbing someone, causing Kanao to seethe with rage. Doma fails to taunt her and instead fondly recalls that Shinobu had only a short time with him due to his abilities, and decides that this night might be really good, having two gorgeous meals at once, all while licking Shinobu's hair pin and commenting on his fine evening to have feasts come to him one after another. As the Upper Rank continues to taunt her, Kanao admits that somehow, she feels the people important to her will be alive tomorrow, yet there is no way she can promise it can happen with such certainty just from her own hopes. Zenitsu approaches a room and calls for the individual inside to come out. They only respond that Zenitsu's beckoning is the improper address to a senior. Kaigaku walks out and taunts him for being as dainty and seedy as ever, but Zenitsu responds back that as a demon, Kaigaku is no longer his senior.

Chapter 144 is the one hundred and forty-forth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Tanjiro and Giyu run through the Infinity Castle, the former nearly falls through an opened floor, only barely managing to grab the ledge and save himself. As Giyu warns him to keep aware and alert, Tanjiro remarks it is as if the castle is alive, actively trying to separate him from Giyu. Knowing he must reach Muzan and the rest of the Corps' members, he then realizes Tamayo is running out of time, and yet they don't know where Muzan is. A Kasugai crow then calls out the announcement that Shinobu is now dead, killed in a battle against Upper Rank Two. Upon hearing it, Tanjiro wells up with tears thinking about Kanao and the girls of the Butterfly Mansion. At the same time, Giyu notices the crow has a piece of paper attached to its neck, remarking that messages are being sent rather quickly. Similar pieces of paper, talismans of Yushiro's Blood Demon Art, appears on the head of Kiriya Ubuyashiki and his sister Kanata and Kuina. Kuina confirms Shinobu's death to Kiriya and notes the remaining Hashira are alive. He asks if she is the only one to have faced an Upper Rank and Kuina answers she is not; he then asks Kanata if all the crows sent with Yushiro's vision talismans have reached half of the Demon Slayers, to which she answers they have not. Being the eldest son, Kiriya has now taken the mantle of Oyakata at the age of eight. Despite the deaths of his parents and sister, Kiriya does not mourn them and instead focuses on the mission, having no time to shed tears. Kuina and Kanata have also pushed their grief aside to help him. His deceased elder sisters were Nichika and Hinaki, who never left their parents' side. As a father, Kagaya was strict in rearing his children due to his short life, quickly raising them into adulthood; Amane was similarly firm as well. With his death, Kiriya is now the leader of the Demon Slayer Corps. Due to their lacking information, Kiriya orders the crows to spread as many talismans as possible. Kuina confirms Muzan's location has not change and the Hashira are spread thin; he orders them to head north. Kuina adds that the two Demon Slayers currently facing Upper Ranks are Kanao and Zenitsu, who is facing Upper Rank Six. Kaigaku remarks that Zenitsu has not change and believes he remains weak. He rhetorically asks if he is now a Hashira and if he still uses only the first form. Zenitsu merely questions if he is excited to fill the bottom place of the Upper Ranks, a statement that surprises the demon to see Zenitsu talk back. He asks for why he, a Thunder Breathing user, had become a demon before angrily telling him that their trainer Jigoro Kuwijima has killed himself and was alone. In committing seppuku, an additional person must finish off the sentenced to prevent a drawn out death, yet Jigoro died in agony to atone by not slitting his throat to end it quickly, all because a Thunder Breathing user has become a demon. The demon disregards Zenitsu's statement and mockingly asks if he should feel remorseful. He claims he does not care about those who don't value him and only serves those who see his worth. He mentions he did everything to please Jigoro in training, yet in the end, the "senile" former Hashira decided to make him and Zenitsu co-successor to his mantle. Zenitsu laughs and retorts that Jigoro wasn't senile; if he himself was a terrible successor for only knowing the first form, then so was Kaigaku for only knowing the other five, pitying Jigoro for having lousy students to succeed him. Kaigaku becomes enraged by Zenitsu's taunts and uses Thunder Breathing, Fourth Form: Distant Thunder. He lunges at the Demon Slayer and swing his katana, only for Zenitsu to appear behind him and remark he is too slow. To the Upper Rank's shock, Zenitsu has already slit his neck, with Kaigaku noting that he now moves like a completely different person.

Chapter 145 is the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Kaigaku remembers his unfortunate encounter with Upper Rank One, remarking that it was not shameful to kneel before an overwhelmingly strong opponent. He believes that as long as he remains alive, it would all work out in the end. It does not matter if dirt is rubbed in his face, he is forced to drink dirty water, or people curse him for stealing money; what mattered was that he was alive and that someday, he would succeed. Kokushibo then asks if Kaigaku wants to become a demon and get stronger, drawing blood from his hand to drink. If Muzan recognizes him, he will transform into a demon. He explains that to become one takes time, a process that is longer the stronger a person is; Kokushibo himself took three days to transform. Additionally, to counteract the effects of Total Concentration, much blood must be drunk, and rarely does a person's body not allow them to become a demon. Kokushibo tells the Demon Slayer to be grateful for the blood he received, threatening to behead him should he spill a drop. He reminisces on the intense fear he felt as he put the blood into his mouth, as if his cells were screaming and crying. Compared to facing Zenitsu now, the Upper Rank is not worried. Despite gaining some strength, he believes Zenitsu remains a worthless coward, crying without dignity or perseverance. He recalls when Jigoro had offered to make them both his successors and curses his former trainer for comparing him to his junior. As he angrily declares that they both deserved to die, Kaigaku uses Thunder Breathing, Second Form: Rice Spirit, attacking Zenitsu with five consecutive slashes and injuring his face. Zenitsu remarks that with the consecutive attacks, Kaigaku has already eaten much victims, believing he can't tell good from evil anymore. Kaigaku responds he does know, using Third Form: Thunder Swarm to envelope Zenitsu in black lightning, burning him. The demon tells him the true difference is that those who know his worth are good and those who don't are evil. Using Fifth Form: Heat Lightning, Kaigaku slashes and burns Zenitsu simultaneously, asking if he enjoys his blade infused with his Blood Demon Art, before attacking him again with Sixth Form: Rumble and Flash, wounding Zenitsu all throughout his body; Kaigaku gloats that with his immense power both burning and slashing him, he has become a demon to surpass Thunder Breathing. As Zenitsu falls, with the demon remarking he is truly different to him, he recalls Jigoro's lesson to use Kaigaku as an example; Thunder Breathing as a style revolves around using the first form as a foundation; as such, it didn't matter if someone could use the other forms when they could do the first. Knowing this, he recalls that even when Kaigaku was a lesser user of the style, he retained an arrogant personality, dismissing anyone who he perceived to be beneath him, despite himself knowing that Kaigaku could never be a Hashira as a result. He understands why Kaigaku hates him, but despite also returning the sentiment, he still respected Kaigaku for his hard work. To him and Jigoro, Kaigaku was a special person, yet none of it satisfied him. He compares Kaigaku's heart to a box with a hole that held his happiness; despite whatever went in, it could never fill up. Apologizing to Jigoro for the two of them taking different paths, he uprights his body and plants his feet along the wall to stop his descent. As Kaigaku watches with surprise, Zenitsu apologizes to him and attacks with Thunder Breathing, Seventh Form: Honoikazuchi no Kami, instantly decapitating Upper Rank Six. As he plummets, Kaigaku tries to comprehend what had just happened, unable to see the rapid attack. He curses Jigoro for favoring Zenitsu by teaching him an exclusive form, but Zenitsu denies their trainer was such a person. This form is of his creation, one he had hoped to use to fight with him.

Chapter 146 is the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After Zenitsu beheads Kaigaku with Seventh Form: Honoikazuchi no Kami, both fall in the Infinity Castle to their deaths. Zenitsu plummets while unconscious as the disintegrating Kaigaku grows furious at his defeat by Zenitsu's hand, angered that the one he believed to be weaker than himself had managed to create a seventh form. He comforts himself with the idea that he too will die with him when he hits the bottom. Suddenly Yushiro enters Kaigaku's vision, telling him that those who never give anything will one day never gain from others, and that only wanting is the same as having nothing when they cannot create for others, before coldly telling the fallen Upper Rank that it is pitiful to die alone. Yushiro leaps across the walls and catches the unconscious Zenitsu, while the fallen Upper Rank disintegrates to ash, marking a pathetic end to the prideful and traitorous Demon Slayer. Zenitsu see himself in the afterlife, a land full of red spider lilies; he sees his master Jigoro across the Sanzu River, separating the two. He apologizes to him for never getting along with Kaigaku despite his attempts to reach out, believing if it wasn't for him, Kaigaku wouldn't have been goaded into becoming a demon. He apologizes for never repaying his debts, and adds that he truly wanted to become a Hashira whilst he was alive. However, Jigoro remains silent, and Zenitsu, believing he still hates him, asks for his trainer to say something to him. Suddenly, the lilies begin to wrap around his feet, pulling him into the ground. Watches as he sinks lower, Jigoro tearfully informs his former student, "Zenitsu... I'm proud of you", causing him to tear up as well. In reality, Zenitsu awakens to Yushiro patching his wounds, surrounded and guarded by more Demon Slayer. Murata, who recognizes him, asks on his condition and whether he can be saved. Annoyed by his yelling and begging, Yushiro only tells him to keep on guard. Murata does not taken kindly to his orders and demands to know his rank but the demon ignores him while administering a styptic to stop Zenitsu's bleeding, though he notes that the cuts on his face might worsen. Murata chastises him for his pessimism and comforts Zenitsu, as the others tell him he will be saved as well. Yushiro remarks was lucky that Kaigaku had not mastered his techniques, saying he could have killed him had he progressed in a years. Murata once again demands he keep positive, but his screaming draws the attention of several demons. Yushiro, the only demon to not be created by Muzan Kibutsuji, recalls when Tamayo had told him to act naturally as he assisted the Demon Slayers, though his dissatisfaction was plainly written on his face. After changing his eye color and donning a uniform, the others did not suspect Yushiro to be a demon, though they sensed that something was not right. Murata struggles to sever a demon's neck, causing Yushiro to demand he hasten his effort. He uses a Kasugai crow with his talisman to sense his surroundings, but grows concerned when something is nearby. As Tanjiro and Giyu continue through the castle, he notices they have not encountered any Upper Ranks, before wondering on the whereabouts of Muzan and the other Hashira. As he tries to tell himself they will succeed, the hallway they are in begins to shake violently as something approaches them. He wonders if it is a battle but senses it is approaching them, recognizing its scent. Giyu warns him to stay back as the ceiling cracks open; Akaza lands down to face the two and taunts Tanjiro, surprised that someone as weak as him is still alive, before lunging at Tanjiro while yelling his name. Angered to see the familiar face, Tanjiro dodges and in return, yells out his name, ready to fight Upper Rank Three. Elsewhere, hovering above a bottomless shaft, Tamayo finds herself trapped in a fleshy cocoon. Noticing it is able to decompose the human-conversion, she realizes it will absorb her as well in enough time and pleads for someone to save her.

Chapter 147 is the one hundred and forty-seventh chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. While in the process of mapping out the floor plan for the Infinity Castle, Kanata begins to envision the recently deceased members of her family. Her emotions begin to overwhelm and her eyes well up with tears, but Kiriya tells her to stop crying and continue with her task, reassuring her that they will win. Kanata acknowledges his orders and recomposes herself to continue. Sitting outside the room of the Ubuyashikis are the former Hashiras Tengen Uzui and Shinjuro Rengoku. Tengen marvels at Kiriya's mental fortitude, continuing his mission despite the lingering anguish of his father's death. Shinjuro agrees and is amazed that children so young have taken on an enormous responsibility. He promises to risk his life to protect them, as Kyojuro did, in order to no longer bring shame to his family name. Elsewhere in the estate, Sakonji tends to an unconscious Nezuko; despite using Tamayo's human-conversion drug on her as told, she seems to be in pain, sweating profusely and groaning. He notes that if she truly can be human again, Muzan's scheme will fall apart, losing the only demon in a thousand years to ever be resistant to sunlight. However, Sakonji himself is also trembling and sweating in his nervousness. Whenever he thinks about the battle's eventual endgame, he grows anxious to realize the ancient war of humans and demons might soon end, something he will witness. He reminisces on Tanjiro and realizes he had always played a pivotal part. Since bringing his sister to him, Sakonji had felt as if cogs had begun to turn. The ancient war is but a giant machine, and with the introduction of him and Nezuko, it is as if two added cogs have shifted the stagnant situation to begin moving. He hopes that the siblings will not lose. As Akaza throws a punch at Tanjiro, the Demon Slayer performs Hinokami Kagura: Fire Wheel to flip over him and catch his arm with his blade. He summons the strength to slice it off, but Akaza regenerates it back and quickly retaliates by swinging his fist back at his head. Using Hinokami Kagura: Fake Rainbow, he evades the blow and appears behind the demon, while also managing to slash his face. Giyu is impressed to see Tanjiro has progressed his technique so much, as Akaza stares curiously at his attacker; he remarks that he can confidently say his ability is now that of a Hashira's to be able to handle an Upper Rank. On the first day they met, all Tanjiro could do was despair in his weakness and beg for Nezuko's life to be spared; now, able to fight, Tanjiro won't ever again lose his life or his dignity. Akaza suddenly remembers Kyojuro's words, "This boy is not weak. Do not insult him", and realizes now he was telling the truth. He remarks that Tanjiro is certainly no longer weak, and to show he has earned his respect, Upper Rank Three performs Technique Development: Compass Needle, to celebrate his opponent's new strength in a battle.

Chapter 148 is the one hundred and forty-eighth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Using Water Breathing, Third Form: Flowing Dance, Giyu maneuvers around Akaza and evades his numerous attacks; he remarks that it had been fifty years since he fought a Water Hashira. The demon uses Destructive Death: Disorder to force him to retaliate, with Giyu using Water Breathing, Eleventh Form: Dead Calm to dispel the shockwaves. Akaza becomes impressed, having never seen the technique as the last Water Hashira he had killed did not use it. Tanjiro attacks him from behind, using Hinokami Kagura: Raging Sun to go for his neck. Akaza evades the slashes and appears behind him, attempt to chop off his head. He fails to perform Fake Rainbow in time but is saved when Giyu slashes off the Upper Rank's arm with Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel, though he regenerates the limb instantly. The two clash head on; attacking again from behind him, Tanjiro tries using Hinokami Kagura: Flame Dance to cut down the demon but Akaza uses Destructive Death: Leg Type, Crown Splitter to fend him off. He blocks the attack with his sword but the demon's leg grazes him, causing his nose to bleed from the sheer force. As Akaza evades Giyu's slashes, he marvels at his superb technique and demands to know his name, wishing to remember. Giyu refuses to divulge his name to the demon and tells him he hates talking; the amused Akaza responds that he enjoys talking in battle and decides he will continually ask for it instead. Using Destructive Death: Leg Type, Explosive Flurry, Akaza kicks at Giyu in rapid succession and launches him away with his shockwaves; despite blocking the attack with his sword's handle, Giyu is sent flying through numerous walls. Tanjiro attempts to call out to Giyu but Akaza appears before him, satisfied to know the Hashira's name. The Demon Slayer and Upper Three clash, with Tanjiro performing Hinokami Kagura: Burning Bones, Summer Sun and Akaza retaliating with Destructive Death: Eight-Layered Demon Core. The attack's vibrations ring loudly in his sword but Tanjiro is able to escape the attack unharmed. Akaza compliments him for his growth and his training to reach his level. He commends Kyojuro for Tanjiro's success, recalling their first encounter when he was lying on the ground too weak to be notices, but as of right now, he is happy and excited to battle him. He tells Tanjiro he is glad that Kyojuro is dead, believing he had already reached his peak because he valued being human. Upon hearing the demon's statement, Tanjiro becomes furious and demands he take back his words. Confused, Akaza responds he is praising the two of them, but Tanjiro retorts he is only insulting those he calls weak. The demon believes Tanjiro misunderstands him and states that he only despises the weak because it disgusts him; to him, it is the law of nature to weed out the weak. Tanjiro tells Akaza that him standing now is proof he is wrong; everyone begins life as a baby, born weak and needing help from someone, including him. He states that the true law of nature is that the strong protect the weak, and the weak become stronger to help those less than them; telling Akaza his way of thinking is unforgivable, he declares his days of doing what he pleases are over, causing the demon to clench his fist in anger.

Chapter 149 is the one hundred and forty-ninth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Facing off against Tanjiro, Akaza cannot brush aside the repulsive feeling he is giving him. He is unsure why he feels angry fighting him since he knows Tanjiro is no longer weak, yet he cannot shake the feeling of his eyes, voice and words cutting into him. At that moment, someone seemingly grabs Akaza's shoulder and confirms Tanjiro's words; everyone starts off weak, then they get help from everyone around them and learn, but that he should only compare his own progress against himself, not that of others. The man tells him what is important is becoming stronger than he was yesterday, and by developing himself, soon he can be the one to help people. Angered, Akaza tries to punch behind him to hit the man, but strikes nothing. As a bewildered Tanjiro sees Akaza punch the air suddenly, Upper Rank Three angrily mutters, "Tanjiro, you really are unpleasant". Akaza suddenly lunges at Tanjiro and uses Destructive Death: Crushing Type, Ten-Thousand Leaves Flashing Willow, rupturing the ground around him, with Tanjiro just barely dodging the attack. As he becomes stunned to see Akaza's new speed and precision, the demon quickly engages the Demon Slayer again from below and uses his Destructive Death: Leg Type, Flying Planet Thousand Wheels, with Tanjiro enduring the blow and vomiting blood as a result. Akaza swings at him but Tanjiro barely ducks down to avoid it, all while he tries to rationalize how the Upper Rank's attacks are so potent. With his techniques possessing unparalleled precision, as if his fists are magnetized to his vital areas, he tries to understand what he is gauging his attacks on, thinking back to his battle with Kyojuro to find the answer. Using Hinokami Kagura: Solar Heat Haze, Tanjiro slashes at Akaza's neck; his blade seemingly distorts as it slashes him, despite Akaza believed he dodged it by moving away from it. He is amused to see the unusual technique and asks how he performed it, continuing to attack Tanjiro as the Demon Slayer struggles to fend off the relentless onslaught. At the Rengoku estate, Senjuro prays to his older brother; a large battle has begun and their father is away to protect the Oyakata, asking that Kyojuro protect him and Tanjiro. He thinks back to the letter he sent to Tanjiro; though it was a trivial matter, he had written to him about a conversation the Sengoku era's Flame Hashira had with a user of Sun Breathing. The swordsman had explained his experience of fighting Muzan, but upon hearing his story, the Hashira lost his confidence. Despite this, Senjuro prays that Tanjiro won't lose, wondering if Kyojuro agrees. In the midst of the battle, it is revealed that Senjuro's Kasugai Crow has indeed entered the Infinity Castle, but has not given Tanjiro his letter and is watching the battle behind cover, forcing him to defeat Akaza in order to read it. Tanjiro uses Hinokami Kagura: Dance and swings down at the demon, but Akaza catches the blade mid-slash and attempts to break it. In a desperate move, he headbutts Upper Three, but Akaza only compliments him for his efforts. He kicks Akaza in the chin but he continues to maintain his hold. As the blade begins to creak, Akaza's hands are suddenly slashed off, saving Tanjiro. He looks up and sees Giyu has returned, as the Water Hashira becomes angry at the severe pain in his back from being launched by Akaza.

Chapter 15 is the fifteenth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. At the udon vendor from earlier, the owner yells Nezuko for not eating his food. She sits there puzzled by his anger until Tanjiro returns and takes the chopsticks from the vendors hands and quickly slurps down the noodles. He thanks and compliments the vendor's cooking before leaving with Nezuko, and the man is left somewhat angry but still flattered by his compliment. As they walk down the street, Tanjiro apologizes for leaving Nezuko alone but is suddenly stopped by her wariness of someone at the end of the street. Tanjiro calls out him who turns out to be the demon from earlier, letting him know that there was no need to wait for him as he could've followed the scent back to the hideout. The demon rejects his claim saying that there was no way that they could be tracked and questions Nezuko's presence -since she's a demon- while simultaneously calling her a hag. Tanjiro is insulted by his remark and argues that his sister is in fact considered his town's beauty. They travel behind the demon until they arrive at a house with a pinned piece of paper. When they enter the building they stumble upon the demon lady treating the injured woman who was attacked by her spouse. Out of curiosity, Tanjiro questions if it is hard for the woman to resist wanting to attack the humans that she treats. Before she is able to respond, the demon beside him elbows Tanjiro and berates him for asking such a ridiculous question. The woman chides her assistant to stop being violent and formally introduces themselves as Tamayo and Yushiro. Going back to Tanjiro's question, she explains that she is different from normal demons since she has altered her body and removed Muzan's curse. She goes into detail saying that she doesn't need to feed on human flesh, and only needs to drink small amounts of human blood in order to survive. Her methods involve purchasing blood from poor individuals under the facade that they would be used for medical transfusions, explaining why they do not have a distinct demon scent. Tamayo reveals that Yushiro requires less blood then she does and that he was the only individual that she was able to successfully transform into a demon after experimenting for more than 200 years. Being stunned by her claims, Tanjiro brazenly asks Tamayo how old she truly is, causing Yushiro to hit him in a rage. She sternly warn him not to hit Tanjiro again, before then explaining that she does not have ill intentions to increase the number of demons in the world; she simply strives to find a solution to treat the incurable so they can live a little longer. Tanjiro senses her pure intent and decides to seek Tamayo's help in finding a way to turn demons back into humans. In an alley at another part of the city, walking down the street, a demon playing with a temari ball is seen accompanying a second demon with eyes on his hands, who begins to track a set footprints on the floor. The Arrow Demon accurately identifies their provided targets, and when the Temari Demon asks how they will kill them, he answer they will do so brutally. Tamayo confirms Tanjiro's suspicions on being able to turn a demon back into a human. He rushes forward to Tamayo eager to know the method but Yushiro flips him back, preventing him from getting too close to Tamayo. She angrily warns Yushiro again not to hit Tanjiro to which he cheekily responds, "I just threw him. I did not hit him". Tamayo tells Tanjiro that in order to establish a cure, she would need to study Nezuko's blood and that he would need to collect samples from demon who contain high concentrations of Muzan's blood. She goes on to inform him that Nezuko has a rare and special condition regarding the fact that she had slept for two years to regain her strength and since she hasn't consumed human or animal flesh within that period. Tamayo warns Tanjiro that the task of collecting demon blood would not be easy and questions if he would still be willing to try. Tanjiro responds, " If that's the only way, I'll do it. It will help, not just Nezuko but lots of others right?", and a relieved Tamayo smiles at his optimism; Tanjiro blushes slightly at her smile but quickly realizes that Yushiro is displeased. At that moment, a speeding temari begin to destroy the house's interior.

Chapter 150 is the one hundred and fiftieth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Giyu and Akaza face each other, Giyu rationalizes why he fights as an individual. Though he is usually hesitant to draw his sword and isn't one to fight for amusement, standing now and facing an opponent who can overwhelm him, he realizes his senses have sharpened in a short amount of time; senses that once lie dormant in him and just now are brought out onto the battlefield he stands on. He finally understands the intense struggle to increase one's own skills; as Tanjiro looks on, the Water Hashira manifests a splash-like mark on his cheek. Giyu makes a powerful swing at Akaza, just barely missing his mark. The demon responds with a punch straight to his head but Giyu ducks down and slashes his neck, forcing Akaza to back away. Tanjiro notes that with his Mark manifested, Giyu's speed has increased greatly; the Hashira uses Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide and attacks Upper Three head-on, splitting the demon's arm but sustaining a gash to his head. Watching from a distance, Tanjiro notes that despite both fighters moving at tremendous speeds, Akaza was able to quickly adapt to Giyu's enhanced abilities. Realizing that a lengthy battle will decided by a demon's endless strength and that their true goal is defeating Muzan, he scrambles to find a way to beat Akaza. He tries to understand how the demon attacks so precisely and is able to react to attacks he cannot immediately see. Recalling when Akaza had complimented Kyojuro on his highly developed fighting spirit, he attempts to define what it is and recalls a conversation he had with Inosuke. In the Butterfly Mansion, Inosuke informs Tanjiro he feels a tingle where an opponent is aiming at him, which Tanjiro surmises is the reason he was able to survive when Gyutaro had stabbed him from behind. He claims that even when someone is behind him, he can determine where they are looking; as a demonstration, he asks Tanjiro to look at his back, upon which he correctly answers that he was looking at his right shoulder. Inosuke adds that when someone looks at him with the intent to kill, he can tell immediately. Remembering this moment, Tanjiro realizes Inosuke was able to do so because of his honed sense of touch. At the same time, Inosuke had angrily remarked that if someone isn't looking at him with hostility, he cannot sense them; he points out the old woman at the Wisteria House, as she once sat behind Inosuke without him able to detect her. He believes that if he was able to get close to an opponent without emitting hostility, they wouldn't be able to detect him. However, Tanjiro added that while an elderly lady had no reason to harm him, it would be impossible to kill a demon without showing hostility. Despite remembering the moment as a silly conversation, he realizes it was still able to help him learn. What Akaza senses is fighting spirit but he remains unsure of what it is exactly and whether he can use it to disrupt Akaza's Compass Needle. As the two continue to clash, Akaza parries Giyu's blade, throwing him off-balance and attempting to throw a punch. Tanjiro goes for his exposed neck and uses Hinokami Kagura: Dance, but the Upper Rank grabs his sword from behind him and throws a punch with his other hand, mocking Tanjiro for leaving himself open. He is barely able to dodge the blow and sustains a cut across his stomach. Giyu engages him again as Tanjiro backs away, attempting to find what Akaza is sensing until he has an epiphany.

Chapter 151 is the one hundred and fifty-first chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Tanjiro remembers how his father seemed like a plant; he was never temperamental and was always calm, maintaining his demeanor until his death. Whenever he remembers him, he immediately thinks of his gentle smile and calming voice. Tanjiro recalls a time he had asked him about what he thinks when he performs the Hinokami Kagura. Even as a child, Tanjiro knew that the practice was physically demanding, as it involved performing all twelve forms from sunset to sunrise continuously. Worried about his frail body, Tanjiro asks if he can be the one to do it next year. Tanjuro thanks his son for his concern but brushes aside his worry, stating that in the last few years he performed it, he never believed it to be difficult. He remembers learning it from his own father, but comments that even though he was younger and healthier back then, doing it exhausted him greatly. He surmised it was because the forms had unnecessary movements; instead, what matters was maintaining proper breathing and control, making the most efficient moves to exert the most strength. Tanjuro states that by doing this, your mind gradually becomes clear. In the beginning, he must learn to pick up the movements and sensibilities to open all his senses and become conscious of his own body, down to his very blood vessels. It is this process that is extremely strenous and presents the most self-doubt in himself, maybe even believing that he will not succeed despite his progress. After gaining the knowledge, he will know to remove what is unnecessary and close himself off. Eventually, he can control the vessels and muscles in his body as easily as blinking, and once he clears his head, he will see the Transparent World, though only through pushing himself to his strength limits. When Tanjiro asks if he can attain it, Tanjuro reassures him that he can with diligent work, before presenting him with new warajis. Ten days before Tanjuro's death, a bear had come to the mountain they lived in and killed people. As the Kamado family sleeps through a blizzard, Tanjuro suddenly awakens and gets up from, after which he asks his eldest son to accompany him. As Tanjuro and a still sleepy Tanjiro wandered outside, the two encounter the bear, standing almost nine "shaku" tall and believed to have killed six people. Hiding behind a tree, Tanjiro watches his father confront the bear despite his illness and armed with only an axe; they had strung ropes with bells attached as a warning but his father knew it was nearby without hearing them. Tanjuro apologizes for its hunger but warns the creature not to come any closer; if anything tries to harm his family, he will show it no mercy and take its life. As the bear roars and lumbers forward to kill him, Tanjuro swings his axe and leaps up, decapitating the bear before it could move a step. As its giant head drops to the ground, Tanjiro tries to piece together what had happened; in that moment, Tanjuro would have had to swing twice to get completely through its neck, and with his sense of smell, he realizes he never wavered in the slightest. Before and after killing it, he showed no fear, no ill will, and maintained his usual calm self. As he turns to ask if his son had observed him, Tanjiro answers that he did and hugs him; Tanjuro tells him to remember the events of today. Looking back at that night, he realizes his father had given him a lesson to see the Transparent World, much like his descendants before him had to learn. It is then he understands his father's advice and how he was able to dodge Akaza's potentially lethal strike. For just an instant, when the demon grabbed his blade and was poised to swing, Tanjiro had entered the Transparent World, his vision was heightened and he could see Akaza's muscles through his body. Managing to close off his other senses to dodge something unavoidable, his body became even faster. Realizing he should have never doubted Inosuke for his advice, he resolves to take down Akaza whilst he battles Giyu.

Chapter 152 is the one hundred and fifty-second chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Having seen the Transparent World momentarily, Tanjiro realizes his own perception and speed had increased dramatically; he was able to predict Akaza's attacks and evade them. His breathing and the flow of his blood became visible to him, and he even saw his own muscles contract; he determines that by closing off his Fighting Spirit, he may be able to behead him. As the now desperate Giyu uses Water Breathing, Tenth Form: Constant Flux against Akaza, the demon only sustains a shallow cut to his neck, while the Hashira is wounded in his shoulder. He notes that making any powerful attack on Akaza will only responded to with equal force, leaving him nowhere to go when his attempts to attack him are now predictable. He marvels at the sheer power of Upper Rank Three, a killing machine whose only purpose is to fight. As Akaza taunts Giyu for using all his forms, he prepares to end the battle and expresses surprise he had lasted thus far. Tanjiro, watching as Akaza gets close to Giyu, observes the demon and attempts to concentrate. Giyu slashes down on the demon's neck, but Akaza intercepts the slash, using his fist to break off the Hashira's Nichirin katana. Shocked at his weapon breaking, Giyu stands helplessly as Akaza bids him goodbye and aims a punch at his chest. Blood sprays from his hand is but it is Akaza's own, his hand has been suddenly sliced off as Tanjiro uses Hinokami Kagura to save Giyu, who notes that the sound of his breathing has changed. Observing the Demon Slayer as he stands to face him, Akaza grows alarmed as he senses the changed Tanjiro is now exceedingly dangerous. Using Technique Development, Final Form: Blue Silver Chaotic Afterglow, Upper Three summons his Compass Needle and launches numerous explosives shockwaves in an omni-direction wave. Giyu panics at his increased power and wonders if he can negate it with Dead Calm, but now seeing into the Transparent World, Tanjiro instead wonders if time has slowed or Giyu and Akaza have. Though he uses his eleventh form, Giyu sustains severe wounds across his body as the shockwaves pass through his defensive stance. Akaza is impressed to see the Water Hashira survive the attack and offers to transform him into a demon, telling not to die like Kyojuro and Tanjiro. Instead, Giyu is stunned to see Tanjiro standing behind the Upper Rank, who is now unable to sense him. As Tanjiro looks at Akaza's neck, he angrily calls out the demon's name, causing Giyu to chide him for giving away his position. Akaza swings but Tanjiro evades the punch and goes for an attack. Initially surprised Tanjiro has survived his attack, he pays no attention and believes his Compass Needle will sense him. However, he is unable to sense anything as his Fighting Spirit is now absent. Taken aback at first, Akaza composes himself and waits for the attack to be detected, but Tanjiro has already used Hinokami Kagura: Setting Sun Transformation and beheaded the Upper Rank, much to his and Giyu's shock.

Chapter 153 is the one hundred and fifty-third chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After being beheaded by Tanjiro, Akaza reflects on the moment; in the last few hundred years, he had never seen someone without Fighting Spirit; even a baby crying shows it is fighting to live. Tanjiro's Fighting Spirit had disappeared completely, like he was fighting a plant, an anomaly that should not exist and caused his Compass to not respond. Still, he pushes past the challenge of not sensing Tanjiro, knowing that in battle, it is vital to immediately understand and handle the unexpected. Yet, he understood that Tanjiro had grasped something and surpassed his speed, attacking head-on to defeat hundreds of years of martial arts experience. His eyes bored no malice or Fighting Spirit and Akaza realizes he had perceived the "Domain of Supremacy", a Selfless State whose vague existence was something he knew but could never have attained. Akaza puts his detached head back onto his body and attempts to heal, vowing to keep fighting and get stronger. Tanjiro realizes what he is trying to do and Giyu responds by hurling his broken sword at the demon's head, knocking it away from his body. Despite his head now separated, Akaza still attempts to will himself and continue getting stronger, but the head begins to disintegrate to ash, eventually leaving Giyu's sword where it lands. Tanjiro grows relieved as he sees he has won, but his body begin to tremble from reaching his limit. However, the two notices that Akaza's body has not faded yet. As they look on in anxious anticipation, the body performs Technique Development: Compass Needle and takes a fighting stance, the neck staunching its wound to stop the bleeding. The headless body attacks Tanjiro and attempt to chop off his neck, only barely missing when he dodges the blow. As it attempts to grow a new head, it kicks Tanjiro in the side and sends him crashing into a wall. In pain and shock, Tanjiro questions how he could behead Akaza but fail to kill him. He initially believes he has a special condition, as with Gyutaro and Daki, but remember that he saw the severed head burn to ash; instead, Akaza is attempting to evolve even further, and like Muzan, he is trying to extend his weakness beyond his head. As he attempts to getting up, Tanjiro finally loses consciousness, having reached his body's limit. Watching from behind them and see him vulnerable, Giyu picks up his broken sword and uses Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide, but the headless body heals the slashes almost instantly. Without his Mark, Giyu is quickly overwhelmed by Akaza's attacks and is brought down. The demon turns to Tanjiro with the intent to kill but the Hashira yells at the demon that he is still alive, and if he wants to get to Tanjiro, he must defeat him first. A voice rings in Akaza, telling him that indomitable wills won't ever break in any hardship, and that while "they" are not samurai who carry a sword, they carry swords in their heart and use their fists. Akaza disregards the voice as a nuisance and attempts to confront Giyu, but he is held back by a young woman, who tearfully tells him, "Hakuji, that's enough."

Chapter 154 is the one hundred and fifty-fourth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Giyu readies to fight Akaza once more, he realizes the direness of his situation; his left ear hearing is gone, his right hand is numb, and he can't tell how much strength he has left. As with how sprinting can only be done for so long till the point of exhaustion, reaching past one's physical limits results in precision being lost and heavy strain on the muscles, hands, and feet. Demons on the other hand, don't feel pain, nor do they tired; it is a miracle anyone can battle an Upper Rank with just a Breathing Style. Despite the odds, Giyu resolves to save Tanjiro and prevent the death of another person who saved him. The woman urges Akaza to stop and holds onto his hand, who demands she let go and asks who she is. She begs him to leave but the demon wishes to kill Giyu and Tanjiro. When asked why he wants to kill them, he answers that he must become stronger, and when the woman asks why he must, Akaza responds, "Because... if I'm not strong, I can't bring it back. Medicine for my father." As his life flashes before his eyes, he remembers he wanted to get stronger so that he could steal money, fight back against his victims when they retaliate, and endure beatings at the magistrate's office when he is caught. Tied up and bloody from his lashings, Akaza, then known as Hakuji, is presented before the magistrate, who warns him after getting tattooed for his crimes, the next punishment is losing a hand. Hakuji laughs and dismisses the threat, claiming that without hands, he can still use his feet, vowing to never get caught again. The magistrate reminds him even at the age of eleven, he is already a repeat offender and endures beatings severe enough to make a grown man faint, calling him a 'demon child'. After leaving the office, Hakuji laughs off being insulted as a demon child and claims he was born with teeth. Suddenly, a man informs him that his father had hung himself upon learning he was caught. At the cemetery, holding a letter from him in his hand, he finds his father's headstone. The letter he wrote to him reads: "Dear Hakuji. Live a righteous life. You can still change. I didn't want to live if it meant stealing from people. I am sorry for troubling you". Clutching his headstone, Hakuji mourns his father, angrily asking if the poor were even allowed to live and cursing the world for his death. Hurt and enraged, Hakuji walked into a town and started a brawl, brutally beating several men as they tried to fight back against him, all while denouncing them for being alive as his father dies. He yells out that he wasn't a bother who needed to apologize for anything, and for his sake, he could take any punishment they give him no matter the severity. His father's condition had begun to worsen but he was sure he could save him, yet he chose to hang himself and die, a choice he was prepared to make himself and do for him. As his victims lay unconscious and Hakuji takes time to breathe, a martial artist offers him a slow clap and commends his skill. He notes he had been summoned with the news that a child was about to be killed, only to instead see that said child has knocked seven grown men unconscious. The man tells Hakuji he has promise and is impressed by his skill to fight bare-handed; Akaza wonders who he is as he realizes he is seeing his memories. When the man asks if he could come to his dojo since he has no students, Hakuji angrily dismisses his offer and threatens to kill him. He notes that he has tattoos branding him as a criminal from Edo, meaning he was banished and came here, but Hakuji pays no heed and claims it has nothing to do with him. The man tells him it is time he is reborn and takes a fighting stance; Hakuji lunges at him with all his rage but the man throws numerous rapid punches at the boy, knocking him unconscious. When he regains consciousness, the man is amazed at his toughness despite the severe beating he received, only waking up after an hour. He introduces himself as Keizo, a martial teacher at a dojo that teaches the Soryu Style, though he earns a living through odd jobs due to having no students. As Hakuji follows behind him, Keizo explains his new job is to nurse his sick daughter whilst he is away; his wife grew tired of having to care for her and drowned herself, and burdened by her death, he became weak-willed. Hakuji questions if Keizo would want a criminal to care for his daughter, but Keizo notes that since he had defeated him, it is okay with him now. It is then that Akaza realizes the reason he dislikes Tanjiro is because he reminds him of Keizo, a figment of his worthless life's story. Keizo introduces him to his daughter Koyuki, and her condition reminds Hakuji of his father's own illness. He asks if she is feeling better than before and introduces her to the boy behind him, who refuses to give his name. Keizo asks that she get it before he comes back and leaves to go to work. Alone with Hakuji, Koyuki asks if he is okay, seeing his injuries; Akaza remarks that his worthless life was nothing but lies.

Chapter 155 is the one hundred and fifty-fifth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Hakuji questions why the ill are always apologizing, whether it's because they inconvenience others, coughing loudly, or their inability to work. They want to do things themselves but cannot, and despite their suffering, they insist they are to blame. While helping Koyuki, she apologizes to Hakuji because he is unable to train or have fun with her; her condition had worsened, leading to him spending all night changing her bedding and towels, even giving her water and helping her relieve herself. Hakuji did not mind; he had helped his father with his illness and he had superior endurance to most people and was not bothered. He tells Koyuki he spends his time training anyway and does not mind not being out. She insists that he must leave her sometimes, having heard that there would be fireworks tonight and believing he must go. He responds he can simply carry her and they can go see them together. She becomes confused, and he explains that even if she can't go today, they will be on each year and she can go see them then. Upon hearing this, Koyuki begins to cry; dismayed, Hakuji notes it is the one thing he didn't like about nursing her, believing that being sick and bedridden was making her sad, something he didn't enjoy. While taking a drink with Keizo, the master notes that the kanji for "Haku" in Hakuji is the same as "Koma" in Komainu, believing that both of them must protect something like a Komainu protecting its shrine, a fact that makes Keizo laugh. Hakuji recounts how he came to own the dojo; though he wasn't a samurai, Keizo owned the land because he had saved the owner from bandits. The man was impressed with his Soryu Style, and due to not having an heir, he gave Keizo his land and dojo. However, others who wanted the land were displeased Keizo came to take ownership; a neighboring kenjutsu dojo began to harass the Soryu dojo, leading Keizo to have difficulty finding students. Despite this, lessons with him and helping Koyuki healed Hakuji's heart. Years later, Hakuji is now eighteen and Koyuki is sixteen. No longer sick, she was bright, cheery, and eager to help in the dojo, happy to live normally. One day, Keizo calls Hakuji over to speak with him. In the main room, he asks if Hakuji would like to be his successor to the dojo, adding that Koyuki likes him, rendering both teens speechless. Having been branded a criminal, he could have never imagined himself with a future, let alone one where someone likes him. He realizes he is now able to live a righteous life, as his father had asked him, giving him the hope that he could start anew. Hakuji bowed in gratitude to Keizo, recalling at that moment, he would give his life to Koyuki and Keizo, and as such, he could have never imagined them poisoned to death. Hakuji went to his father's grave to tell him he would be getting married, but while returning, he saw people at the front of the dojo, giving him a terrible nauseous feeling. Someone sadly tells him that the well they drank from was poisoned, because the assailant couldn't beat him or Keizo in a battle. Inside the dojo, Hakuji saw the bodies of Koyuki and Keizo, their faces covered and blood all over their clothes. He lamented that once more, a crisis has happened and he wasn't there to save the people he loved, even when he promised. Previously, while watching a display of fireworks, Koyuki asked him if he had remembered when they both talked about seeing them, to which he vaguely recalls. She tells him that even such a minor conversation made her happy, because even when she couldn't see them then, he had told her she could see them next year. Koyuki couldn't imagine living another year; her mother felt the same way, not wanting to see her die, which she believes is the reason she killed herself. She knew that even her father had given up on her because she was so weak. Despite it, she remarks when he told her about the coming years, it was as if Hakuji could see her future and stated it as a matter of fact. She asks if he would be her husband, holding his hand. Hakuji holds hers and says yes, promising to become stronger than anyone else and protect her for life; Akaza bitterly remarks that in the end, he never lived up to his promise. Records at the magistrate's office recount details of a gruesome massacre; enraged at losing the people he loved once again, Hakuji attacked the neighboring dojo and killed 67 of its members with his bare hands. The dojo was strewn with smashed heads, crushed organs, and bodies mangled beyond recognition, a hellish scene with jaws, eyeballs, brains, and limbs scattered along the walls and ceiling. The maid who witnessed the massacre lost her mind, and thirty years later, the records were destroyed because it was so unbelievable, it was thought to be fictional. Dripping with blood and dazed in exhausted, Hakuji walked mindlessly until he came to a footbridge. The man on it, Muzan Kibutsuji, remarks about hearing of the dojo's massacre as he didn't recall sending a demon to the town, disappointed to know it was a human who committed the murders. Hakuji threatens to kill the stranger when he suddenly lunges and impales his head with his hand. Planning to create a group of twelve powerful demons, he asks Hakuji if he could withstand the blood he will received. The mentally shattered Hakuji only replies that he did not care anymore. As a demon, now going by the name Akaza, Hakuji had lost his memories but was still drawn to seeking greater strength, even when he had nothing he wanted to protect. He didn't want to live in a world without his family, and for over the next century, he would go on to commit countless acts of pointless violence, denouncing his entire life as "a horribly sad, laughable, and ridiculous story."

Chapter 156 is the one hundred and fifty-sixth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Akaza laments he cannot go to heaven like his father, Keizo and Koyuki, he becomes furious that Tanjiro and Giyu have reminded him of his painful past. He curses humans as weak, soft, brittle, they die right away, they're brittle and disappear into nothing. Tanjiro awakens from his ordeal, shocked at how he fainted mid-battle. As Akaza begins to regenerate his head, he begins to deploy his Annihilation Type. As Tanjiro yells at him to stop, the demon becomes shocked that Tanjiro has manage to survive his kick. Declaring he will behead Akaza again, Tanjiro's sword ignites with the fires of the Hinokami Kagura. However, his sword slips out of his grasp, forcing Tanjiro to punch Akaza's face instead. The punch reminds him of when he first met Keizo, making him remember why he hates weak people. Weak people never fight face to face, they poison wells, they're impatient. He killed these weak people with his fists. He suddenly realises throughout his life as a demon, he turned his master's fighting style into a bloody weapon and never respected his father's last words, finally realising who he must truly kill. As Tanjiro panics about his lost sword and seeing Akaza about to use the same technique that killed Rengoku, he suddenly notices Giyu in the attack's range. Though Giyu tells to not worry about him, Tanjiro grabs him and throws both themselves out of the technique's path. Suddenly, he sees Akaza, smiling slightly, followed by an immense explosion. The attack leaves the surroundings devastated, as well as Akaza's body, now a broken, bloody mess. Wondering why Akaza would attack himself, Tanjiro smells a scent of gratitude from the corpse, as well as asking himself why he had smiled before hitting himself. The body begins to regenerate, but Akaza stops the process, telling himself the fight is over, he had lost fair and square. He comments Tanjiro had magnificent technique, anticipating and slashing before he could react. The broken body begins to walk away, while Akaza's spirit comments he would go to hell as a man. When he stops, to Tanjiro's confusion, his spirit meets with his father's. Asking if he was alright, his father comments yes, calling him Hakuji and thanking him. As he bows and crouches down, apologising for being unable to fix himself, his head is held by Keizo's spirit. Keizo tells him that they would never abandon him, no matter what, despite Akaza not being able to go to heaven with them. As he calls out for his master, Muzan appears, grabs his head and scolds him, reminding him to get stronger and continue fighting. With that, his body regenerates even quicker. Akaza voices his will to keep his promise and get stronger, declaring once again he will kill everyone. Suddenly, Koyuki touches his face, thanking Hakuji and saying that he has done enough. Though Muzan appears again, calling him Akaza once more, he overcomes Muzan's control and grabs Koyuki's spirit on the verge of tears, once again the human Hakuji. He tearfully apologizes for being unable to protect her, for not being there when she need him, for not being able to keep his promise. Crying for forgiveness, Koyuki is glad that Hakuji had remembered them all despite his long, demon life and returning as a human again. With the words, "Welcome back, my husband", Akaza stops his regeneration. Tanjiro watches as his body finally fades into ash.

Chapter 157 is the one hundred and fifty-seventh chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Hakuji calls out to his father, Keizo and Koyuki that he is back home, his spirit becomes engulfed in the fires of hell, joined by Koyuki. Tanjiro watches as Akaza's body finally fades into nothing, declaring the battle over. Realizing he must reach Tamayo to help her, his body can no longer handle the fatigue and he falls on his face unconscious.
