Walking to the closest body of a comrade, Tanjiro silently releases his rage, which startles Inosuke greatly. He only tells his friend that they must continue and Inosuke quietly agrees. They travel quickly through the forest and approach the strong odor of a demon, however they begin to panic as they realize that it is a headless body being used as a puppet. Tanjiro attempts to formulate a plan to take down the puppet, however Inosuke charges forward and engages with the being. To his disadvantage, Inosuke sustains multiple slashes and unknowingly gets entangled by a spider's thread, panicking as the headless puppet prepares to pierce through him. At that moment, Tanjiro quickly comes to Inosuke's defense and parries the puppet's attacks, he manages to push back the puppet and yells to Inosuke that they need to fight together in order to defeat it. In an angered protest, Inosuke calls him out saying "I won't let you embarrass me anymore!" The puppet charges forward to attack, however the boys prepare their counterattack together, Tanjiro bends over to evade the attack and tells Inosuke to go over his back. He successfully slices both of the daggers from the puppet and leaps into the air off of Tanjiro's box, meanwhile Tanjiro uses the Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide to demobilize the puppet by slashing its legs. As Inosuke descends from above, his jealousy at Tanjiro's skills and abilities builds up and he powerfully delivers the final blow to defeat the puppet demon. Tanjiro is amazed by Inosuke's final cut but becomes stunned when Inosuke suddenly charges at him. Inosuke exclaims that "I can do anything you can do dummy!" and furiously throws him up into the air. Nearby in the forest, Mother sits defeated on her rock after her strongest doll was defeated. She upsettingly blames Rui for her defeat since he had threatened her to do well. As Tanjiro spots her from above and prepares to attack, Mother panics when trying to formulate a plan however she comes to realize that she will find freedom and peace in death. She holds out her arms and accepts her fate. Tanjiro notices the change in her demeanor and switches from using the Water Breathing, First Form: Water Surface Slash to Fifth Form: Blessed Rain After the Drought, giving the frightened demon a merciful death.

Chapter 32 is the thirty-second chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As she is beheaded, Mother notes that she feels as if she is being showered by a gentle rain. She experiences no pain whatsoever and she had never imagined her death to be so gentle. She then remembers when she had her eye injured by a hulking demon for seemingly no reason. Begging for mercy and unsure why he is angry, Rui coldly tells Mother it is her own fault for not realizing why. Behind a tree, another demon watches the scene and laughs that "Dad's angry at Mom again!". As the giant demon grabs Mother, another female demon sees the abuse from high in the trees, watching with a cautious look. Mother looks at Tanjiro's eyes and sees they bore only kindness and are practically transparent, not hiding anything by sympathy. She remarks that when she was human, someone must have looked at her eyes with the same kind expression, though she does not remember who and wonders where they may be now. As thanks for bringing her peace, Mother tells Tanjiro that the Twelve Kizuki are on the mountain. Tanjiro becomes shocked and questions her final words. He realizes that the Twelve Kizuki contain high concentrations of Muzan Kibutsuji's blood and that he would need to collect it in order to create a cure for Nezuko. He suddenly remembers Inosuke and runs back to meet him. Inosuke asks if he had defeated the demon, which Tanjiro answers that he had. When asked if he is alright, Inosuke proudly claims he is fine and will soon have a head harder than him. However, Tanjiro is dismayed at the extent of Inosuke's wounds and is saddened at being unable to save his fellow Demon Slayers. He looks back at Mother's final moments and how she smelled so strongly of fear and suffering, enough that she wished for death. Tanjiro questions the mountain's nature, wondering why the Twelve Kizuki are present and if a family of demons lives within the forests, since demons do not group up. Elsewhere in the forest, Zenitsu feels a pain in his hand while walking in the woods searching for Tanjiro and Inosuke. He is annoyed by the forest's stench and is additionally repulsed by the spiders' sound. Suddenly, something moves behind him and he demands it to stop, only to look down and see a giant spider with a human head. Horrified and confused, he sprints away and wonders if he is actually trapped within a nightmare due to his situation. He soon finds himself within a clear and finds threads strewn across the trees. Hanging on them is a wooden house and attached to the threads are Demon Slayers transforming into spiders. Even more worried and now nauseous from the overwhelming smell, Zenitsu receives a bigger surprise when a giant spider demon emerges from within the suspended house. Zenitsu sprints away in fear but the demon unexpectedly tells he that he has already lost. Unwilling to talk to the giant spider, Zenitsu flatly denies what he had said only to be told to look at his hand. To his shock, it appears bruised and swollen. The Spider Demon tells him that since he had been bitten by a spider, he will soon transform into one.

Chapter 33 is the thirty-third chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After revealing to Zenitsu that he has been poisoned and will begin to transform into a spider, the Spider Demon pulls out a pocket watch and begins to describe the different phases of his transformation. He explains that within a span of a few hours, Zenitsu's hands and feet will begin to tingle, the feelings of dizziness and nausea will set in, followed by the feeling of intense pain, until his body finally shrinks and he loses consciousness. When he awakens, he will find that his body would have finished transitioning into a demon spider. Zenitsu becomes even more horrified as the spiders crawl around his feet. He dashes away while openly admitting that he is already aware that running away will not help his situation, and ends up climbing a nearby tree. Witnessing Zenitsu's episode of panic, the demon laughs at him and reassures him that he has nothing to fear, as once the Demon Slayer finishes his transformation, he will no longer have a mind of his own or any sense of emotions. In response to his taunt, Zenitsu rambles saying that he doesn't want any of that and subtly insults him by saying "I bet you don't have any friends! People must hate you!", leaving the Spider Demon glaring at him with spite. As Zenitsu continues to cry about his fate, the situation is reminiscent of when he had climbed up a tree in the past. A voice can be heard sternly yelling at him to pull himself together, as Zenitsu squeals about his impending death if he continues to train. His trainer stubbornly calls him an idiot and tells him that training won't kill him, commanding him to get down from the tree at once. Zenitsu continues to wail, calling the old man "Gramps"; he cries out that he loves him, much to his trainer's surprise, and that he is eternally grateful for paying off his debt. Nonetheless, he believes himself to not be capable enough to be a Demon Slayer. He rants about his inability to make progress, describing how he trains to the point of lacking sleep but never sees any fruit to his labor and eventually lets out his anger at his failure. As Gramps tries to calm Zenitsu and claims he truly possesses talent, a sudden bolt of lightning strikes Zenitsu. Gramps looks on in horror as Zenitsu finally falls from the tree with his new striking blonde hair. Zenitsu remarks that he hates his lack of self faith; though he means to do good, he ends up getting scared and fleeing. He insists that he wants to change and become better, yelling out loud that he is working as hard as he can, but transforming into a monster now, he can no longer handle even more issues. The Spider Demon is confused at his opponent's weird rants, as the spiders crawl up the tree. Zenitsu yells at them to leave but discovers that clumps of his hair are falling out, since the demon had not mentioned it before hand. Fear finally causes Zenitsu to fall asleep, driving even more confusion to the Spider Demon, in disbelief he had been sent to kill his family. As he falls off the tree to the forest floor, Zenitsu begins to breathe and preforms Thunder Breathing, First Form: Thunderclap and Flash to jump off the trunk and initiate his attack on the Spider Demon. In response to the sudden maneuver, the demon spews his Poison Sputum to try deter Zenitsu, but he is able to evade his attack midair. As Zenitsu lands on the ground he immediately attempts to utilize First Form: Thunderclap and Flash but is swarmed by numerous spiders. He continuously dodges their attacks and tries to use his form but is constantly hounded by the acidic poison of the Spider Demon, who realizes to his amusement that Zenitsu is capable of only one form. Zenitsu thinks back to when Gramps had encouraged him that it was alright to only know one form, though he notes that before encouraging him, he was furious since Thunder Breathing had six forms. He remembers when his trainer began to pound his head continually, explaining that when a sword is made, the steel is beaten till all impurities are removed to refine it. Though Zenitsu understands, he claims he is not made with steel but flesh. The Spider Demon, seeing him standing still without attacking, believes Zenitsu will soon fall. Gramps motivates his student to master his one form; he may cry and run but he must never give up. He tells Zenitsu to believe that all his training, no matter how hellish, will eventually pay off. "Be rid of all your impurities. Become a blade that is stronger than anyone!"

Chapter 34 is the thirty-fourth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Zenitsu recalls Gramps's message to master even a single thing, the Spider Demon launches another Poison Sputum blob, nearly hitting his body and dissolving his haori. More of the demon's spiders appear and force Zenitsu on the defensive, who begins to feel the poison making his hands and feet numb. He realizes that the poison will soon cause him pain. He remembers a time in his past when he was berated by another unnamed student of Gramps. The boy angrily scolds Zenitsu for crying all day and wonders why he was still being taught the Thunder Breathing techniques. The student feels he is worth their trainer's time, unlike Zenitsu. When he tries to interject and explain Gramps' reasoning, the boy throws a peach in his face and tells him to stop calling their trainer "Gramps" as an act of familiar. He remarks that their trainer is a former Hashira, and as one of the most highly regarded men in the Demon Slayer Corps, he believes training Zenitsu to be a waste of time and angrily dismisses him. Zenitsu remarks that being an orphan meant he had no one to give hope or believe in him. "No one dreamed of a future where I'd latch on to something and fulfill a dream." Be it being useful or protecting someone, no one had the expectations that he could succeed. No one except Gramps. He would scold him continuously, and whenever Zenitsu tried to run away, he was there to pull him back, and though he was at times harsh, Gramps never gave up on him. The Spider Demon commands his spiders to inject Zenitsu with more poison; using their barbed tongues, they attempt to stab him but miss. Zenitsu suddenly vomits blood while moving to evade them, allowing the spiders to pile on him. Suddenly, the Demon Slayer grips his blade and the air begins to vibrate, causing the spiders to fall off of him. He uses Thunder Breathing, First Form: Thunderclap and Flash, Sixfold and speeds towards the Spider Demon, launching six powerful dashes before decapitating his opponent instantly. As the demon dies, Zenitsu falls atop the house, satisfied that he had accomplished his dream of protecting people. He realizes that the time spent with Gramps was truly not wasted, but as the poison takes hold, he struggles to cling to life. He urges himself not to give up and uses his breathing to slow the circulation of the poison. He fights to survive, unwilling to let Gramps or Tanjiro be disappointed. Elsewhere in the forests, Tanjiro hears the sound of a lightning strike — Zenitsu's attack — but becomes confused since he doesn't smell thunderclouds. Inosuke is not bothered to investigate while Tanjiro intends to. He tells Inosuke to descend the mountain but his friend vehemently denies being hurt, much to his confusion. Suddenly, they hear a nearby splash across the river: a pale young demon. Inosuke immediately gives chase but the demon calls out to her father. Emerging from the forest, a giant humanoid Spider Demon appears, angrily demand the Demon Slayers stay away from his family. He throws a punch against the riverbed that knocks back Tanjiro and Inosuke from the sheer force.

Chapter 35 is the thirty-fifth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Using Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel, Tanjiro attempts to slash off Father's right arm but discovers his blade are unable to cut through his thick skin. The demon tries to punch him but has his left arm pinned by Inosuke, who is similarly unable to cut further than the surface. Father flings them away and charges towards Tanjiro, demanding they stay away from his family. Inosuke attempt to attack from behind but is spotted and punched away, hurtling into the river. Tanjiro uses Water Breathing, Second Form: Improved, Lateral Water Wheel, cutting through a tree in front of him and causing it to land on the giant demon, pinning him and saving Inosuke. Seeing his chance, he prepares to using Water Breathing's Tenth Form to finish off the demon but Inosuke warns him to remain on guard, too weak from blood loss to intervene. Father picks up the fallen tree and swings it into Tanjiro, causing his blade to become stuck. With the Demon Slayer neutralized, the Spider Demon flings him away into the forest. Startled, Inosuke calls out to "Kentaro" as he hurtles away. Tanjiro, believing Father to be the Twelve Kizuki demon, warns Inosuke of the danger and advises him to stay alive and wait for him, promising to be back. Atop the suspended house, Zenitsu's condition worsens and he struggles to breathe, to the concern of the transformed Demon Slayers he rescued. As he apologizes to Nezuko, a butterfly appears to float above him and flutters down, revealed to be Shinobu. She gently asks if Zenitsu is alright but the Demon Slayer doesn't respond. To stop himself from hitting the ground too quickly, Tanjiro uses Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel, slowing his momentum to a full stop safely. As he composes himself, a scream is heard nearby; looking behind him, Tanjiro finds Rui cutting Daughter's face with a web in his hands, the threads coated in her blood. Rui, surprised to see him, asks what he is looking at for, claiming their situation isn't a show.

Chapter 36 is the thirty-sixth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Having stumbled into a conflict between Rui and Daughter, Tanjiro questions Rui on why he is harming his friend. To this, Rui claims they are closer than just a superficial friendship. They are a family and the current matter is only between him and his older sister, threatening to carve up Tanjiro for interrupting. Tanjiro remarks that all bonds are precious, not just family but even friendships and that not being blood related doesn't make it superficial. He states that while he can smell the scent of a strong bond, all he senses from him and Daughter is the smell of fear, hatred, and loathing. He flatly declaring their bond fake, angering Rui. Entering the situation, a lone Demon Slayer spots him and deems the demon to be an easy kill. As Tanjiro wonders who he is, the swordsman warns him not to take his kill, thinking that slaying the "kid demon" will make his rank and pay go up. He remarks that most of his unit is now dead but slaying one demon should suffice. As he charges towards Rui, Tanjiro warns him to stop but the demon flings a web at him, slicing the Demon Slayer into several pieces. Tanjiro stares in horror at Rui's swift movements and sees him glaring with pure rage, sensing his menacing aura. Rui furiously dares him to repeat his words, worrying Daughter. Tanjiro grips his blade as he realizes that he must defeat Rui before he is able to return to Inosuke's aid, then proceeds to stubbornly repeat that the ties between Rui and Daughter are fake. Elsewhere on the mountain, Inosuke can be seen hiding behind a tree while trying to formulate a plan to deal with Father. The tree is suddenly smashed with such power that Inosuke is forced to get up and run away, thinking to himself that he has find a solution in order to survive until Tanjiro returns. Once Inosuke realizes that he's starting to depend on Tanjiro's help, he becomes infuriated with himself and decides to attack Father head on. He tries to slice through the demon's arms, and uses his anger and frustration to successfully cut through. He expresses his excitement and proclaims his newfound strength, while he gloats on his accomplishment he sees Father running away and becomes infuriated by his audacity. He gives chase and hunts the Spider Demon down to a nearby tree, and witnesses him begin to tremble, thinking that he is doing so out of fear. However, Father begins to molt from his body into a larger, more menacing form. Inosuke can only stare in paralyzed fear as the newly transformed demon lands down to face him again.

Chapter 37 is the thirty-seventh chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As the newly evolved demon towers menacingly over Inosuke, he remarks having never felt such pressure seeing an opponent. Believing he will die, he remembers Tanjiro's words to wait for his return. Trying to find the motivation to continue, he remembers when Hisa had told him to live his life with pride and wished him good fortune. Realizing he cannot lose now, he takes a stance and declares he is "Inosuke Hashibira of the Demon Slayer Corps", commanding the demon to face him. Father immediately punches Inosuke so hard, he slams into several trees. The demon quickly approaches the downed Demon Slayer to finish him off, but Inosuke avoids the blow and leaps into the air to attack him from behind. He tries to slice the Spider Demon's neck by using his Beast Breathing, Third Fang: Devour but his blades break when trying to slice through the thick skin. Father becomes infuriated and once again slams Inosuke into another nearby tree, knocking the wind out of him. He picks Inosuke up by the throat and squeezes him, yelling once again for him to "stay away from my family." Inosuke refuses to succumb and uses his Beast Breathing, First Fang: Pierce as a last ditch effort to escape, but his broken weapons fail to damage the giant Spider Demon. Father squeezes even harder and crushes his opponent's throat, and life begins to flash before his eyes. Inosuke recalls a memory of a woman coated in blood apologizing to him as an infant, and he also envisions the faces of Tanjiro, Zenitsu, and Hisa. As he wonders who the woman is, blood begins to pour from his mask. Father's arm is suddenly sliced off and Inosuke drops to the floor. The Spider Demon squeals in shock as Giyu Tomioka enters the battle. Father quickly regenerates his arm and sprints towards Giyu with extraordinary speed, but the Hashira preforms the Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide and dismembers the demon instantly. Inosuke gets up from the floor and stares at Giyu with admiration, becoming excited trying to figure out who he is as the latter nonchalantly proceeds to sheath his sword with the process of . Elsewhere on the mountain, Rui eerily reveals his intentions to slowly torture Tanjiro to death, but reassures him that if he takes back what he said, he will not prolong his demise. Despite sustaining several wounds, Tanjiro stubbornly refuses to take back his words and goes on to justify his reasons saying that Rui is the one that's in the wrong. Tanjiro braces himself and smells out the threads to avoid them as he approaches Rui. He uses the Water Breathing, First Form: Water Surface Slash to slice through Rui's threads, but looks on in shock as his blade is split into two pieces by the thread.

Chapter 38 is the thirty-eighth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After defeating Father of the Spider Family, Giyu is confronted by the Demon Slayer he had just saved. Seeing he has killed a Twelve Kizuki demon, Inosuke demands that Giyu fight him so that he can defeat him and rise up through the ranks. The uninterested Hashira simple tells him to go back to training, angering Inosuke; Giyu also mentions that the demon was not a member of the Twelve Kizuki while unbundling some rope. Inosuke quickly retorts his statement, claiming he was right about not believing the demon was of the Twelve Kizuki and only repeated what Tanjiro had said, but he suddenly finds himself tied up in a tree. Stunned by his immense speed, he tries to call out to Giyu, who only tells him to stay out of battle if he doesn't recognize his own injuries. Inosuke yells out that he cannot hear him but the Hashira has already left him alone. As he tries to dodge the thread that sliced his sword in two, Tanjiro sustains a long cut along his face. Shocked to see that the threads are even stronger than Father's body, he apologizes to Sakonji and Haganezuka. Rui then manipulates more to surround the Demon Slayer and close around him, as Tanjiro struggles to move away, remarking that the threads seem to be alive. Before he can get hit, Nezuko appears in front of him and takes the brunt of the attack, enduring numerous cuts throughout her body. Tanjiro looks on in horror as Nezuko bleeds from her wounds, and he quickly carries her away to safety. Seeing her sudden appearance from the box, Daughter surmises that she is a demon. As Tanjiro apologizes to her for getting herself injured, Rui begins to tremble and points to Nezuko, asking if they are siblings. Tanjiro angrily answers that it doesn't matter if they are, examining the severity of her injuries. As the demon realizes that he has witnessed siblings protecting one another, much to Daughter's worry, he declares Nezuko's actions as a bond between family and something now he wants for himself. Sensing his sudden change in demeanor, Daughter tries to claim that she is his sister and begs him not to abandon her. Suddenly, Rui lashes out and releases several threads from his fingers, slicing the demon to pieces along with several distant trees. He angrily claims that none of his family had ever fulfilled their roles as the dismembered Daughter states that even he recognized her as a sister at some point. When she asks for a chance to make up for her mistakes, Rui tells her to kill the remaining Demon Slayers on the mountain, willing to forgive her if she does. Daughter picks up her head and runs away. Now left alone with Tanjiro and Nezuko, Rui begins to strike a deal with the siblings. He informs the two of how their bond had made him shiver, but despite the fact that it might break his heart, he would still have to kill them. Rui then goes on to inform them that the only way that he will spare them would be if Tanjiro handed Nezuko over to him. Enraged by his audacity, Tanjiro holds Nezuko tightly and angrily proclaims that he will never hand her over, claiming that she has her own feelings and free will to choose. Rui responds to his claims by stating that he will use fear to forcefully form a bond with her, which infuriates Tanjiro even more. Again, Tanjiro angrily yells that he will never hand Nezuko over to him and that he will cut off Rui's head before she is taken from him. Realizing that Tanjiro will not give up easily, Rui claims that he has no choice but kill him and take Nezuko by force. He acknowledges his fighting spirit and pulls his hair to the side to hauntingly reveal that he is Lower Five of the Twelve Kizuki.

Chapter 39 is the thirty-ninth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Rui recounts his belief of what the father and mother's roles are in a family, stating that the parents protect the children, and the older children protect the youngest, even with their lives. He adds that people who do not fulfill their roles in life are not worthy of living and informs Tanjiro that his sole role in life is to give up his sister or die, because he cannot win against him. As Tanjiro contemplates a plan in order to defeat Rui, the demon becomes annoyed by his look of determination and wonders if he believes he has a chance of killing him; he uses his threads to capture Nezuko from behind Tanjiro and proceeds to hold her hostage. Desperate to save his sister, Tanjiro charges at Rui and demands that she is released, but as the demon begins to spindle more threads, Nezuko unexpectedly claws at his face, forcing him to release her. Lower Five launches threads at his opponent but Tanjiro flips back to avoid Rui's attack, only to end up losing sight of Nezuko. As he looks around to locate her, a splash of blood falls onto his face and he looks up in horror to see his sister, profusely bleeding and strung up in the demon's threads. Rui calmly demands that Tanjiro stop his screaming since as a demon, Nezuko won't die. However, he believes she must accept her new role and decides he will let her bleed, adding that if she still doesn't obey him, he can leave her to burn when the sun rises. Despite his anger, Tanjiro regains control of his emotions and concentrates his breathing. When he looks into the sky, Rui notices that Nezuko has lost consciousness and senses an "odd feeling" resonating from Nezuko, different to normal demons. Attacking the Lower Rank once again, Tanjiro performs the Total Concentration: Water Breathing, Tenth Form: Constant Flux to charge at Rui. Using increasingly powerful slashes by building up power with each swing, he successfully cuts the threads using his broken blade, catching Rui off guard. However, the demon is amused to think Tanjiro had believed he was using his strongest threads and infuses his blood into new ones, casting Blood Demon Art: Cutting Thread Cage in order to quickly end Tanjiro's life. Tanjiro smells the immense danger coming from the unavoidable attack and believes he is going to die, unable to build up the power to cut through. Suddenly, his life begin to flash before his eyes. As the many moments of his life flood before him, Tanjiro recollects the theory that he is being given a chance to search through his memories to find a method to escape. At that moment, he remembers a memory from his childhood in which he played with Nezuko as their father watches them, before telling Tanjiro to control his breathing and ""become like Hinokami.""

Chapter 4 is the fourth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Sakonji explains to Tanjiro that the Demon Slayer Corps consists of a few hundred members, and though it is not recognized by the government, it has fought demons for a long time and continues to battle demons today. However, its leader is shrouded in mystery. He goes on to tell Tanjiro more about demons. While it is unsure how they began, there are things that are known with certainty, such as that they must eat humans in order to survive and have special abilities, such as being able to regenerate when they're physically injured. Others can even change form or use special powers. The only way they can be destroyed is through exposure to sunlight or by decapitation with a specialized blade. The organization of the Demon Slayers have continued to hunt them with their mortal bodies across a number of generations. Sakonji then introduces his role as one of the many 'cultivators', individuals who train and furnish swordsmen with a variety of techniques and skills. He instructs Tanjiro that if anyone desires to join the ranks of the Demon Slayers, they must first survive an event known as Final Selection, held at Mount Fujikasane. Sakonji tells Tanjiro that he will be the one to decide if Tanjiro is qualified to participate in Final Selection. After numerous descents down Mount Sagiri, Tanjiro has grown stronger and his sense of smell has sharpened. However, the traps have become deadlier at the same time. When he makes a descent while holding a katana, it gets in the way and causes him to be ensnared in traps again. Next, he is taught the sword, swinging it repeatedly and Sakonji explaining how slicing along the direction of the blade is the way to make a cut, as it may break when used incorrectly. Then, he is taught to get back up after a fall, with Sakonji repeatedly felling him over a whole day. He then instructs Tanjiro to attack him armed whilst he is bare-handed. The old trainer effortlessly flips him into the air and defeats his student. He is taught breathing forms, but when told to take a deep breath, Tanjiro's long inhale is answered by a slap in the stomach for its incorrect method. Meanwhile, Nezuko has fallen into a deep sleep while Tanjiro trains for half a year. Sakonji calls a doctor who comes by to look at her, but he finds nothing wrong with the demon. Worried that she will die soon, Tanjiro steels himself and trains harder. After a year of training, Sakonji tells Tanjiro that he has nothing else to teach the boy. Taken aback, Tanjiro notes the time that has passed since their arrival. Sakonji tells the boy to continue improving his techniques and challenges the boy to split a huge boulder in half in order to prove his worth and participate in Final Selection. Tanjiro starts to panic, as the task at hand seems impossible with a mere blade, but from that day onwards, Sakonji ceases to teach Tanjiro new skills. As another half year passes, while his technique and body has gotten more refined, Tanjiro is still unable to split the rock no matter how hard he practices. Feeling extremely disheartened, he yells in frustration, to which a voice asks him to silence himself. Surprised, Tanjiro observes that the voice came from a person wearing a fox mask who was perched on top of the boulder, a person who did not have a scent nor a presence. The masked boy tells Tanjiro to bear his suffering like a man and attacks him with a wooden blade, which Tanjiro clumsily blocks. The boy notes the extent of Tanjiro's weaknesses, deeming him unsuitable to be a Demon Slayer.

Chapter 40 is the fortieth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. On a cold wintery night, a young Tanjiro watches with his mother as his father performs a ceremonial kagura. Kie tells him that as their family works with fire, to keep themselves safe, they offer a dance and prayers to Hinokami, the fire god, at the start of each year. Tanjiro watches his father intently, looking at his attire and movements. In another time, he asks his father on how he could perform for so long in the cold, remarking his lungs could freeze. Tanjuro tells he there is a special way of breathing that doesn't allow him to tire no matter how much he moves. If he can learn it, he'll be fine even in the cold and he could dancer forever. His father then makes him promise to wear his earrings when he performs the kagura, and to always wear them so they are not lost. After seeing his memories, Tanjiro's Water Breathing ignites in fire as he uses Hinokami Kagura: Dance, slicing Rui's strongest threads before him. The demon instantly forms new ones in his path but Tanjiro pushes on and is determined to behead him, knowing that by switching to Hinokami Kagura from Water Breathing, he will reel from the exhaustion when he stops. He senses the Opening Thread but only his arm will reach him. He asks his father to forgive him as he closes in on Rui, believing that saving Nezuko can only be done if he sacrifices himself to kill the demon.Nezuko, still strung in the threads, is visited by Kie, who asks her to wake up and tells her daughter she is now able. She tearfully tells her that if she doesn't act now, Tanjiro will die. Nezuko suddenly regains consciousness and stretches out her arm as she spots Rui and Tanjiro. Using Blood Demon Art: Exploding Blood, she wills her blood on the threads in Tanjiro's path to burn and destroys them, surprising Rui to see his attacks on fire. With Tanjiro's attack being countered by Rui, he had strung threads to kill him as he gets close, but Nezuko's blood stained on them has burned them away without harming Tanjiro. His sword, containing a drop of Nezuko's blood, reaches Rui's neck, and despite the demon believing he won't be able to cut through, Nezuko's burning blood gives enough force for the blade to cut through, as Tanjiro declares that the bond between them won't be severed by anyone. With one final push, the Demon Slayer beheads Lower Five in a bright circle of flames.

Chapter 41 is the forty-first chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After being dismissed by Rui, Daughter flees as she realizes her mistake of ruining the family; made up of demons who were all strangers to one another, they feared the Demon Slayers and wanted companions. Because he possessed all the abilities, Rui splits his powers amongst them, and since he was a favourite of Muzan, they agreed; his first act was to change their appearance to match his. It is also shown that despite her appearance, Mother was actually a young girl, who had only been recently been turned into a demon, thus she retained her human memories. She mourned her lost humanity and couldn't play her role sufficiently, which, along with failing to maintain her appearance, caused Rui to punish her. Anyone who disobeyed him or failed to play their role was punished by Rui, through slashing them, taking away their intelligence, or leaving them in the sun. Daughter only cared about herself and dismissed the others as fools, but it is she who has made a mistake now. She recalls when she had told Rui that their mother and "older brother" have been defeated and asked him on what they should do with the Demon Slayers closing in. When Rui does not respond, she suggests that they should flee, unaware that her eyes have reverted to their original appearance. Notices this, Rui only glares at her with displeasure. While wondering if Rui would eventually realize his goal to have a family is hopeless, she sees Murata, who notices her as well but is trapped in her Blood Demon Art, Acid Cocoon. He attempts to cut his way out, but the silk is too soft and durable. Daughter ominously tells him that the acid will first melt his clothes, before liquifying his body into her meal. Out of nowhere, Shinobu stands behind the demon and asks if she spins her silk from her palms. Shocked by her appearance, she fails to respond when Shinobu greets her and makes note of the moon's lovely appearance. Daughter launches ropes of her silk but Shinobu evades the attack, surmising that the demon does want to befriend her. The demon comments that her attacker's strong aura is like Rui's, but instead, it feels cold and frightening, as if death is next to her. She then pleads for Shinobu's help, claiming that Rui is forcing her to act and if she crosses him, she will be punished. Shinobu seemingly pities her and responds that she will help if they can get along, but she must confirm something first. She asks the demon on how many people has she killed, to which Daughter answers she has killed five, worried over her intentions. The Hashira tells her not to lie since she knows she has killed 80. When Daughter denies this, she notes that she came from west of the mountain and saw hordes of cocoons, all with its captives dead, adding that she saw fourteen in one spot alone. Shinobu states she is not angry and simply wants an accurate number. When Daughter asks what good it is to be accurate, she answers it is so she can be punished and reborn to truly befriend her. She goes into graphic detail about how she will torture her; gouging her eyes, sliting her stomach, and pulling out her intestines so that she can be forgiven. The demon becomes horrified to hear this, and Shinobu taunts her by adding that as a demon, she won't have lasting wounds. Daughter tries once more to trap her in silk, but Shinobu uses Insect Breathing, Butterfly Dance: Caprice and stabs her multiple times. She reaches her neck and sees she hasn't been beheaded, noticing Shinobu is too small to behead her. However, her heart rate climbs and she begins to bleed all throughout her body before slumping to the ground in pain. Shinobu tells the demon not to feel safe if she wasn't beheaded, as there are those who use poison. She introduces herself as Shinobu Kocho, the Insect Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps; she is the only one who cannot cut off a demon's head, but makes up with her usage of poison; she then offers a false apology to the dead demon because she cannot hear her anymore.

Chapter 42 is the forty-second chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Shinobu stabs the cocoon to free Murata, who emerges coughing and sputtering from his ordeal. She asks if he is alright, to which he responds he is fine, noting that she simply poked the cocoon with her blade to break it. Murata asks if it is safe to leave the demon unfinished, and Shinobu explains that the demon is dead due to her poison, made with wisteria and her chemistry expertise. She then comments that while his clothes have dissolved, his body is fine, causing Murata to cover himself in embarrassment. After beheading Rui, the exhausted Tanjiro is relieved he has won, thanks to his father's help; despite not knowing if the kagura of his family would work, it has enabled him to save Nezuko. However, his vision is blurring, his ears are ringing, and his body is racked with pain, yet he realizes that Inosuke still needs him. He sees the unconscious Nezuko a distance away and begins to crawl towards her, unaware of Rui's body behind him. He then smells blood, instead of the scent of ash that is present when a demon dies. Rui's body walks towards him as he reveals his head is attached to his threads, taunting him for believing he had killed him and revealing he had sliced off his own head to avoid his attack. Now planning to kill him and Nezuko, Rui remarks he has not been angry in a long time; Tanjiro attempts to catch his breath but is still too weak. The demon notes that Nezuko's flames only burned him and his threads, but is otherwise thankful he is alive, stating that now, he is so enraged, he can slice up the Demon Slayer without any regret. As Tanjiro tries more desperately to regain his breathing, Lower Five uses Blood Demon Art: Murderous Eye Basket, surrounding him in a shrinking web of threads, and despite his efforts, he remains too exhausted to even pick up his blade. Before the web can close and kill him, Tanjiro is saved when Giyu intervenes, slicing the threads apart. As he wonders if the new figure is Zenitsu, Giyu commends him for holding on till his arrival, while Rui denounces the Demon Slayers as scum who continue to interfere with him. Using Blood Demon Art: Cutting Thread Rotation, the demon infuses his threads with blood and launches the spinning web at Giyu, who responds with Water Breathing, Eleventh Form: Dead Calm. As the web gets close, it suddenly disintegrates before hitting Giyu; shocked to see his strongest threads destroyed, he tries again but is easily decapitated by the Hashira. While Sakonji's Water Breathing only has ten forms, Giyu has developed an exclusive eleventh form based on a dead calm, when the sea has no waves and the still surface reflects like a mirror; when an attack get close, the form calms it into nothing. Rui's severed head curses Giyu and threatens to kill him before killing Tanjiro and Nezuko, only to see the Demon Slayer embracing his sister. Stunned by the sight, he recalls when Mother had asked him what he wanted, but he could not answer at the time because he did not have his human memories; he created the Spider Family when he thought the memories would return if he felt a familial bond, realizing now that he had wanted to remember his parents.

Chapter 43 is the forty-third chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Since birth, Rui had always been weak, so much so that walking was hard. One night, he was visited by Muzan, who transformed him into a demon to "save" him. His parents were upset to discover what had happened; while he became strong, he could no longer be out in the sunlight and was forced to feed on human flesh. They once found him after he had killed someone; Rui's father demanded to know what he had done while his mother cried in anguish. Previously, he had heard a story about a father who drowned saving his child from a river. He was touched and considered it an act of true parental love. To him, dying to save your child was a parent fulfilling their role, before then questioning why his parents tried to kill him. Rui awoke to his father raising a knife to kill him, while his mother sobbed nearby. He fatally wounded them and sat outside, remarking that his mother's love was fake and that they weren't a real family. To his surprise, she apologized to Rui for not giving him a strong body despite giving him life, before dying. Upon hearing her last words, he remembered his father had said that he will die with him as well; in his anger, he failed to realize his father was willing to die and share his sin of killing someone. It was then that Rui understood they truly had a strong family bond and he was the one to have just severed it. Muzan then appeared to comfort the young demon, stating that his parents were to blame because they could not accept what he became and telling him to be proud. Unable to bear the weight of his actions, Rui believed him, despite knowing that he was at fault. Even when he irrationally blamed his parents, he sorely missed them; creating his demonic family did not stop the feeling of emptiness, and because he was the strongest, no one in his family could truly protect him. As Giyu looks on, the demon's burning body falls short of reaching Tanjiro while recalling that the stronger he became, the less his human memories remained. In the end, all he could do was reach out to connections he lost and failed to recreate. Tanjiro senses the scent of sadness from his body and places his hand on him, Rui remarking it is as if warm sunlight is on him. Having remembered his parents once more, he wishes he could apologize to them for something he accepted is his fault, but knows that by killing scores of people, he will go to Hell and doesn't deserve to be with them. In the afterlife, a hand comforts Rui and tells him that where he goes, they will go too. His father and mother appear, who tells him that even in Hell, they will go with him. As his appearance returns back into a human, Rui breaks down in tears and hugs them tightly, incessantly apologizing for his actions, as the fires of Hell consume the family; Lower Five finally fades into nothing. Giyu steps on the demon's clothes and accosts Tanjiro for showing sympathy, stating that even when he looked like a child, he was still a centuries-old monster that ate people. Tanjiro retorts that to appease the spirits of those killed by demons and prevent more bloodshed, he will not hesitant to behead them, but he will not belittle the demons who regret their actions and suffer because of it, "Because demons were once human. Because they were human like me!", begging Giyu to move his foot. To Tanjiro, they are not ugly and worthless, but pitiful creatures who now exist as empty shells of their former selves. Giyu then recognizes him and Nezuko, much to his surprise, before he then looks up to see something moving towards him. He swings his sword and blocks Shinobu's attempt to kill Nezuko. Surprised to see his actions, she recalls when Giyu had said that demons and humans cannot coexist, before saying his actions are why he is hated.

Chapter 44 is the forty-fourth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. After being treated and placed with the rest of the injured Demon Slayers, Zenitsu looks around to see masked figures quickly cleaning up the scene. He notices the girl leading them is from Final Selection, and she wears a similar hairpin to Shinobu. One man asks for where the wounded will go and she answers that they go to her place, the so-called Butterfly Mansion, before leaving to clear up any nearby demons to allow them to work in peace. The figures also find the tied up and unconscious Inosuke. As Shinobu orders again for Giyu to move, he instead asks for why she said that everyone hates him, to Tanjiro and Shinobu's surprise. Shinobu slyly replies she was unaware he believed he was hated and apologizes for letting it slip, surprising Giyu and Tanjiro further at the unusual scene; she then tells the Demon Slayer he is guarding a demon and advises him to move away. Tanjiro states she is half-mistaken as the demon is in fact his younger sister, but Shinobu's response is offering to kill her with a gentle toxin, worrying him. Giyu speaks up and orders him to carry Nezuko and flee in spite of his wounds. A grateful Tanjiro takes Nezuko in his arms, thanks the Hashira and runs away. Seeing this, Shinobu tells him that his actions are against the Corps' rules. Tanjiro grabs Nezuko's box as he runs through the forest, despite the immense pain his body is in. Nezuko soon wakes up as Tanjiro wonders if he will be forced to leave the Demon Slayer Corps as he knows they would not accept a Demon Slayer carrying a demon, let alone a sibling. Suddenly, the girl from earlier leaps from behind the trees and steps on his back, causing Tanjiro to fall and drop Nezuko; she raises her blade and tries to behead her but Tanjiro pulls her haori and causes her to miss. He calls for Nezuko to run away but is knocked unconscious by a swift kick to the head. The girl pursues the fleeing demon but Nezuko shrinks down to make herself harder to hit; initially confused as to why she isn't fighting back, she sets aside her doubts and tries to kill her as she was taught. After restraining the Insect Hashira, Giyu is questioned on why he is acting against the rules by interfering with the slaying of a demon, Shinobu asking for him he explain himself. When she asks again, he replies it was because of something that happened two years ago, but she instead wonders if he is trying to bore her with a long-winded story to get back at her for saying he is hated by people, earning Giyu's ire. Shinobu deploys a blade in her shoe and attempts to escape his hold, but a Kasugai crow interrupts with an announcement, with her only barely missing his face. The crow gives the message that Tanjiro and Nezuko are to be taken back to their headquarters; the girl chasing Nezuko hears the message and asks her for her identity. Tanjiro is soon found by the masked people, who notes his severe wounds; one of them feels guilty for having to tie him up. These agents are known as Kakushi; the clean up brigade of the Corps in the aftermath of a battle, as most members lack the skill in swordsmanship. As Tanjiro lies on the ground in a garden, still tied up and unconscious, a voice repeatedly orders him to wake up before yelling at him to do so. He looks up to see a group of swordsman looking at him, with the voice telling Tanjiro he is now in the presence of the Hashira.

Chapter 45 is the forty-fifth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Confused by his surroundings, what a Hashira is, and who are the people around him, Tanjiro's uncertainty is answered when Shinobu tells him he is at the Demon Slayer Corps Headquarters and will now be put on trial. Within the Corps exists the Hashira, the nine most skilled and powerful Demon Slayers in the organization. Whereas lower-ranked members die quickly and frequently, the Hashira provide stability within the Corps. Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku believes a trial is unnecessary; since protecting a demon is plainly against the rules, he advises them to kill Tanjiro and Nezuko summarily. Sound Hashira Tengen Uzui offers to do the task, promising to flamboyantly spray Tanjiro's blood with panache. On the other hand, Love Hashira Mitsuri Kanroji is against killing "such a cute kid" and refuses to act. While the Stone Hashira, Gyomei Himejima, pities the siblings for being born, Mist Hashira Muichiro Tokito is instead looking at the clouds above him, ignoring the situation. As the Hashira talk amongst themselves, Tanjiro scans his surrounds for Nezuko and wonders on the whereabouts of Zenitsu, Inosuke, and Murata. One Hashira ignores him and wonders what they will do with Giyu; sitting the trees, Serpent Hashira Obanai Iguro recalls Shinobu stating that Giyu broke the Corps' rules, and he wonders on what punishment he should take, even becoming annoyed to see him standing freely. As Mitsuri comments on Obanai's demeanor, Giyu, the Water Hashira, ignores Obanai's threat, much to Mitsuri's additional excitement. Shinobu believes they can settle on a punishment later, given that Tanjiro came without a fight; she is more interested in questioning him; Tanjiro becomes dismayed to see Giyu is now in trouble because of him. Still injured, he begins to cough as he explains himself and is provided water with an additional painkiller by Shinobu. He states that his sister was transformed into a demon but that she has not eaten human flesh, claiming that she won't or ever will. Obanai refutes him, believing that Tanjiro is biased to protect his sister, and Gyomei believes they must kill him quickly for thinking such things. Tanjiro begs them to listen and states he became a Demon Slayer to protect her, mentioning it has been two years and she hasn't bitten anyone. Tengen instead believes that his explanation is circling endlessly, disregarding that Nezuko hasn't attacked anyone as empty words, while Muichiro looks at a bird. However, Mitsuri is unsure they can proceed without their master's knowledge, urging her peers to wait for him. Tanjiro yells out that Nezuko has fight beside him, and that she too can fight for the Corps and protect people. Someone enters the scene and enjoys the tense situation; as a Kakushi urges the individual to put down Nezuko's box, he insults Tanjiro as the "idiotic Corps member" who travels with a demon; Wind Hashira Sanemi Shinazugawa demands to know what he is trying to do. As Mitsuri admires his rugged appearance, the Kakushi apologize to Shinobu for allowing his interruption. Unexpectedly, Shinobu, with a stern expression, orders Sanemi not to act rashly. However, Sanemi questions Tanjiro's own actions, asking how he could believe a demon could possibly fight for the Corps. Dismissing it as a completely impossibility, he draws his blade and stabs into Nezuko's box in front of everyone, impaling the demon in her shoulder. Tanjiro sprints at the Hashira and declares he will not let anyone hurt Nezuko, as Sanemi dismisses his challenge and prepares his blade. Giyu suddenly calls out that the master is arriving, causing Sanemi to lose focus and miss his swing, allowing Tanjiro to head butt squarely in the face. Mitsuri bursts out in laughter but quickly recomposes herself as the Hashira look at her with confusion. Obanai, despite noting Giyu's intervention, is impressed he has landed a blow on Sanemi. Tanjiro stands in front of Nezuko and advises Sanemi to quit if he can't tell between good and bad demons. Enraged, Sanemi threatens to kill him, but the tense standoff is diffused when the master's arrival is announced; the man greets the Demon Slayers, and Tanjiro looks at him with curiosity.

Chapter 46 is the forty-sixth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. The Master bids everyone a good morning, remarking about the pleasant weather and happy to see that in their bi-annual Hashira meetings, not one member has changed. Tanjiro remarks about the man's unusual appearance, wondering if he carries scars or is sick, when he is suddenly shoved to the ground by Sanemi. Stunned by his tremendous speed, he soon notices the rest of the Hashira bowing before the master. Sanemi warmly greets the Master and prays for his increased happiness and good health; as the Master thanks him for his kind words, Mitsuri quietly laments not being able to greet him. Before their meeting can start, Sanemi brings up the issue of Tanjiro, a Demon Slayer who travels with a demon, while Tanjiro himself notes that despite his earlier brutish demeanour, Sanemi is now speaking remarkably politely. The Master apologizes for surprising them with the situation but reveals he has accepted the siblings, wanting the Hashira to do so as well. The Hashira are stunned to hear this; Gyomei, despite knowing it is his request, cannot accept a demon, and Tengen "stylishly" opposes as well. Mitsuri wholeheartedly agrees with the Master, as does Muichiro since he will forget he agreed with him later on. Shinobu and Giyu remain silent, Obanai and Kyojuro vehemently disagree with this, and Sanemi demands that Tanjiro and Giyu are both punished. Having received their answers, the Master asks for his aide to read a letter; she explains it was written by the former Water Hashira Sakonji Urokodaki and reads a portion to the Hashira. In it, Sakonji wishes for Tanjiro and Nezuko to be forgiven, believing that through strong spiritual training, Nezuko has maintain her humanity, even refusing to eat humans when she starves. For two years, she has persisted, and though it seems inconceivable, it is the truth. Ultimately, should Nezuko ever attack a person, along with Tanjiro and Giyu, he will atone for her actions by committing seppuku. Tanjiro looks at Giyu and tears up at the realization of his devotion towards Nezuko. Sanemi dismisses Sakonji's vow and believes it doesn't prove anything, and Kyojuro adds that killing a human is an irreversible act. The Master acknowledges this but adds that they cannot prove Nezuko will attack, silencing the two. Since it is a fact that Nezuko has not killed anyone for two years, and three people have staked their lives on her, he urges them to offer an argument stronger than Sakonji's promise, causing them to remain silent. The Master also mentions that Tanjiro has crossed paths with Muzan Kibutsuji. Everyone is shocked to hear this as not one member of the Hashira has ever encountered Muzan. Tengen asks Tanjiro for his appearance and what his abilties were, while Muichiro asks if he fought him. Sanemi pulls Tanjiro's hair and bombards him with questions such as his actions and his lair; when he and Tengen enter a confrontation over getting answers first, the Master wordlessly raises a finger and they silence themselves immediately. He reveals Muzan has sent demons after Tanjiro, and while it could be as simple as wanting to kill Tanjiro, he has truly revealed himself for the first time and they cannot let the opportunity escape; he adds that perhaps Muzan sees something unexpected in Nezuko as well. When he asks the Hashira if they now see the importance of the siblings, Sanemi once again objects and believes that while sanctioning a human is one thing, sanctioning a demon is entirely different. He draws his sword and cuts open his forearm, shocking everyone; aiming to prove to the Master that demons cannot be trusted, he drips his blood over Nezuko's box.

Chapter 47 is the forty-seventh chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Obanai tell Sanemi to avoid the sunlight or Nezuko will not emerge. Sanemi apologizes for his discourtesy to the Master and leaps into the shade. As he draws his sword, Tanjiro calls out to Nezuko when Obanai suddenly drives his elbow into his back, preventing him from breathing and moving. Sanemi stabs Nezuko again and taunts her with his blood, when the door of her box flies open. She emerges from inside and stares at him, breathing heavily. Shinobu warns Obanai he is pushing too hard on Tanjiro and asks that he ease his hold, but Obanai believes he is trying to escape. She tells Tanjiro not to breathe with his lungs compressed or risk rupturing his blood vessel, but Tengen becomes excited and demands he rupture them, much to Mitsuri's concern. Gyomei pities Tanjiro for his situation. As Nezuko verges closer to attacking Sanemi, Tanjiro, with great difficulty, summons the strength to break free of restraints, while Obanai's arm is grabbed by Giyu to stop him. Knowing he can't intervene, he calls out to Nezuko, who turns to see her brother. Recalling Sakonji's words message to help humans and not hurt them, her mind is flooded with memories of her family, finally seeing Tanjiro and reiterating that she must never hurt humans. She turns away from Sanemi's bloody arm, surprising him; as the Master is blind, he asks his aide for what has happened, who tells him that Nezuko turn away from Sanemi. Despite being stabbed three times and being directly offered his blood, she did not attack him. The Master sees this as proof that Nezuko will indeed not attack humans, surprising Sanemi and Tanjiro. Obanai pulls his arm from Giyu and demands to know what he is doing, who ignores his question. The Master tells Tanjiro that despite the events of today, there will be those who will still view Nezuko unfavorably. With the proof he needs, he declares both siblings members of the Demon Slayer Corps; as he listens, Tanjiro notes a floating feeling in his head from the Master's voice. He urges Tanjiro to slay a member of the Twelve Kizuki and believes the Hashira will see his value then. Tanjiro vows that he and Nezuko will defeat Muzan Kibutsuji and end the pain caused by demons. The Master remarks that he is still not ready for such a task and advises him with the Kizuki demon instead, causing Tanjiro to recompose himself from his confident promise. As Tengen and Mitsuri hold back their laughter at Tanjiro's misplaced intentions, the Master tells Tanjiro that the Hashira are tremendously talented, and through laborious training, they have defied death, pushed themselves, and defeated members of the Twelve Kizuki. As such, people shows the Hashira their respect and welcome them, asking Tanjiro to mind how he speaks in front of them, which Tanjiro understand. Finally, he addresses Obanai and Sanemi and asks them not to torment those younger than themselves, which the two acknowledge. The Head of the Demon Slayer Corps is a man named Kagaya Ubuyashiki. His voice and rhythm are known to soothe those he speaks to; known as 1/f fluctuation, it is a skill that is found in those who are charismatic and have the strength and presence to move masses of people. Concluding his trial, Kagaya advises Tanjiro to leave as the Hashira meeting commences.

Chapter 48 is the forty-eighth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Shinobu offers to house Tanjiro at her mansion, and at her signal, two Kakushi appear to take him away. Eeven before Kagaya can begin, Tanjiro interrupts him and begs for more head butts on Sanemi, one for each time he stabbed Nezuko. As the Kakushi attempt to reel him in, he claims that head butts are not against their rules but is suddenly knocked down by three flying pebbles. Muichiro tells the Demon Slayer that interrupting Kagaya is rude, causing the Kakushi to abruptly apologize to the Master and the Mist Hashira; Mitsuri notes that despite his aloof behavior, Muichiro really was aware of the situation. As Tanjiro is taken away a second time, Kagaya asks him to give Tamayo his regards. While being taken away, Tanjiro ponders on Kagaya's final statement to him about Tamayo, while the Kakushi instead confront him for his behavior because the Hashira frighten them, demanding that he apologize now for antagonizing them. When they arrive at Shinobu's place, the Butterfly Mansion, they see no one at the front and head to the back; as the Kakushi carrying Tanjiro asks if he can walk by himself, Tanjiro remarks his entire body is in pain. They see a girl in the garden and realize she is a Tsuguko. She is Kanao Tsuyuri, and a Tsuguko is a highly skilled Demon Slayer trained by a Hashira. Tanjiro remembers her as the girl from Final Selection, but the Kakushi carrying him believes he forgot Kanao was the one to knock him unconscious. They asks for her permission to enter the mansion, under Shinobu's orders, but Kanao simply smiles at them. A loud voice then calls them from behind and asks who they are, startling them. When she realizes they are Kakushi and carry an injured person, she takes them in. Inside the mansion's hospital, Zenitsu bemoans being forced to take unpleasant tasting medication five times a day for three months, much to the concern of the girl tending to him. When she asks that he calm himself, Zenitsu instead yells for answers about his situation. The girl leading the Kakushi, Aoi Kanzaki, sees his complaining and demands he accept his circumstances, threatening to tie him to the bed. Tanjiro sees his friend and asks if he was hurt and if he came to the mountain. Zenitsu is relieved to see him and explains how a large spider injected him with a poison, and yet, Aoi is seemingly worse, while being eyed by the visibly annoyed Aoi. When he asks for Inosuke and Murata, Zenitsu does not know the latter but points to Inosuke in the next bed. Tanjiro gets off the Kakushi and crawls to his bed, relieved to see him and tearfully apologizing for not helping him. Inosuke quietly forgives him, surprising Tanjiro with the hoarseness in his voice. Zenitsu explains his throat was crushed and his neck was severely injured, yet he continued to yell afterwards, leaving his throat in terrible condition. He adds that since his injuries, Inosuke has been mellow and calm, much to his relief, though his delight at Inosuke's misfortune leads to Tanjiro questioning his friend's sanity. Tanjiro's listed injuries are multiple cuts, abrasions on his face and limbs, sprains throughout his body, pulled muscles, and contusions in his jaw. Zenitsu was poisoned, leaving numbness in his right arm, right leg, and trembling in his left arm. Inosuke suffered trauma to his larynx and vocal cords, while Nezuko only sustains a lack of sleep. The four eventually recover; Nezuko sleeping in her box, Tanjiro persisted despite great pain, Zenitsu continued to complain about taking his medication, and Inosuke, though depressed over his weakness, was continually encouraged by his friends. A while later, a visitor appears to greet Tanjiro; Murata, who only sufferd a jammed finger. He tells them about how he was summoned to the Hashira meeting to report about the incident on Mount Natagumo, and how during said meeting, they were all angered by the Demon Slayers' lackluster skill and believed their quality had been declining; Murata was especially interrogated on his peers' trainers and whether they followed orders As he continues to bemoan his unpleasant encounter with the Hashira, they are joined by the Insect Hashira herself, causing Murata to flee at the sight of her. Shinobu asks the three on how well they are doing; when they answer they are much better, which the exception of Inosuke, Shinobu states it is now time for them to begin Rehabilitation Training.

Chapter 49 is the forty-ninth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. As Zenitsu continues to heal, he has been dutifully following his routine of medication and sunlight exposure, and while he knows he would recover, he hears that some of the recovered Demon Slayers had suffered after effects. He recalls the sounds Shinobu make and that it is unlike anything he has heard, almost scary; despite this, when she saved the transformed Demon Slayers, she appeared almost like a goddess, causing them to tear up. Zenitsu adds that Shinobu is very attractive. However, each time she took Tanjiro and Inosuke to Rehabilitation Training, they would return broken and exhausted, refusing to talk as they went back to bed, which unnerved Zenitsu. Soon, he recovers and joins his friends in rehabilitation. In the Butterfly Mansion's training hall, Aoi introduces Zenitsu to the three steps of his rehabilitation. He will first be stretched by the mansion's three helpers to loosen his muscles. Then comes reflex training where, on a table with cups of medicinal tea, the objective is to splash the opponent with a cup without them doing so in return. Finally is full-body training, which is essentially a game of tag between her and later Kanao. As Tanjiro and Inosuke bemoan having to train again, Zenitsu only appears shocked. He asks Aoi for a moment and tells Tanjiro and Inosuke to follow him; they are caught off-guard when Zenitsu drags them outside. In the yard, he demands the two ""idiot jerks" to listen to him; Inosuke does not take kindly to the insult but is suddenly punched into the wall by Zenitsu. Tanjiro orders him to apologize but Zenitsu instead demands they apologize to him, asking why they act forlorn when they "were actually in heaven"". He is angered by their haggard expressions after spending an entire day with girls; Tanjiro reprimands him but Zenitsu continues by listing the things they get to do, namely touching them during each step of training, before mentioning all the things the girls have that attract him. Inosuke retorts that losing to them is embarrassing but Zenitsu does not pity his failures and believes he has not spent time with girls, to which Inosuke clarifies he has "stepped" on plenty of them, angering him. Tanjiro notes that for better or worse, the two are now motivated to train, but believes it is wrong to do so with impure motives. He and Inosuke watch Zenitsu laughing blissfully during the rigorous stretching procedure. In reflex training, Zenitsu bests Aoi each time but refuses to splash her to be chivalrous, annoying Aoi. In full-body training, he grabs her and is punched in the face, to which Zenitsu remarks that he "won the game, but lost the fight". Inosuke, not one to like losing, mercilessly defeats Aoi by splashing her in the face and grabbing her by the legs, causing Tanjiro to fall behind. However, despite initial success, all three were unable to beat Kanao in both reflexes and full-body training; Tanjiro notes that despite finishing the same Final Selection as them, she remains far ahead. For five days, Kanao remains unbeaten; it is especially hard on Inosuke with his dislike of losing, and Zenitsu eventually accepted that he was well enough. Both began to skip training; Aoi, despite being annoyed by them not taking training seriously, did not mind and even asked Tanjiro to skip if he wanted too. Though he was motivated to keep trying, ten more fruitless days pass. He tries to understand how she is so different; she is so fast, even if he did recover, Tanjiro remains sure he still wouldn't beat her. Her scent is also different and closer to that of the Hashira, and he notes that she has unique eyes. His train of thought is interrupted by the girls of the mansion, who give him a towel to dry himself. They ask if he maintains Total Concentration Breathing across the entire day, but he becomes confused. The girls ask again if he uses it morning, noon, and night, even when he sleeps. Tanjiro responds that he doesn't and does not see it as possible; when they tell him it will make the difference, he notes that he even struggles to use it. They inform him that some can do it, such as the Hashira and Kanao, to which Tanjiro thanks them for the idea and promises to try it the next day.

Chapter 5 is the fifth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. The boy with a fox mask challenges Tanjiro to a fight to which he declines, as the stranger is only wielding a wooden sword while Tanjiro has with him a real sword. The boy laughs at Tanjiro believing he had a chance and declares that as someone who had succeeded in splitting the boulder, he wouldn't be hurt by someone weaker. Shocked by learning the boulder can be split, Tanjiro is beaten down by the stranger's superior technique, who continues to admonish him for only remembering Total Concentration Breathing as a fact without understanding it, much less use it. Tanjiro claims he has tried to do so but the boy tells him that trying and doing it is not the same. Ordering him to attack with all his strength, Tanjiro swings at the stranger, who dodges and strikes him in the chin, knocking him unconscious. With his opponent defeated, the masked boy turns his attention to a girl entering the forest, only telling her, ""I'll leave the rest to you". When Tanjiro awakens, he sees the girl and asks her if she had witnessed the fight. Tanjiro tells her he wants to be as skilled as the boy someday. The girl replies that he will indeed be able to master those techniques one day, and she will be there to witness his strength. Tanjiro requests for her name, thinking to himself that the girl is cute. She introduces herself as Makomo and the boy with the fox mask as Sabito. Over time, Makomo acts as Tanjiro's teacher to aid him in correcting his sword postures, bad habits, and breathing techniques. When Tanjiro asks why she was willing to teach him, she only replies, "We really like Urokodaki"", to Tanjiro's confusion. Makomo also informs Tanjiro that Sabito and her are not siblings, rather orphans taken in by Sakonji along with many children that are currently watching him. Makomo teaches him the importance of Total Concentration Breathing. It accelerates blood flow and increases the body's temperature, enabling them to match a demon's strength. By expanding the lungs, one can force much air into the body and become stronger. Tanjiro is perplexed by this understanding; when asking Makomo how it is possible, she only says, ""You must train so hard that you could die. Basically, I don't think there's anything else you can do". Over time, even after excessively training, to the point where his arms feels as if they may fall off and his heart and lungs burn in his chest, Tanjiro is still unable to defeat Sabito. Six months pass since Tanjiro has met Sakonji's students, culminating in a final spar with Sabito now armed with a real blade. A determined and changed Tanjiro tells Sabito that he will win. In a simple head-on contest, the stronger and faster blade wins: Tanjiro and Sabito clash but it is Tanjiro who strikes first, cutting through Sabito's fox mask. It falls off, revealing Sabito smiling at him. A smiling Makomo tells him: "Win Tanjiro...against them too"". Sabito and Makomo disappear in a haze, and Tanjiro realizes that his sword, believing had cut through Sabito's mask, has actually sliced the boulder in half.

Chapter 50 is the fiftieth chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. In his first attempt at maintaining Total Concetration, Tanjiro quickly collapses as the physical toll proves too much; he is startled by a loud sound in his ears and believes his heart will pop from them. Seeing he has not recovered, he recalls the basics from Sakonji; the lungs are essential in breathing and he'll have to improve them to progress. The helpers of the mansion see him hard at work and decide to bring him rice balls and gourds. While eating, Tanjiro observes the gourd they have brought, which he must blow into. One of them explains that Shinobu instructed Kanao to do the same as training. When he believes them to be an instrument, she instead tells him the objective is to make them burst, who surprises Tanjiro. He taps the gourd and notes the dried texture, to which she adds that as it is harder than normal gourds. Tanjiro is aghast to learn a petite girl like Kanao is capable of such a task, and the girls reveal the gourds Kanao is now able to break, which are as large as them. Both stunned and motivated, Tanjiro promises to try the new training method. Fifteen days later, while sitting atop the roof of the Butterfly Mansion, Tanjiro remarks he feels his strength returning; he can run for longer and his lungs are much stronger. During the day, he trains his lungs with fast movements, and at night, he trains by breathing slowly to circulate his oxygen to every part of his body. Sakonji had taught him that meditation improves concentration, but he momentarily loses focus when he imagines Haganezuka, who would understandably be furious to learn his Nichirin sword is broken. Additionally, he may have fought one of the Twelve Kizuki but he failed to take their blood, noting that Tamayo's cat is looking at him disapprovingly. As he attempts to regain concentration, he is met by Shinobu, who is impressed by his dedication to train, whereas Zenitsu and Inosuke are doing something else. Initially blushing at the sight of her, he is put as ease when Shinobu sits beside him and asks if he is lonely training, to which Tanjiro reassures her that once he learns to maintain Total Concentration, he can teach it to Zenitsu and Inosuke. She tells him he has a pure heart; when Tanjiro asks why she brought them to her mansion, she replies it is because they learned of Nezuko's true nature and his injuries. Additionally, she hoped to entrust her dream in him; to have demons and humans coexist peacefully. Tanjiro then asks if she is angry, which surprises her; he notes that despite her smile, she always has the scent of anger. Shinobu confirms this, explaining that it began with the death of her elder sister and that her anger has only grown from seeing the continual harm demons cause humans. It is an anger she cannot silence and adds that the Hashira all feel the same way; even after seeing Nezuko show her restraint, the Hashira will not attack her only because of Kagaya's wishes. Shinobu mentions that her sister was kind like him and felt sympathy for demons, even pitying them as she died, while she herself could not feel sympathy to those who kill humans. Despite this, she believes she must carry out her sister's wish, and if there is a way to avoid killing pitiful demons, she must find it without losing the sunny disposition her sister enjoyed in her. Shinobu remarks she is tired of trying, seeing that demons are irredeemable, always lying to save themselves and killing without reason. As she stands up, the Insect Hashira tells the Demon Slayer to keep fighting and defending Nezuko, and when she believes he is succeeding at her sister's dream, she will be put at ease, before vanishing from view. Seeing her trust in him, Tanjiro vows to do his best. He instructs the girls of the mansion - Naho, Kiyo, and Sumi - to help him train by beating him with carpet beaters when he fails to maintain Total Concentration when he sleeps, to which they oblige to. That night, while sleeping and breathing, Tanjiro begins to snore, causing the three to beat him awake. Ten days later, while training with the largest gourd, Tanjiro takes a deep breath and blows into it. With the girls' encouragement, he successfully breaks it open, much to their excitement. In full-body training, Tanjiro chases Kanao and keeps up with her with his improved speed; while still not fully mastering Total Concentration throughout the entire day, it is a sign he is getting close and his body has changed, and he grows excited to swing a Nichirin sword with his new strength. Eventually, he successfully grabs her hand and wins. Partaking in reflexes training, Tanjiro and Kanao trade blows at incredible speeds, seemingly neck and neck. Unwilling to lose focus, he perseveres and is able to grab a cup before she can block it, but realizes it would be rude to splash her with its unpleasant smelling contents. Instead, he taps her head, which Kiyo and Naho notes is still a successful victory. As the girls and Tanjiro celebrate his success, Inosuke and Zenitsu stare in disbelief at his improvement.

Chapter 51 is the fifty-first chapter of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba. Summary. Having just witnessed Tanjiro beat Kanao during his rehabilitation test, Zenitsu and Inosuke stagger as they try to learn Total Concentration Breathing from Tanjiro. However, despite numerous attempts, the two boys were unable to grasp the concept of the technique and struggle to master it. During one of Tanjiro's lessons, Shinobu interrupts to provide guidance, and words of encouragement to both Inosuke and Zenitsu. The methods she uses to encourage them include, doubting Inosukes ability in order for him to get fired up, as well as tell Zenitsu she's personally "cheering" for him specifically so he gets excited. Nine days pass after her visit, and both Zenitsu and Inosuke have successfully mastered the breathing technique. On this day, Tanjiro calls Inosuke to inform him that their Nichirin Swords have been repaired and are being delivered. The two boys rush outside of the estate to see the swordsmiths approaching. When he sees Hotaru Haganezuka approaching, Tanjiro cheerfully yells out to greet him, but once Hotaru begins to run at a faster pace he pauses. He sees that Hotaru is holding a knife in his hand, and narrowly dodges from being impaled by the angry swordsmith. Hotaru confronts Tanjiro in disbelief at the fact that he broke his sword, but when Tanjiro tries to explain himself, the swordsmith says he's going to kill him and chases him for an hour. Having controlled his emotions a bit, Hotaru and the others sit to present the blades. The other individual who was seen with Hotaru introduces himself as Kozo Kanamori, and explains that he has forged Inosuke's blades. He gives Inosuke the swords and admires the color that it transitions to, he also asks Inosuke how the blades feel. Instead of answering him, Inosuke walks outside into the garden, and begins to pick up and sort through multiple rocks. He finally picks one up and unexpectedly slams it down onto his new blade to form the same rigged shape as his old one leaving Tanjiro and the swordsmiths horrified. He cheekily remarks that the chipped is better which enrages Kozo, he lunges out at Inosuke while screaming that he's going to kill him as Tanjiro holds him back. Elsewhere, Zenitsu is seen leaning up against Nezuko's box as he explains to her the events that had occured that day, while telling her that he'll take her out at night to see flowers that bloom in the garden. In an undisclosed location, a female demon can be heard strumming the strings of an instrument as the Lower Rank 6, Kamanue, arrives. He becomes amazed while watching the warp around him when the female demon strums her . Within moments, he finds himself clustered alongside the other members of the Lower Ranks, and turns to see a woman glaring down at him. The woman commands that they all lower their heads and bow to her, and at that moment they realize that its Muzan Kibutsuji disguised as a woman. Lower Rank 4, Mukago, begins to apologize for failing to recognize him, but she's cut off by Muzan who questions her audacity to speak, leaving Mukago trembling with fear. Muzan strictly reminds them to only answer his questions, and informs them that Lower Rank 5, Rui, was killed. He proceeds to ask why the Lower Ranks are so weak and die easily in comparison to the Upper Ranks who haven't been changed for over a century. Kamanue thinks to himself on how Muzan expects him to respond, but to his horror, Muzan responds by repeating his thoughts word for word.
