Kagaya Ubuyashiki/Relationships Relationships. Gyomei Himejima. When he was fourteen, Kagaya had heard of a monk who was imprisoned and sentenced to death for the murder of several children under his care. Realizing it was untrue and that a demon was the true culprit, he saved the man from his death sentence. That man, Gyomei Himejima, would later become the Stone Hashira, serving under his command and acting as his confidante. Kagaya knew him for the longest among the Hashira and was arguably the closest with Gyomei outside of his own family; as such, he entrusted only Gyomei with his plan to sacrifice himself in order to stall Muzan Kibutsuji long enough for them to, knowing the remaining Hashira would not agree to his plan. Despite his hesitation, Gyomei honored Kagaya's wishes and kept the plan secret until its activation. Sanemi Shinazugawa. During Sanemi Shinazugawa's first meeting as a member of the Hashira, he harshly criticized Kagaya for his calm demeanour in sending his fellow Demon Slayers to their deaths, and mistakenly believed he had placed himself above them, much to the ire of Gyomei and Tengen Uzui present. Kagaya apologized and explained that he was unable to fight because of his condition, which surprised the angry young man into silence, and he further explained that despite the respect people show him, he does not believe himself to be above them. Sensing his grief, Kagaya gave Sanemi his friend Masachika Kumeno's will, prompting the Wind Hashira to tear up at the remembering of his friend. Sanemi would later become an extremely loyal follower of Kagaya. Sanemi was deeply affected by his leader's death, demanding Muzan Kibutsuji for answers upon seeing the demon and being unable to see Kagaya in the aftermath of his suicidal plan. When he fell into the Infinity Castle and was attacked by numerous demons, Sanemi chose to sit down and lament his inability to save Kagaya instead of caring about his own wellbeing, before rapidly slaughtering the demons all around him in a fit of rage. Kanae Kocho. Kanae Kocho was one of the first Hashira to be under Kagaya's command. She was present during Sanemi's first meeting and saw how the Wind Hashira became angry seemingly at Kagaya's lack of care in sending his troops to their deaths. Out of concern, Kanae attempted to speak up on his behalf, but Kagaya assuaged the situation and insisted that he is willing to listen to his words, putting Kanae at ease. Instead of being angry, Kanae told Sanemi that Kagaya was not the person he believed him to be and told him that their leader had memorized the names of every fallen Demon Slayer under his command as a show of gratitude to their cause. Shinobu Kocho. Like her older sister before taking her position as Hashira, Shinobu Kocho was extremely loyal to Kagaya. He entrusted her with overseeing the mission to Mount Natagumo upon hearing a report of mass casualties in the forests. During a meeting with the Hashira, Sanemi once spoke of his concern for Kagaya's safety and believed that the Hashira should be guarding him. Gyomei explained that Kagaya had always believed them to be of greater importance and forgone his own wellbeing, which was corroborated by Shinobu's mention that the Ubuyashiki family had never once been watched by bodyguards of any sort. It was under Kagaya's orders that Shinobu worked with the demon Tamayo to jointly create a drug that would be used to weaken Muzan Kibutsuji. Mitsuri Kanroji. Kagaya met a young Demon Slayer named Mitsuri Kanroji, who was troubled by her sense of identity over her abnormal physical strength and unique physical features. In her first meeting with him, he told her that she was a gift from the gods, and that anyone who spoke ill of her was simply jealous of her strength. Touched by the man's acceptance of who she was, the girl bowed down and cried in relief that someone could accept her for who she is. Mitsuri would go on to become the Love Hashira. Mitsuri was extremely loyal to his cause; during the trial of Tanjiro Kamado by the Hashira, only she spoke out about their hasty treatment of the situation, believing it was important that Kagaya was present during the trial to oversee and give his word. When Kagaya revealed that he had sanctioned Tanjiro and his sister, Mitsuri was one of the first to instantly agree with him. In her battle against Upper Four Hantengu's most powerful manifestation Zohakuten, Mitsuri recalls Kagaya's acceptance of her within the Demon Slayer Corps, allowing her to push past mental blocks that held her back and attacking the Upper Rank demon with renewed vigour. Likewise, she was horrified by the explosion rocking the mountainside that killed Kagaya in his attempt to stall Muzan Kibutsuji for her to attack. Kyojuro Rengoku. Kyojuro was first summoned to a Hashira meeting as a Kinoe-ranked Demon Slayer, after his father refused to attend. An altercation occurred between him and Sanemi, who was offended that someone that wasn't a Hashira was in their presence, but before the situation could escalate, Kagaya arrived and chided the Wind Hashira, causing the angry Sanemi to quickly bow down and apologize, surprising Kyojuro that the man could order and command such a fierce and temperamental individual. Later on, after killing the Lower Rank Two, Hairo, Kyojuro was promoted as the new Flame Hashira under Kagaya's command. As with the rest of the Hashira, Kyojuro was faultlessly loyal to the Oyakata; even during Tanjiro Kamado's trial for harbouring a demon, when Kyojuro had question Kagaya's decision to sanction the siblings, he acknowledged Kagaya's argument of his importance and accepted them. After his mission assigned on the Mugen Train unexpectedly ended with his death at the hands of Upper Rank Three, Kagaya acknowledged Kyojuro's heroics actions, calling him a "remarkable child" for his act of prevent not a single passenger of the 200 onboard from dying. He also was not saddened by the Hashira's demise, as he stated that he would join him shortly afterwards. Tengen Uzui. Kagaya learned that among his ranks was a former shinobi who decided to become a Demon Slayer to escape his past. During a personal meeting with the young man, Tengen Uzui and his kunoichi wives, he told the shinobi that he pities him for the difficult choice he had to make to leave everything he only knew behind to make a new future, praising him for his new path. Tengen was touched by Kagaya's sympathy and became a loyal subordinate under his command. It was during his battle against the dual holder of Upper Rank Six that Tengen reminisced on his meeting with Kagaya and recalled his words of encouragement, giving him the drive to fight back against Daki and Gyutaro together. Tanjiro Kamado. Upon learning that a Demon Slayer amongst his command had harbored a demon, Kagaya immediately chose to sanction the boy's actions. The Demon Slayer, Tanjiro Kamado, and his demon sister Nezuko, was about to be executed by the Hashira until Kagaya gave them his word about his status. Tanjiro himself was perplexed by the Oyakata's appearance, wondering if he truly was the Demon Slayer Corps' leader, though whenever he spoke, Tanjiro noted the floating, calming feeling in his voice. After seeing evidence that Nezuko can be trusted with humans, Kagaya officially recognized the siblings as Demon Slayers. A gracious Tanjiro then vowed to kill Muzan Kibutsuji on his behalf, though Kagaya calmly noted that he was still ill-equipped. Like the Hashira, Tanjiro grew to be very loyal to Kagaya and cared for his wellbeing, as during Muzan's attack on the Oyakata, he detected the smell of Kagaya's burning blood in the explosion and immediately became horrified by the situation. His anger at Kagaya's demise, coupled with his own rage at Muzan, drove Tanjiro to attack the immensely powerful demon head-on with the Hashira. Muzan Kibutsuji. Over a millennia ago, a member of the Ubuyashiki family was transformed in an experimental treatment to cure his terminal illness. The man, Muzan Kibutsuji, would become the first demon to ever exist. Subsequently, males of the Ubuyashiki family would be cursed with a terrible condition that would deteriorate their bodies and lead to an untimely death at a young age. Since then, the Ubuyashikis had submitted themselves with the single goal of leading the Demon Slayer Corps in the hopes of finally killing Muzan. Kagaya met Muzan for the first time when the demon secretly entered his household. Muzan insulted the man for his sickly appearance, comparing him to a corpse and laughing at the belief that all the murders he has committed have gone unpunished by the gods. Kagaya, who has since lost his vision, calmly spoke to the Demon King and asked for his desires, a question that surprised Muzan. Upon telling Kagaya that his dream is to be immortal and it can be achieved by devouring Nezuko Kamado, Kagaya uncharacteristically taunted the demon by claiming that his dream would never succeed, and that only human feelings can exist forever. Insulted, Muzan dissuaded his taunts, but Kagaya then spoke of Muzan's own continual prodding of the Demon Slayer Corps with numerous deaths, and the rage they all feel will kill him without fail. When Muzan threatened to kill him, Kagaya calmly stated that his death was meaningless in the grand scheme of the Demon Slayer Corps. Kagaya then secretly triggered an explosion to destroy his entire house, killing himself, his wife, and two of his daughters, in the hopes of stunning Muzan for an attack by the Hashira. As he healed from the fireball, Muzan was enraged by his inability to see the obvious rage Kagaya had felt towards him on the inside, begrudgingly acknowledging his skill to hide his bloodlust with a smile until it was too late. Amane Ubuyashiki. Kagaya first met Amane when he was thirteen, having already taken his late father's position as Oyakata of the Demon Slayer Corps. Amane was selected to be his caretaker when his condition would deteriorate, but Kagaya only agreed to marry her under the condition that she cared for him under her own free will. Amane was loyal to Kagaya without a fault, caring for his every need as his illness worsened, and eventually taking over his position to speak at meetings with the Hashira when he was no longer able to do so. Later, when Kagaya decided to sacrifice himself to stall Muzan, Amane chose to stay with him until the very end and die by his side. Kiriya Ubuyashiki. Kiriya was Kagaya's only son, thus making him his successor in the event of his death. Like his father, Kiriya undertook important roles in the Demon Slayer Corps, such as overseeing Final Selection and attending to his medical needs. In the aftermath of Kagaya's death, Kiriya immediately became the new Oyakata and undertook the immense task of coordinating the limited manpower of the Demon Slayers to combat specific Upper Ranks demons. Despite several setbacks and decisions that have led to several deaths, Kiriya had realized that his father and ancestors have all faced the same stress and pressure in the same position, valiantly continuing his mission. When Nezuko Kamado, who had been cared for as her human-conversion drug was administered, suddenly left the Corps headquarters on her own volition, Kiriya panicked and believed that Muzan has taken control of her. Before Kiriya could give an order, Kagaya's spirit touched his son on the shoulder and told him to let Nezuko do as she wants. His sisters were confused by his lack of action but Kiriya tearfully tells them that their father had spoken to him.

Kagaya Ubuyashiki/Synopsis History. Kagaya was born into the Ubuyashiki clan. As a male born into the family, he was cursed to suffer an illness that slowly afflicted his entire body, due to Muzan Kibutsuji's blood relation with the clan. When he was only 4 years old, his father and the previous family head, was a sensitive man who committed suicide at the age of 19 because he could not bear the thought of his troops getting hurt or dying. The children he had were all boys, and he lost all of them except Kagaya who assumed the role of Oyakata-sama after his father's death. When he was 13 years old, he first met his wife Amane. She was specifically selected by a priest to become Kagaya's wife in order to care for his medical needs, but he only agreed to the marriage on the condition that she cared for him on her own free will. When Kagaya was 14, he learned of a blind monk who was imprisoned for the deaths of eight children under his care. Having realized that the monk was innocent and that the deaths were the result of a demon's attack, he intervened and prevented his execution. This man, Gyomei Himejima, would later become a Demon Slayer and go on to become one of Kagaya's most trusted confidants and the Stone Hashira. Sometime later, Kagaya met with a shinobi turned Demon Slayer named Tengen Uzui. Tengen had left his past behind, unwilling to become a ruthless killer like his father and brother. Kagaya praised Tengen for his decision, citing the great difficulty the young man must have endured to leave everything behind and accept a new direction in life. Touched by his words, Tengen expressed gratitude and became intensely loyal to Kagaya, later becoming the Sound Hashira. During his first meeting as a member of the Hashira, Sanemi Shinazugawa harshly insulted Kagaya for sending Demon Slayers under his command to die with an unconcerned smile on his face, angering Gyomei and Tengen, and worrying the Flower Hashira Kanae Kocho. Despite their concerns, Kagaya allowed the Wind Hashira to continue speaking his mind. When Sanemi accused him of being a weak leader to the Demon Slayers, Kagaya apologized to him, shocking the angered young man. He explains that due to his condition, he cannot even swing a blade ten times without his blood pressure becoming dangerous, and if he wanted to become strong, he would but cannot. He apologizes to Sanemi for making him do what is difficult, the once furious Hashira calmed by his voice and gentle expression. Kagaya would go on to tell Sanemi that if he believed the Demon Slayers were pawns to him, that he too was one as well since his replacement is already set. Additionally, he explains that he is not above anyone; the Demon Slayers simple treat him with respect but he does not have to. He apologizes for summoning him soon after the death of his partner Masachika Kumeno. In disbelief in hearing his name, Sanemi would be told by Kanae that Kagaya remembers the names of every single Demon Slayer under his command. The Corps leader gives him Masachika's will to read, causing him to tear up. Since seeing his genuine dedication to the Demon Slayer Corps, Sanemi has also become extremely loyal to Kagaya. Kagaya encountered a young Demon Slayer who was ostracized for her abnormal strength and unusual traits. Taking pity on her, the Demon Slayer leader told her that her strength was a beloved gift from the gods and anyone who spoke ill of her was merely envious. The girl, Mitsuri Kanroji, was deeply touched by Kagaya's words, crying and bowing before him in relief and thankfulness. She would later go on to become the Love Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps. During Muichiro Tokito's career as a Demon Slayer, he was visited by Kagaya and Amane during his recovery. Seeing the confused and heavily wounded boy, Kagaya extended words of advice to him, telling Muichiro that one's survival is foremost and that once he survives, lost memories will come back. At a later time, he then asked him not to be so rigid with his perception of the world, telling the boy if he can find his true self, he can become unstoppable.Muichiro would later become Kagaya's Mist Hashira. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. Following Final Selection, Kagaya is informed that there were a total of five survivors. Satisfied that the number of his "children" has increased, he wonders what kind of Demon Slayers they would eventually become. Mount Natagumo Arc. During the mission to Mount Natagumo, a Kasugai crow flies from the mountain to the Demon Slayer Corps headquarters to inform Kagaya of the massacre that has occured. Believing the Twelve Kizuki are involved and the deployment of the Hashira to be necessary to rescue the survivors, he sends the Water Hashira Giyu Tomioka and Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho to intervene. Rehabilitation Training Arc. During Tanjiro Kamado's trial by the Hashira for harbouring his demon sister Nezuko, Kagaya appears for their semi-annual meeting and comments on the lovely weather. The Hashira bow before him and Sanemi extends greetings to Kagaya. The Wind Hashira then questions him on the circumstances regarding Tanjiro but to the Hashira's surprise, Kagaya has accepted Tanjiro's situation and wishes for them to accept it as well. Gyomei, Tengen, Sanemi, Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku, and Serpent Hashira Obanai Iguro disagree due to the nature of demons but Muichiro and Love Hashira Mitsuri Kanroji accept it, while Shinobu and Giyu stay silent. With his answers, Kagaya informs them about a letter from Sakonji Urokodaki, the former Water Hashira, writing that he believes Nezuko to be fully able to resist attacking humans and that he, Giyu, and Tanjiro would commit seppuku should it ever happen. Kyojuro and Sanemi still disagree and claim that it cannot be proven Nezuko won't attack but Kagaya points out that it is also unsure if she would, and citing the fact that 3 people are putting their lives on the line, he asks them to provide a stronger argument. Additionally, he adds that Tanjiro has met Muzan Kibutsuji in the past and has had demons sent to kill him. Though the Hashira realize how important he is, Sanemi attempts to prove Nezuko's demonic nature by stabbing her and taunting the demon with his own blood. He apologizes to Kagaya for his rude intrusion and enters the headquarters to open her box. When Nezuko proves herself capable of resisting his blood, Kagaya, being blind, questions what has happened, to which he is informed that Nezuko turned away from Sanemi. Believing this to be indisputable proof, Kagaya is pleased and addresses Tanjiro, who notes the floating feeling he experiences hearing his voice. Kagaya informs him that there will be those who would not accept her sister and tells him to prove his worth by killing a Twelve Kizuki. Tanjiro, feeling elated by his acceptance, vows to kill Muzan, though the Master humorously implores him to start small with a Kizuki demon. He then addresses Sanemi and Obanai, gently asking them not to torment those younger than themselves, which they acknowledge. With Tanjiro's trial now finishes, Shinobu takes custody of him and Nezuko to live in her estate. Kakushi bow before Kagaya and the Hashira and quickly take the siblings away. However, before Kagaya can continue speaking, he is interrupted when Tanjiro runs back and tries to headbutt Sanemi for stabbing Nezuko, asking for Kagaya's permission. He is quickly knocked down by Muichiro flinging pebbles and taken away again, but before the boy leaves his presence, Kagaya asks for Tanjiro to ""give Miss Tamayo my regards"", surprising him. Later that night, Kagaya and the Hashira continued their meeting. All were angered by the growing threat of demons on humanity and noted the declining skill in the newer Demon Slayers. Gyomei addressed the issue that since only people who know about demons become Demon Slayers, they cannot bolster their numbers easily. When Kyojuro noted that Tanjiro has encountered a Twelve Kizuki early into his career, Kagaya mentions that Lower Five's drastic actions on the mountain would mean that Muzan was no where near, due to always creating an distraction. While disappointed in demons becoming more dangerous than ever before, Kagaya expressed his faith in the Hashira, deeming them the strongest since feudal times and looking forward to his "childrens'" success. Later that night, while alone in his quarters, Kagaya vowed that they will kill Muzan without fail. Mugen Train Arc. When he learns that not one of the 200 passengers aboard the Mugen Train was killed in the demon's attack, Kagaya praises the fallen Kyojuro for his sacrifice. He is not saddened by the Hashira's death, as he remarks that he himself does not have long to live for and will be joining him and the other deceased soon. Entertainment District Arc. Following Tengen's mission in Yoshiwara that resulted in the deaths of the Upper Rank demons Daki and Gyutaro, Kagaya, whose health has visibly deteriorated and worsened, is informed of the news by a Kasugai Crow in his estate. He is ecstatic to learn the accomplishment was performed by Tengen, Tanjiro, Nezuko, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira. Amane assists Kagaya; despite his severe coughing now causing him to bleed, he states that an Upper Rank's death has not occurred in over a hundred years and grabs his wife's hand in joyous realization, telling her that the death is an omen for the coming future changing in their favour. He remarks that the consequences of such a death will spread far and in time, they can kill Muzan once and for all. His coughing suddenly begins to worsen and Amane orders their children to fetch his medicine, as they worriedly call out to their dying father. Swordsmith Village Arc. After saving a young swordsmith from a fish-like demon, Muichiro initially moves on ahead to protect the Swordsmith Village, having realizes that the demon was actually a Blood Demon Art. The smith, Kotetsu, instead begs him to save two swordsmiths who are alone and fending for themselves from the demons. Though at first he ignores him to go his way, Muichiro suddenly remembers a moment when Kagaya and Amane had visited him following an attack by a demon that left him severely wounded. Kagaya, noticing the boy's confusion, calmly tells him that his survival is paramount. Should he survive, his lost memories will come back too, telling him to not miss the opportunity, as even trivial events can trigger them to come back. Taking his leader's advice, Muichiro forgoes his initial plans and grabs Kotetsu to rescue Kozo and Hotaru. Though he is initially hesitant to abandon his post, Muichiro trusts in Kagaya's advice and remarks he can succeed as the Mist Hashira recognized by him. During his confrontation with Muichiro, Gyokko, after trapping the Mist Hashira in his Water Prison Pot, told him that one of their objectives is to kill Kagaya, along with destroying the Swordsmith Village, in the hopes of crippling the Corps of leadership and weapons. At a later time, after killing Gyokko, Muichiro recalls a past meeting he had with Kagaya, who gentle asked him to ease his rigid perception of his surroundings. He tells the Mist Hashira that once he finds his true self, he can become unstoppable. True to Kagaya's advice, Muichiro realizes that by focusing his boiling rage on a target without losing himself, he was able to defeat Upper Rank Five. While stunned from Zohakuten's Compressed Sound Waves, Mitsuri reminisces on her past and how she gradually realized that acceptance from others of her unique traits would be nearly impossible. Upon joining the Corps however, Kagaya immediately told her that she was special, and that anyone who speaks ill of her was simply afraid of her strength. Hearing whole-hearted accepted of her true self brings the once uncertain and unconfident young woman to tears, bowing and thanking Kagaya for his words. Hashira Training Arc. After some time in the present day at the Ubuyashiki Mansion as the Hashira Training began, the curse of his illness slowly continued to deteriorate across his entire body due to the fact that he would soon die in result of his illness continuing to develop any further. His health visibly worsened much more clearly everyday; relying on his wife, Amane to tend towards his weakened condition by lending aid with covering his face and arms in bandages in hopes of attempting to slow down the effects of Kagaya's curse. She had also gone to the Hashira Meeting in Kagaya's place to inform the remaining Hashira of a demon who has conquered the sun. She also took in Kagaya's order of writing a letter to Tanjiro, who was still recovering in the Butterfly Mansion from the events that happened at the Swordsmith Village. Kagaya's letter to Tanjiro sent by his own Kasugai Crow revealed that Kagaya was stuck into a vulnerable state and became ashamed to admit towards any of the other Hashira of his condition debilitating him to the point where he could no longer move in order to confront Giyu himself, and urgently requested of Tanjiro to encourage him of participating in the Hashira Training by visiting his mansion in order to convince him to join training with the other Hashira, preparing to take appropriate measures before the final battle against Muzan Kibutsuji.

Kaigaku is a supporting antagonist in the Infinity Castle Arc of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". He is a demon affiliated with the Twelve Kizuki, holding the position of, replacing Daki and Gyutaro after their deaths. Kaigaku was a former Demon Slayer and Zenitsu Agatsuma's senior disciple under the former, Jigoro Kuwajima. However, sometime during Hashira Training, Kaigaku went on a mission and encountered Upper Rank One, Kokushibo, quickly surrendering to him to save his own skin and later becoming a member of the Twelve Kizuki. Appearance. As a human, Kaigaku is a muscular young man of average height who has short, spiky black hair, with two thick strands framing his face, and a pair of dull, cold turquoise eyes framed by thick, arched eyebrows. He has an unfriendly face, that is always set in a semi-permanent snarl. After becoming a demon, he gains many demonic traits like four black flame-like markings on both sides of his cheeks, elongated canines that resemble fangs, sickly pale skin, sharp blackened nails, and pointed ears. By becoming a member of the Twelve Kizuki and rising to the position of Upper Rank Six, his eyes are etched with the kanji of and of . When he was still human, who is still undergoing training under Kuwajima, he is shown to be wearing a black kimono with a white collar, worn loosely to expose his chest and his signature magatama-necklaces around his neck. When he became a Demon Slayer, he wore the Corps' standard uniform consisting of a black "gakuran"-like jacket, a pair of equally black pants held up by a white belt, tucked into white wrapped around his ankles, and a pair of and . When he became a demon, he is shown to be wearing his signature kimono secured with a blue obi over his Demon Slayer uniform that has yellow flame-like markings near the chest area. His forearms are seemingly wrapped in "kyahan"-like material. He also wears multiple necklaces on his neck and wrist with green colored strings that hold together blue -like pendants that were yellow in color when he was human. Personality. Though outwardly brash and arrogant, Kaigaku is in fact cowardly and selfish. Like many orphans living on the streets, he grew up resorting to thievery and other immoral means to survive. He even goes so far as to sacrifice the lives of all the orphans under Gyomei's care to save his own skin. This has caused him to develop an intense form of self-preservation, often doing what in his own best interest at the expense of others. At some point after this, Kaigaku met and became the disciple of Jigoro Kuwajima. Because of his great talent with a sword, he was poised to become the next Thunder Hashira. However, unlike other orphans who join the Corps, Kaigaku never developed a desire to slay demons or protect people. When confronted with a stronger opponent, Kaigaku quickly surrendered. Furthermore, he seems to have developed a sense of hypocritical self-righteousness. He called Zenitsu Agatsuma worthless for having no dignity or perseverance and was repulsed at the idea of succeeding Jigoro along with him. Kaigaku also seems to have a twisted perspective of 'right' and 'wrong', believing that those who judge him right (i.e., say he is worthy) are good and those who judge him wrong and have a low estimation of him are evil. Additionally, he also has an inflated ego, viewing himself as a special and gifted person. In the end, after being beheaded and being at death's door, Kaigaku remains unrepentant and is pleased to know that at least Zenitsu would die with him. However, Yushiro arrives and begins mocking him that he will be given nothing since he never learned how to give, and Kaigaku's fate was sealed once he decided to let his desire inflate and take control of him. Upon seeing Yushiro rescue Zenitsu, Kaigaku screams in anger as the remainder of his body disintegrates. History. Kaigaku was an orphan and a thief who had to eat scraps and steal to survive. He was one of the orphans Gyomei Himejima cared for at his temple. After he was caught by the other children for stealing temple money, he was chased out at night and encountered a demon, which he then let in to the temple in exchange for having his life spared. Kaigaku developed the belief that strength and survival were the only things worth respecting and was willing to grovel and beg for his life if it was what it took to survive. Eventually, he was taken in by Jigoro along with Zenitsu, learning Thunder Breathing. He became determined to become Jigoro's successor and the new Thunder Hashira. Jigoro, however, insisted that both he and Zenitsu would become his successors, despite Zenitsu's weakness and timid nature. Synopsis. Mount Natagumo Arc. During his battle against Son of the Spider Family. Zenitsu recalls a moment during in his training when Kaigaku had admonished him for wasting the time of Jigoro, who he had respected, because of his constant whining and cowardice. When he called their trainer "Gramps", Kaigaku threw a peach at him and demanded he never attempt to act familiar with him. Hashira Training Arc. During Hashira Training, Zenitsu receives word that Kaigaku had become a demon, and that Jigoro committed seppuku as atonement. Kaigaku had the unfortunate luck of encountering Kokushibo, and, upon witnessing the Upper Rank's immense power, kneeled before him and surrendered in order to save his own skin. Kokushibo offered the Demon Slayer a chance to become a demon and gave him a handful of Muzan's blood to intake, believing if Muzan believes him to be worthy, he can join the Twelve Kizuki. Despite fear consuming his body, Kaigaku eventually obliged and drank the demon's blood, transforming him. Even in the short time he was a demon, Kaigaku had already eaten numerous people, and eventually became powerful enough to take his position as the new Upper Rank Six of the Twelve Kizuki. Infinity Castle Arc. During the Demon Slayer Corps attack on the Infinity Castle, a hidden Kaigaku is detected by Zenitsu and forced to show himself. Kaigaku dismisses his fellow trainee's commanding tone, claiming it was improper manners to speak to a senior in such a way, but Zenitsu tells him that now that he is a demon, he does not recognize him as so. Kaigaku mocks the Demon Slayer for still only using Thunder Breathing's first form but is taken aback when Zenitsu insults his spot as Upper Rank Six as a vacant position at the bottom of the ranks. Zenitsu then angrily told him of Jigoro's agonizing death, as he had committed seppuku to atone for his transformation but no one was there to finish the task, leaving him to die alone. To this, the unrepentant Kaigaku only laughs in his face and claims only he had valued who he is, believing that Jigoro never saw his worth for attempting to place him in the same position as "scum" like him. Zenitsu then retorts that if he was as pathetic as he made him to be, then so would he since Jigoro saw them as equals. Angered, the new Upper Rank Six responded by attacking him with Thunder Breathing, Fourth Form: Distant Thunder. To Kaigaku's shock, Zenitsu blitzes past him and slices into his neck, shocking the Upper Rank as he did not expect Zenitsu to change so drastically. Recalling his encounter with Kokushibo and reaffirming his belief that everything he did to live was in the right, Kaigaku then focuses his anger on Zenitsu and attacks him with Thunder Breathing, Second Form: Rice Spirit. Zenitsu is shocked to see consecutive attacks and believes Kaigaku had eaten much victims. He then uses Third Form: Thunder Swarm and successfully hits Zenitsu, before attacking again with Fifth Form: Heat Lightning to strike Zenitsu with his lightning. As Kaigaku revels in his new power, he attacks again with Sixth Form: Rumble and Flash, severely wounding the Demon Slayer and causing him to fall. Watching Zenitsu's body plummet down the castle, Kaigaku claims he is different to him. To his utter shock, the demon sees him land upright along the walls and is suddenly attacked with Thunder Breathing, Seventh Form: Honoikazuchi no Kami, instantly decapitating him. Unable to see the attack, he curses Jigoro for teaching Zenitsu an unknown move, to which Zenitsu tells him the form was something he created to use alongside him. As his severed head and Zenitsu's unconscious body fall, Kaigaku is taken aback by Zenitsu's creation of a seventh form, and he can only grumble at the thought of someone weaker than him attaining such a feat. As he burns to ash, Kaigaku refuses to accept he had lost to Zenitsu, reassuring himself that with Zenitsu no longer having any strength remaining, he will die with him. A demon enters his view and tells him that someone who never gives can never receive, and that wanting is the same as nothing when one cannot make it himself, before telling Kaigaku that dying alone is pitiful. As Kaigaku disintegrates completely, the demon catches Zenitsu and leaps to safety, denying the new Upper Rank Six's revenge on his killer. Abilities. Overall Abilities. As a transformed Demon Slayer and a member of the Upper Ranks, Kaigaku was an extremely powerful demon. This is supported by the fact that he had to receive a lot of Muzan Kibutsuji's blood for him to turn into a demon as users of Total Concentration Breathing are more resistant to the effects of the Demon King's blood. Zenitsu also noted that Kaigaku had eaten a lot of humans in the short period of time between Hashira Training and his encounter with him, further testifying his strength. According to Yushiro, during Kaigaku's short tenure as Upper Rank Six, he has yet to master his techniques and abilities and could have killed Zenitsu immediately in a year's time. Physical Abilities. Immense Speed & Reflexes: As a Thunder Breathing user turned Upper Rank demon, Kaigaku possesses tremendous movement speed and reflexes due to the Thunder Breathing swordsmanship style placing a heavy emphasis on swiftness and bursts of speed. This combined with assimilating a large amount of Muzan's blood makes Kaigaku an extremely fast fighter, as shown when he could more than keep up with Zenitsu Agatsuma, a seasoned and skilled Demon Slayer that had trained under the same teacher to learn the same Breathing Style, and even overpower him for the majority of their clash. Fighting Style. Master Swordsman: As the one who was initially supposed to inherit Jigoro's position as the Thunder Hashira, it is implied that Kaigaku is an extremely proficient swordsman with great skill in Thunder Breathing. His swordsmanship is different compared to most Demon Slayers as he places his sword sheath at his back rather than on either side of his waists. Nonetheless, his swordsmanship skill could match that of Zenitsu who had previously fought Upper Rank demons. With his Blood Demon Art, Kaigaku's swordsmanship was greatly enhanced and became even more dangerous. Breathing Style. After becoming a demon and developing a Blood Demon Art, Kaigaku's Thunder Breathing has manifested into reality as he can manipulate actual lightning and electricity, greatly improving the offensive power of this Breathing Style. Kaigaku even stated that he has "surpassed Thunder Breathing". Blood Demon Art. Electrokinesis: Complementing his Breathing Style, Thunder Breathing, Kaigaku's Blood Demon Art grants him special electrokinetic abilities which allow him to generate and manipulate black colored lightning and electricity from his flesh and blood. This lightning-like Blood Demon Art creates a special effect which cracks and rends his target's flesh while burning it, greatly augmenting the lethality and offensive capability of his attacks. The bleeding caused by Kaigaku's sword effect nearly destroyed Zenitsu's eyeballs and left him severely injured after the fight. Kaigaku uses this Blood Demon Art to great effect, utilizing lightning in conjunction with his Thunder Breathing techniques to enhance his attack range and speed, which even Zenitsu had trouble keeping up with. It is implied that this Blood Demon Art helped make up for Kaigaku's own inability to perform the most fundamental technique of the Thunder Breathing style, Thunderclap and Flash. Techniques. <tabber> </tabber> Equipment. Flesh Katana: Similar to the demon who would transform him, Kokushibo, Kaigaku carries around a modified version of the Nichirin katana he used when he was a Demon Slayer that is made from his flesh and blood. However, unlike Kokushibo's katana, his katana isn't heavily distorted and is nearly identical to his original one. His flesh katana has a black lightning pattern on both sides of his yellow tinted blade along with a black and gold handle. Kaigaku's katana has a tsuba identical to the one used by Zenitsu Agatsuma, which is circular shaped with four slight indentations, the center has a silver tone with small triangles and has a golden border. It is implied that his flesh blade facilitates the use of his Blood Demon Art, as he can channel his blood through it when he unleashes his techniques. Unlike most swordsmen, Kaigaku places his sword sheath on his back instead of by his waist.

Kakushi The are a brigade of people who work as attendants to the Demon Slayer Corps. Overview. The Kakushi are a brigade responsible for different tasks pertaining to providing support for the Demon Slayers, which include: Joining. It is unknown how many members the Kakushi have, as well as how they recruit members, making these members quite mysterious. In some cases, Kakushi members are retired Demon Slayers or Slayers who have been injured or disabled to the point they can't fight anymore. There are also individuals who failed to pass the Final Selection examination but became Kakushi in order to still be of use to the Demon Slayer Corps. Attire. They wear dark-tinted versions of the standard Demon Slayer uniforms consisting of a modified gakuran jacket and hakama pants. Said gakuran jacket has a longer hem and puffed sleeves to allow them to move freely, with the kanji of the brigade's name inked on the back (隠). Their forearms and their shins are covered in a black stretchy fabric, securing their sleeves and hakama respectively, with a white buckled belt holding it up. For footwear, they wear plain white jika-tabi with reed-colored flats. To protect their identity, they wear dark head coverings with white linings, and a paper-like mask with three dark lines tied around their face, divided into two sections, one in the front and the back, left to hang freely to allow them to speak and breathe easily. History. During the golden era of the Demon Slayers in the, a traitor Demon Slayer named Michikatsu Tsugikuni became a demon and soon after killed the then-acting leader of the Demon Slayer Corps. He took the leader's head to Demon King Muzan Kibutsuji. Ever since then, more effort was put into hiding the residence the Corps' leader lived in. This was the time when the Kakushi were first formed. With Muzan's defeat and the Demon Slayer Corps officially disbanding, the Kakushi also ceased to exist.

Kamado Nezuko no Uta is an insert song for Kimetsu no Yaiba Season 3. It is produced by and performed by . Description. Kamanue was a member of the Twelve Kizuki, having held the new position of . Appearance. Kamanue was a short young man of pale skin complexion, his face decorated by a thick line of dark green under both of his eyes and across his nose that ran up vertically into another, shorter horizontal line on his forehead. Four large dots were also placed at the far ends of the line on his cheeks, the middle of the one on his forehead, and below his lower lip. His eyes were cat-like in shape, the pupils slit and the irises pale blue with a white ring around the sides. The kanji for and was etched onto his left eye, which signified his position. Kamanue also possessed dark brown hair with bright orange tips that was worn swept back but fluffed out on either side of his head and neck. He wore a white with a yellow scale pattern down the sleeves, as well as a white button-up shirt and dark pants. Personality. Kamanue was a very anxious and restive individual. He constantly wore a scared expression due to the fact that he felt weak and vulnerable as the lowest of the Lower Ranks. He appeared to be constantly skittish during his short time at the Infinity Castle. As with most demons, his loyalty to Muzan Kibutsuji, though steadfast, was built on great fear, sweating profusely when he heard the Demon King's voice and being unable to say a word when he was challenged to continue speaking his mind when Muzan questioned his loyalty. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. After the death of Rui, Lower Rank Five, Kamanue was summoned to the Infinity Castle by Nakime. He was surprised to find himself in the immense fortress, visibly nervous as to why he is here since he had never seen it before. He quickly noticed Wakuraba and Mukago in the distance, before turning around and finding Enmu and Rokuro in the castle with him, and he realized a gathering of the Lower Ranks had never happened ever. Before he could question the situation further, Nakime transported the demons to a platform in front of her and another female demon. He wondered who the woman in front of them is, only to be answered with a familiar threatening voice. Kamanue and the Lower Ranks quickly bowed down when they realized the demon before them was Muzan Kibutsuji himself, who had disguised himself to lower their alertness to the situation. When Mukago attempted to apologize on their behalf, Muzan silenced her and went on to explain the death of Rui, before he demanded to know why the Lower Ranks are so weak. Muzan lectured them about how being in the ranks of the Twelve Kizuki isn’t the end; it was only the beginning of what is to come. He stated their sole purpose is to consume blood so they can be of use to him. He continued explaining that it had been over a century and the Upper Ranks have remained unchanged, and it had always been them who have disposed of the Hashira, yet the Lower Ranks were replaced frequently if not constantly. When he heard this, Kamanue scoffed at how it seems easy for Muzan to talk about, only for Muzan to repeat the phrase aloud. Capable of reading the minds of his demons, Muzan asked Kamanue why he couldn’t be told that. When he realized he is in trouble, he heard as Muzan angrily demanded him to continue his words, before expanding and extending his arm into a tentacle to grab the Lower Rank by his body. Kamanue tearfully attempted to apologize, but was promptly devoured by Muzan as the rest of the Lower Ranks, except Enmu, keep their heads lowered in shocked silence. Abilities. Overall Abilities: Little was known about Kamanue's strength and abilities as a demon, but it can be assumed that he was much stronger than the average demon and likely surpassed Kyogai, the former member of the Twelve Kizuki whose place he took.

Kanae Kocho was a minor character in "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She was a Demon Slayer and the late . She is the older sister of Shinobu Kocho and the adoptive older sister of Kanao Tsuyuri. She was slain several years prior to the present story by Upper Rank Two, Doma. Appearance. Kanae was a young woman of a slender build who was rather tall for her age and had notably red lips in contrast to her pale complexion. She had long, straight, black hair that reached just below her hips, worn down with two shorter clumps over her shoulders, and arched, ear-length bangs on either side of her face. Her eyes were a pale violet and slanted towards the sides of her face, bright and bug-like, with many notable white sparkles reflecting light off of them. Kanae wore a dark purple-tinted version of the standard Demon Slayer uniform and tattsuke hakama pants as well as a piece of black fabric around her calves and with pale purple straps. She also sported a pair of green and pink butterfly hairpins that she wore adorned on either side of her head - one of which was later used by her adoptive younger sister, Kanao Tsuyuri, as a memento. She also wore the white butterfly-patterned haori that fades to pale turquoise then pink toward the cuff and hem, which Shinobu Kocho now wears in the present. Personality. Kanae is shown to be a good-natured girl with an easygoing personality; in Shinobu and Kanao's flashbacks, she is almost always seen with a gentle smile on her face. When Sanemi Shinazugawa lashed out against their leader, Kagaya Ubuyashiki, she displayed concern for Kagaya and gently informed Sanemi how Kagaya truly cares for the Demon Slayers under his charge. Kanae also had a dream of someday being able to live peacefully alongside demons despite all the suffering and death they have inflicted on humans, which later inspired Shinobu to do the same. However, Kanae had a much stricter side, as shown when Shinobu was on the verge of defeat during her battle with Doma. Kanae's spirit ordered her to stand up and face her opponent, brushing away the excuses forming in her mind that she was too delicate to take on demons. Kanae was also keenly observant, seeing through Doma's acting and lies, and deducing that he was in fact emotionless and empty. According to Kanao, Kanae felt sorry for him due to his emptiness, even though he mortally wounded her. History. The Kocho sisters lived a peaceful, privileged life with their wealthy and loving parents, who continuously doted on and cared for them. Growing up wanting for nothing, the two sisters were content with their simple life together. However, this all came crashing down when a demon attacked their home. Their parents tried to protect the two but were slaughtered before their daughters' eyes. They would have been next, but they were saved by the timely arrival of Gyomei Himejima, who killed the demon immediately before it could kill either of them. After these traumatic events, the two sisters made a promise to both join the Demon Slayer Corps to stop the demons from inflicting the same horror and pain they experienced on others. Both of them soon became successful Demon Slayers after completing their training and developing their own Breathing Styles. At some point down the line, Kanae became the Flower Hashira. She was present at Sanemi's first Hashira meeting, looking at him in alarm when he rudely confronted their leader. When Kagaya mentions Masachika Kumeno by name, Kanae informs the surprised Sanemi that Kagaya made a point to memorize the names and backgrounds of each Demon Slayer who died in combat. One day, while traveling through a village, Kanae took notice of a little girl being dragged along by a leash by a man. Even though the girl was nameless, dirty, and didn't speak, Kanae approached her and attempted to convince the man who purchased her to let her go. When he demanded money in compensation, Shinobu flung money in the air, grabbed the rope he released, and ran off with the girl. They then took her to the Butterfly Mansion, adopted her, and named her Kanao. When the girl proved unresponsive without orders, Kanae gave her a coin to flip to help her make decisions until she could make decisions on her own. Some years later, Kanae ran into the Upper Rank Two of the Twelve Kizuki, Doma. She was fatally wounded during the encounter, but he was forced to flee from the rising sun before he could devour her. As she lay dying in Shinobu's arms, she tries to convince her sister to leave the Demon Slayer Corps to live a normal life, but her sister is dead set on avenging her. With the last of her strength, Kanae described Doma to Shinobu before succumbing to her wounds. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. During Tanjiro Kamado's training to become stronger with Rehabilitation Training, Shinobu met the boy and commended him for his spirit and will to push on. To Shinobu's shock, Tanjiro unexpectedly asks her if she is angry, despite having a smile on her. Her expression saddens as she states that she had always been angry at demons, seeing them as unredeemable, unlike her beloved older sister Kanae. Kanae, like Tanjiro, saw sympathy in demons; when she was killed, Shinobu attempted to maintain a friendly and cheery façade in remembrance of her but couldn't hold the same sympathy for demons, seeing them as irredeemable. Infinity Castle Arc. After being pulled into the Infinity Castle along with the rest of the Demon Slayer Corps, Shinobu happens upon Doma, Kanae's killer. He eventually recognizes Kanae's haori and recollects how he missed out on eating her, enraging Shinobu. When she is on the brink of defeat, Kanae's spirit commands her to continue fighting. After Doma's death at the hands of her adoptive sister Kanao and Inosuke Hashibira, Shinobu and Kanae's spirits pat the exhausted Kanao on the head, commending her for doing well. Shinobu and Kanae are seen in kimonos, running towards their parents as they all go to heaven. Kanao, who previously internalized her emotions from her abuse, apologizes to Kanae because she could not cry during her funeral, despite no one blaming her. She saw Kanae's hair pin broken and found Shinobu's pin in the lotus pond, before clutching memoirs of to her sisters to her chest and crying for the first time, mourning Kanae and Shinobu. Abilities. Overall Abilities. During her time as a Demon Slayer, Kanae was a Flower Breathing user that was skilled enough to hold the position of the Flower Hashira, a position only reserved for Demon Slayers who have slain one of the Twelve Kizuki or have successfully battled and slain at least 50 demons, further implying her incredible skill and natural born talents. Unlike her younger sister, Shinobu, who lacks the strength to cut off a demon's head due to her small body and thus compensated by using a uniquely-designed Nichirin Sword and new fighting style, Kanae wielded an ordinary-looking blade. A further testament to Kanae's strength is that she was able to fended off Upper Rank Two, Doma, until sunrise, showing that although she was incapable of defeating him and was severely injured in the end, she was at least able to battle him to a standstill. Fighting Style. Master Swordswoman: As a Hashira, Kanae would be one of the most powerful combatants in the Demon Slayer Corps, which is supported by the fact that she was able to battle with the second strongest Upper Rank for until sunrise, though it was not specified when the fight started. Equipment. Standard Nichirin Katana: Kanae carries around a standard sized and shaped Nichirin katana that is light pink in color. Her katana's handguard seems to be the same as her younger sister, Shinobu Kocho's: a four-petaled aqua-colored flower, trimmed with orange. As a Hashira, Kanae's blade should have the words engraved on the side. Her katana broke during her encounter with Upper Rank Two, Doma. Relationships. Shinobu Kocho. Shinobu Kocho is her biological younger sister and only surviving relative, the two of them shared a strong and loving sisterly bond. Kanae's death becomes Shinobu's main motivation for becoming stronger in order to avenge her death; she even goes as far as turning herself into living poison with the intent of being devoured to weaken Doma from the inside so that Kanao can complete their vengeance. Kanao Tsuyuri. Kanao Tsuyuri is her adoptive younger sister after saving her from poverty and adopting her. Kanae did not reprimand her for her inability to make decisions for herself, and instead gave her a coin to flip to help her make decisions. Kanao continued to use this coin up until a chance interaction with Tanjiro Kamado—the person who opened up her heart. Although Kanao was unable to cry at Kanae's grave due to her past trauma, her adoptive sister's death affected her greatly. She agrees to be part of Shinobu's plan for revenge against Doma, and his hand in both her sisters' deaths causes her to display a strong emotion for the first time: hate. Following Doma's defeat, Kanao overcame her emotional trauma and cried for the first time, mourning both her sisters. Doma. Despite being fatally wounded by the demon, Kanae pitied him for his lack of true emotions. Doma, after being reminded of her by the haori that Shinobu now wears in the current day, commended her strength and was regretful that he was forced to retreat before he could devour her.

Kanae Kocho/Relationships Relationships. Shinobu Kocho. Kanae was noted to have a very close and loving sisterly relationship with her biological younger sister, Kanae having been seen to be very close to Shinobu since early childhood and having spent their childhoods happily together with their parents. The sister's bond was incredibly deep and caring, as seen where the two of them both took an oath to protect others from demons and ensure no one else goes through their tragedy upon the two of them surviving the Demon attack that killed their parents. During this time the sisters developed a unique familial dynamic, where Kanae would frequently make lighthearted, whimsical decisions without thinking first, which then causes Shinobu great expiration and worry due to her elder sister's behavior. But Shinobu is still shown to trust her sister deeply and support her sister's decision despite not initial agreeing with her at first, as seen when the two adopted and made off with their adoptive little sister Kanao Tsuyuri. Later, Kanae's deep love for her sister was truly shown during her last moments after fighting Doma, where Kanae begged Shinobu to leave the Demon Slayer Corps and simply live her life free and happy, stating that the only thing that would make her happy is knowing that Shinobu would be able to live a full happy life and die peacefully as an old woman, showing just how much she loved her younger sister. Shinobu in turn showed her own immense love for her elder sister by swearing that she couldn't possibly live like that and begged her sister to tell her which demon killed her, swearing eternal vengeance against whoever killed her sister. Kanao Tsuyuri. Kanae took an interest in Kanao when she saw her being led away as a slave on the bridge. Along with her sister Shinobu, they purchased Kanao from her master and trained her within the Butterfly Mansion. Kanae defended Kanao when Shinobu worried about her indecisiveness and said that if given time, Kanao's heart could blossom. She was the person who gave Kanao the coin she uses to make decisions whenever she is unable to decide things for herself. After Kanae's death, Kanao found herself unable to cry at the funeral, but wears one of Kanae's hairpins as a memento of her. She remembers Kanae's advice in times of trouble, and thinks highly of her. She expresses deep remorse at the fact that she could not cry during Kanae's funeral. Sanemi Shinazugawa. Not much is currently known about Kanae and Sanemi's relationship. Gyomei Himejima claims that Sanemi had a crush on Kanae, though we do not have conformation from Sanemi. We also do not know if these feelings were reciprocated. In Kimetsu Academy, Sanemi is claimed to enjoy talking to Kanae in his free time. Doma. Prior to the beginning of the series, Kanae faced off against Doma. The two fought until dawn, forcing Doma to escape before the arrival of the sun. Kanae was left with major injuries and died soon after their battle. Doma himself recognizes Kanae's haori which her younger sister, Shinobu now wears in the present, and recollects how he missed the opportunity to eat her. As stated by him, Doma acknowledged Kanae's strength during their fight and commended her for it, when he faced Shinobu years later. As revealed by her younger sisters, Kanae was able to tell that Doma lacked the ability to feel and experience genuine human emotions and pitied him for his apathy and inability to feel them. After her death, both Shinobu and Kanao made a point of using this information to insult and degrade Doma out of spite for killing her, genuinely enraging Doma due to them seeing past his supposedly friendly persona.

Kanao Tsuyuri is a major supporting character of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She is a Demon Slayer of the Demon Slayer Corps, Shinobu Kocho's Tsuguko and the adopted sister of Shinobu and Kanae Kocho. Appearance. Kanao is a girl of short stature, with large and gentle eyes of a dark lilac color that are framed by thick eyelashes. She has thin black hair, tied into a ponytail on the right side of her head and fastened by a pink and green butterfly ornament that once belonged to her adoptive sister, Kanae Kocho. She has a straight fringe and two loose, chin-length strands that curve downwards from above each of her ears. Kanao wears a slightly purple-tinted version of the standard Demon Slayer uniform, just with a knee-length pleated skirt in place of the usual pants. Over this, she wears a short white cloak, fastened on one side by a dark pink triple knot, also sporting knee-high lace-up white boots with tan soles, heels and toes. Sometime between then and her next appearance in the Infinity Castle, the color of Kanao's hair changes as the ends now appear tinted slightly purple before fading to a neon pink around halfway down her ponytail. After her battle with Doma, Kanao begins to wear Shinobu Kocho's hairpin rather than Kanae's, as her's was shattered during the battle. She also loses much of the vision of her right eye due to her using Flower Breathing's final form to take out the Upper Rank with her eye gaining a defined pupil with a dark ring around it and becoming deprived of its gradient. Personality. At first, Kanao was an indecisive and quiet girl due to the abuse she endured in her past before meeting the Kocho sisters. She became unable to make decisions by herself and repressed her emotions as a defense mechanism. In order to help rectify this, Kanae Kocho gave her a coin to flip to decide which path to follow when she didn't know what to do. For many years, Kanao continued to show little emotion or desire. Despite this, after seeing what demons did to Aoi Kanzaki, Kiyo Terauchi and Shinobu Kocho's loved ones, Kanao developed a strong hatred against demons directly from her own will. Shinobu, oblivious to this fact, was afraid that she wasn't acting on her own volition. Since Kanao couldn't do housework and nursing at the Butterfly Mansion like her colleagues, she opted to be a Demon Slayer. Without their knowledge, Kanao learned Flower Breathing by watching her sister Kanae. Despite her perceived lack of emotion or desire, Kanao undertook Final Selection of her own volition, without consulting her superiors for permission, which would imply that her will had been strengthening all along. Initially, Shinobu instructed Kanao to simply cut off the heads of demons without thinking since Kanao seemingly had no will of her own. However, Kanao also eventually developed her own desire to fight. Between Kanae's death and the events during Rehabilitation Training, she recovers slightly but still relies on her coin to make decisions. She displays a somewhat mechanical response in conversations; when Tanjiro Kamado approaches her to bid to her farewell, she repeats "goodbye" when he attempts to continue the conversation. However, he eventually manages to start bringing her out of her shell and she starts to make more of her own decisions, in turn relying less on her coin. She also gains the ability to speak unambiguously and Kanao gradually becomes able to express her emotions and wants more openly as seen when Tanjiro recovers from his injuries and she displays relief when she tells Shinobu that she wishes to train alongside her, and when she expresses shock and distress at Shinobu's plan to defeat Doma. In her battle against Doma, Kanao takes uncharacteristically sadistic glee in pointing out his own lack of emotions. Fueled by hatred and spite due to her sisters' deaths by his hand, she attacks him verbally to the point where he drops his normal carefree demeanor. Kanao also demonstrates extreme determination and a deep care for her family, crying for the first time in the wake of Shinobu's death and expressing that she had wished to go home together with her elder sister. Kanao has also now been shown to express a greater sense of camaraderie and care for her fellow Demon Slayers other than Shinobu, as seen when she becomes visibly angry and sympathetic on Inosuke Hashibira's behalf when Doma begins gloating about his mother's death. She shows immense rage at the demon's taunts, insulting him and telling him to silence himself, which is a complete step up from the original emotionally distant relationship she had with her comrades. Later, during the final battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, Kanao was shown to have completely regained the ability to properly express her emotions and make her own choices. Over the course of the battle, Kanao shows visible feelings of anger and terror towards the Demon King as her and her fellow Demon Slayers take him on. Even after the battle is over she continues to show emotion, proving herself to genuinely love and care for both Tanjiro and Nezuko Kamado after watching the latter's desperate attempts to reach out to her now transformed brother, which even reached the point of her sacrificing her one remaining eye to inject Tanjiro with Shinobu's last vial of the human-conversion drug in an attempt to save him. Abilities. Overall Abilities. Kanao is the Tsuguko of Kanae Kocho and Shinobu Kocho who has been personally trained by the both of them in the art of combat. As such, Kanao possesses extremely refined physical abilities, sharpened skills and prowess that potentially marks her as a future member of the Demon Slayer Corps' Hashira. Tanjiro Kamado, another promising candidate, even states that, during their first meeting together, he could already sense that Kanao was the closest to the Hashira out of the existing Demon Slayers, just by smelling her scent and feeling her aura, which further confirms her skills. Indomitable Will: Like most Demon Slayers, Kanao possesses an undaunted will and spirit, refusing to give up and die when fighting even the most formidable foes that defeated her masters, Doma and later on, the Demon King, Muzan Kibutsuji. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: Kanao has attained incredible physical strength through harsh training. She can jump extremely high distances incredibly quickly, showing her incredible leg strength. In terms of arm strength, she can swing her katana at tremendous speeds incessantly without tiring. She was even able to slash through the midsection of Doma, a demon whose body boasts incredibly high durability. Immense Speed and Reflexes: Kanao is extremely fast. During Rehabilitation Training, she can consistently outspeed Tanjiro Kamado, Zenitsu Agatsuma and Inosuke Hashibira all at once before they mastered the . During her battle with Doma, she was capable of reacting and fighting on par with the Upper Rank during their fight. Doma noted that her body is similar to that of a spring, bouncing back from his attacks with her own high speed attacks and movements. She was also capable of dodging attacks of his Blood Demon Art techniques. In the final against Muzan Kibutsuji, she was able to attack him for several moments. Immense Stamina and Endurance: Kanao has incredible stamina and endurance. During her battle with Upper Rank Two, Doma, Kanao is able to exert herself even farther than her limits and fight against the demon, being able to endure numerous attacks. She is able to keep fighting despite the injuries that she had suffered from the fight and recover enough to then confront Muzan shortly afterwards. Supernatural Abilities. Enhanced Vision: Kanao possesses extremely sharp eyesight, being able to accurately predict her opponent's next attack and movements by simply observing the subtle shifts of their muscles, joints and the slight movements of their eyes. This allows her to make effective counterattacks and dodges and stay ahead of her opponents. The Upper Rank Two, Doma, comments on this feat and remarks that due to this skill, Kanao may be more skilled than Shinobu Kocho. This ability is enhanced with the Flower Breathing, Final Form: Equinoctial Vermilion Eye. Fighting Style. Master Swordswoman: As an immensely gifted individual, Kanao is an incredible powerful swordswoman, to the point even Doma thought that she was likely more talented than Shinobu Kocho. Her combination of refined skills and acute sense of vision allows her to fight against the Upper Rank by herself for some time before Inosuke Hashibira's intervention. She was also able to contribute to the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, alongside her fellow Demon Slayers. Equipment. Standard Nichirin Katana: Kanao carries around a standard sized and shaped Nichirin katana which is light pink in color. The katana's tsuba is circular shaped with a light pastel blue center and border, filled 3 red five-leafed flowers and a winding pattern that is light green in color. The handle is pink, decorated with white cords and capped with a gold kashira. Along with her katana, she also has a standard sword sheath that is black in color.
