Kanao Tsuyuri/Relationships Relationships. Tanjiro Kamado. When Kanao first saw Tanjiro at the Final Selection, they did not have any sort of interaction as she remained aloof and quiet at the end of the ceremony. Later on in the series, when they meet again on Mount Natagumo, Kanao gets into a physical altercation with Tanjiro as he tries to protect his sister from getting killed and as result gets knocked out cold by Kanao. Tanjiro is brought to the Butterfly Mansion to recover and sees her in the garden, he immediately recognizes her as one of the survivors from the Final Selection but fails to recognize her as his assailant. Later on when they begin to train, Tanjiro struggles to beat Kanao in all of the tasks due to her advanced abilities but he is able to adapt and beat her. During one of the games; the task is to splash the opponent with a strong smelling tea, however, instead of dumping it on Kanao, Tanjiro instead places the cup on her head to avoid splashing her, thinking it would be cruel to splash her with something so foul-smelling. When he bids her farewell after recovering, Tanjiro encourages her to be optimistic and for her to open her heart, and flashes her a smile as he bids her farewell. Kanao is seen holding her hands close to her chest and slightly blushing, and falls flat on her face when Kiyo unexpectedly calls out to her from behind. It is implied in an extra chapter following the end of the Functional Recovery Training Arc that she may have had a crush on Tanjiro. As the story progresses, Kanao starts showing more emotion and decisiveness, especially when Tanjiro is brought back to recover at the Butterfly Mansion following the battles in the Entertainment District. Upon discovering that he had awaken, she drops the flower vase on the floor and tears up while telling him she's glad he had awoken. When the other inhabitants of the Mansion begin to bicker while visiting Tanjiro, she tries to get everyone to quiet down but ultimately ends up yelling at everyone after he falls asleep again. During the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, Kanao is left as the only conscious Demon Slayer left and tries to will herself to continue fighting. As Muzan is about to deliver the final blow, Tanjiro momentarily immobilizes Muzan and manages to carry Kanao to safety. Realizing that he has awaken, Kanao sheds tears as she repeatedly calls out his name and he responds to her by apologizing for being late. After Tanjiro turns into a Demon, Kanao cries when seeing Nezuko trying to calm her brother. Her sympathy for the siblings leads to her once again using Flower Breathing Final Form: Equinoctial Vermilion Eye and create an opening to inject the Demon-to-human cure into Tanjiro, putting her own safety at risk and showing how much she cares for them. After Tanjiro successfully returns to his human form, she cries of happiness and is visibly relieved to see him safely back as a human, the two exchanging tearful smiles as they lie across from each other. Kanao and Tanjiro would eventually marry and start a family, having two great-great-grandchildren by the names of Kanata Kamado and Sumihiko Kamado between them. Kanae Kocho. Kanae took an interest in Kanao when she saw her being led away as a slave on the bridge. Along with her sister Shinobu, they purchased Kanao from her master and trained her within the Butterfly Mansion. Kanae defended Kanao when Shinobu worried about her indecisiveness and said that if given time, Kanao's heart could blossom. She was the person who gave Kanao the coin she uses to make decisions whenever she is unable to decide things for herself. After Kanae's death, Kanao found herself unable to cry at the funeral, but wears one of Kanae's hairpins as a memento of her. She remembers Kanae's advice in times of trouble, and thinks highly of her. She expresses deep remorse at the fact that she could not cry during Kanae's funeral. Shinobu Kocho. Shinobu was the one who snatched Kanao away from the slave driver and, along with Kanae, rescued Kanao from her captive lifestyle. Despite being the one to impulsively buy her, she quickly became frustrated when Kanao could not make her own decisions, declaring that she was dangerous to herself and others. Over time however, Shinobu warmed up to her, eventually even making Kanao her Tsuguko. She is very happy when Kanao expresses her wish to train beside her, and the two have a strong sisterly relationship. Before the decisive battle in the Infinity Castle, Shinobu entrusted Kanao with avenging Kanae's death while she used herself as a sacrifice. Even though their revenge goes as planned, Kanao is nonetheless filled with hatred and spite towards Doma. After she and Inosuke kill Doma for good, she fishes through the water to find Shinobu's hairpin as a keepsake of her departed sister. Kanao cries for the first time in the wake of Shinobu's death. Aoi Kanzaki. How close they are is somewhat uncertain, but the two get along and seem to have a somewhat sisterly relationship. Kanao attempts to stop Tengen from taking Aoi with him at a time when it was highly unusual for Kanao to make her own decisions or go against her orders. As seen in the novel, Aoi previously thought of Kanao as difficult to deal with, since she never showed her own emotions. She also felt inferior to Kanao, since Kanao could fight demons and Aoi could not. However, once Kanao starts to open up and make her own decisions, Aoi and her begin to grow closer. Eventually their friendship grows strong enough that, next to Shinobu, Aoi becomes the closest person to Kanao and one of the people she cares for the most, even considering her something akin to another sister. Kanao in particular comes to enjoy eating every single dish Aoi cooks for her and considers them all her favorites. Aoi in turn is shown to truly love Kanao and has come to genuinely see her as a sister. So much so that during the time it was Kanao’s decision to chose a last name for herself, Aoi attempted to discreetly convince her to take her last name to make them as close as genuine sisters. Inosuke Hashibira. Kanao interacts minimally with Inosuke throughout training. Sometimes, his actions make her see him as a weirdo e.g. - wall-crawling or dislocating all the joints in his arm and relocating them. However, the two end up forming an unlikely duo in the battle against Doma, each fueled by a desire for revenge. During the course of their battle against Doma, Kanao comes to genuinely emphasize and care for Inosuke. After the Upper Rank's retelling of Kotoha Hashibira's death in which he happily insults and mocks her for her "stupidity," Kanao becomes visibly angry, showing a strong degree of camaraderie and friendship between the two. They make for an effective team against Doma, aided as well by Shinobu's poison, and are able to decapitate the Upper Rank 2 despite neither human combatant even being a Hashira. After the battle, Kanao and Inosuke do not seem to share any dialogue, but quietly grieve their respective and shared losses. When they return to fight Muzan, they exchange some brief banter, and seem to work well together. Doma. Much like Shinobu, Kanao holds a strong resentment and hatred towards the Upper Rank for killing Kanae. This grudge grows even deeper after Doma devours Shinobu following their duel, even if it was part of their plan for revenge. Kanao takes immense pleasure and satisfaction at calling Doma out on his inner "emptiness" and non-existent emotions, taunting him by asking him why he was even born and why he continued to bother living if he couldn't feel anything like a normal person would. She eventually kills him with the help of Inosuke and Shinobu's poison.

Kanao Tsuyuri/Synopsis History. Kanao lived an impoverished lifestyle before she was taken in by Kanae Kocho and Shinobu Kocho. Her parents were incredibly abusive towards her and her siblings, beating them and drowning them if they did anything they disliked. Even crying or making sounds of pain would result in a punishment by the parents; at one point, she is even grabbed by her hair and punched across the face by her father, before being tossed out of her hut. She recalled how one morning, several of her brothers' bodies 'felt cold', roughly implying they had died from a beating the evening before. She broke psychologically because of this, becoming an empty shell who was eventually sold off into slavery. As she was being led off, tied around the waist by a rope held by her purchaser, they were approached by the Kocho sisters. After confirming she was a slave, Shinobu distracted the man by flinging money in the air. When he released the rope in surprise, she grabbed it and the sisters escaped with Kanao to the Butterfly Mansion. Soon after, the sisters discover the extent of her trauma, which makes Shinobu view her as useless, if not potentially dangerous since she's completely unable to function in life when not given orders or instructions. Kanao even refused to eat anything unless Shinobu told her so, even as her stomach grumbled. Kanae, unperturbed, gives Kanao a coin and instructed her to flip it if she ever needs help making a decision. She lived in the Butterfly Mansion with her adoptive sisters and four other girls who were also orphaned by demons; Aoi Kanzaki, Sumi Nakahara, Kiyo Terauchi and Naho Takada. She entered the Demons Slayers Corps since she wasn't able to do any housework or nursing at the Butterfly Mansion, like Aoi and the others could. Kanae and Shinobu didn't condone it, but Kanao learned the Flower Breathing just by watching them, and she took the selection exams without their permission. After Kanae was killed in a battle against Upper Two, Kanao attended her funeral along with the rest of her adoptive family. Although she was disturbed by her own inability to cry at her beloved sister's death, nobody judged her for it. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. Kanao appears as one of the nearly twenty participants in Final Selection. Following the seven days to test them, she is one of the five to survive; notably, she is the only one with no visible injuries or bruises. She says nothing during the final day, merely gazing at a butterfly or at her Kasugai crow and ignoring the commotion around her. Mount Natagumo Arc. As Shinobu's Tsuguko, Kanao accompanies her and Giyu Tomioka to Mount Natagumo on Kagaya Ubuyashiki's orders. She pursues Tanjiro and Nezuko Kamado when they attempt to flee from Shinobu, successfully catching up and knocking an injured Tanjiro unconscious by kicking him in the back after he tells Nezuko to run. She catches up to Nezuko as well and tries to cut her head off, but to her surprise Nezuko dodges by shrinking into child-size and continuing to run. The chase continues as Kanao fails to land her subsequent hits, and through all of it, Nezuko doesn't attempt to fight back. Though Kanao is left baffled at the idea of a Demon not attacking humans, she decides not to ponder on it since her orders were to kill any and all Demons. Once she receives orders by a crow to capture the siblings, she immediately stops attacking and even asks the Demon if she is Nezuko. It is implied that Kanao somehow restrained Nezuko and placed her back in her box, as she is next seen ordering the Kakushi during the clean-up while Zenitsu Agatsuma watches. Zenitsu recognizes her as "the girl from the Final Selection", but does not tell this to anyone. Rehabilitation Training Arc. As Tanjiro and Nezuko arrive at the Butterfly Mansion, Kanao is seen standing quietly in one of the gardens, surrounded by butterflies. When the Kamados' escorts asks her if they can enter the Mansion, she simply stands there silently with a vacant smile on her face, until Aoi comes over to let them in. During Tanjiro, Zenitsu and Inosuke Hashibira's daily recovery training at the Mansion, Kanao takes turns with Aoi to play the cup game with each of them, a game of speed in which the aim is to throw sour medicine over your opponent before they do you, as well as a simple game of tag, and she beats her opponents every time in both games. Her winning streak continues until Tanjiro begins training his total concentration breath techniques to increase his speed and stamina, after which he is able to win both games against her. In later training, it's stated that the two had a fairly even streak of wins and losses to each other as they continued to play. After the trio made a complete recovery and begin to prepare to leave the Butterfly Mansion, Tanjiro finds Kanao sitting alone in one of the gardens, and walks over to her to thank her for all her help with their training. Kanao smiles up at him, but says nothing, even as he goes on to praise her for her strength and status as a Tsukugo. After more silence, Kanao reaches into her pocket and takes out her coin, flipping it high into the air. It lands on tails, and, after seeing the result, she looks back up at Tanjiro and says that he needn't thank her since she just followed her instructor's orders, and waves him goodbye. An amazed Tanjiro asks what the coin was and why she flipped it, to which she replies that it's something she uses to make decisions when nobody's ordering her. Confused, Tanjiro askeds why she needed to do this, wondering what happened to make her like this, and Kanao just dismisses him, saying that it doesn't matter. After some thought, Tanjiro asks Kanao if he can borrow her coin, and, after receiving it, flips it high into the air and says that the result will determine whether or not she'll listen to her own heart from then on, instead of just following instructions. He calls that it will land on heads, which it does, and Tanjiro cheers, grabbing Kanao's hands and telling her that she's now free to live how she desires. Before Kanao can reply to this, Tanjiro waves her goodbye and runs off over the garden. Kanao calls after him, asking why it had landed on heads since she didn't notice him using any tricks, and Tanjiro turns, smiles at her, and says that it was totally by chance, and even if it had landed on tails, he would have flipped it in the air again and again until it land on heads, before continuing his exit. Tanjiro saying that he would have flipped the coin over and over shows Kanao his will to continue, which inspires her. Entertainment District Arc. Kanao witnesses the Sound Hashira, Tengen Uzui, arrive at the Butterfly mansion, forcefully abducting Naho and Aoi for his mission to Tokyo. While Kiyo and Sumi tearfully plea him to stop, Kanao panics as he is within his right as a Hashira and Shinobu is not present to help defend them. She tries to rationalise the situation with a coin toss but suddenly remembers Tanjiro's advice to "follow her heart". She overcomes her fear and stops Tengen from walking away, grabbing on his clothes and attempting to pull Aoi and Naho free. Kiyo and Sumi join her but the three are unable to do much more than annoy the far taller and stronger demon slayer. Tanjiro arrives to help, attempting to headbutt Tengen. Tengen disappears, causing Naho and Sumi to fall and for Tanjiro and Kanao to help them. Kanao quietly assists in Tanjiro's protest that he can't simply force them to join his mission, then witnesses him volunteer to take Aoi's place, along with Zenitsu and Inosuke. Kanao sees the demon slayer depart for their mission from outside the Butterfly mansion. After a lengthy confrontation ends with the defeat of the Upper Moons Daki and Gyutaro, Tanjiro is left unconscious from his ordeal. Two months after the battle, Tanjiro suddenly wakes up. Holding a vase while entering his room, Kanao sees him and suddenly drops it. She walks over to him and explains what had happened since the battle, tearfully saying she is relieved to see him awake. Swordsmith Village Arc. Goto enters the room with the castella he brought over, and Tanjiro thanks him, which greatly shocks the kakushi, who then yells to Kanao that she should've told someone Tanjiro was finally awake, before also yelling the news to Kiyo, Naho and Sumi. The three come rushing over, cheering and crying, glad that Tanjiro is finally awake, and Aoi joins them shortly after, expressing her guilt and gratitude to Tanjiro for going to the Red Light District in her place. Tanjiro asks them how everyone else is doing, to which Sumi and Goto reply that Zenitsu had awoken the day after the incident and had gone back on the job two days ago, and Tengen had made it back without any help from the kakushi, just with the support of his wives. Tanjiro expresses his gladness that they're okay, and asks how Inosuke is doing. Sumi and Aoi explain that Inosuke was very close to death at one point due to his bleeding and the poison circulating around his body, and Tanjiro says that he must just be hallucinating the boar-headed Demon Slayer on the ceiling of the room then. Everyone looks up, realising that Inosuke is indeed there, as he jumps down and lands at the end of Tanjiro's bed, saying he's impressed Tanjiro noticed him and boasting that he woke up a whole seven days before he did. As Inosuke continues ranting at him, Kiyo shows Tanjiro a picture of a honey badger and says that Shinobu said Inosuke was just like it, since he's nearly impossible to kill. Inosuke exclaims that he's immortal, but Goto says he's just a moron, which stirs up commotion in the room, with the former trying to attack the latter as Aoi attempts to hold him back. As they continue to argue, Kanao tries to tell them to be quiet, but they ignore her until she raises her voice and shouts that Tanjiro has fallen back asleep so they should let him sleep peacefully. Infinity Castle Arc. During the raid on Muzan's castle, Kanao fights Doma in the wake of Shinobu's death, having previously been told of Shinobu's plan to defeat Doma; the plan required that Shinobu be killed and consumed by Doma in order to deliver a lethal dose of wisteria poison to the Upper Rank in order to weaken him. Shinobu is absorbed by the Upper Rank just as Kanao arrives at the scene, but just before her death she manages to signal to her Tsuguko with her hand. Her death causes Kanao to go berserk in order to try and save her, only to be repelled by an irritated Doma, who tells her not to interfere when he's in the middle of absorbing someone. He successfully devours Shinobu's body until her butterfly-shaped hair piece is the only thing left of her. Doma notes aloud that Kanao must have been told something by the signal Shinobu gave her shortly before her death, wondering what she could have told her, as Kanao stands silently before him, enraged. As he licks Shinobu's hairpin, he says that it is a good night, as such fine feasts keep showing up one after another. After Akaza's death, Doma says that he felt as if the Upper Rank had turned into a different creature before he died, and that his demise was inevitable because he never ate any women. Doma begins to cry over his 'best friend's' death, but Kanao just tells him to stop with the lies. She explains that she knows that every word that comes out of his mouth is nothing but random babble, and that it's impossible for him to be genuinely sad over Akaza because he can't feel anything at all. She says that every person born into the world has feelings, but Doma cannot understand these feelings and covers this up by spitting lies. He has never felt happiness, joy, pain and bitterness, and she says that he is nothing but an empty shell, and she finishes her words by sarcastically asking Doma why he was even born. Doma's face turns serious, and asks how Kanao can say something so cruel, to which the young Demon Slayer responds that she simply hates the Demon and wants to send him to hell this instant. Suddenly, Doma appears behind Kanao, attempting to use one of his fans to cut her head, but she quickly dodges and delivers a blow to his stomach, causing some of his organs to fall out. He doesn't seem to feel her blow, simply sending some of his ice lotuses at her and noting that her reaction speed has risen as she's able to adapt to his attacks. As he regenerates his body, he thinks to himself that Kanao could actually be stronger than Shinobu, a Hashira. Trying to suppress her rage, Kanao attacks Doma with the Flower Breathing, Fifth Form: Peonies of Futility, which he avoids with ease, smiling and commenting on how pretty her attack is before sending his Blood Demon Art: Barren Hanging Garden at her, which she barely fends off with Flower Breathing, Second Form: Honorable Shadow Plum. Doma notices that she is only able to counter and dodge his attacks because of her sharp eyes, since she takes note of the subtle movements of his shoulders, gaze, toes, elbows and knees to predict what he'll do next, and decides it's best to prevent this by taking her eyes out with a swing of his fans. Kanao dodges, and charges at him with Flower Breathing, Sixth Form: Whirling Peach which is nullified by Doma's next Blood Demon Art: Freezing Clouds. The Upper Rank sends two more attacks, Blood Demon Art: Lotus Vines and Cold White Princesses, her way, which she only just avoids before his Wintry Icicles begin to rain on her from above. Kanao dodges again, moving farther away from the Demon, who laughs at her and says that she can't keep moving backwards if she wants to cut off his head. At a speed too quick for the eye to process, Doma runs at Kanao and snatches her blade, returning and planting it in the ground a distance away from her. He says she better come and get it quickly if she wants to survive him, before sending his Blood Demon Art: Scattering Lotuses at the Demon Slayer. At that moment, Inosuke breaks through the ceiling of the room, protecting Kanao from Doma's attack with his Beast Breathing, Fifth Fang: Crazy Cutting. He looks at Doma's eyes and notices that he's Upper Two, which he screams out, happily shouting that if he beats the Demon he'll become a Hashira and asking Kanao what his Hashira title should be. Inosuke notices Kanao's beaten-up face, and asks, surprised, what had happened, saying that Shinobu will get mad if she finds her Tsuguko in that state. Kanao remains silent, and the boar-headed Demon Slayer comes to a realization and asks her if Shinobu is dead, to which Doma replies that she isn't; she will live inside of him for all eternity because he has "saved" her from her pain and suffering. Inosuke recalls Shinobu's kindness to him, and vows to Doma that he'll kill him as he rushes towards the Upper Rank with his Beast Breathing, Fourth Fang: Slice 'n' Dice. Kanao shouts out a warning to him not to breathe in Doma's cold air as the Demon remarks on how messed-up his technique is. Doma attempts to slice off Inosuke's head with one of his fans, but the Demon Slayer flips away from him, launching himself from the flat edge of the fan and landing next to Kanao. He hands her her blade, which he had taken back from Doma, and tells her never to let go of it again. Doma smiles and compliments Inosuke's speed as he jumps towards him, and the two swiftly engage in quick combat, launching Breath Styles and Blood Demon Arts at each other at alarming rates. Inosuke kicks Doma in the stomach, sending him skidding backwards as he dislocates the joints in his right arm and prepares to swing his sword at the Upper Rank's neck. He misjudges his swing and instead slices through Doma's eyes with his Beast Breathing, Ninth Fang: Extending Bendy Slash, and the Demon laughs at his unusual technique as his joints relocate. Doma calls Inosuke messed-up and says that he's never met a kid like him before despite his long lifespan, to which the Demon Slayer replies that that's obvious, since he is the great Inosuke. At an incredible speed, Doma lurches forward and snatches his mask from his head as he's speaking, and Inosuke, enraged, yells at him to give it back. The Demon notices his face, and says he remembers Inosuke from somewhere, asking him if they'd met before. Inosuke responds that they hadn't as he would remember meeting someone like Doma, and Kanao agrees that he was likely making it up due to his tendency to fake things. However, the Upper Rank insists that they have, proceeding to stick his finger through his skull and into his brain to try and jog his memories, which Kanao and Inosuke are visibly disgusted by. Doma says that he knew Inosuke's mother, as his cult took her in, but Inosuke denies that he has a mother since he was raised by boars. Doma laughs and says that he must have a human mother since he's a human, and Inosuke shouts at him to quit spouting lies and give him back his boar mask, rushing in to attack the Demon again with Beast Breathing, Sixth Fang: Palisade Bite. His torso is slashed twice by Doma's fans, who smiles slyly and tells him not to interrupt before sending him flying back to Kanao with his ice. Doma then tells the story of Inosuke's mother, Kotoha, and how she and her baby son joined Doma's cult only to end up running away after she realized the Demon was eating his followers. He explains that she met her demise by Doma's hands, who still believes he was saving her from her abusive household by eating her, but dropped her son off a cliff before the Demon's attack in the hope that he would survive. Memories of her begin to come back to Inosuke, who recalls the song she used to sing to him. Doma calls Kotoha stupid and unfortunate, saying that there wasn't a happy moment in her life, and Inosuke, now enraged, thanks Doma for allowing him to remember this story and promises to not only to kill him for what he did to Kotoha and Shinobu, but to put him through hell beforehand. Doma smiles again, and tells Inosuke that there is no heaven or hell in this world since they're nothing but fantasies created as a coping mechanism for weak humans, as Kanao stares at him in silence, enraged. Inosuke shouts that he doesn't care if there's no hell because he can just make one himself, and tells Doma not to talk about his mother like she was unhappy. The Demon sends his Freezing Clouds at Inosuke, which he blows away with Beast Breathing, Tenth Fang: Whirling Fangs as Kanao prepares to use another Breath Style to attack him from behind. Doma bats her away with one of his fans and moves away, and Inosuke yells at him to get back down so they can continue fighting. He replies that he can't, since Akaza has been defeated and he doesn't have time to play anymore, and uses his Blood Demon Art: Crystalline Divine Child to create smaller clones of himself for Inosuke and Kanao to fight instead. The clones attack the Demon Slayer duo with Doma's techniques as the real Doma starts to walk away, the clones using his Blood Demon Art: Scattering Lotuses, Frozen Lotus and Cold White Princesses attacks to hold the duo back. Now at the exit, Doma thinks about how Inosuke has managed to avoid breathing in the icy air from his techniques, and takes note of his sharp senses, saying he will make sure to remember him. He spectates their battle for a few seconds, observing how they use each technique so that he'll be able to kill them quickly the next time they fight, and then turns back towards the door. Doma decides to create three more clones to let loose around the castle in order to kill the rest of the Demon Slayers there, and overhears Kanao shouting to Inosuke that they have to hold their ground just a little longer against the crystal children. He wonders what this could mean, but then dismisses it and begins to reach for the door handle. Suddenly, Doma's face begins to melt. He drops to the floor, one of his arms snapping off, and his crystal children begin to crack and disintegrate as he wonders what's happening. Inosuke asks if it's a trap but Kanao, having been informed prior to the battle of Shinobu's plan to kill Doma, tells him that it isn't and explains that the Demon is being melted by the poison Shinobu had in her body when he consumed her. She tells Inosuke to aim for his neck to finish him off, and, in a panic, Doma plays his final and most powerful card, Blood Demon Art: Rime, Water Lily Bodhisattva. Doma's ice Bodhisattva statue slams down its hand on the floor of the room, creating a small earthquake that sends Inosuke and Kanao up into the air. Kanao notes that his technique lacks precision, and was clearly the Demon's last effort to protect himself with the little energy he had left, deciding to use her final form, Flower Breathing, Final Form: Equinoctial Vermilion Eye to try and break through him. Doma's statue grabs Inosuke in one of its hands as Kanao leaps towards the Upper Rank, hitting her blade against his neck. She is unable to cut it, so Inosuke, on the spot, comes up with and uses Beast Breathing: Sudden Throwing Strike to hurl his blades at Kanao's to give it the extra strength needed to cut Doma's neck. They succeed in beheading him, and Upper Rank 2 and his statue begin to disintegrate. After successfully defeating Doma, Kanao searches the ground for Shinobu's lost hairpin, and realizes that Kanae's has broken. She recalls that when Kanae died, she was unable to cry, but no one judged her for it. Kanao remembers how Kanae had advised her to value her comrades, and wonders if she did so correctly this time, as she cries for Shinobu. Once she finds Shinobu's hairpin, Kanae and Shinobu's spirits assure her that she has done well. Sunrise Countdown Arc. Just as the Hashiras and the other swordsmen partaking in the final battle against Muzan were on the verge of losing, Kanao, Zenitsu, and Inosuke suddenly appear in the battlefield, with Yushiro's paper talismans seen on their foreheads. Sanemi then continues with his attack, Wind Breathing, Seventh Form: Gale, Sudden Gusts, the same paper talisman on his forehead, paving a way for the other swordsmen to continue attacking. As the swordsmen continue to inflict their attacks on Muzan, Gyomei suddenly shouts about the Transparent World, to inform the other swordsmen. They then focus on what Gyomei said and realized that they were able to see the insides of Muzan's body due to their respective marks appearing all over their bodies. When, all of a sudden, Muzan inflicts a huge amount of damage to the swordsmen with his tentacle-like body parts, leaving Kanao kneeling near the demon as she cowered in fear. So, she struggled to move and stand up to end the Demon King once and for all. As she knelt on her knees, Aoi and the girls were seen in her memories, before thinking that she will beat Muzan even if she dies, comparing herself to Shinobu Kocho. A member of the Kakushi abruptly appears, running towards Kanao in hopes of saving her from death, when, Tanjiro also appears, with his Hinokami Kagura, Beneficent Radiance, thus cutting Muzan's arm off, to which he regenerated with ease. Kanao then thinks of the lad, repeating his name in her thoughts, as Tanjiro appologizes for arriving late. He then ordered the nearby Kakushi who tried to save Kanao to bring her to safe grounds, to which the Kakushi readily complied. Kanao was then able to rest as Tanjiro took his turn to face Muzan in order to end him now.

Kanao Tsuyuri and Inosuke Hashibira vs Doma Kanao Tsuyuri and Inosuke Hashibira vs Doma is a battle that takes place in the Infinity Castle, between Demon Slayers Kanao Tsuyuri and Inosuke Hashibira and Upper Rank Two Doma. It occurs immediately after Shinobu Kocho's duel against Doma. Prologue. As Shinobu is being absorbed by Doma, Kanao Tsuyuri arrives at the scene, and Shinobu manages to signal to her Tsuguko with her hand. Her death causes Kanao to go berserk in order to try and save her, only to be repelled by an irritated Doma, who tells her not to interfere when he's in the middle of absorbing someone. He successfully devours Shinobu's body until her butterfly-shaped hair piece is the only thing left of her. Doma notes aloud that Kanao must have been told something by the signal her master gave her, wondering what she could have told her, as Kanao stands silently before him. Shortly after, after Akaza's death, Doma begins to cry for his lost 'friend', but Kanao just tells him to stop it with the lies. She continuously insults him until the Upper Rank's face turns serious. Battle. Suddenly, Doma appears behind Kanao, attempting to use one of his fans to cut her head, but she quickly dodges and delivers a blow to his stomach, causing some of his organs to fall out. He doesn't seem to feel her blow, simply sending some of his ice lotuses at her and noting that her reaction speed has risen as she's able to adapt to his attacks. As he regenerates his body, he thinks to himself that Kanao could actually be little more skilled than Shinobu. Trying to suppress her rage, Kanao attacks Doma with the Flower Breathing, Fifth Form: Peonies of Futility, which he avoids with ease, smiling and commenting on how pretty her attack is before sending his Blood Demon Art: Barren Hanging Garden at her, which she barely fends off with the Flower Breathing, Second Form: Honorable Shadow Plum. Doma notices that she is only able to counter and dodge his attacks because of her sharp eyes, since she takes note of the subtle movements of his shoulders, gaze, toes, elbows and knees to predict what he'll do next, and decides it's best to prevent this by taking her eyes out with a swing of his fans. Kanao dodges, and charges at him with Flower Breathing, Sixth Form: Whirling Peach which is nullified by Doma's next Blood Demon Art: Freezing Clouds. The Upper Rank sends two more attacks, Lotus Vines and Cold White Princesses, her way, which she only just avoids before his Wintry Icicles begin to rain on her from above. Kanao dodges again, moving farther away from the Demon, who laughs at her and says that she can't keep moving backwards if she wants to cut off his head. At a speed too quick for the eye to process, Doma runs at Kanao and snatches her blade, returning and planting it in the ground a distance away from her. He says she better come and get it quickly if she wants to survive against him, before sending his Scattering Lotuses at the Demon Slayer. At that moment, Inosuke breaks through the ceiling of the room, protecting Kanao from Doma's attack with his Beast Breathing, Fifth Fang: Crazy Cutting. He looks at Doma's eyes and notices that he's Upper Rank Two, which he screams out, happily shouting that if he beats the Demon he'll become a Hashira and asking Kanao what his Hashira title should be. Inosuke notices Kanao's injuries and asks what happened, saying that Shinobu would be mad if she found out she was injured, and Doma explains that Shinobu is dead because he has absorbed her. Enraged, Inosuke rushes towards the Upper Rank with his Beast Breathing, Fourth Fang: Slice 'n' Dice. Kanao shouts out a warning to him not to breathe in Doma's cold air as the Demon remarks on how messed-up his technique is. Doma attempts to slice off Inosuke's head with one of his fans, but the Demon Slayer flips away from him, launching himself from the flat edge of the fan and landing next to Kanao. He hands her her blade, which he had taken back from Doma, and tells her never to let go of it again. Doma smiles and compliments Inosuke's speed as he jumps towards him, and the two swiftly engage in quick combat, launching Breathing Styles and Blood Demon Arts at each other at alarming rates. Inosuke kicks Doma in the stomach, sending him skidding backwards as he dislocates the joints in his right arm and prepares to swing his sword at the Upper Rank's neck. He misjudges his swing and instead slices through Doma's eyes with his Beast Breathing, Ninth Fang: Extending Bendy Slash, and the Demon laughs at his unusual technique as his joints relocate. Doma calls Inosuke messed-up and says that he's never met a kid like him before despite his long lifespan, to which the Demon Slayer replies that that's obvious, since he is the great Inosuke. At an incredible speed, Doma lurches forward and snatches his mask from his head as he's speaking, and Inosuke, enraged, yells at him to give it back. The Demon notices his face, and says he remembers Inosuke from somewhere, asking him if they'd met before. Inosuke denies this, but Doma remembers his interactions with Kotoha Hashibira, Inosuke's mother, and, after evading a Beast Breathing, Sixth Fang: Palisade Bite attack from Inosuke by slashing his chest, explains to her son that he killed her. Doma calls Kotoha stupid and unfortunate, saying that there wasn't a happy moment in her life, and Inosuke, having remembered this story and now enraged, thanks Doma for allowing him to remember this story and promises to not only to kill him for what he did to Kotoha and Shinobu, but to put him through hell beforehand. The Demon sends his Blood Demon Art: Freezing Clouds at Inosuke, which he blows away with Beast Breathing, Tenth Fang: Whirling Fangs as Kanao prepares to use another Flower Breathing Form to attack him from behind. Doma bats her away with one of his fans and moves away, and Inosuke yells at him to get back down so they can continue fighting. He replies that he can't, since Akaza has been defeated and he doesn't have time to play anymore, and uses his Blood Demon Art: Crystalline Divine Child to create smaller clones of himself for Inosuke and Kanao to fight instead. The clones attack the Demon Slayer duo with Doma's techniques as the real Doma starts to walk away, the clones using his Scattering Lotuses, Frozen Lotus and Cold White Princesses attacks to hold the duo back. Now at the exit, Doma decides to create three more clones to let loose around the castle in order to kill the rest of the Demon Slayers there, and overhears Kanao shouting to Inosuke that they have to hold their ground just a little longer against the crystal children. He wonders what this could mean, but then dismisses it and begins to reach for the door handle. Suddenly, Doma's face begins to melt. He drops to the floor, one of his arms snapping off, and his crystal children begin to crack and disintegrate as he wonders what's happening. Inosuke asks if it's a trap but Kanao, having been informed prior to the battle of Shinobu's plan to kill Doma, tells him that it isn't, and that the Demon is being melted by the poison Shinobu had in her body when he consumed her. She tells Inosuke to aim for his neck to finish him off, and, in a panic, Doma plays his final and most powerful card, Blood Demon Art: Rime - Water Lily Bodhisattva. Doma's ice Bodhisattva statue slams down its hand on the floor of the room, creating a small earthquake that sends Inosuke and Kanao up into the air. Kanao notes that his technique lacks precision, and was clearly the Demon's last effort to protect himself with the little energy he had left, deciding to use Flower Breathing, Final Form: Equinoctial Vermilion Eye to try and break through him. Doma's statue grabs Inosuke in one of its hands as Kanao leaps towards the Upper Rank, hitting her blade against his neck. She is unable to cut it because she got frozen, so Inosuke, on the spot, comes up with and uses Beast Breathing: Sudden Throwing Strike to hurl his blades at Kanao's to give it the extra strength needed to cut Doma's neck. They succeed in beheading him, and Upper Rank Two and his statue begin to disintegrate. Aftermath. As his head falls to the floor, Doma thinks about how pathetic he must be to have lost to a poisoner like Shinobu, someone who didn't even have the strength to kill a Demon by cutting its head. He thinks to himself that he shouldn't give up, and that he should try and regenerate his head like Muzan can and Akaza almost did, but soon comes to realize that that would be futile, and that he is going to die. In his final moments, Doma says that he is not afraid of death or even frustrated that he lost, and recalls his past as a human and his inability to feel any emotion.

Kanata Kamado is the great-great-grandson of Tanjiro Kamado and Kanao Tsuyuri, and the older brother of Sumihiko Kamado. He is a teenage student currently going to the same school as his brother and Toko and Yoshiteru Agatsuma. Appearance. Kanata is a young man of reasonable height with short black hair, cut into a neat fringe that hangs over his forehead. His eyes are gentle and of a dark violet color with paler rings of lavender around their edges, and he's usually seen with an expressionless face. Overall, his appearance bears a strong resemblance to that of his ancestor Kanao Tsuyuri. Kanata wears his high school's uniform, consisting of a pale blue dress shirt with a sleeveless, white v-neck cardigan worn over the top, and plain black pants. He wears a black necktie, as well as a pair of dark brown dress shoes and a watch with a white band on his left wrist. Personality. Kanata takes after Kanao in terms of personality as well as appearance, as he is often seen with a blank expression and communicates with most everyone in a monotonous manner. He is said to say whatever is in his mind right away. Kanata also appears to be rather mathematical, as he accurately counted and recalled the amount of times he told his brother to wake up. However, it's shown that he'll drop this personality when around Toko Agatsuma, as he's seen smiling at her and calling her cute when they meet up on the walk to school. Synopsis. Sunrise Countdown Arc. Kanata is first seen trying to wake up his brother, Sumihiko, so he won't be late for school. He remarks that he's told him to get up 28 times that morning, and, when a dozing Sumihiko replies that he "is" up, Kanata argues that he isn't, and tells his brother that he's an ugly sleeper. As he walks to school alongside two smaller boys who resemble Kotetsu and Kozo Kanamori, Kanata is greeted by Toko and her brother Yoshiteru Agatsuma. Kanata notices that Toko curled her hair and tells her it looks cute, leaning over to poke her cheek as they hold hands and telling her that she's the cutest girl in the world, much to the anger of Yoshiteru. The three set off, and, when asked where Sumihiko is as they pass by a kindergarten, Kanata replies that he's still asleep. Toko asks Kanata if he wants to stop by the snake-decor diner with large portion sizes the way home, to which he replies that he doesn't know if he can ever show his face there again. Toko asks why, and Kanata explains that last time they were there, Yoshiteru wouldn't stop staring at the chest of the woman who worked there, causing her husband to throw a knife at the two. Relationships. Sumihiko Kamado. Sumihiko is Kanata's younger brother. Toko Agatsuma. Kanata and Toko are on very close terms and are seen walking hand-in-hand on their way to school, with both of them becoming visibly brighter and happier when they're around each other. They are additionally distant relatives since Toko's great-grandmother was Nezuko Kamado, and Kanata's great-great-grandfather was Tanjiro Kamado. Yoshiteru Agatsuma. Although very rarely seen interacting, Yoshiteru and Kanata appear to be on good terms as it's noted that they visited a diner together, and Yoshiteru is the younger brother of Toko. Yoshiteru seems to dislike when Kanata and Toko talk to each other in a flirtatious manner, but this is likely out of jealousy rather than protectiveness for his older sister. Abilities. As a regular human, Kanata hasn't been shown to possess any form of unnatural power.

Kanata Ubuyashiki is the youngest daughter of Kagaya Ubuyashiki. She currently serves her older brother, the current head of the Ubuyashiki Household, Kiriya Ubuyashiki. Appearance. Kanata has pale, light skin and a set of large, dark eyes. Her hair is shaped into a blunt white bob haircut similar to the rest of her siblings. She adorns an elongated wisteria headpiece on the right side of her head as opposed to the left side like her brother. During the Final Selection Arc, Kanata wore a purple, flower-patterned with a dark indigo juban under it. She also sported a sheen green with a dark indigo and a plum-red tying it. During the Infinity Castle Arc, Kanata wore a purple with a white juban under it, sporting a black obi with a white obiage and a pink obijime, completely identical to her twin sister Kuina Ubuyashiki. Personality. Kanata's first appearance during the Final Selection depicts herself to be a professional, intelligent, and focused individual on her given task of explaining the proper details regarding the exam. Kanata also displays a degree of emotional aloofness when describing the fatal consequences of the exam, given the likely chances that not even half of the gathered trainees would survive the test. This indifferent attitude is also seen during the exams ending when Kanata doesn't display any form of panic, fear, or intimidation despite being manhandled and threatened by Genya Shinazugawa. However, Kanata does show a fragile side after the death of her parents and older sisters, breaking into tears when remembering them. Nonetheless, she is able to regain her composure when Kiriya reminds her to concentrate at the task at hand. History. Kanata was born to Kagaya Ubuyashiki and Amane Ubuyashiki as their youngest-born daughter of their five children, Her quintuplets siblings are Hinaki, Nichika, Kiriya and Kuina. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. Kanata appears at the Final Selection along with her brother Kiriya and explains to the recruits what awaits them at the selection. She later appears at the end of the Selection, congratulating all the survivors, and helps her brother explain how the Demon Slayer organization works. She is later hit and grabbed by Genya Shinazugawa by the hair, but is stopped by Tanjiro Kamado. Infinity Castle Arc. Kanata and Kuina help Kiriya map the Infinity Fortress. Abilities. Extraordinary Memory: During the infiltration of the Infinity Castle by the Demon Slayer Corps, Kanata displays immense skill in memorization, having successfully memorized and mapped out the fortress's constantly changing structures. She also tracks the routes and locations of every Demon Slayer and Hashira within the fortress, providing logistical support to them along with her brother and sister.

Kasugai Crow are crows that are used by the Demon Slayer Corps, primarily for communication. Each of them is assigned to a Demon Slayer Corps member. They are resposible for the deliver missions to their designated members. Description. These crows are special in that they can speak in full sentences, though their speech is very loud and limited. Most generally look and speak similarly, exceptions being Muichiro Tokito's crow, who has feminine eyelashes and can speak normally most of the time, and Zenitsu Agatsuma's Kasugai Crow, Ukogi, who is actually a sparrow instead of a crow and can't actually talk.

Kazumi was a minor character in "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". He was a villager in Northwest Town whose fiancée, Satoko, was kidnapped and eaten by the Swamp Demon. Appearance. Kazumi is a young man with dark-brown hair and brown eyes with white pupils. He wears a dull, blue with a dark-colored and light-brown . He was eventually seen with bruises in his face. Personality. Kazumi was shown to be a loving and kind person who enjoys spending time together with his fiancée. Despite his grief over her disappearance, he was shown to be quite trusting, as he believed in Tanjiro's way of trying to find Satoko. Upon learning that she was in fact dead and Tanjiro had encouraged him to move on, Kazumi became upset and asked how he could know his pain, only to quickly realize his savior did indeed endure a terrible loss as well, becoming regretful of his harsh words. Unlike most civilians, Kazumi seems to know some knowledge about demons and Demon Slayers, having heard about their existence through rumors, though he remains surprised to see them in reality. History. At some point, he met and got engaged to Satoko. Synopsis. Kidnapper's Bog Arc. Kazumi is seen walking together with his fiancée, Satoko, when she suddenly disappears. During the next day, while Kazumi is walking in town, dishevelled after a severe beating from Satoko's father, Tanjiro Kamado approaches him and asks for specifics on his situation. Kazumi shows Tanjiro the place where Satoko had disappeared, thinking he wouldn't be believed. However, Tanjiro reassures him that he does believe his word. As Tanjiro picks up the scent of the demon and runs after it, Kazumi follows, confused and later surprised, with Tanjiro's physical abilities, realizing that demons and Demon Slayers do indeed exist. Tanjiro manages to save Tokie from the demon and entrusts her to Kazumi. After Tanjiro has a brief scuffle with the demon, Kazumi demands the demon return Satoko. The demon shows his collection of hairpins from girls he had eaten and Kazumi recognizes Satoko's hairpin, realizing with despair that she was devoured. With Nezuko's help, Tanjiro is able to overwhelm and defeat the Swamp Demon. Afterward, he approaches Kazumi, still in shock with the knowledge that Satoko is dead, and tries to comfort him, saying that no matter how much loss he goes through, he must continue living. Kazumi angrily questions Tanjiro on how he could possibly understand his pain. However, through Tanjiro's continued understanding and tolerance, Kazumi realizes that he too had suffered through a terrible loss. Right before Tanjiro leaves, he gives the cloth with all of the hairpins. Kazumi takes the cloth, and apologizes for saying he hadn't suffered, while thinking to himself that Tanjiro shouldn't have had to experience such devastating loss as a young child, and notes his hardships through the scars and roughness of his hands, though he still remains impressed upon by his ever kind eyes. Entertainment District Arc. While Tanjiro battles against Upper Rank Six, Daki, Kazumi briefly appears in his memory as someone he doesn't want to go through a bad experience again as a result of demons. Abilities. As an ordinary human, he doesn't possess any additional powers or abilities.

Keizo was the owner of a martial arts dojo that taught the Soryu fighting style, and was the master of Hakuji, who would then go on to become the Upper Rank Three demon, Akaza. Appearance. Keizo was a middle-aged man with a muscular body and unshaven stubble. He kept a shoulder length black hair which was tied and his eyebrows appears to be quite bushy. Keizo wore a uniform consisting of a top and pants that is tied with a with the kanji for his fighting style at the back. Personality. Keizo was a kind and cheerful person who did his best to protect the others with his abilities, and he was optimistic and empathic enough to assign Hakuji, a former convict, to take care of his daughter, teaching him his Soryu martial arts style and ultimately welcoming him into his family by allowing him to marry Koyuki and be the next head of his dojo. His memory and instructions impacted Hakuji enough even after his transformation as a demon and the loss of his memories, especially after meeting Tanjiro Kamado who shared his same beliefs and benevolence. History. One day, Keizo saved a man from bandits, who gave him the land his dojo was on as a gift. He was married and had a daughter, Koyuki, who was ill. Because he had no students, he took on handyman jobs to make money and had to leave Koyuki's care to his wife. Eventually the stress of Koyuki's needs and the fear of seeing her child die young led his wife to drown herself. After that, he did his best to balance making money and caring for Koyuki, even though he did not believe she would live long either. While on a trip, Keizo was asked to address an aggressive youth beating up people indiscriminately. He agreed, and faced the the boy Hakuji, knocking him out easily and taking him to his dojo. Seeing potential, Keizo offered Hakuji training and lodging in exchange for taking care of Koyuki. One day, the heir to the nearby kenjutsu dojo developed an attraction to Koyuki. He acted on his feelings by dragging her out of her home for a date, but he abandoned her on the ground when she had an asthma attack. When he found out, Keizo was so upset that he arranged to have a match between the two dojos. He and Hakuji prevailed even though Keizo went easy on them, leading to the head of the dojo vowing to never again cause trouble for them. Eventually, Koyuki's health improved around the time she turned 16, at which point he offered Hakuji ownership of the dojo and Koyuki herself to take as a bride. Hakuji agreed, but left to visit his father's grave and share the good news first. However, by this point the rival dojo's head had died, and the heir who had caused so much trouble chose not to honor his father's vow of peace. While Hakuji was visiting his father, the new head and a few underlings poisoned the well Keizo and Koyuki took water from. The two unknowingly drank the poison, and upon realizing what happened, Keizo carried Koyuki to and ran to the doctor's home, unaware his daughter had already died. Being stronger than Koyuki, the poison took longer to kill him, and Keizo spent several hours suffering before he died. Synopsis. Infinity Castle Arc. Keizo appeared when Akaza faced Tanjiro Kamado; the boy's actions and personality had reminded the demon of Keizo's own righteous ideals and beliefs, causing Akaza to lash out at him for presenting a reminder of his hated past to him.Later on in the battle, Akaza is beheaded but continues to fight, all while imagining Keizo speaking to him as he attempts to kill Tanjiro and the Hashira Giyu Tomioka. Eventually, Akaza is seemingly stopped from attacking Giyu by Koyuki's spirit, causing him to relieve his past. When Akaza commits suicide by destroying his own body and ceasing his regeneration, Keizo appeared to him and told Akaza that they would never abandon him, even though he could not be in Heaven with them. Abilities. Overall Abilities. Despite being a normal human, Keizo was an exceptionally skilled martial artist, capable of defeating a group of bandits singlehandedly and knocking Hakuji, a boy of renowned skill, endurance, and violence, unconscious with a series of extremely quick punches. He was also a highly capable teacher, teaching his Soryu Style to Hakuji, who would go on to master the style and use it as the basis of his martial arts-based Blood Demon Art, Destructive Death. Physical Abilities. Peak Physical Condition: Even as a human, Keizo was very fast. able to punch Hakuji in rapid succession before the boy could even react to him. Additionally, Keizo was remarkably strong, as he could knock Hakuji unconscious for over an hour, despite Hakuji possessing enough physical stamina to endure judicial beatings severe enough to make grown men faint as an 11 year old boy. Kidnapper's Bog Arc The is the second story arc of Kimetsu no Yaiba. Synopsis. As Tanjiro begins to walk the path of the Demon Slayer, his search for the demon who murdered his family leads him to investigate the disappearances of young girls in a nearby town. With the help of Kazumi, one of the bereaved villagers, Tanjiro tracks down a morphed demon with the ability to open portals to its own hidden swamp.

Kie Kamado is a minor character in "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She was the wife of Tanjuro Kamado and the mother of Tanjiro and Nezuko Kamado. She was killed by Muzan Kibutsuji. Appearance. Kie was a woman with a noticeably light complexion, kind, dark purple eyes that appear a lighter color around the rims of their irises, and a small beauty mark located on the left of her face below her lower lip. She had black hair, worn tied back in a messy bun with a few loose strands left to dangle over her face. She wore a purple and cream checkered kimono with a white and long-sleeved over the top, she also sported a white cloth that she wears around her head, covering most of her hair. Personality. Kie was a warm and loving person; as the mother of 6 children, she was always seen displaying a very affectionate and caring personality. Since she was a single mother, Kie always tried to be as warm and kind to her children as she could to fill the gap her husband left. She was very protective of her children, but at the same time, she also taught them to be independent. Kie also demonstrated a positive and encouraging vibe, especially during her appearance in Nezuko Kamado's subconsciousness, encouraging her to wake and help her brother to fight and telling her to do her best. History. At some point in her life, Kie married Tanjuro Kamado and had their six children. After her husband’s death, she was left to take care of them by herself, managing to support and keep her whole family safe and sound through all of the hardships they endured. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. As he departs to sell charcoal in the evening, Kie stops her son, Tanjiro, and notes that his face is dirty, kneeling down to wipe off the ash from each of his cheeks and telling him that he doesn’t need to go down to the village and sell charcoal on such a snowy night. Tanjiro replies that he wants to go so everyone can eat to their heart’s content, and Kie smiles and thanks him. As her other children gather around Tanjiro, complaining that they want to go down with him, Kie told them that they can’t because they can’t walk as fast as him, and can’t be carried by cart since he isn't taking it. Kie and the rest of their family waved Tanjiro off, hoping for his safety and quick return. That night, Muzan entered her home and proceeded to inject her with his blood, hopeful that he could turn Kie into a Demon who could withstand sunlight. However, he was disappointed when Kie didn't survive, believing that creating a Demon capable of withstanding sunlight not so easy, with Nezuko unknowingly left as the only survivor but transformed into a demon. Tanjiro would later learn that the Muzan is the one to be responsible for the massacre. Mount Natagumo Arc. During her battle against Lower Rank Five Rui, Nezuko becomes trapped in his webs and loses consciousness from the blood loss. As Tanjiro nears beheading him but is at risk of sustain more fatal wounds, a vision of Kie appears beside Nezuko and tearfully begs her to wake up and save him, causing Nezuko to use her own Blood Demon Art for the first time and aid Tanjiro in beating Rui. Mugen Train Arc. While trapped in Enmu's Blood Demon Art, Tanjiro dreams he is back with his family before their deaths and his journey as a Demon Slayer. Happy to be reunited, he forgets his mission to stop Enmu. Kie asked him to fetch water but while doing so, Tanjiro realizes then that he is in a false dream. Despite longing to stay with his family, Tanjiro makes the difficult and painful choice to leave them behind, with Kie watching him leave in sadness. During his battle with Enmu, the demon forcibly puts Tanjiro inside a nightmare where his family accuses him of abandoning them to their deaths. Instead of being afraid, Tanjiro becomes enraged at his memories being manipulated and beheads Enmu, declaring they would never say such things. Entertainment District Arc. In her battle against Upper Rank Six Daki, Nezuko, now in a berserk rage following the Upper Rank's attempt to kill Tanjiro overwhelms her in battle but accidentally injures a bystander. In her frenzied state, she almost kills the innocent civillian but is stopped by Tanjiro. On Tengen Uzui's joking advice to sing a lullaby, Tanjiro sings a song that Kie used to sing to them, causing Nezuko to imagine herself and her mother on a mountain trip in the past. The memory of her mother causes Nezuko to cry and calm down, shrinking from her enhanced demon form and going to sleep to heal. Sunrise Countdown Arc. As the humanizing drug takes effect, Nezuko regains her memories and recalls the day when Muzan came to their home and attempted to transform them into demons, witnessing Kie's death.

Second Grade Fourth Grade Middle School (中等部). First Year - Autumn Leaves Class (紅葉組): Second Year - Taro Class (里芋組): Second Year - Gingko Class (銀杏組): High School (高等部). First Year - Bamboo Shoot Class (筍組): First Year - Kabosu Class (かぼす組): First Year - Hydrangea Class (紫陽花組): Second Year - Violet Class (菫組): Second Year - Persimmon Class (柿組): Second Year - Sanshō Class (山椒組): Third Year - Yomogi Class (蓬組): Third Year - Eboshi Class (烏帽子組): Third Year - Mole Class (土竜組): Staff. Due to its old age, Kimetsu Academy is known to be inhabited by ghosts, the, which are frequently spotted within the High School Department building during the night. Unlike other schools, Kimetsu Academy maintains the tradition of a night watch, where the designated High School teacher on duty is responsible for eliminating these supernatural beings upon sight. The teacher places a talisman on the yōkai's head and performs a gesture, combined with a powerful demon annihilation spell, to accomplish this task. This practice is kept from the students. Media. Kimetsu Between the Scenes! is a spin-off series from the Kimetsu no Yaiba manga written by Ryoji Hirano, based on Kimetsu no Yaiba by Koyoharu Gotoge. Description. The series is a colored, chibi version of the original series, which follows a yonkoma structure. The series was released during the original run of the anime and thus only covers the Final Selection Arc through the end of Rehabilitation Training Arc.

Kimetsu Gakuen! is a manga series written and illustrated by Natsuki Hokami, which takes place in the world of Kimetsu Academy, based on "Kimetsu no Yaiba" by Koyoharu Gotoge. It was serialized in Saikyo Jump from August 4 2021 to March 4 2024. Synopsis. This is Kimetsu Academy, a private elementary, junior high, and high school... Kimetsu no Yaiba (Anime) is the anime adaptation of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba, animated by . Its first season was announced for a 26-episode run in the 27th issue of Weekly Shonen Jump, on June 4th, 2018, and premiered on April 6th, 2019. The first 5 episodes were also seperately compiled into a Japan-exclusive movie, . The first season was followed by a continuative adaptation of the Mugen Train Arc, which would later be complied into its second season along with the Entertainment District Arc, which premiered on October 10th, 2021. Currently, Kimetsu no Yaiba can be watched on Hulu, Prime Video, Vudu, Apple TV, Netflix, and Crunchyroll. Plot. It is the Taisho Period in Japan. Tanjiro, a kindhearted boy who sells charcoal for a living, finds his family slaughtered by a demon. To make matters worse, his younger sister Nezuko, the sole survivor, has been transformed into a demon herself. Though devastated by the grim reality, Tanjiro resolves to become a "demon slayer" so that he can turn his sister back into a human, and kill the demon that massacred his family. A sorrowful tale of siblings in which the fate of humans and demons intertwine... begins now! Cast. <tabber> Japanese Cast= English Cast= </tabber> Seasons. Additional songs used:

Kimetsu no Yaiba (Manga) is a manga series written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotoge. It has been serialized in "Weekly Shonen Jump" since February 15, 2016. The series is republished in English by . The series officially ended on May 18, 2020 ("Weekly Shonen Jump" Issue #24) with a total of 205 chapters. Synopsis. Kimetsu no Yaiba is set in the Taisho era, Japan. The life of Tanjiro Kamado, a kindhearted boy who sells coal for a living, changes one day after his family is murdered by a demon. In order to turn back his sister, the only one who survived but turned into a ferocious demon herself, the two go off on a journey to seek the demon who killed their family. A tale of bloodstained swords!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 1 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the first light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. It covers chapters 1 to 28 of the manga, specifically when Tanjiro's group leaves Hisa's house. Synopsis. As long as anyone can remember, there have been rumors of man-eating demons living in the woods. Even in the more enlightened, the townspeople never go near there at night. Tanjiro Kamado, a kind boy who has been supporting his family as a coal seller since his father died, quickly learns that the local superstition is more than just rumors when he returns home one day to find his family slaughtered by demons. Only he and his sister Nezuko manage to survive, but she is transformed into a demon. Determined and resolute, he is recruited into the Demon Slayer Corps and his quest to help turn his sister human again and avenge his family's deaths begins. Differences. While the novel almost perfectly follows the plot of the manga, there are some differences:

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 10 , written by Makimi Hano, is the tenth and final light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. The battle between Muzan, the progenitor of the demons, and Tanjiro reaches the final phase...! The drug administered by the demon Tamayo, an enemy of Muzan, weakens him. What will be the fate of Tanjiro, Nezuko, and the Demon Slayer Corps...!? A battle to the death that puts everything on the line, will finally be decided! And to the future...!!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 2 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the second light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. After joining the Demon Slayer Corps, Tanjiro meets Zenitsu and Inosuke, two other rookie Demon Slayers. The three decide to work together. Their latest assignment takes them to Mount Natagumo, where they are forced to fight against the Spider Family of demons living in the mountain. But they quickly find themselves outmatched and struggling for survival. But just when things look dire, the Hashira appear!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 3 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the third light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga movie adaptation . The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. Tanjiro, along with Zenitsu, Inosuke, Nezuko, arrives at their next mission's destination, the Mugen Train, where over 40 individuals have vanished within a brief span of time. Teaming up with Kyojuro, the Flame Hashira, Tanjiro confronts the hidden demon lurking within the train. However, what awaits them is an endless dream...!?

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 4 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the fourth light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. The novel covers the second part of the Mugen Train Arc and the full Entertainment District Arc from volumes 8-11 of the original manga. Synopsis. Tanjiro and co’s next assignment takes them to the lively entertainment district in Yoshiwara, where a demon is rumored to be terrorizing the area. They are joined by the flashy Sound Hashira Tengen Uzui, and once there, each of them takes on the disguise of a courtesan in training and infiltrates a different house to gather information. But little do they know the district is ruled by a ruthless and sadistic “Fallen Princess” oiran who happens to be an Upper Rank demon in disguise!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 5 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the fifth light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. For the first time in 100 years, an Upper Rank demon is successfully defeated by Tanjiro and his friends. After the battle, Tanjiro heads to the Swordsmith Village to have his Nichirin Sword repaired after it was chipped in battle. However, another Upper Rank demon is waiting in the wings and attacks! Love Hashira, Mitsuri, and Mist Hashira, Muichiro, are also active!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 6 , written by Shuka Matsuda, is the sixth light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. The Demon Slayer Corps initiates the "Hashira Training" to bolster the skills of the Demon Slayers and to cultivate the Hashira. However, the leader of the Corps, Kagaya, is confronted by Muzan, the Demon King! Furthermore, an account of Shinobu's clash with the Twelve Kizuki member, Doma, is also documented in its entirety!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 7 , written by Makimi Hano, is the seventh light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. The Demon Slayer Corps finally entered Muzan's base, the Infinity Castle. Tanjiro and Giyu face off against Upper Rank Three demon Akaza to get revenge for Kyojuro, but find themselves outmatched by his overwhelming power. Meanwhile, Kanao and Inosuke clash with Upper Rank Two demon Doma, who attacks using sharp fans frozen in ice!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 8 , written by Makimi Hano, is the eighth light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. Inside Muzan's base, the Infinity Castle, the Demon Slayer Corps continues its battle against the Upper Rank demons. Inosuke and Kanao find themselves in a tight spot after being attacked by Upper Rank Three demon Doma’s powerful Blood Demon Art. Meanwhile elsewhere in the castle, Muichiro Tokito and Sanemi Shinazugawa take on Upper Rank One demon Kokushibo!

Kimetsu no Yaiba Novelization 9 , written by Makimi Hano, is the ninth light novel based on the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" manga. The illustrations are created by Koyoharu Gotoge. Synopsis. The Demon Slayer Corps has settled the score with the Upper Rank demons in Muzan's base, the Infinity Castle. However, within the depths of the castle, Muzan begins to stir, and finally confronts Tanjiro and the others! Meanwhile, the past of Obanai, who secretly has feelings for Mitsuri, will also be revealed...!?

Kimetsu no Yaiba Season 1 Season 1, subtitled, is the first season of the Kimetsu no Yaiba manga series' anime adaptation. It was announced for a 26-episode run in the 27th issue of Weekly Shonen Jump, on June 4th, 2018, and premiered on April 6th, 2019. The series is licensed in North America by Aniplex of America, and streams on Crunchyroll, Hulu, and FunimationNow. The series is also licensed in Australia and New Zealand by Madman Entertainment and streams on AnimeLab. In July 2019, Aniplex of America announced that an English dub of the anime was in production. The English dub, produced by Bang Zoom! Entertainment premiered on October 12th, 2019 on Adult Swim's Toonami programming block in the United States. The first season adapts the Final Selection Arc to the Rehabilitation Training Arc. All of the story arcs in this season are collectively part of the Unwavering Resolve Arc. Plot. Since ancient times, rumors have abounded of man-eating demons lurking in the woods. Because of this, the local townsfolk never venture outside at night. Legend has it that a Demon Slayer also roams the night, hunting down these bloodthirsty demons. For young Tanjiro Kamado, these rumors will soon to become his harsh reality. Ever since the death of his father, Tanjiro has taken it upon himself to support his family. Although their lives may be hardened by tragedy, they've found happiness. But that ephemeral warmth is shattered one day when Tanjiro finds his family slaughtered and the lone survivor, his sister Nezuko Kamado, turned into a demon. To his surprise, however, Nezuko still shows signs of human emotion and thought. Thus begins Tanjiro's journey to seek out the demon who killed their family and turn his sister human again. Kimetsu no Yaiba Season 2 Season 2 is the second season of Koyoharu Gotoge's Kimetsu no Yaiba by . It is a direct continuation of the first season and is split into 2 cours, respectively subtitled and to reflect the story arcs they cover. The first cour contains an extended cut of the original 2020, featuring all the movie's content in episodic format alongside brand new content made for the TV anime broadcast. The second cour is entirely new content. Plot. Following their battles on Mount Natagumo and recovery at the Butterfly Mansion, Tanjiro, Zenitsu, Inosuke, and Nezuko are tasked with aiding the investigation of the Mugen train, where over forty disappearances have occured. They join one of the most powerful swordsmen within the Demon Slayer Corps, the Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku, to face the demon aboard the Mugen train and rescue the passengers. Later, Tanjiro and company join alongside another of the Demon Slayer Corps' top ranked swordsmen, the Sound Hashira Tengen Uzui, and travel to a place where demons are said to dwell – the Yoshiwara Entertainment District – to investigate a supposed powerful demonic presence that lurks the city at night amidst bustling human activity and residence. Kirimise is a subsection of the Entertainment District located in, Japan. It is the impoverished section where poor performing, and sick courtesans live. History. Attempting to inform her husband, Hinatsuru poisoned herself in order to escape Daki's surveillance and is sent to one of the Kirimise Houses as an attempt to escape. However, Daki's obi held Hinatsuru hostage and she is left unable to escape. Synopsis. Entertainment District Arc. After interrogating the master of the Kyogoku House for her whereabouts, Tengen Uzui enters the Kirimise and is able to locate Hinatsuru, ill and still bound in obi. He cuts her free and gives her an antidote, whilst she explains why she was unable to contact him. Telling him to leave her and fight the demon, Hinatsuru is hugged by Tengen before he leaves for battle, leaving her to heal. Eventually, Hinatsuru gains enough strength to leave the Kirimise to join the battle. It is unknown whether the area was destroyed at the end of the battle, though it is very likely it was, given the immense range and power of Gyutaro's final attack.

Kiriya Ubuyashiki is the only son and middle child of Kagaya Ubuyashiki and the head of the Ubuyashiki Household. After his father's passing, he leads the Demon Slayer Corps as the 98th and final leader. Appearance. Kiriya has light, pale skin and large eyes. He has the same hairstyle as the rest of his siblings; a blunt bob with a fringe covering his eyebrows, colored black. As he was raised as a girl, he takes on a more feminine appearance during his first appearance. During the Final Selection test, Kiriya wears a purple with patterned flowers and a green, supported with a white and indigo along with a white juban under everything. His head is adorned with a wisteria headpiece. Later on in the manga, after he becomes the leader of the Demon Slayer Corps, he wears a black kimono with a long white that's reminiscent of his father. Personality. During his first appearance in the series during the Final Selection test, Kiriya portrays himself to be polite, competent, and somewhat emotionally detached having calmly and politely greeted the trainees in sync with his sister, professionally explaining the details regarding the test. He is somewhat unfazed when Genya Shinazugawa roughly manhandles his sister. Later, upon his father, mother and sisters' deaths, Kiriya shows an entirely different side to himself, displaying his capabilities as a leader. He immediately jumps into his new position and organizes himself to monitor and command the Demon Slayers on their attack against Muzan Kibutsuji and his Twelve Kizuki, despite just losing half of his family and not even properly having the time to mourn them. He shows more mental fortitude and emotional strength in comparison to his younger sisters, who momentarily broke into tears in grief. However, once his plan results in the slaughter of many Demon Slayers, Kiriya breaks under stress and stops giving orders, much to his sisters' dismay. He is able to pull himself back together after Kuina slaps him. History. Kiriya was born to Kagaya Ubuyashiki and Amane Ubuyashiki as their third child and only son of five children. He was born after his two older quintuplet sisters and before his two younger quintuplet sisters. As the sole son of the family, he becomes the male heir, the next head of the Ubuyashiki family and the first in line to inherit his father's position as commander of the Demon Slayer Corps. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. Kiriya appears along with his sister, Kanata, at the Final Selection to greet and inform the Demon Slayers in-training of what their last trial will entail.After the test concludes, Kiriya describes the ranking system of the Demon Slayer Corps and asks the survivors to pick an ore for their Nichirin Sword. Entertainment District Arc. Shortly after the battle in Yoshiwara ended with the deaths of Upper Rank demons Gyutaro and Daki, Kiriya's father Kagaya became ecstatic at the news. However, his celebration of the new turn of events was short-lived as his health began to deteriorate quickly, coughing blood as Amane rushed for her children to fetch his medication. Kiriya was summoned to help Kagaya, worriedly calling to his father as he watched him coughing more and more. Hashira Training Arc. Kiriya joined his mother and sister in leading the emergency Hashira meeting. He explained that the only swords of information regarding the marks on Muichiro Tokito and Mitsuri Kanroji were from a journal by a Demon Slayer who used the first Breathing Style. However, when Mitsuri attempted to explain how it manifested on her, it instead left Kiriya bewildered by her demonstration. Legacy. Over a century after Muzan's defeat, Kiriya is still alive and the oldest living person in Japan. This achievement caused him to be interviewed by a reporter, although he remained unresponsive due to his elderly age. The fact he lived so long is proof that the illness which previously cursed their family is now gone along with Muzan. Abilities. Extraordinary Memory: Kiriya has shown extremely good memory. He and his sisters are able to map out and memorize the nearly constantly changing Infinity Castle, creating accurate maps to navigate and guide the Hashira through it in real-time. Foresight: Similar to his father and his ancestors, Kiriya has a high, almost prophetic intuition, being able to make accurate guesses and hypotheses that were often proven right through intuition alone. Leadership Skills: Much like his father, Kiriya displays advanced skills in leading and commanding an army into battle despite his young age. He is able to immediately take command of the Demon Slayer Corps' command structure and assist the Hashira as logistical support, guiding them into battle. Longevity: Due to their relative, Muzan, becoming the first demon, men within the Ubuyashiki family were cursed with a mysterious illness, causing them to usually die in their thirties. However, after Muzan's death, the curse was seemingly lifted. In fact, Kiriya was blessed with a unusually long life, still being alive over a hundred years later and currently being the oldest living person in Japan.
