Kyojuro Rengoku/Relationships Relationships. Tanjiro Kamado. During their initial meeting at the Ubuyashiki Estate, Kyojuro develops a strong dislike for Tanjiro since he broke the Demon Slayer Corps rule of not protecting a Demon and such he rules in favor of killing Nezuko as well as in seeking punishment for Tanjiro. However, as the story progresses, he begins to take a liking towards Tanjiro after meeting him again on the Mugen train. The two boys develop a mutual respect for each other as fellow Demon Slayer Corps members, to the point where Kyojuro offers to make Tanjiro his Tsuguko. Tanjiro develops a strong admiration and affinity for Kyojuro, to the point where he calls him "Aniki" showing their brotherly bond. Just before he dies, Kyojuro entrusts his will to Tanjiro, suggesting that he had grown very fond of the young Demon Slayer for the few hours they knew each other for. Soon, Kyojuro's hilt is passed down to Tanjiro by his younger brother Senjuro. His death and final message is one of the driving forces that motivates Tanjiro to keep moving forward in his battles, remembering his words to "set your heart ablaze" in his confrontations with Daki and Muzan. Inosuke Hashibira. As with most new people he meets, Inosuke doesn't particularly like Kyojuro when they first met. He even became angry upon being given an order by him, yet was begrudgingly in awe of his power. During the battle against Akaza, Inosuke admits that Kyojuro was in a completely diferent dimension, beyond what he himself was capable of, leading him to respect the Flame Hashira. In the wake of the battle and his demise, Inosuke is the one to pick Tanjiro back up and remind him of the words Kyojuro had shared in the final moments with them before he died and the fact that the Hashira believed in them. Despite trying to encourage him to keep getting stronger, Inosuke himself uncharacteristically broke down in tears in the aftermath of his death, remaining depressed for some time. Mitsuri Kanroji. Kyojuro was Mitsuri's mentor, and the two were very close, with Mitsuri even thinking of him as an older brother. While training under him, Kyojuro was notably strict with her training but still showed patience and at times doted on her. The two of them share a gluttonous side and enjoyed snacking on their breaks. Mitsuri derived her own unique Breathing Style, Love Breathing, from his Flame Breathing. She holds extreme gratitude towards Kyojuro for his guidance and kindness. Mitsuri was greatly shocked and saddened after she heard of his death. Akaza. Kyojuro hates Akaza because of their contrasting beliefs; the Upper Rank believes that weak humans just get in the way of others and that their existences are worthless where Kyojuro believes the weak and valuable and should be protected by the strong. Akaza takes a liking to Kyojuro because he can sense that his battle spirit is strong, and offers for him to become a Demon, but Kyojuro says that he would never sacrifice the beauty of humanity for immortality. Senjuro Rengoku. Senjuro is Kyojuro's younger brother. Kyojuro cares deeply for him and fills in the role of his mentor for Flame Breathing. According to Senjuro himself, he failed to master the technique due to his lack of skills so he gave up. However, Kyojuro appears to still be proud of him. He was deeply saddened and depressed after he had heard of his death. Shinjuro Rengoku. Kyojuro's father and the former Flame Hashira. When Kyojuro was younger, he and his brother trained under their father and he described him as a passionate man. After the death of his wife and his retirement from the Demon Slayer Corp, their relationship grew distant. Even after Kyojuro succeeded him as the Flame Hashira, Shinjuro showed little care over the news and dismissed it. After his death, Shinjuro insulted his son in a drunken stupor and seemed to not care about his passing. Kyojuro on the other hand never stopped caring about him even after he became distant and his final message was for him to take care of himself and his body. After hearing this, Shinjuro came to regret his harsh words and cried in grief of his deceased son. During the final battle against Muzan, Shinjuro rejoined the Demon Slayers along with Tengen Uzui as the final line of defense protecting Kiriya Ubayashiki, vowing to not bring shame to the Rengoku family and Kyojuro's memories. Ruka Rengoku. Kyojuro's mother who passed away from an illness when he was young. As seen in his memories of her, she was very stern towards him and at the same time warm and gentle towards him. She proved to be a big influence in his overall philosophy as she explained to him that he was born strong to protect the weak, and to never use such a gift for selfish gain. She deeply loved Kyojuro as she expressed gratitude in tears that she was blessed to have him as a child, someone born both strong, kind, and gentle. Kyojuro deeply cared for and loved her in return, as her words towards him gave him the final push to hold down Akaza in a final attempt to kill him despite his grievous wounds. In his final moments, Kyojuro envisioned his mother's spirit who expressed that he did well and she was greatly proud of him, allowing him to pass on with a smile on his face. Demon Slayer Corps. Kyojuro was respected and well liked amongst all of the Hashira because of his constant positive attitude and passionate spirit. Tengen escpecially had high praise for Kyojuro, considering him a truly talented Demon Slayer unlike himself. Even Giyu, Iguro, and Sanemi, who are usually anti-social and unapproachable to most, considered him a good person and pleasant to be around. They all acknowledged his strength, responding in both shock and disbelief that he lost to an Upper Moon and were upset and saddened to hear of his death. Kagaya acknowledged him as special for not allowing even a single person to die in his mission against Enmu and the untimely arrival of Akaza and was not saddened by his passing, instead being grateful for his duties.

Kyojuro Rengoku/Synopsis History. Kyojuro was the eldest son of Shinjuro Rengoku. His father was known as the Flame Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps until his unexpected retirement. Kyojuro also had a younger brother who trained alongside him until their father ceased to teach them. His mother, Ruka Rengoku, passed away after battling an untreatable disease some time after giving birth to Senjuro. His father on the other hand became negligent and abusive, due a mixture of grief from his wife's death and disillusionment after discovering the existence of Hinokami Kagura, and it's superiority to all other breathing styles. Kyojuro was still close to his brother and helped encourage his pursuit in swordsmanship, even when his brother lacked the talent to do so. He was eventually promoted to being the Flame Hashira, like his father before him, although he reacted with nihilistic apathy. During his tenure, he trained a young, abnormally strong girl. Although the two were very fond of each other, she couldn't master Flame Breathing, instead opting to use a style derived from it, known as Love Breathing. He also encountered a demon who was part of the Twelve Kizuki, Lower Rank 2: Hairo. The demon mistook him for his father, whom he held a grudge against, but Kyojuro, with the aid of his protégée, defeated the demon. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. Kyojuro is present with his fellow Hashira when Tanjiro Kamado awakens.Shinobu Kocho notes that Tanjiro is on trial, for which Kyojuro sees no need for as he was protecting a demon, which is a clear violation of conduct; he states that it was a matter they could deal with themselves. He then agrees with Gyomei Himejima's idea to kill Nezuko Kamado, witnessing shortly afterward Tanjiro's coughing fit, and remains silent when his former student, now Love Hashira,Mitsuri Kanroji asks if they should be dealing with their subordinate's trial without Kagaya Ubuyashiki's input. After Tanjiro headbutts Sanemi Shinazugawa, Kyojuro looks at Mitsuri when she laughs with a neutral expression. Mugen Train Arc. Kyojuro is sent to investigate a series of brutal attacks plaguing a small village, believing it to be related to the incident surrounding the disappearance of forty passengers aboard the Mugen train. He meets with another Demon Slayer at a ramen shop and they discuss their next plan of action, to which he is informed the Mugen Train is being held at a maintenance facility after being put out of service. After finishing their meal, they set off to a nearby train station. They encounter a young girl, Fuku, saddened by the lack of customers buying her bento boxes as the news of the attacks is scaring everyone into staying inside after dark. Kyojuro unabashedly tells her he is looking for a demon, to which she angrily hurls her bean bun and retorts that demons don't exist. However, he is unfazed by her actions. After being calmed by her grandmother, Fuku apologizes and asks if he would like to buy some bento boxes. He happily buys them all and gives them to his companion, telling him to return to the Demon Slayer Corps. as the bentos will make great gifts. Kyojuro, carrying a crate of bento boxes, boards a train headed for maintenance, believing he will be taken to the same facility as the Mugen train. After being confronted by a train conductor and told the Mugen train's actual location, he leaps off the train and heads to the train maintenance facility. There, he sees the train and senses the faint scent of a demon, confirming a demon is responsible for the disappearances. He is met by the chief engineer, to whom Kyojuro claims he was sent to the facility to give the workers the bento boxes. As the workers eat, Kyojuro is told the train is being repaired and will be put back into service again, unnerving him. Suddenly, a scream is heard, forcing Kyojuro to confront the situation. A marked demon appears, responsible for the attacks reported, clutching a young worker in his claws and causing him to bleed heavily. Kyojuro tells the culprit to surrender him, but the demon tells him human food disgusts him now, stepping on a bento box, to which he adds that he only eats humans he find palpable and kills the ones he doesn't. The demon activates his Blood Demon Art, enabling him to speed around the Hashira and taunt him. Kyojuro acknowledges his speed but warns him to not get cocky facing him. He informs the demon the woman he attacked is slated to make a full recovery, angering him. Seeing the destroyed bento box, the demon decides to kill the bento vendors to spite Kyojuro. He tries to kill the worker, but Kyojuro slices off both his hands and forces him to retreat. After treating the boy's injuries, he is met with other demon slayers, telling them to take charge here while he confronts the demon. Kyojuro heads towards the demon's trail and follows the train tracks, using his Total Concentration Breathing to accelerate him to incredible speeds. The demon finds Fuku and tries to kill her but is momentarily distracted by Fuku's grandmother. Fuku tries to escape but he catches her outside and tries to crush her throat. Kyojuro arrives in time, slices the demon's achilles and saves Fuku. He confronts him again as he tries to kill Fuku's grandmother, repeating his words not to get cocky. The demon tries to challenge him over who is truly faster; if he is able to kill him before he kills her. To which Kyojuro responds that the challenge is unnecessary. He mocks the demon for being slow and rushes forward instantly, decapitating the unsuspecting demon with his Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire. The scene reminds Fuku's grandmother of when she herself was saved by the Flame Hashira, recognizing Kyojuro's haori and manner of sheathing his blade. To this, Kyojuro states that it was likely his father Shinjuro who saved her; he is simply following in his footsteps to save people from demons. As Kakushi arrive on the scene, Kyojuro confirms the demon is dead and the Mugen train will be repaired for service the next day. When his companion expressed relief that the situation finally over, the Hashira adds that it was likely a more powerful demon that what he just faced that is responsible for the train's disappearance. As the sun sets, Kyojuro boards the Mugen train for his investigation when he meets Fuku and her grandmother again. They offer beef pot bento boxes in gratitude for his heroic actions, to which he happily accepts and takes Fuku's entire stock. The two bid him good luck on his mission and the train leaves the station. During the journey, while devouring his eleventh bento box while shouting "delicious," Tanjiro, who was told to meet him, introduces the Hashira to Inosuke Hashibira, Zenitsu Agatsuma and Nezuko, who he recognizes during Tanjiro's trial with the Master. After he finishes his food and Tanjiro explains his question about Hinokami Kagura, Kyojuro energetically answers that he doesn't know what Hinokami Kagura is and that this is his first time hearing about it. He says that he's delighted that Tanjiro applied his father's dance to his fighting style, then swiftly changes the subject and tells Tanjiro that he should become his Tsuguko. Tanjiro tells him to slow down and asks if he can at least try and help a little more to answer his question. Kyojuro says that Flame Breathing has a long history, and says that there has always been a Hashira in every age who uses Water Breathing and one who uses Flame Breathing. He explains that the other Breathing Styles were derived from either those two or Wind Breathing, Stone or Thunder. Kyojuro then asks Tanjiro what color his Nichirin Sword is, to which the latter responds that it's black, and Kyojuro laughs out and says that that must be unfortunate. Tanjiro asks why that is, and, as the train starts to take off, Kyojuro explains that he's simply never seen a swordsman with a black blade become a Hashira before, and that he's heard people whose blades turn black don't even know which Breathing Style to master. Seeing Tanjiro's face, he tells him not to worry and that he'll train him up back at his house. The Train Conductor then comes over to the four of them to stamp their tickets. Tanjiro smells something unusual, and Kyojuro appears to sense it too as he asks the conductor to step aside, simultaneously preparing his sword. A large-bodied demon appears at the other end of the carriage, and Kyojuro wonders if it was hiding with its Blood Demon Art unbeknownst to him ,before darting forward to behead it with the Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire. The demon's dead body falls to the floor, only for Kyojuro to add that a second one is nearby, prompting Tanjiro and Inosuke to follow him. As the frightened crowd flee to another carriage, they find the demon cornering a single passenger, leading Inosuke to charge ahead and ignoring the two. When he is nearly hit by its long arms, Kyojuro rushes forward to save Inosuke and the passenger, before using his Flame Breathing, Second Form: Rising Scorching Sun to kill it. An amazed Tanjiro, Inosuke and Zenitsu all declare they would love to be his Tsuguko, leading him to laugh and state that he would gladly train them all. Sometime later, when the four are all asleep, Kyojuro dreams that he's back at his house, telling his father, Shinjuro, about his promotion to Hashira. Shinjuro dismisses him, saying it's pointless and doesn't matter because neither Kyojuro or himself will ever become great people anyway. Kyojuro gets up and walks out of the house, out into the garden, his little brother, Senjuro, coming to greet him and asking if their father was happy about the news and wondering if he would acknowledge him too if he also becomes a Hashira. Kyojuro remembers how his father used to be, a happy man who was passionate about training his children as swordsmen, and how he changed after their mother's death. He admits to his brother that Shinjuro wasn't happy to hear the news, but enthusiastically adds that his passion won't die because of that and that he'll never be disheartened. Senjuro still looks upset, but his big brother comforts him, saying Senjuro's not like him because he has an older brother to look out for him. He reassures him that whatever path he takes, he'll be a wonderful person, and, as Kyojuro hugs his brother, he tells him to do his best and keep on living, no matter what. Still within the dream, Kyojuro begins to tutor Senjuro in his sword skills. In reality, a young girl, who's working for Enmu, ties her wrist to his unconscious body with a special piece of rope that was made by the Upper Moon, allowing her to enter Kyojuro's dream. Enmu has sent her in to destroy Kyojuro's spiritual core, which, when destroyed, would render him a lifeless shell unable to put up a fight against the demon. The spiritual core lies in the area of unconsciousness just outside of Kyojuro's dream realm, and she quickly slips past him and Senjuro without either noticing. She finds his subconscious realm, which lies past the wall surrounding his garden, and breaks into it, only to find herself in an unusually hot and flame-ridden one. The girl locates his spiritual core, but, as she goes to break it, she is suddenly lifted tightly by the neck by an invisible force. On the train, Kyojuro grabs her throat but remains unconscious, his survival instinsts enabling his body to sense the threat and stop it. But with the two still unconscious, they are locked together. Tanjiro soon wakes up from the dream he was having and asks Nezuko to burn the rope connecting Kyojuro and the girl, removing the girl from the Hashira's dream. After the young Demon Slayer's confrontation with Enmu, Kyojuro too wakes up and tells Tanjiro that he, Zenitsu and Nezuko will defend the eight train cars from the demon while Tanjiro and Inosuke go down to the front of the train to defeat him.After Tanjiro and Inosuke have successfully defeated Enmu and escaped the out of control demon train with Nezuko, Zenitsu and Kyojuro, the Hashira checks on an injured Tanjiro as Inosuke goes to rescue another passenger. He applauds the young Demon Slayer for his recently-acquired ability to use Total Concentration Breathing all the time, and says that this is the first step to him becoming a Hashira.Kyojuro then notices that Tanjiro is bleeding from the abdomen and tells him to focus his breathing in order to heal himself, which the young Demon Slayer manages with some guidance from Kyojuro. The Flame Hashira tells Tanjiro that if he can master his breathing, he'll be able to accomplish many more things and become stronger tomorrow than he was yesterday. Just as Kyojuro starts to tell Tanjiro that he doesn't need to push himself any further because everyone's been saved, something jumps down just behind the two Demon Slayers with a great force, scattering the dust around them. The dust clears to reveal Upper Rank Three, who immediately launches himself towards Tanjiro with the intention of killing him, but is stopped by Kyojuro's Flame Breathing, Second Form: Rising Scorching Sun attack, causing him to leap backwards, away from the Demon Slayers. The demon immediately regenerates his injuries and compliments Kyojuro's katana. The Hashira asks him why he was targeting an injured person, to which the Upper Rank says that he thought Tanjiro would get in the way. Kyojuro asks if they have any business together and that he already hates the demon, despite it being their first time meeting, and the demon says that he hates weak humans too. The Upper Rank then asks Kyojuro if he wants to be a demon too. Kyojuro swiftly declines, but the Upper Rank persists. Kyojuro says that he is the Flame Hashira, Kyojuro Rengoku, and the demon introduces himself as Akaza. Akaza keeps persisting, saying that Kyojuro would have more time to get stronger as a demon than a human since he wouldn't have to worry about death.Kyojuro says that dying is the very beauty of being human, and that he thinks it is the reason that humans are so unique and precious. He says that Akaza shouldn't insult Tanjiro and that he is not weak, and then says that he will never become a demon. As he begins to use Technique Development, Destructive Death: Compass Needle, Akaza says that he will just kill Kyojuro if he won't become a demon. He attacks Kyojuro as the Hashira runs towards him with his Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire attack readied. Akaza jumps back, and says that none of the Hashira he's killed have ever agreed to his invitation to become a demon and that he finds that hard to understand. He tells Kyojuro to die now, while he's young and strong. Akaza unleashes Destructive Death, Air Type, which Kyojuro counters with Flame Breathing, Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation. The Hashira notes that Akaza is attacking him from a distance, punching into the air and moving at a fraction of a blink, and realizes that he'll have to get closer to him if he's to defeat him. Kyojuro suddenly appears in front of Akaza, who compliments his reaction speed as the Hashira attacks him with his flames. The Upper Rank praises his sword skills, and wonders to Kyojuro how sad it'll be if they're lost early, to which the Hashira replies that it won't be sad because it's only natural for people to die. Tanjiro begins to get up, wanting to help the Hashira out, but Kyojuro tells him to stay where he is, because his wound could be fatal if reopened. Akaza tells him not to take notice of "the weaklings" and to focus on who he's fighting and Kyojuro, angered, attacks the demon with Flame Breathing, Fifth Form: Flame Tiger as Akaza unleashes his Destructive Death, Disorder. The residue stirred by their attacks clears, and Akaza tells Kyojuro, who's now bloodied and beaten, not to die on him just yet. Tanjiro and Inosuke panic, the latter wanting to jump in to help Kyojuro but soon realizing that he'd only be a hindrance, as the Hashira and Upper Rank seem to be in an entirely different dimension to him. Akaza says that Kyojuro fighting with his body is pointless since he can't heal his wounds instantly like a demon, and that humans will never be able to defeat demons. Tanjiro tries to pick himself up to go and help Kyojuro, but is unable to generate any strength into his limbs because of the aftermath of the Hinokami Kagura, which he used to defeat Enmu. Kyojuro turns back to face Akaza, smiling and saying that he'll fulfil his duties before beginning to ready another attack. Impressed, Akaza compliments his fighting spirit and technique, and laughs as he says that Kyojuro really should've chosen to become a demon, asking the Hashira to fight with him for all eternity. The two clash again, Flame Breathing: Ninth Form - Rengoku meeting Destructive Death: Annihilation Type, and the dust this time disperses to reveal that Akaza has stuck his arm through Kyojuro's stomach. Akaza screams that he's going to die, and asks Kyojuro one more time to become a demon. This causes Kyojuro to remember his mother, Ruka, and a flashback shows one of their final moments together. Ruka asks a younger Kyojuro if he knows why he was born stronger than other people, and asks him to think hard about this question. Kyojuro ponders this for a while, then barks out that he doesn't know the answer. Ruka explains that he was given such strength to protect the weak, and that power should be used for the world and for the people, not for abusing it in order to hurt others. Ruka hugs Kyojuro to her chest and, as she begins to cry, tells him that, even though she won't be alive much longer, it was a blessing for her to have been the mother of such a strong, gentle child. Now back in the present, as he summons the last of his strength to swing his sword into Akaza's neck, Kyojuro thanks Ruka as well for being his mother. Kyojuro lets out a shout as he drives his sword deeper in, and, as Akaza tries to hit him with a punch to the face, the Hashira grabs his wrist and stops the attack before it reaches him. Akaza is incredibly impressed by Kyojuro's strength, and then he looks behind Kyojuro and begins to panic as he realizes that the sun is about to come up. Akaza tries to free himself from Kyojuro's hold, but the Hashira holds on tightly to his wrist, not letting him escape. Tanjiro finally finds the strength to pick up his sword, and starts to run over towards the pair with the intention of dealing the finishing blow to Akaza. With a loud shout of effort, Akaza tries again to pull himself away from Kyojuro, but he fails again as Kyojuro's blade moves deeper into Akaza's neck. Tanjiro yells to Inosuke to move for Kyojuro's sake, and, just as the boar-headed Demon Slayer readies his Beast Breathing: First Fang - Pierce, Akaza manages to pull himself away from Kyojuro. The Upper Rank quickly jumps backwards, both of his arms now severed, and runs into the forest beside where they'd been fighting, leaving Kyojuro to fall onto his knees, defeated.As the demon retreats, Tanjiro throws his sword at Akaza, screaming at him not to run away from the fight and calling him a coward. The young Demon Slayer yells that Kyojuro is better than Akaza will ever be because he fought until the end and didn't let anyone die, and that Kyojuro was the rightful winner of their fight. Tanjiro lets out a final scream and collapses to his knees, crying, and Inosuke starts to shake. Kyojuro looks over at him and smiles, telling Tanjiro to come over to him so they can have a final chat before he dies.Kyojuro tells Tanjiro that he should try to visit Rengoku House if he wants to learn more about Hinokami Kagura, since he remembered that his father had some notes that had been left behind by the Flame Hashira who came before he and his son. Tanjiro tells Kyojuro that that's enough, and asks him if there's any way for him to recover from the injuries Akaza inflicted on him, to which he says there isn't and asks Tanjiro to hear him out while he can still talk. Kyojuro asks him to tell his little brother Senjuro that he should proceed down the path his heart tells him to, the one he thinks is right, and to tell his father to take care of himself. He then looks Tanjiro in the eye and tells him that he believes in Nezuko, and fully accepts her as a member of the Demon Slayer Corps after seeing her protect so many humans on the Mugen train. Kyojuro tells Tanjiro to live with his head held high and that he shouldn't worry about him dying here, since it's only natural for a Hashira to give his life protecting his junior. He looks to Tanjiro, then to Inosuke and to Zenitsu, and says that he believes in them and that he thinks they will become the next generation of Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps.The Flame Hashira then sees the spirit of his mother in front of him, and asks her if he did well, to which she replies that he did a wonderful job. As the last seconds of his life slip away, Kyojuro smiles. Legacy. Kyojuro's colleagues were very fond of him and as such were deeply troubled by his death. He would not be forgotten though, as the late swordman would be remembered by Sound Hashira Tengen Uzui during his fight with Upper Six, Gyutaro, and Mist Hashira Muichiro Tokito after defeating Upper Five, Gyokko. In addition, his young protégée, Tanjiro Kamado, would be particularly devastated by the loss of his mentor and friend, becoming catatonic for months, and even going as far to begin to wish that he had died instead of Kyojuro. His younger brother Senjuro reacted with grief when the news reached him. However, when Tanjiro visited the Rengoku household to read the notes Shinjuro Rengoku kept, the jaded former Hashira drunkenly insulted his deceased son and claimed that his death was due to a lack of worth and talent. After a physical altercation with the boy, Shinjuro was given his elder son's final words to him by his remaining son. Not being able to hide behind his wall of denial and apathy anymore, Kyojuro's father broke down in tears, a starting point for the man to finally turn his life around. Tanjiro would adopt his sword guard and use it for his newest sword. Before it was attached however, it ended up saving a young boy's life by protecting him from a near-fatal laceration from a fish demon that Gyokko summoned. When Tanjiro once again encountered Akaza, alongside the Water Hashira, Giyu Tomioka, Kyojuro was brought up several times by the Upper Rank demon. Akaza, now witnessing Tanjiro's newfound strength, claimed to have now understood what Kyojuro meant by rebuking the claim that he was weak, and later went on to say that he was glad Kyojuro had died because of his foolish mindset and believed that he wouldn't have gotten any stronger. Tanjiro was infuriated at what he perceived as an insult to his late mentor, but Akaza claimed that he was actually praising him. Later on, when Tanjiro was turned into a demon after the defeat of the Demon King, Muzan Kibutsuji, he was among the many hands to pushed him back towards being a human alongside many of his colleagues whom had also fallen in battle, when the spirit of Muzan attempted to sabotage the serum administered to cure Tanjiro's condition. Several years into the future, Tanjiro's final sword, still donning Kyojuro's tsuba, would be hung in the Kamado household as an antique.

Kyojuro Rengoku vs Akaza Kyojuro Rengoku vs Akaza was a battle that took place outside the destroyed Mugen Train. It focuses on the battle between the Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku against Upper Rank Three Akaza. Prologue. After Tanjiro Kamado and Inosuke Hashibira have successfully defeated Enmu and escaped the out of controlled demon train with Nezuko Kamado, Zenitsu Agatsuma and Kyojuro, the Flame Hashira checks on an injured Tanjiro as Inosuke goes to rescue another passenger. He applauds the young Demon Slayer for his recently-acquired ability to use the, and says that this is the first step to him becoming a Hashira. Kyojuro then notices that Tanjiro is bleeding from the abdomen and tells him to focus his breathing in order to heal himself, which the young Demon Slayer manages with some guidance from Kyojuro. The Flame Hashira tells Tanjiro that if he can master his breathing, he'll be able to accomplish many more things and become stronger tomorrow than he was yesterday. Just as Kyojuro starts to tell Tanjiro that he doesn't need to push himself any further because everyone's been saved, something jumps down just behind the two Demon Slayers with a great force, scattering the dust around them. Battle. The dust clears to a strange human figure with glowing eyes to which Tanjiro looks at and sees the specific kanji in his irises revealing it to be Upper Rank Three, deeply horrifying him. He then becomes perplexed as to why an Upper Rank would be here of all places. Before adding on to his confusion, the Upper Rank almost instantaneously dashes towards Tanjiro swinging his fist to crush his skull. Kyojuro quickly uses Flame Breathing, Second Form: Rising Scorching Sun, which cuts the demon's arm in half and causes him to leap backwards, away from the Demon Slayers. The demon immediately heals his arm and compliments Kyojuro's Nichirin Blade while licking the blood off his own arm, whom the latter then asks him why he was targeting an injured person. The Upper Rank says that he just thought Tanjiro would get in the way between himself and Kyojuro, to which the latter responds by asking if they had something to talk about and saying that he despises him despite it being their first time meeting. As he smiles, the Upper Rank says that he hates weak humans too and that they disgust him. Kyojuro responds that the two appear to have practically complete opposite moral values, and the Upper Rank then asks if Kyojuro would like to become a demon himself.Kyojuro immediately declines, but the Upper Rank doesn't back off, saying that he knows the Hashira's strength just by looking at him and that he's getting close to "supreme territory". Kyojuro says that he is the Flame Hashira, Kyojuro Rengoku, and the demon introduces himself as Akaza. The Upper Rank then goes on to explain that, despite him being so close to it, Kyojuro will never reach supreme territory because he'll just grow old and die before it can happen. Akaza says that if he becomes a demon, Kyojuro can keep training for hundreds of years to become even stronger than he is right now.Kyojuro says that growing old and dying is the very beauty of being human, going on to explain that people are only lovable and precious because of this aspect. What humans call strength, the Hashira says, isn't a word that they use in regards to the body, and that Tanjiro is not weak and should not be insulted by Akaza. Kyojuro looks the Upper Rank in the eyes and tells him that he will never ever become a demon, no matter the explanation. Disappointed, the Upper Rank begins to use his Technique Development, Destructive Death: Compass Needle, Akaza simply declaring that he will just kill Kyojuro if he won't become a demon. He quickly dashes towards Kyojuro and the Hashira returns his advance, readying the Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire attack, and Tanjiro notes that they're moving so fast that he can't follow them with his eyes only seeing sparks in the process. They clash, and Akaza leaps up in the air, saying that none of the Hashira he's killed so far used Flame Breathing and that none of them ever agreed to his invitation to become a demon. Akaza says that he finds them hard to understand, especially since only those who are chosen get to become demons. The Upper Rank says he is saddened by the thought of the decline of someone wonderfully talented, and tells Kyojuro to die now, while he's young and strong. Being launched into the air and upside-down, Akaza unleashes his Destructive Death: Air Type, which Kyojuro counters with the Flame Breathing, Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation. The Hashira notes that Akaza is attacking him from a distance, punching into the air and moving at a fraction of a blink, and realizes that he'll have to get closer to him if he's to defeat the demon. Kyojuro suddenly appears in front of Akaza, who compliments his reaction speed as the Hashira attacks him with his flames. The two exchange blows with each other on equal ground. The Upper Rank praises Kyojuro’s sword skills, and wonders to him how sad it'll be if they're lost early, to which the Hashira replies that it won't be sad because it's only natural for people to die. Inosuke arrives and Tanjiro begins to get up, wanting to help the Hashira out, but Kyojuro tells him to stay where he is, because his wound could be fatal if reopened. Akaza tells him not to bat an eye at "the weaklings" and to focus on who he's fighting and Kyojuro, angered, uses his blade to launch Akaza into a nearby forest then proceeds to run inside to finish him off. To his surprise, Akaza ambushes him from below, complimenting his exceptional movements. Kyojuro immediately dodges his attack and cuts of his arm, but Akaza retaliates by using his legs to launch him outside the forest. Tanjiro and Inosuke call out to him, worriedly as Kyojuro, slightly enervated stumbles to get up. Akaza regenerates his lost arm and tells him to continue fighting and says that he has no other option. Which Kyojuro unhesitantly refuses and reiterates his hatred towards him. Kyojuro then dashes toward Akaza and performs the Flame Breathing, Third Form: Blazing Universe, which creates a shallow wound near Akaza's shoulder which he heals instantly while expressing his amazement over Kyojuro's beautiful attack. Akaza unleashes his Destructive Death: Air Type technique which Kyojuro barely blocks the shockwave and flies backward, then dashes towards him and continues his assault. Inosuke looks on in amazement and horror, remarking that even if he wanted to help we would only be a hindrance, and that only death awaits if he even tries to approach them, as both seem like they're in a completely separate dimension. As both the Hashira and Upper Rank continue to exchange blows, Akaza queried whether Kyojuro is certain in continuing to fight him, as it might spell his end. Kyojuro ignores his banter and continues to attack but gets countered by Akaza's fist which creates a shallow cut on the left side of his forehead. Kyojuro backs up momentarily then proceeds to use the Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire which severs both of Akaza's arms which regenerates almost instantly. He then calmly remarks that it would be a pity to kill Kyojuro right then as he hasn't reached his full potential yet. Akaza suddenly dashes forwards and punches Kyojuro's guts, which causes it to bleed. Kyojuro coughs out saliva and vomit but remains steadfast and performs the Flame Breathing, Second Form: Rising Scorching Sun. Akaza dodges his technique and attempts to attack Kyojuro while he barely manages to parry all his blows with his katana. While preparing to attack Kyojuro with a stronger attack, Akaza continues to convince him to become a demon, saying that in one or two years his strength and power would be able to grow exponentially. Akaza attempts to attack Kyojuro with a strength-enhanced strike, to which Kyojuro barely blocks his attack. However, Akaza's strength was able to overwhelm Kyojuro and crush his eye with his fists. Kyojuro stumbles back but continues to grit his teeth in the onslaught he is facing and uses both his Flame Breathing, Third Form: Blazing Universe and the Flame Breathing, Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation. Akaza dodges both attacks and takes his stance while Kyojuro does the same, both then proceed to unleash different techniques, the former using his Destructive Death: Disorder attack while the latter using the Flame Breathing, Fifth Form: Flame Tiger. Both close in on each other and Kyojuro manages to cut of Akaza's arm and cause a shallow cut on his chest. The residue of their attacks clear, and Akaza tells Kyojuro, who's now bloodied and beaten, having lost the functionality of his left eye, not to die on him just yet. Tanjiro and Inosuke panic, the latter wanting to jump in to help Kyojuro but soon realizing that he'd only be a hindrance, as the Hashira and Upper Rank seem to be in an entirely different dimension to him. Akaza says that Kyojuro fighting with the intention of sacrificing his body is pointless, showing him that the injuries he'd inflicted on him had already completely healed and comparing this to the severe wounds that now covered Kyojuro. He explains that Kyojuro can't recover from this anymore as he is, but could regenerate himself in the blink of an eye if he was a demon. Akaza says to an exhausted Kyojuro that humans will never be able to beat demons. Tanjiro tries to pick himself up to go and help Kyojuro, but is unable to generate any strength into his limbs because of the aftermath of him forcefully switching from the Water Breathing to the Hinokami Kagura, which he used to defeat Enmu. Kyojuro turns back to face Akaza, still smiling and saying that he'll fulfill his duties before beginning to ready another attack. Impressed, Akaza compliments his fighting spirit and technique, and laughs as he says that Kyojuro really should've chosen to become a demon, asking the Hashira to fight with him for all eternity. Kyojuro commands himself to set his heart ablaze and burn beyond his limits. With that, he proudly proclaims his identity as the Flame Hashira as he readies his family's most powerful Breathing technique, Flame Breathing, Esoteric Art: Ninth Form, Rengoku. Akaza also readies his Destructive Death: Annihilation Type. The two techniques clash head-on, only this time, when the dust disperses, it is revealed that Akaza has impaled his arm through Kyojuro's solar plexus. Akaza screams that the Hashira going to die, and asks Kyojuro one more time to tell the Upper Rank that he'll become a demon, saying that he is one of the chosen ones. This causes Kyojuro to remember his mother, Ruka Rengoku, and a flashback shows one of their final moments together. Ruka asks a younger Kyojuro to think hard about what she's about to ask him, then presenting him with the question of whether or not he knows why he was born stronger than other people. Kyojuro ponders this for a while, then barks out that he doesn't know the answer. Ruka explains that he was given such strength to protect the weak, and that power should be used for the world and for the people, not for abusing it in order to hurt others. She says that it is the obligation of those born strong to protect those who are weak, and tells Kyojuro never to forget that. Ruka hugs Kyojuro to her chest and, as she begins to cry, tells him that, even though she won't be alive much longer, it was a blessing for her to have been the mother of such a strong, gentle child. Now back in the present, as he summons the last of his strength to swing his sword into Akaza's neck, Kyojuro thanks Ruka as well, saying it was an honor for him to have had her as his mother. Kyojuro lets out a shout as he drives his sword deeper in, and, as Akaza tries to hit him with a punch to the face, the Hashira grabs his wrist and stops the attack before it reaches him. Akaza is incredibly impressed by Kyojuro's strength, as he still managed to stop the demon's attack while his fist was stuck right through his solar plexus. He then looks behind Kyojuro, and begins to panic as he realizes that the sun is about to come up. Akaza tries to free himself from Kyojuro's hold, but the Hashira holds on tightly to his wrist, not wanting to let him escape.Tanjiro finally finds the strength to pick up his sword, and starts to run over towards the pair with the intention of dealing the finishing blow to Akaza. With a loud shout of effort, Akaza tries again to pull himself away from Kyojuro, but the grip of the Hashira, determined, remains firmly around his wrist. Kyojuro's blade moves deeper into Akaza's neck, now reaching its center. Tanjiro yells to Inosuke to move for Kyojuro's sake, and, just as the boar-headed Demon Slayer readies his Beast Breathing, First Fang: Pierce, Akaza manages to pull himself away from Kyojuro, stomping the ground to form shockwaves that stop Inosuke and Tanjiro. The Upper Rank quickly jumps backwards, healing his hand to shield his face from the sun, and runs into the forest beside where they'd been fighting, leaving Kyojuro to fall onto his knees, defeated. Aftermath. As the demon retreats, Tanjiro throws his sword at Akaza, screaming at him not to run away from the fight and calling him a coward. The insult angers Akaza, questioning whether Tanjiro has a brain and thinking to himself that he was not running from Tanjiro but the sun and that the battle is already decided given Kyojuro's wound as he completes his escape into the forest's shadows. The young Demon Slayer yells that Kyojuro is better than Akaza will ever be because he fought until the end and didn't let anyone die, and that Kyojuro was the rightful winner of their fight. Tanjiro lets out a final scream and collapses to his knees, crying, and Inosuke starts to shake. Kyojuro looks over at him and smiles, telling Tanjiro to come over to him so they can have a final chat before he dies.

Kyojuro Rengoku vs Hairo Kyojuro Rengoku vs Hairo was a battle that took place in a city within Tokyo, Japan. It focuses on the battle between Kinoe-ranked Demon Slayer Kyojuro Rengoku against Lower Rank Two Hairo. Prologue. Hairo, Lower Rank Two of the Twelve Kizuki, is haunted by a traumatic encounter with the Flame Hashira, Shinjuro Rengoku. Consumed and driven mad with revenge, Hairo launches a plan to attack the city of Tokyo, an area in the jurisdiction of the Flame Hashira, in the hopes of getting his tormenter's attention and a chance to finally rid his life of his source of pain. After Shinjuro refuses to perform his duties as Hashira, Kinoe-ranked Kyojuro Rengoku offers to take his place. During the Hashira meeting he is supposed to attend, despite the doubts of the Hashiras present, including Tengen Uzui and Sanemi Shinazugawa, Demon Slayer Corps leader Kagaya Ubuyashiki expresses his faith in the young man, acknowledging that he knows the process of becoming a Hashira. Assigning him to a mission in Tokyo, due to reports that a demon, potentially one of the Twelve Kizuki, is lurking within the city, Kagaya tells Kyojuro to prove his worth and become the Flame Hashira. Partnered with newly officiated Corps member Mitsuri Kanroji and a squadron of more Demon Slayers, Kyojuro sets off to Tokyo to find the demon. He orders them to split up, assigning the squad to investigate one half of the city, while he and Mitsuri survey the other. Battle. While scouring Tokyo for a potential demonic presence, a timed bomb explodes within a building very close to Kyojuro and Mitsuri's position. A second explosion follows near the squadron of Demon Slayers. Suddenly, Mitsuri narrow misses getting shot from a rifle as she attempts to run and help, the rifle being in the hands of Hairo. Hairo spots who he believes is the Flame Hashira and attempts to shoot him, but finds he has suddenly vanished in the moment. Kyojuro appears before the demon and uses Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire to slash at him. Hairo addresses the young man as Rengoku and tells him he will have his revenge. Kyojuro recognizes the kanji in Hairo's eye as the mark of Lower Rank Two, realizing that by killing him, he will become the Flame Hashira. He denounces the demon's attack against innocent lives as unforgivable, but Lower Two instead tells Kyojuro he had never forgotten him, preparing to exact vengeance. Stunned by the threat, Kyojuro brushes aside his supposed association with him and tells the demon he does not know who he is. The angered Hairo then shoots himself in the mouth, confusing the Kinoe. Another explosion shakes the city behind the Demon Slayer, but as he turns to see the blast, Kyojuro is struck by numerous bullets from an array of rifles and pistols within Hairo, though the bullets hit his blade and miss his body. Kyojuro runs behind cover but a shadowy portal appears before his feet, and more rifles emerge to fire at him. Using Flame Breathing, Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation, he destroys the weapons and attacks Hairo directly. Hairo fires a rifle at Kyojuro but only grazes his cheek as he slashes into his neck. To his shock, the katana does not cut through, trapped within Hairo's shadowy aura, prompting Hairo to taunt Kyojuro for his short-sightedness. Lit sticks of dynamite then manifest from the demon and explode around them. Mitsuri watches the explosion from below, but as she rushes to Kyojuro's aid, Hairo appears behind her and pins her to the ground. Holding her at gunpoint, he threatens to torture her to torment Kyojuro mentally, only for Kyojuro to suddenly appear, using Flame Breathing, Fifth Form: Flame Tiger to attack the demon and save Mitsuri; the attack cuts into Hairo's neck. Seeing the demon's unusual fixation on him, Kyojuro promises to defeat him, prompting Hairo to laugh and remark that his neck is nearly uncuttable. Hearing this, the Kinoe proudly declares that he will defeat him and become the Flame Hashira, as his family has done for generations. Preparing to fight the Demon Slayer, Hairo uses Blood Demon Art: Capture Cavity, Shadow Wolves; dark wolf-like shadows armed with rifles in their mouths manifest and attack Kyojuro. He uses Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation and destroys the shadowy wolves, but Hairo throws Molotov cocktails into the air to douse Kyojuro in fire, all while remembering his past encounter with the Flame Hashira. Angered by the painful memories, Hairo shoots himself in the mouth again; Kyojuro sees the moment as his chance to attack but is shot numerous times by the demon's Gatling gun, as he hears the demon loudly proclaiming he will have his revenge. In severe pain, Kyojuro hunches down, recalling a memory when his brother Senjuro had asked him about his father after their mother had died. Kyojuro, who was instilled his drive to use his strength to protect the weak by his mother, promises to fulfill his promise to her; he stands up and attacks Hairo head-on, determined to become the new Flame Hashira. Summoning more guns within his body, Hairo shoots Kyojuro away but notices he does not hear any more explosions, nor does he feel the presence of his wolves. To his surprise, Kyojuro slashes through his rifles and cuts into his neck. He shoots him with another volley of bullets but the Kinoe continues to stand up and begins to walk towards him. Hairo is angered and confused at how a mere human with only a sword can endure so many of his powerful attacks, questioning if he is actually facing the Flame Hashira who tortured him. He aims his revolver at Kyojuro but the gun is empty, his ammunition reserves having been depleted by the Demon Slayer. Kyojuro taunts him and asks if he is finished, causing Hairo to yell out in anger and push the gun to his own head, throwing it down when it does not fire. He claims he is not done yet and tries to find a way to deny Kyojuro of something, angered by his persistence. His Blood Demon Art then manifests a katana, causing the demon to relive painful memories of experiencing the inferiority of swordsmanship against the use of firearms. Kyojuro lunges at the demon but is knocked back as a powerful blast erupts from in front of him. Hairo uses Blood Demon Art: Capture Cavity, Warwolf of Horror and has manifested into a dark tenebrous wolfman, cloaking himself in his shadows. Kyojuro sees this and realizes that Hairo is now more dangerous than ever, as even getting close to him will result in being cut down. Hairo gives the Demon Slayer his name and asks that he give him the honor of killing him with a sword. Kyojuro answers his challenge, while determining that with stronger shadows than even the wolves of before, his blade will be trapped in the demon the moment he touches him, and he would have to surpass the demon's swordsmanship with his own to succeed. The Kinoe and the Lower Rank lunge at each other and clash blades, causing a powerful blast to explode from their weapons. Hairo tells Kyojuro his efforts are futile as his sword will never overcome his Blood Demon Art, but to the demon's shock, Kyojuro's katana begins to burn away the shadows. As he persists, the shadows continue to be destroyed by his Flame Breathing, culminating in Kyojuro using the Breathing Style's last and most powerful form, an attack that the user pours their entire body and soul into, allowing him to burn anything. With his final attack, Flame Breathing, Ninth Form: Rengoku, Kyojuro overcomes Hairo's Blood Demon Art and slashes through the demon's neck. As the Lower Rank begins to disintegrate to ash, his final words are a compliment to Kyojuro's swordsmanship. Aftermath. As the last of Hairo's remains fade, Kyojuro attempts to stand despite his extreme fatigue, and is determined to disarm the bombs around Tokyo. Suddenly, Mitsuri appears and hugs him, welling up with tears as she commends him for defeating a member of the Twelve Kizuki, allowing him to become the new Flame Hashira. The squadron of Demon Slayers soon appear around them, though their attempts to pull Mitsuri away from the wounded Kyojuro fails. His mind and thinking hazy, Kyojuro looks to the sky. Kyojuro returns home with Mitsuri and is embraced by Senjuro, who is ecstatic to learn that Kyojuro has officially succeeded their father. At a later Hashira meeting, Kagaya calls Kyojuro a remarkable child and asks if he would continue to do his duties as the new Flame Hashira. Kyojuro answers with a proud, "Yes!".

Kyojuro Rengoku vs Slasher Kyojuro Rengoku vs Slasher was a battle that took place at a train yard. It focuses on the battle between the Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku against the Slasher, a demon responsible for numerous attacks in a town. Prologue. During his investigation of the Mugen Train, Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku goes into the yard where the train is being repaired. He offers food to the workers as he speaks to one of the workers about the train when they suddenly hear a scream. Rushing into action, he finds a marked demon holding a boy hostage and driving his claws in. Battle. The demon taunts Kyojuro, claiming he's the fastest and that the Hashira can't kill him without injuring the hostage. Additionally, the demon also claims to have slashed up a girl the night before, however Kyojuro counters his boast by saying that they saved the girl and that she will recover with no injuries. Angered, the demon decides to kill the vendors that Kyojuro befriended, but first he will kill his hostage. Kyojuro is quick to react and cuts off the demons arm's, saving the hostage. The demon decides to retreat using his Blood Demon Art, his speed dramatically increasing as he runs along the train tracks to find the vendors. Kyojuro stays with the now-former hostage as he heals him, assuring the workers that he'll be okay. As more Demon Slayers turn up, Kyojuro goes after the demon, using Total Concentration Breathing to increase his speed and catch up to the demon. The demon finds the young vendor and goes in for the kill; but is distracted when the older vendor throws bento boxes at him. The box's contents disgusts the demon, causing him to hold his face. The young vendor takes this opportunity to escape but is caught by the demon and is about to be killed when Kyojuro arrives in the nick of time, slashing his achilles and causing him to drop the vendor. The demon then rushes and confronts the older vendor, but is accosted by Kyojuro. Still believing he can win, the Slasher then issues a speed challenge to the Flame Hashira; either the demon kills the older vendor or he decapitates him. Instead Kyojuro tells him the demon he is slow, and in an instant, he lunges forward and decapitates the Slasher using Flame Breathing, First Form: Unknowing Fire. Aftermath. With victory won, Kyojuro preforms the process of . As he does this, the older vendor is reminded of an incident 20 years ago, where a similar looking Demon Slayer killed an attacking demon. Believing this was him, she thanks him profusely for saving her again, to which he responds it was probably his father who had saved her, but he is glad he could follow in his footsteps. He then leaves to board the Mugen train and continue his investigation.

Love Breathing is a Breathing Style derived from Flame Breathing. Overview. Love Breathing is a Breathing Style that is based on the emotion of love, and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. Most, if not all, known techniques inculcate a gymnastic and movement-oriented rhythm into the user's attacks, making use of their superhuman flexibility, dexterity, and agility to perform wide, winding and weaving slashes that have mid-to-long range applications. Users of Love Breathing also visualize themselves seemingly creating pink and green sparks as well as pink lines that follow the direction of their attacks. This Breathing Style is the personal creation of Mitsuri Kanroji, made by altering the Flame Breathing she learned from Kyojuro Rengoku to suit her flexibility and strength. It takes advantage of her body's unique muscle density, which grants her inhuman strength without making her physically bulky, to deliver fast and powerful blows while moving with incredible flexibility and agility. As it relies on her body's special composition, it is a style only she can use. It can also be assumed that this Breathing Style is most effective with a whip-like katana, however, a regular one can also be used as shown in the . Known Techniques. Love Breathing has 6 forms at minimum, with 5 known forms. Demonstrations. <tabber> </tabber>

Lower Ranks Meeting The was a gathering and massacre that immediately followed the death of Rui, Lower Five of the Twelve Kizuki. It occurred in the Infinity Castle and covered Muzan Kibutsuji's lack of faith in the Lower Ranks and his subsequent decision to kill them all. Prologue. The Twelve Kizuki is an organization consisting of the twelve most powerful demons who serve directly under the Demon King Muzan Kibutsuji. Split into 6 member rankings, they consisted of the Upper Ranks and the Lower Ranks. The Upper Ranks of the Twelve Kizuki remained unchanging for nearly 113 years, with no single member dying to the Demon Slayer Corps; as further credence to their strength, only the Upper Ranks have been successful at killing members of the Hashira. In stark contrast, the Lower Ranks would continue to lose and change members in that same time, shifting positions and possessing an inconsistent and lacking strength that disappointed Muzan. Eventually, the death of Rui, a powerful and favoured member of the Lower Ranks, at the hands of the Demon Slayer Corps would drive Muzan to deem the echelon as a whole to be entirely useless to him. He subsequently ordered the Biwa Demon Nakime, owner and manipulator of the Infinity Castle, to summon each of the five remaining members. Meeting. The Lower Ranks are summoned to the castle in numerical order. Enmu, Lower One, is taken to the castle first, followed by Lower Two Rokuro, Lower Three Wakuraba, Lower Four Mukago, and finally, Lower Six Kamanue. Enmu calmly walks about the castle, while his peers stay still in worried anticipation. Kamanue, being the lowest and weakest member, becomes confused the moment he was summoned, having never seen the Infinity Castle before and (correctly) assuming the Biwa Demon in the castle's centre is the owner of the space. He sees Enmu and Rokuro in the distance and notices Wakuraba and Mukago nearby as well. Seeing that it is only the Lower Ranks that have been summoned to the Infinity Castle, he wonders on the whereabouts of Lower Five. Before long, Nakime strums her biwa to take them all to a platform in front of her; Rokuro, Wakuraba and Mukago look around their surroundings in fear and uncertainty, while Enmu, being the highest ranking member, calmly looks on ahead. Kamanue sees what Enmu is looking at; an elegantly dressed female demon calmly standing before them. They do not recognize the demon until it utters in a familiar voice, ""Lower your heads and crouch down. Prostrate yourselves". Suddenly struck by the demon's aura, the Lower Ranks bow down before the figure. They quickly realize the demon is Muzan Kibutsuji himself: Kamanue grows terrified coming face to face with the Demon Progenitor, sweating profusely at his incredible ability to disguise himself completely and flawlessly. Mukago attempts to apologize on the behalf of her peers, only to be silenced by Muzan for voicing her "worthless thoughts". Muzan states that they are in the castle for only one reason. He tells them about the death of Lower Five Rui, and demands to know why they are so weak. He tells the Lower Ranks that as members of the Twelve Kizuki, all they should do is eat humans and gain strength, as it is only then that they can be useful to him. He compares them unfavourably to the Upper Ranks; while they have not changed positions in over 100 years and have killed members of the Hashira, it is the Lowers who continue to change and get replaced. Kamanue finds it unbelievable that Muzan is placing seemingly impossible expectations on the Lower Ranks, only for Muzan to repeat and say his thoughts out loud: "That's easy for you to say, but we...". He realizes this and panics that he has been caught outright and Muzan grows enraged at this act of doubt in his methods. He demands that Kamanue continue speaking his mind; when Lower Six does not responds, he is grabbed and hoisted into the air by Muzan with a large and monstrous arm. Kamanue tearfully begs for forgiveness but is ruthlessly devoured by the unfeeling and cold Muzan; his blood sprays across the platform and Rokuro, Wakuraba, and Mukago are left paralyzed with fear over his gruesome death. Enmu remains obedient and continues bowing down. Wakuraba wonders if he too will be killed, despite all his efforts to attain his position in the Twelve Kizuki and believing he was destined to achieve more. Muzan questions them on whether they fear the Demon Slayers more than they fear him; Wakuraba panics and nearly says a word, only for Mukago to speak up and deny her fear of them. He challenges her and claims that all she thinks about when encountering the Hashira is trying to escape. Mukago tears up under the pressure and defends his honour, claiming that she would put her life on the line for him. However, Muzan only sees her begging as refuting his statement, and Mukago can do nothing but watch as his monstrous arm is brought down onto her, crushing Lower Four instantly. He proceeds to devour her remains and absorb her. Realizing their minds are being read and that they will be killed regardless of what they say, Wakuraba tries to think off an escape plan. Knowing they are powerless to fight him, he sees Muzan is busy absorbing Mukago's body and leaps up from the platform with immense speed. He sprints around the Infinity Castle's walls and platforms, traversing the unusual gravity and making his way further and further from the center; Enmu sees his actions and calls him a fool for doing so. Lower Three manages to gain a considerable distance but suddenly finds himself back in Muzan's hand as a severed head; Muzan states that it would be best if the Twelve Kizuki is made up of only the Upper Ranks, hence why he is killing them. Wakuraba is stunned as he did not hear the sounds of the biwa, nor why he is not regenerating. Muzan hurls the demon's head in front of the last two Lower Ranks and asks if they have any last words. Rokuro asks for a reprieve and promises to be of use to him. When Muzan asks how long of a reprieve and how he intends to do so with his current strength, Lower Two asks for a portion of his blood, swearing to acclimate to its power without fail and to fight as a stronger demon for him. Angered, Muzan asks how he can simply order him for his blood and brands the demon as shameless for his actions. Rokuro begins begging for forgiveness and states that he has misunderstood his intentions, only to have his master silence him and state that his word alone is absolute. Muzan claims he is never wrong and coldly states that he deserved to die, because "You tried to tell me what to do"". As Rokuro's blood spill off of the platform, only Enmu remains; Wakuraba believes that he too will be killed since their lives hang on to Muzan's mood, as his own life ends. As his last words, Enmu states that the situation before him is his dream, always wanting to die through the hands of his master and speaking of his enjoyment in watching his fellow Lower Ranks' last gasps of life. He feels blessed to see their pain as the despair and agony of others gives him immense joy and thanks Muzan for leaving him last to be killed. The Demon King remains quiet and still, only to suddenly stab Enmu in the neck with a spine from his arm and inject him with a large amount of blood. As Lower One writhes in pain, Muzan praises him for giving an answer he had wanted to hear. He tells Enmu that the amount of blood he had injected might kill him, but should he survive, he will become even more powerful. Muzan orders Lower One to kill the Hashira and gives him another incentive; should he kill the Demon Slayer wearing earrings, he can gain more blood, much to Enmu's pleasure. Concluding the meeting, Nakime manipulates the Infinity Castle with strums of her biwa, taking Muzan to a balcony at the top and changing Enmu's position to drop him through several doors, landing in an unknown town. Aftermath. Whilst on the ground, as Muzan's blood flows through him, Enmu sees a vision of his chosen target and becomes excited at the thought of getting more blood once he kills him and a Hashira. He would initiate his plan by locating a train that has been reported to have numerous disappearances on board; perhaps unbeknownst to him, this was the work of two hidden demons on the train. Months later, with over 40 missing passengers reported on the Mugen train, the Demon Slayer Corps dispatches the Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku to investigate, accompanied later by three Demon Slayer: Tanjiro Kamado, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira, setting in motion Enmu's battle with the Demon Slayers.
Makimi Hano is a Japanese writer and the author of several of the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" novelized light novels.

Makio is a supporting character of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She is a and one of Tengen Uzui's wives. Appearance. Makio is a young woman of average height possessing a voluptuous figure with pale skin and large golden brown eyes framed by eyelashes with prominent ones present on both the upper and lower lashes, and thin eyebrows arching downward which gives her a determined and headstrong look. She has black hair tied up with golden-brown bangs which hang loosely, framing her face. Makio is seen wearing a red, sleeveless striped dress that ends mid-thigh which also reveals her cleavage and secured with a black where she stores her . She has gray-colored bandages wrapped around her calves and up to her thighs. Her footwear consists of a pair of with red straps. During her time as Daki's captive, she is seen with cuts and bruises across her body. Personality. Makio's personality is similar to Inosuke Hashibira: bold and confident in the way she acts. Out of her two co-wives, Makio tends to have less patience with Suma. When the women fought Daki's obi in the underground cavern, Makio can be seen berating her for being condescending. Later on when the three wives reunite, Makio can also be seen slapping Suma and calling her an idiot after she makes insensitive remarks about Hinatsuru dying. Despite her headstrong and fierce temperament, Makio does have a softer side that shows when dealing with Tengen. She is seen worrying about his declining health following their major battle, and clings to him in relief after Nezuko heals him. History. At some point of her life, Makio married Tengen Uzui, along with Suma and Hinatsuru. After she left the clan, her family journeyed to see Kagaya Ubuyashiki in order to fight as a part of the Demon Slayer Corps. At some point in the past, Makio was instructed alongside Suma and Hinatsuru by Tengen on his personal ideology: to put their own lives first, then respectable humans, and lastly himself. Makio questioned this approach to life in private, as it went against what they had been taught as kunoichi, Hinatsuru assured her that it was okay to put her own safety first. Synopsis. Entertainment District Arc. Makio initially arrives at the district to work undercover as a courtesan at the Ogimoto House. She tries to gather intel on reports of a demon within the district and sends back information to Tengen via crow. One day, Makio is discovered by Daki and captured by her obi, which interrogates her over who she is sending the letters to. Refusing to disclose her mission, Makio is taken to Daki's underground bunker and sealed within a sash. When Inosuke later discovers the bunker, he cuts the obi freeing both Makio and Suma from within it and the two women assist him in protecting the girls from getting reabsorbed by the Obi. After they reunite with Tengen in the cavern, Makio and Suma are freed and lead the evacuation of the citizens within the district. Once Makio and Suma succeed in evacuating the citizens, they return towards the end of the battle and discover the aftermath. Makio alongside her co-wives hurry to provide first aid to Tengen, but discover their antidotes aren't working to cure Gyutaro's poison. After initially panicking over what to do, Nezuko approaches the group and heals Tengen with her abilities, allowing the women to rejoice and embrace him. Swordsmith Village Arc. As Kakushi appear in Yoshiwara so that clean up can begin, Makio and her co-wives can be seen assisting Tengen off of the battlefield so he can begin his recovery. Hashira Training Arc. Makio assists Suma and Hinatsuru in Tengen's stage of Hashira Training, giving out food to the exhausted participants. She greets Tanjiro when he appears to begin his training. Abilities. Overall Abilities: Makio does not possess any form of superhuman abilities. However, as she was raised as a, Makio possesses impressive shinobi skills, being capable of wielding a as well as performing maneuvers and fighting much more proficiently than regular people can. Equipment. Standard Kunai: As a, Makio carries around two standard black for combat purposes, 2 of which she uses for melee combat and the rest as ranged projectiles.

Makomo was a former apprentice of Sakonji Urokodaki. She appeared to assist Tanjiro Kamado in his preparations for the Final Selection exam. Appearance. Makomo was a young girl of short stature and pale skin, who possessed gentle eyes of a deep cyan color, their pupils rectangular and white, that were a notably paler turquoise near the bottom. She had black hair that came down to her shoulders, spiking outwards at the ends, and short micro bangs over her forehead. Makomo wore a red yukata with a pink and white flower dot pattern, over which she sported a dark-purple sleeveless haori and a paler brown piece of fabric tied around her waist. On her feet, she wore a pair of sandals of a similar design to the ones worn by Mitsuri Kanroji, tied around her ankle from her heel and closed at the toe. As with the rest of Sakonji Urokodaki's apprentices, Makomo's white warding mask, hand-carved by her master himself, took the shape of a fox's face, hers additionally being decorated by two blue flowers painted on its left-hand side. Personality. Completely opposing to Sabito's aggressive and form personality, Makomo was a girl of quiet, patient, and kind nature. She was always helping Tanjiro Kamado by pointing out any mistakes in his technique and correcting any bad habits he had unconsciously developed during his training under Sakonji. Makomo's pet phrase is that she loves Sakonji very much. She is also a somewhat mysterious person, as she always speaks in an abstract and dreamy way without ever giving straight answers to questions about her past. Makomo and the other spirits of Sakonji's children entrust Tanjiro with putting their foster-father's mind at ease. She and Sabito watch over their loved ones, including Tanjiro, who helps put their souls to a peaceful rest. History. Makomo was orphaned from her family and adopted by Sakonji, who trained and later permitted her to attend the Demon Slayer Corps' Final Selection. During her seven days on Mt. Fujikasane, Makomo encountered a powerful morphed demon, this demon claiming to have eaten many of Sakonji's children. The demon said he hoped the old man feels responsible, and Makomo, overcome with emotion and without control of her movements, attacked him erratically, resulting in her being swiftly ripped apart by the demon and left to join the ranks of the other children he had already killed. Makomo's soul return to Mount Sagiri, as she cannot rest due to their failure and Sakonji's grief. Although, as Makomo was taken in and died a period of time before Sabito, they didn't meet each other in person until after he died. Final Selection Arc. Sakonji eventually takes on a new student named Tanjiro Kamado, and, after one and a half years of training, when Tanjiro is still unable to pass Sakonji's final test, Sabito challenges the boy and defeats him using a wooden sword. Afterwards, Sabito entrusts the boy's training to Makomo, who introduces herself to Tanjiro when he awakens after the fight. She tells him he can be like Sabito one day, and also that she loves Sakonji Urokodaki very much and all of his children are guiding Tanjiro. Makomo corrects the bad habits in his form and teaches him more about Total Concentration Breathing, and, when he asks how he can master all of these techniques, Makomo simply tells him to "train to death". She trains Tanjiro for six more months until he is finally able to defeat Sabito in a duel. Makomo commends Tanjiro and tells him to never forget what he's done. She disappears into the mist, asking him to defeat a certain someone. Thanks to Makomo's guidance, Tanjiro is finally able to slice the boulder. Tanjiro enters Final Selection, and the spirits of Sakonji's children continue to watch over him. Makomo asks Sabito if he thinks Tanjiro is strong enough to overcome the demon they failed to defeat, to which Sabito only replies he doesn't know because it's never enough when they try. When the fateful battle between Tanjiro and the Hand Demon arrives, Makomo worries that he may lose as well. Sabito says that he can't predict the outcome, but he reminds Makomo that Tanjiro is the one who split the largest, toughest boulder of all. Tanjiro uses all his training to defeat the Hand Demon and finally put an end to the wicked cycle. The souls of Sakonji's children appear before Tanjiro, finally able to rest, and Makomo bids farewell to Tanjiro and disappears into the fog one last time. Sunrise Countdown Arc. In the modern day, Makomo, alongside her fellow pupil, Sabito, were reincarnated. Their reincarnations are friends with Giichi Tomioka, the descendant of Sabito's close friend, Giyu Tomioka. Abilities. Overall Abilities: While not much is known about her prowess as a Demon Slayer candidate, Makomo was deemed strong enough to earn Sakonji's permission to enter Final Selection. She underwent his training and was able to survive until encountering a powerful morphed demon, who, although he claimed Makomo didn't have much power, commended her agility since she was able to evade most of his attacks. Equipment. Standard Nichirin Katana: Makomo had a standard sized and shaped Nichirin katana with a handguard that is round shaped and a blue core, decorated with small pink flowers and an overlapping a blue border.
