Muzan Kibutsuji/Relationships Relationships. Demon Slayer Corps. The Demon Slayer Corps has been fighting and battling Muzan and his created demons since the beginning of the demon race's spread to the entirety of Japan during the time of Antiquity and as such are Muzan's eternal enemies in a thousand year struggle, where the Corps have attempted time and time again to kill him and end his threat to humanity and his own struggle to annihilate them and put a stop to their constant attempts at his life and ruining and interfering with his plans. During the Corp's early history before the creation of the Breathing Styles, it was implied by Muzan that he himself never considered them to be any great threat to him or his plans and initially considered them as mere minor annoyances due to the fact that they initially barely posed a genuine threat to him and his demons. However with the joining of Yoriichi Tsugikuni and his invention and spread of the Breathing Styles Techniques, Muzan gradually became more and more aware of them and keep a much more keen eye on the rapidly growing organization due to the now substantial threat they now posed to him as they began to annihilate his created demon's by the hundreds thanks to their newly acquired techniques. However despite this and due to his own immense arrogance and inflated ego, Muzan himself initially bared little to no fear for the newly empowered demon slayers and in fact instead became curios with the slayers themselves during the initial years of the Slayer's "Golden Age" and the specific changes and enhancements their breath styles did to their bodies and instead developed the desire to study these physical enhancements up close to help his own research. Eventually to satiate this curiosity, Muzan approached and calmly asked a single Demon Slayer if he wanted to become a demon and convinced him to turn due to observing that due to the immense power that certain demon slayers obtained their bodies were fated to die at age 25, targeting the man's desire to become stronger and live longer and successfully convincing him to defect and join him. Eventually, upon convincing the renegade Demon Slayer to transform into a demon, Muzan successfully researched and studied his physiology and biology as a powerful Breath User and the enhancements further done to his body upon transforming into a demon. After doing so, Muzan stated that he had then lost nearly all interest in the Demon Slayers. However this mindset quickly changed upon nearly being killed by Yoriichi Tsugikuni. Muzan quickly became more vicious and paranoid with the Demon Slayer Corps upon realizing that people that can genuinely kill him do indeed exist and that the techniques to do so are found only with the Corps, causing the Demon Progenitor to now take more active attempts to annihilate the Demon Slayer Corps and began taking much more careful and intricate steps to further insure his own safety for the next hundred years due to his heightened paranoia. During of which Muzan and his subordinate insured to eliminate each and every single person both in and outside of the Corps that know the Breathing Style of Yoriichi to further insure that no one can learn them and has begun actively sending his strongest demon's to eliminate the Corp's strongest members to insure no one else of Yoriichi's power can appear ever again. Muzan himself, due to his selfish mentality and arrogant point of view and inflated ego, has deemed the Demon Slayer Corps as a group of unnatural, obsessive freaks who continuously chase after him for no reason due to his own belief that he and his demons are something akin to a natural disaster, something that is indeed destructive and kills people, but something completely unavoidable and natural. And that the demon slayers are "strange" due to them holding a grudge over losing their loved ones to them and comparing their justified anger to something as ridiculous as holding a grudge and picking a fight with air, fire, earth, or water whenever there is a earthquake, flood, forest fire, storms, or twisters that kills their family. Yoriichi Tsugikuni. When he first encountered Yoriichi, Muzan was arrogant and stated that he wasn't interested in Demon Slayers who use Breathing Styles, before dismissively attacking Yoriichi as if he'd be an easy kill. However, much to his surprise, Yoriichi struck him multiple times with his bright red blade, wounding him with deep slashes that the Demon King was unable to regenerate. Muzan quickly fled the scene, barely still alive, and developed a loathsome fear of the Breath Style Progenitor, prompting him to systematically murder all of the other Sun Breathing users to prevent anyone else like Yoriichi from emerging. Even 400 years later, Muzan's fear of Yoriichi remained fully intact, as simply laying eyes on Tanjiro's hanafuda earrings caused him to recall their clash. Although Yoriichi was long dead, his visage appeared in the blood memory of Daki after Tanjiro awakened his Demon Slayer Mark, causing Muzan's fear to once again grow. Ultimately, Yoriichi is the only being Muzan ever feared as he personally saw him as the true """monster" between the two of them and to the very end he remained baffled as to how a being like Yoriichi came to exist. Tanjiro Kamado. Tanjiro is considered to be Muzan's main nemesis throughout the series. After murdering the Kamado family, he was personally sought out by Tanjiro in Asakusa, Tokyo when the Demon Slayer recognized his scent from the scene of the murder. Although Muzan had never met Tanjiro before then, he knew immediately that he needed to eliminate him after recognizing the hanafuda earrings he wore to be the ones his would-have-been killer previously donned, as later revealed. In an attempt to flee, he created a diversion by transforming a young man into a demon to deter Tanjiro, but not before Tanjiro professed his goal to kill him, claiming that he would chase him to the ends of the earth if he had to. Enraged by his threats, Muzan would send multiple demons to kill Tanjiro such as Yahaba, Susamaru and Enmu throughout the series. As mentioned, it is revealed that Muzan's desire to destroy Tanjiro stemmed from his hatred towards his previous nemesis, Yoriichi Tsugikuni. After recognizing the earrings Tanjiro wore in Asakusa, Muzan realized that he was a Sun Breathing user, a wielder of the incredibly powerful technique Yoriichi had developed and that Muzan had sworn to eradicate its users after it almost killed him. This is why, upon seeing Tanjiro for the first time, the Demon King felt threatened and became frantic in trying to kill him. As Muzan begins to disintegrate, he becomes so overwhelmed with emotion that he decides to pass on his dream to Tanjiro. After realizing his abilities to use the Sun Breathing, Muzan decides that Tanjiro is capable of surviving to make his dream come true, and become the King of Demons. Nezuko Kamado. At the very beginning of the story, Muzan tried to turn Nezuko and the entire Kamado Family into demons, however all of them failed to survive the transformation, except for Nezuko. He soon found her to be a defiant nuisance much like Tamayo, able to escape his curse and become uncontrollable. However after Nezuko developed a resistance to sunlight, Muzan didn't hesitate to attack the Demon Slayer Corps alongside the remaining Upper Ranks in an attempt to devour Nezuko and achieve his long-sought desire to become invincible. Later on when Nezuko regained all of her memories, including the painful and traumatizing memories of losing her family to Muzan in his attack on her home, she is shown to harbor immense hatred and rage towards the demon's actions and was shown to barely be able to control herself as it all came back to her. As shown in her recollection, Muzan was shown to have attacked the Kamado family purely out of a whim, with him later injecting Nezuko with a gigantic amount of his blood only to see if she could survive or not, when she had seemingly died, Muzan was shown to have been initially disappointed and wondered if he could ever create a demon that could resist the sun. Ubuyashiki Family. The Ubuyashiki Family have been leading the Demon Slayer Corps since the times of antiquity and have continued to do so for a thousand years in their mission to kill the Demon Progenitor. Due to them being the main ringleaders of the Demon Slayer Corps, Muzan deeply despises the Ubuyashiki Family and for centuries, has made it one of his top priorities to eliminate the entire clan and end their bloodline in order to permanently rid of himself of the Demon Slayer Corps. This is seen where Muzan clearly stated to his Upper Ranks that the Ubuyashiki Family themselves is one of the primary targets they need to eliminate and one of the primary reasons why Muzan was so disappointed and enraged with them was due to their lack of success in permanently ending the Ubuyashiki Family. As revealed by Kagaya Ubuyashiki, the Ubuyashiki family themselves are in fact related to Muzan by blood, with them being the descendants of his relatives from a thousand years ago. According to Kagaya, the Ubuyashiki bloodline was cursed for having produced the Demon Progenitor and all the children born into their clan was stated to have been sickly and weak, dying before they were even fully grown. After consulting a priest, his relatives were told the reason for their curse was due to Muzan having orginated from their bloodline and they should devote their lives and their clan into killing him and purging the world of his demons in order to remove their curse. From then hence forth, the Ubuyashiki family would receive their spouses selected for them by Priests, and since then, while those born to the clan still died before they became thirty, they were now at the very least, more resistant to death. Kagaya Ubuyashiki. Muzan's animosity towards Kagaya can almost be described as professional as opposed to personal. Even when they meet, Muzan does not particularly display or feel any real animosity toward Kagaya, instead finding his blood ties to him and his family amusing when he mocked them for their centuries long resolve to kill him. Kagaya and Muzan had completely different personalities, Kagaya viewing his followers as his own children and Muzan viewing his followers as expendable. And whereas Kagaya was willing to listen when his followers gave him advice, Muzan decided to punish those who did the same with death for having the audacity to command him. Twelve Kizuki. Muzan holds these demons in quite a high regard compared to the others, giving them a larger portion of his blood to increase their powers. Despite favoring them more than regular demons, Muzan tends to show that he prefers the Upper Ranks compared to the Lower Ranks. This is evidenced when Muzan killed off the demons during the Lower Ranks meeting out of anger following Rui's defeat, and his criticism of their failure to win against the Demon Slayers and their apparent inability to defeat the Hashira's of the Corps and considered them to be arrogant, negligent failures due to them becoming overly confident at the fact that they became Lower Ranks. However despite Muzan's preference to them, he still views the Upper Ranks as inferior due to the verbal abuse towards them for failing to find the Blue Spider Lily after hundreds of years of searching and their apparent failure to completely destroy the Demon Slayer Corps from existence and eliminate the Ubuyashiki family. In the end, he viewed them all as expendable tools and after emerging from his flesh cocoon to face the Demon Slayer Corp, admonished them all for being useless before declaring that he alone will kill the Demon Slayers. Kokushibo. Muzan first met him when he was known as Michikatsu Tsugikuni, the latter had long desired to become as powerful as his brother but failed, as well as fearing his imminent close death by bearing the Demon Slayer Mark. Taking advantage of this, Muzan persuaded him to change, noting they would both win, as he could live forever and become stronger whereas Muzan would gain a Breathing Style using demon. Taking the name Kokushibo, he became Muzan's most powerful subordinate and was Upper Rank One of the Twelve Kizuki. He was arguably one of the closest to Muzan, who viewed him as somewhat of a business partner.In turn, Kokushibo became intensely loyal to Muzan, acting as an enforcer for the hierarchy he built among the Upper Ranks, as shown when he punished and threatened Akaza for attacking Doma. Kokushibo and Muzan were jointly responsible for nearly eradicating Sun Breathing entirely, after the latter's encounter with the former's brother Yoriichi Tsugikuni. Despite this, Muzan only valued him for his loyalty and dismissed him as useless despite all he had done for him, along with Akaza and Doma, following his death. Doma. During their interaction during the Upper Ranks meeting in the wake of Gyutaro and Daki's deaths, Muzan is shown to be just as annoyed, short tempered and degrading towards Doma as he is to the other Upper Ranks, where Muzan visibly expresses his anger, frustration, disappointment and withering faith in Doma due to his inability to live up to his expectation of finding the Blue Spider Lily and entombing and wiping out the Demon Slayer Corps and the Ubuyashiki Family for him. Doma in turn has not displayed any form of fear, anxiety or anger at the Demon King despite his attitude towards him and the other Upper Ranks or any of the potential punishment he could inflict upon him, in fact Doma himself has not displayed the usual attitude of fear and respect most demons show Muzan and is instead shown to take a more laid back and comedic disposition when interacting with him, as seen where Doma actually seems to be happy and excited on his potential "punishments" as seen where he enthusiastically offered Muzan if he should gouge out his own eye for him or perform any other form of extreme self harm to himself for the Demon King, further angering and annoying Muzan due to his enthusiasm and lack of seriousness/fear when interacting with him. Muzan never really liked Doma, likely due to him noticing the latter's lack of emotions and desires. Akaza. Muzan had first met Akaza when he was originally known as Hakuji, having first met the boy after he had revenge for his teacher and fiancée's murders by killing the Kenjutsu Dojo brutally. Muzan having heard of the carnage and the sheer brutality of the mutilated corpses of the victims was under the assumption that a demon was responsible for the killings, confusing the Demon King due to not having sent any into the region of the killing's location causing him to then go to the place in order to investigate out of curiosity. Having found him shortly after the dojo's destruction, Muzan was both surprised and disappointed to learn that the killer was in fact nothing more than a normal human. After Hakuji threatened to kill him, Muzan rushed forward and pierced his head, before declaring his intentions to form the Twelve Kizuki and asked if he was able to withstand his blood. Eventually Hakuji, now known as Akaza, had fully reached Muzan's expectations and did indeed become one of his Kizuki, specifically his Upper Rank 3, delighting the Demon King and causing him to particularly grant a great amount of his personal favor to Akaza in comparison to his fellow Kizuki. As stated by Doma, that Muzan had tolerated and allowed Akaza's unique aversion to not eating or harming women and even only went as far as only dispatching him on special missions only, a privilege not even given to Upper Rank 1 or 2. He was one of Muzan's favorites since he was loyal and serious. Hantengu. Hantengu is shown to be incredibly fearful towards Muzan, especially during the Demon King's more violent and moody episodes, as seen when he was constantly cowering in fear of him and constantly apologizing to him during the meeting of the Upper Ranks after Gyutaro and Daki's deaths putting him in a bad mood. Muzan in turn sees Hantengu as an "ordinary person" and sees his overly cowardly/submissive personality as annoying, but tolerable. But he nonetheless is still shown to possess a level of trust in Hantengu's abilities and powers as a demon despite his cowardly nature, as seen when he trusted him enough to accompany Gyokko in a mission after the Upper Rank Meeting was adjured. Later it was revealed that Hantengu follows Muzan not strictly out of fear of him, but due to him being genuinely loyal and grateful to the Demon King. This was due to Muzan having "saved" Hantengu from being executed by a "corrupt" Magister who did not believe Hantengu's claims of being "innocent" of the crimes of theft and murder by transforming him into a demon and freeing him from prison before his execution date. Thanks to this, Hantengu believes that Muzan was the first person to "truly" see his "innocent self" and "believe" him, causing the demon to then harbor a deep sense of respect that is even present in his other radically different disposition clones. Upon his death at the hands of Tanjiro Kamado, Muzan was delighted by Hantengu's work, due to him successfully reporting that a demon that can withstand sunlight has appeared, causing the Demon Progenitor to laugh in ecstatic delight and actually compliment the Upper Rank on his work. However, he did not care that he was dead. Nakime. Nakime's exact relationship with Muzan is unknown, but she herself has shown to be incredibly loyal and obedient to the Demon King out of genuine loyalty instead of fear, as seen where she would stoically follow each and every order given to her by Muzan without hesitation. After becoming an Upper Rank and replacing Hantengu, Muzan is shown to have become genuinely impressed and appreciative of Nakime's growth in her abilities and the further development of her powers, as seen where he actually complimented her on her growth and even thanked her for successfully completing her mission of locating each and every Demon Slayer across the country and locating Kagaya Ubuyashiki himself, a rarity due to Muzan's own view of only seeing the Upper Ranks as expendable tools and the usual degrading/arrogant/condescending demeanor he usually shows when interacting with them. She was one of Muzan's favorite Upper Rank, since he believes her ability to be exceptionally useful.However, he showed no qualms about killing her after Yushiro took control of her vision. Gyokko. During the first gathering of the Upper Ranks in hundreds of years, Muzan is shown to particularly dislike Gyokko due to his arrogant and somewhat insolent personality clashing with Muzan's own short temper and narcissism, seen when he angrily ripped off Gyokko's head when the demon attempted to appease his Lord. Gyokko, however, despite being brutally beheaded by him, showed absolute loyalty to the Demon Progenitor, as seen when he showed no fear, pain or anger at Muzan's actions but was instead overjoyed by Muzan holding his severed head in one hand. showing a fanatical amount of loyalty to him and was slightly annoyed by Muzan blowing him off despite him obtaining vital information on the Demon Slayer Corps but in the end considered this a good point of Muzan's personality. Later it was revealed that Muzan in fact considers Gyokko to be one of his favorite Upper Ranks due to his pots, with him greatly liking to the artistic skill he puts into them and the high price he gets by selling them. Daki and Gyutaro. Muzan is shown to have a positive master-servant relationship with Daki, as the young demon seemingly worships and admires the Demon Progenitor immensely, fervently hanging on each and every one of his words and doing her absolute best to accomplish the tasks he gives her. Muzan, in turn, aware of Daki's easily trusting and therefore exploitable personality along with her vanity, takes full advantage of her worship and love by him by emotionally manipulating her, regularly complimenting her, calling her a "special" demon in order to reinforce her loyalty to him. As revealed after her death, Muzan never truly acknowledged Daki as an Upper Rank and instead deemed her to be the main reason why the "true" Upper Rank Six was killed. In truth, he does not think highly of her and instead saw Daki as an unintelligent child. Due to his favoritism to the siblings (particularly to Gyutaro), Muzan was noted to give them the special privilege to actually share the position of Upper Rank 6 between the two of them, something not even seen among any of the other higher ranked Upper Ranks. In truth, Muzan only ever saw Gyutaro as truly being worthy of being his Upper Rank 6, as revealed when Muzan claims that he highly valued him and expected him to grow more powerful due to his greedy, apathetic and violent personality. However, Muzan also seems to look down on Gyutaro due to him believing that his love for his sister was holding him back and that the main reason he was killed was because of her. Enmu. Although their exact relationship was not seen, Enmu was known to have become powerful enough and famous in his exploits in battle to be recognized by Muzan as being a formidable enough to select him to become Lower Rank 1 and further augment his powers with his blood as a reward. However upon Rui's death and defeat, Muzan was shown to have become completely displeased and repulsed by all of the Lower Ranks due to their apparent weakness in comparison to the Upper Ranks, earning the Demon King's ire and intense disappointment due to their apparent failure and contentedness not to advance in power due to becoming a Lower Rank. As seen during the Final Lower Ranks Meeting where Muzan showed obvious disdain for Enmu. Enmu in turn was seen to harbor the utmost respect and admiration for Muzan despite his now hostile view of him and the other Lower Ranks, as seen where he was completely confident on Muzan's power and showed both pity and delight upon seeing Wakuraba's attempt to run away and knowing he stood no chance of surviving or escaping due to Muzan's extreme powers. Later as Enmu was the only surviving Lower Rank left, he expressed complete joy and ecstasy at Muzan's actions of slaughtering his fellow demons and even proclaimed that being killed personally by Muzan's hand was the greatest honor he could ever have in his life as a demon, showing just how intense Enmu's loyalty to him was. Muzan in turn, delighted by Enmu's words of adoration and at his sadism, decided to spare the Lower Rank and give him a chance to prove his worth and even went as far as giving Enmu even more of his blood and further augment and strengthen the demon's power to further assist him in his task. Again causing the demon further joy and happiness at the Demon King's "favor" and caused him to then decided to do everything he could to accomplish his mission in order to receive more blood to strengthen himself from the latter. However, as seen from Akaza having appeared in the wreck of Enmu's Train after his attempt to devour humans in mass failed, Muzan likely did not have high expectations for him despite sparing him and injecting him with more of his blood. This is seen where despite having Akaza stationed close to the train, he did not lend any assistance or back up to the Lower Rank and only entered into the battle after Enmu had been killed. Alluding that Muzan likely expected him to fail to begin with and ordered Akaza to follow him in secret to eliminate the Demon Slayers who successfully killed him when they are weakened from their battle against Enmu. Rui. Although unknown when, how or why, Muzan became aware of and interested in Rui during his time as a human, specifically the fact that he was born as with a sickly and fragile human body that made even the simplest physical actions, such as walking, difficult and cause him to immediately collapse afterwards in exhaustion. Muzan, taking advantage of this, approached the weak young boy and offered to "cure" him of his weak body, an offer Rui happily agreed to due to wanting to make his parent's happy and worry less for his health without fully knowing what Muzan was offering him. Muzan then gave him his blood and successfully transformed him into a demon before once again leaving without telling him of the new characteristics and nutritional needs his new body, but nonetheless kept a close eye on the fledgling demon's progress. Eventually Rui would later devour a person in order to survive, horrifying his parents who then reluctantly attempted to kill their son before he could commit any greater atrocities but instead ended up being killed by Rui in self defense within their home. There, Muzan once again appeared before the young demon who, was going through severe psychological shock and denial of his own actions. Realizing the fragility of Rui's mental state, Muzan proceeded to then manipulate the young demon by telling him that the two dead humans killed at his own hands weren't his "real" family and had never loved him, "assisting" the young demon's tormented and guilt-ridden mind by telling him to rationalize that his "true" family would never try to kill him and that he could simply search for a "new" family as a demon. Eventually obtaining the young demon's loyalty as a result of him "helping" him. After these events, Rui continued killing and devouring humans and was eventually awarded with the position of Lower Rank 5 among the Twelve Kizuki, where Rui soon became something of a favorite of Muzan's. As seen where despite the Demon King's usual policy and law of preventing any demons from banding and teaming up together in large groups, Rui was actually given special permission by Muzan to create his own "family" to satisfy his yearning for one, which then lead to the creation of the Spider Family. A privilege not even given to those of the Upper Ranks. Kyogai. Initially, Muzan had considered Kyogai as a special demon with an invaluable power due to his Blood Demon Arts, earning Muzan's favor and causing him to have high hopes for Kyogai's continued development as a demon as he grew stronger. Eventually causing the Demon King to give Kyogai the rank of Lower Rank Six due to his abilities and possible powerful potential. This in turn caused Kyogai to harbor a powerful sense of loyalty and admiration to Muzan due to him being the first person to truly "value" him for his talents and abilities and upon drinking a small amount of Muzan's blood and having his powers further enhanced, Kyogai respect for the Demon King only deepened due to realizing how mind blowing the amount of power he could obtain from him and took immense pride at him having been accepted by Muzan as one of the Twelve Kizuki. However upon Kyogai reaching his "limit" and gradually losing his ability to eat human flesh and grow stronger, Muzan was shown to have completely lost his original favor to the demon, coldly rebuffing Kyogai upon properly seeing his complete loss of appetite for human flesh despite his pleas for more time to prove himself and swiftly removed him from the position of Lower Rank 6 by cutting his digit rank from his eye. Despite this horrible treatment, Kyogai is shown to still retain his admiration and loyalty towards the Demon King and has instead gone to extreme lengths to strengthen himself and grow his power despite already hitting his "limit" in order to once again reclaim his rank among the Twelve Kizuki by eating Marechi. Tamayo. In their initial encounter, Muzan turned Tamayo into a demon in order to cure her disease, hiding from her the true consequences of the transformation and so causing the death of her husband and kids. Much like Nezuko, Muzan views her as a nuisance to him after she was freed of his control, and desires for her to be killed. He didn't hesitate to mock Tamayo about killing her husband and children as well as going on a rampage out of despair killing other humans in the process, placing all the blame on her without taking responsibility for any of it. Prior to this, hundreds of years ago, Tamayo had attempted to kill Muzan. However, upon realizing that she stood absolutely no chance of winning, Tamayo's mental state was completely defeated, her resolve and determination replaced by a docile, servant-like demeanour. However, upon witnessing Yoriichi's immense power and skill during his fight with Muzan, Tamayo's resolve to kill him was reignited, causing her to once again refocus her efforts onto defeating the Demon King and restart her research into creating drugs for weakening or killing him. Both had the power to turn others into demons, but while Tamayo used her power to save lives, Muzan instead used this power to take them and to transform them into his servants.

Muzan Kibutsuji/Synopsis History. Muzan was born in Japan's Heian era, to a constant struggle to survive on account of his frailty. His heart stopped multiple times in his mother's womb, and when he first entered the world, he was deemed stillborn, having no pulse and not breathing. When he was taken to be cremated, he escaped death by releasing his first cries. Throughout his young life, he struggled with illnesses and that led to his thanatophobia. As a young man, Muzan was diagnosed with a disease that would kill him before he reached the age of 20. The doctor treating Muzan gave him a special experimental medicine, but it appeared to have failed. Enraged by his worsening condition, Muzan killed him. However, it was only after killing the doctor did he realize that the medicine was actually working and had helped him acquire a strong body. He realized he needed to consume the flesh of humans to survive but was not bothered by this. However his new, more serious problem is that he was unable to walk in sunlight anymore, as doing so burned him severely, even realizing that it would kill and turn him into ashes. He deeply resented the thought of having to spend the rest of his life avoiding sunlight during the day and having going out at night, and it was only then that he came to truly regret his foolish decision to kill the doctor before the latter had finished treating him with his medicine. Upon conducting research on the contents of the medicine that the doctor had made for him, he discovered that it contained a rare component called the Blue Spider Lily. Believing that if he consumed one, it could nullify his weakness to sunlight, he searched the entire country for the flower, but couldn't find it as the only person who knew about them was the doctor he killed, and that Muzan was unware that it only bloomed during daytime for at most 2-3 days a year. Obsessed with walking at daytime, even though he had obtained great power, Muzan considered himself to be imperfect and wanted to be rid of his weakness to sunlight. This desire eventually became an obsession that he would chase for the next 1000 years and with the search for the Blue Spider Lily going nowhere, he started to use his blood to turn people into demons, under his control, hoping that one of them would eventually find the Blue Spider Lily, or creating more demons, he hoped that one day, one of them would be able to withstand sunlight; once this happened, he could take their immunity to sunlight for himself by consuming them and then finally achieve his goal of conquering the sun and becoming truly immortal. In his early years as a demon, Muzan settled down with five different women. However, because of his lack of empathy and sensitivity as a demon, he verbally abused all five of his wives to the point it drove them all to commit suicide. Muzan found a young girl named Tamayo, who was afflicted with a disease that threatened her life. She encounters Muzan and, wishing to see her children grow up, allowed him to transform her. Unused to her new body, she inadvertently killed her own family to survive, as well as another group of people. This decision haunted her to no end and she became resentful and hateful of Muzan. But due to Muzan's immense power, she was unable to kill him with success. Muzan enslaved Tamayo and she followed him around as a lowly servant. Sometime after, he finds Michikatsu Tsugikuni, a marked Demon Slayer and user of the Moon Breathing style. Michikatsu wanted to become more powerful than his brother and loathed the fact that his status of being marked meant his life would soon end. Muzan issued a compromise; he wished to have a breath using Demon and in return, he could live forever and perfect his skill. Michikatsu agreed and Muzan gave him an extremely high concentration of his blood, emerging three days later transformed and taking the name Kokushibo. Later, Muzan and Tamayo would encounter Yoriichi Tsugikuni, who was Michikatsu' younger twin brother and another Demon Slayer. The moment the two met, Yoriichi sensed Muzan's malice and anger, comparing him to boiling magma. Simultaneously, Muzan found nothing in Yoriichi that resembled something dangerous and didn't fear his opponent. Already satisfied having Kokushibo as his subordinate, Muzan tried to kill Yoriichi without warning. He, however, was able to dodge the blows and discerned Muzan's weak spots, seven hearts and five brains that move freely around his body. Yoriichi combined all his forms into one strike and turned his blade bright red, enabling him to cut through all of Muzan's weaknesses and overpower him. For the first time in his life, Muzan became stunned, unable to heal, he sat in a pool of his blood and angrily stared at Yoriichi, ignoring his question on what he thought was the value of a life. When Yoriichi moved forward to kill him, Muzan used the remains of whatever power he had left and divided his body in a powerful burst. Though Yoriichi was able to destroy nearly all the fragments, the pieces he missed escaped and allowed Muzan to regenerate again. Muzan was deeply scarred by this encounter and with Kokushibo's assistance, the two slaughtered anyone who used Sun Breathing, in the hopes of preventing another Demon Slayer that had the power to kill him. They were almost successful and able to nearly exterminate Sun Breathing entirely. Greatly fearful of the man he considered the real demon, Muzan never directly confronted the Demon Slayers again and sent demons to do his bidding for the most part. He remained fearful of Yoriichi even after his death. Muzan heard news of a massacre involving the violent deaths of sixty seven people. He travelled to the village before meeting the culprit, an eighteen year old boy named Hakuji. He voiced his disappointment as he believed a demon had committed the act, instead of a human. Hakuji threatened him but was silenced by Muzan piercing his hand through his head. The Demon King spoke of his plan to form a faction of twelve powerful demons and asked the young man if he was able to withstand the amount of blood he was given. Hakuji, broken by his loss and with nothing else left, didn't resist and became the demon Akaza. In time, Muzan eventually succeeded in creating his faction, which would eventually become known as the Twelve Kizuki. He transformed multiple demons and gave them the chance to join his group, rewarding them with a larger share of his blood to make them more powerful. Split into two groups of six known as the Upper Ranks and Lower Ranks, the Uppers remained unchanged for over for a century. The Lowers on the other hand, constantly changed as they were frequently killed by the Demon Slayers, to his growing disappointment. The Kizuki who he personally transformed were Kokushibo, Akaza, a nihilistic but convivial cult leader, a prolific and heinous criminal sentenced to death, a dying child murderer, a frail young boy, and a sadistic young man who he initially devoured but eventually transformed. In time, he allowed for the Upper Ranks to be able to recruit humans by giving them their blood, but they had to be approved by Muzan himself before becoming full-fledged members. More demons would eventually join the Twelve Kizuki, such as a misanthropic brother and sister hailing from the red-light district slums, a twisted and murderous musician, a mocked songwriter, and a traitorous former Demon Slayer. Muzan often gave random civilians his blood in order to create at least one demon with the power to withstand the sun, as a backup plan in case he still hadn't located the blue spider lily. While some painfully died due to the immense power of his blood destroying them from the inside, others were successfully turned into demons but had lost all their memories as humans and became either cruel and murderous, or feral and beastly. This included a single mother of 7, who killed 5 of her own children while in a mindless state before being killed by her eldest. During the Taisho Era, Muzan was able to locate the Kamado family who were keepers of the Sun Breathing technique. When the eldest child, Tanjiro Kamado, was away at town, Muzan attacked them and proceeded to inject them with his blood, hopping that he could turn them into demons that could withstand sunlight. However, he was disappointed when the family didn't survive, and believed that creating a demon capable of withstanding sunlight not so easy after all. He left their home, unaware that one girl, Nezuko Kamado, survived and became a demon. Synopsis. Kidnapper's Bog Arc. Muzan is first mentioned when Sakonji Urokodaki tells Tanjiro Kamado that he is the one responsible for the Kamado family massacre and that he might know how to turn Nezuko back into a human. Asakusa Arc. Traveling through a crowd in Asakusa, Tokyo with his "family," Muzan is accosted by an angry Tanjiro. Muzan's daughter asks him who the young Demon Slayer was, and he asks the youth if there was something he wanted from him. His wife then approached them, asking if Tanjiro was somebody familiar to their family. Muzan denies this, suggesting the boy had mistaken them for somebody else. He then quickly slashes a passing man, turning him into a demon. During the commotion, he and his family leave while Tanjiro is forced to tend to the demonfied man. Afterwards, Muzan sends his family home in a carriage without him, declaring he had some work to do. He wanders through an alley, where a drunk man bumps into him. The man then mocks and insults him, saying he doesn't like wealthy people like him. When the drunk man notes how pale his skin is, Muzan smashes him into a wall and also proceeds to kill the man's older brother with a swift upwards kick. He then turns to the cowering female companion and asks if he looks pale or close to death. Muzan answers his own questions and tells her how he is infinitely close to perfection. He then drills his finger into her forehead, injecting her with so much of his blood that her cells melt. Afterwards, he calls Susamaru and Yahaba and orders them to kill Tanjiro. Rehabilitation Training Arc. Since Muzan is able to discern the locations of Demons whom he has given blood to, he is seemingly capable of locating Nezuko at the Ubuyashiki Estate. However, he is unaware that Tamayo had removed his curse from Nezuko, making him incapable of detecting her whereabouts. The Lower Ranks have a meeting, where Muzan appears in the form of a woman. He is very disappointed after Rui's defeat, so much so that he declares that he will disband the Lower Ranks and that he will now lead only the Upper Ranks. He kills Kamanue after reading his mind when he thought disrespectful thoughts and Mukago for contradicting him. As Wakuraba tries to escape, Muzan decapitates him and renders him unable to regenerate. Rokuro tries to plead with his master and asks for more of his blood to prove himself. Seeing the Demon as a failure, Muzan becomes incredibly angry and kills him for "ordering" his leader. Before killing Enmu, the Demon states how much he enjoys making humans suffer and thanks Muzan for letting him be his final victim. Seeing potential in Enmu, Muzan gives him a high abundance of blood. Enmu almost dies from the new load of power, but manages to survive. Muzan then gives him one last chance to prove that the Lower Ranks are not useless. However, Enmu failed and was killed by the Demon Slayer Corps, putting an end to the Lower Ranks permanently. Entertainment District Arc. Muzan leads another life among humans as a small boy named Toshikuni and pretends to have a skin condition which prevents him from stepping into the sun. After killing Kyojuro Rengoku, Akaza reports to Muzan and tells him of his victory. However, Muzan is not pleased enough by the death of the Hashira and instead shows anger that Akaza let all the other present Demon Slayers get away, additionally berating him for not finding more information on the Blue Spider Lily. In the Entertainment District of Yoshiwara, Muzan visits Daki. He tells her how proud of her he is and that he hopes she will become even crueler and stronger. He also lets her know about Nezuko and tasks her with killing her. Swordsmith Village Arc. After the Upper Six siblings are defeated, he has the other Upper Ranks meet in the Infinity Castle. He is standing on the ceiling and experimenting, trying to heal his sun weakness. Muzan tells them that he won't allow any failures such as Daki and Gyutaro. Muzan regrets putting so much confidence in her and wishes Gyutaro had fought since the beginning. He tells them to serve him with more suicidal devotion and states how he hates change. He believes change only means decline and he didn't change for so long, since he is practically perfect. He then sent Gyokko and Hantengu to destroy the swordsmith village before departing from the meeting. While in disguise as a small boy, Muzan feels through Hantengu that Nezuko is able to withstand sunlight, thus making his assault on the Sun Breathing family a success. His excitement alerts his foster mother and maid, who he immediately kills as he sets his mind on getting Nezuko and devouring her to finally become immortal. Hashira Training Arc. As Muzan prepares to battle the Demon Slayers Corps over Nezuko, he appoints Nakime as Upper Rank 4 and makes her more powerful. He uses her tracking skills to scout out the whereabouts of all Demon Slayers. He is quite impressed by her efforts and compliments her, as he is sure to find Nezuko and the Corps' leaders soon. Final Battle Arc. Infinity Castle Arc. Muzan appears at the Ubuyashiki mansion and sees Kagaya. He mocks him for his weak appearance. Kagaya tries to lecture Muzan and points out how the Hashira will never give up trying to kill him. Muzan laughs and proceeds to attack Kagaya. Before he can kill him however, the mansion explodes, with Muzan caught in it. The explosion, which was enhanced by spike traps, manages to injure Muzan. Before he is able to regenerate fully, Tamayo appears and uses her Blood Demon Art to keep him in place, while using a drug that can turn him into human. Using this opportunity, Gyomei Himejima appears and destroys Muzan's head. However he is able to instantly regrow his head. As all of the other Hashira join the fight, the Infinity Castle appears as if sucking in all the people nearby and scattering them. Muzan claims he will slaughter them all tonight. As the Demon Slayers manage to beat the majority of the Upper Ranks and attempt to locate Muzan, several lower ranked members are able to find his cocoon. Emerging from it, he proceeds to eviscerate all the Demon Slayers in his proximity, as he tries to regain the stamina lost from his struggle against Tamayo. He takes her head and mocks her for being unable to kill him, ridiculing that the drug she designed was useless. Tamayo angrily demands Muzan to return her family to her, to which Muzan replies she should join them on the other side and crushes her head, which Yushiro senses. He further proceeds to slaughter Demon Slayers and reaffirms his vow to kill all of them. Through Nakime's ability, Muzan is placed face to face with Tanjiro and Giyu. Muzan asks Tanjiro why he is so concerned with revenge against him, when he got out of the massacre of his family alive, and thus can resume his life if he wanted to. Comparing himself to a "Great Calamity" he states that it is impossible for humans to take revenge on natural disasters like rain, winds, volcanic eruptions or earthquakes take the lives of dear ones, humans keep on living, and that fighting him amounts to the same kind of folly. He thus concludes that the Demon Slayers fight him because they are a group of deviants, and that he has tired of dealing with them and is the only one who wants to truly put and it to the fight. An enraged Tanjiro claims Muzan should not have been allowed to exist. A battle ensues with Muzan extending his arms into long bladed whips keeping Giyu and Tanjiro at bay, as the latter infuriated at Muzan's inhumanity Tanjiro navigates between Muzan's strikes and attempts at infiltrating but is ultimately unsuccessful and slashed near his eye. Giyu pulls Tanjiro away reminding the latter that Muzan's power is above any of the Upper Demons. Muzan wonders if they can defeat him with just three Hashira, as he declares that Mitsuri and Obanai were killed by Nakime. Muzan performs more sweeps that Tanjiro can hardly avoid due to his injured eye, as he stumbles. Before he can kill Tanjiro, Mitsuri appears smashing the walls and attacking Muzan with her Love Breathing, Sixth Form: Cat-Legged Winds of Love, but is unable to inflict any damage on Muzan, much to her frustration. Obanai also appears revealing both Hashira to be alive. An angered Muzan demands explanations from Nakime only to learn that Yushiro has used his own Blood Demon Art to take control of Nakime and that he will force Muzan out of the Infinity Castle. Further angered by the opposition, Muzan tries to wrestle control of the Castle back from Yushiro as he tries to absorb his cells through Nakime, an attack from Giyu and Obanai, force Muzan in the defensive allowing Yushiro to win control, so Muzan remotely detonates Nakime crushing her head. While her remaining cells still alive, Yushiro uses them to take control of the Castle as it continuously shifts. Muzan performs more sweeps which manage to slash Tanjiro, as the Castle shakes being forced into the outside. Before Muzan can land a critical blow on Mitsuri, Tanjiro throws a broken Nichirin Sword which stabs Muzan in his head, causing him to miss. He grows furious with Tanjiro as the Castle breaks into the surface. Sunrise Countdown Arc. Now at a city, the Demon Slayers are told to stall Muzan for one more hour and a half until sunrise. A furious Muzan now with whips from his spine, emerges from debris and dares them to try, wildly swinging his limbs. The Hashira seize a chance to slash him, but to their surprise he regenerates so fast that he cannot be decapitated. Before he can fatally wound them, hordes of lesser ranked Demon Slayers push the Hashira out of harm's way, ready to die as human shields as Muzan murders dozens of them. He muses that they were fortunate to die immediately and points to Tanjiro as an example of the contrary. Showing a horrible facial burn, Muzan reveals he injected his blood into Tanjiro on his earlier attack, and that his body will be destroyed, boasting that he is already dead. Muzan and the Hashira exchange blows and notices that Demon Slayers with their mark activated can resist the effect of his demonic blood. As Muzan tries to land a killing blow on Mitsuri, Gyomei saves her. Sanemi takes the chance to slash Muzan from behind who reacts to the Hashira's attack. Sanemi tosses vials filled with flammable liquid and proceeds to set Muzan ablaze, to which the progenitor Demon protests as dirty. Sanemi proceeds to insult him and say he is the dirty one and vows to kill Muzan. As the battle rages on the Hashira have difficulty in fighting Muzan who proves to be too powerful for them. An exhausted Mitsuri who does nothing but evade is ultimately injured and forced out of the fight despite her desire to battle. Obanai takes notice and tries to fight harder against Muzan, trying to slice and kick his severed member away to delay his regeneration, but only making a minimal difference. Remembering his own past, decides to fight for her sake and die to meet her in another life. Muzan's blood begins to damage the Hashira, Giyu loses the ability to hold his Nichirin Sword, with only a little more than 15 minutes passing. When all seemed lost, Chachamaru, Tamayo's cat servant, appears and throws syringes at the Hashira, dosing them with a serum that counteracts Muzan's poison. Muzan kills the cat, and grows annoyed how Tamayo still gets in his way even after death. Obanai thinks in how Muichiro may have managed to get his blade to turn bright red, and puts all his focus and effort into his grip, turning it red, however, he starts to lose consciousness due to lack of oxygen, barely able to avoid Muzan's attacks and Giyu unable to reach in time. Obanai is sent mid-air and miraculously manages to avoid Muzan's attack as Muzan's right arm and spinal whips are sliced. Muzan is left wondering how did it happen and realizes it is impossible for any of the Hashira to have been able to cut him, he is then sliced in his left arm now which makes him notice the uneven cut he has in his arm. Muzan correctly deduces that somebody is attacking him while hidden through Yushiro's technique. Feeling the air around him parting, he narrows the location of his three attackers, being none other than Inosuke, Zenitsu and Kanao whom he manages to barely slash. Gyomei is surprised to see them alive and Inosuke boasts that he has an enormous supply of Yushiro's paper so whatever Muzan tries is useless but is scolded for chatting more than necessary. Obanai takes the chance to slice Muzan's arms which regenerate slower due to his bright red blade, a fact Sanemi points out. Zenitsu and Kanao turn invisible again and attack Muzan in unison, causing the demon to complain in irritation at their small tricks. Gyomei is glad to have more support as he is able to clash his axe and iron ball to heat them through friction, increasing their attack power. Gyomei soon smashes the left side of Muzan's torso. Sanemi and Giyu follow suit and clash their blades turning them bright red. The Kasugai Crow proclaims that 1 hour and 3 minutes remain before dawn, with the Demon Slayers regaining advantage. The Demon Slayers take advantage of Yushiro's papers allowing them to see one another and launch a relentless assault on Muzan. Gyomei concentrates and is able to discern Muzan's unnatural biology, advising them to concentrate so they are able to see them too. Suddenly Muzan performs an undisclosed technique allowing him to defeat all his attackers simultaneously, injuring and having them crash on nearby buildings, mutilating Gyomei's left leg and Giyu's right arm in the process. Kanao Tsuyuri is left with a broken blade kneeling in shock. Before Muzan can kill her, a recovered Tanjiro saves her slicing Muzan's arm leaving him shocked, and has her taken to a medic Demon Slayer for safety. Seeing Tanjiro's mutated face as a result of his poison, Muzan comments that he looks terrible, and wonders now who is the true Demon between the two of them. Seeing Yoriichi's image in Tanjiro, Muzan feels disgust at the Demon Slayer, while Tanjiro states it is time they finish things. Their battle begins with Tanjiro remembering the forms of the Sun Breathing he witnessed during his dream, and his father's advice, he comes to realize that the forms must be employed consecutively one after the other, which will lead to the 13th and strongest form. Though he feels discouraged at not having Yoriichi's or his father's skill Tanjiro nonetheless ventures to attack Muzan who sees the ghost of his former enemy on the younger Demon Slayer. Tanjiro is able to discern Muzan's secret technique, an array of additional whips catapulted from his tights at immense speed taking his enemies by surprise after accustoming them to his current attack style. Turning his blade bright red, Tanjiro begins to unleash the Sun Breathing forms, trying to become stronger in the brink of death. Muzan is unimpressed as Tanjiro's technique is far from Yoriichi's level, seeing him losing strength he tries to secure the chance to end Tanjiro once and for all who is weakening from exhaustion and his own injuries. Muzan, however is unable to land a finishing blow much to his own surprise and realizes he too is growing weaker. He deduces that it must be Tamayo's doing as he had absorbed her cells and tries to communicate with her essence in the cells to ask what was the drug she injected him with was truly about. Tamayo's essence merely mocks him, much to Muzan's irritation who proceeds to destroy what remains of her consciousness and scan her memories instead. Witnessing her memories he comes to learn the truth, that Tamayo, Yushiro and Shinobu Kocho did indeed develop a drug that turned Demons into humans but added an additional poison with a powerful aging effect that would trigger with greater potency on its own in the case the humanizing venom would fail, making Muzan age at a rate of 50 years per minute. Muzan realizes that his body has weakened as it is struggling to keep his body youthful. He begins calculating the time the drug has been active, for roughly 3 hours, meaning he has aged 9,000 years. Tanjiro keeps unleashing successive forms of the Sun Breathing, irritating the Demon King with his persistence. With 59 minutes left before dawn Tanjiro is able to connect all the twelve forms and resolves himself to reuse them all faster than before. Chachamaru is revealed to have survived Muzan's attack as Yushiro had demonified the cat before the fight. He proceeds to nurse the injured Demon Slayers. He concludes that Gyomei is unable to fight any longer due to blood and limb loss, before treating the others. Muzan continues to lash at Tanjiro who is slowly being overcome with oxygen deprivation and losing his footing, but is saved by Obanai who was restored to health by Yushiro and who is revealed to have lost his sight during Muzan's earlier use of his leg tentacles. Tanjiro is worried but Obanai reassures him he can see through Kaburamaru. The two split as Muzan chases after Obanai and obliterates a building trying to kill him but fails. Muzan is in disbelief that a mere snake can help the Demon Slayer read his attacks, as Obanai and Tanjiro combine attacks. As Muzan grows weaker from the aging venom and the efforts of the Demon Slayers, scars become visible across all of Muzan's body. Tanjiro realizes those are the wounds inflicted by Yoriichi, burned down to a celular level which never healed despite hundreds of years and which reveal his weak points. Muzan grows horrified at the sight of his wounds, thinking that Yoriichi, a mere man who displayed no apparent hostility was in fact the true monster between the two of them by crippling him the way he did. Tanjiro and Obanai continue their assault on Muzan now with 40 minutes left before dawn. Muzan grows restless and tries to escape trampling over the corpses of the Demon Slayers he slaughtered. This enrages Tanjiro who proceeds to throw multiple Nichirin Swords at Muzan who deflects them reasoning that stabs are much worse than mere slashes now. Obanai stabs Muzan in the neck from behind, making the latter use his spinal whips which are stopped by Tanjiro, who tries to give Obanai a pair of Yushiro's blindfolds so he can share Kaburamaru's vision. Although Muzan wounds the two of them to block their efforts, Kaburamaru succeeds in fetching the papers allowing Obanai to fight in much better condition. Muzan slowly succumbs into panic as he is running out of breath as his strength is reaching critical lows. Their battle is witnessed from afar by Nezuko who cries out of her right eye. Muzan is further pressured by the attacks of Tanjiro and Obanai and with 35 minutes before dawn, Muzan deems it an unnecessary risk to continue the fight and attempts to divide himself into lumps, escaping in the same manner he did against Yoriichi. Tanjiro alerts Obanai of this and panics at the idea that the two of them won't be able to destroy all the flesh lumps. However, Muzan is unable to split as a 3rd drug injected by Tamayo has the property to slow down cell division. Muzan communicates with the essence of Tamayo who gleefully alerts him that there were not three effects but four, with the fourth drug causing Muzan to cough blood as it triggers cell destruction after the 3rd effect activated. The essence of Tamayo taunts Muzan that the death he so much feared is coming for him, further elaborating she doesn't need to be stronger than him to kill him as weakening him suffices, taunting him that just as he will do everything to live, they will do everything to kill him. Muzan ponders that normally the attacks used by the Demon Slayers shouldn't be threatening nor should prolonged regeneration prove tiring, but Tamayo's drugs have turned otherwise manageable attacks into lethal threats and that he is unable to fully get accustomed to the toxins in his body which are much different than those used to kill Doma. In a desperate attempt to live, Muzan opens a gaping mouth in his chest and unleashes a potent discharge against Obanai and Tanjiro, leaving the latter convulsing and stunned. With just 25 minutes left before dawn, the weakened Kiriya who witnesses the fight from afar begs for someone to stall Muzan. His pleas are answered when Inosuke attacks Muzan lunging at the Demon King furious for the previous thrashing and mourning the comrades Muzan has killed and injured. Muzan unable to further use his previous technique retorts to lunging his arm into the ground wrapping Inosuke with his tentacle. Inosuke is saved by the timely intervention of Zenitsu who tells Inosuke that Tanjiro is still alive, begging the latter to remain alive for the sake of Nezuko who is returning to normalcy. Muzan swings his arm at Zenitsu crashing him into a building, but is saved by Inosuke who stabs his arm only to be swathed away by another swing in the process. Muzan is under heavy fatigue and irritated as the boys continue to stand up to fight him. Inosuke and Zenitsu continue his assault on Muzan with the latter using his Thunder Breathing, Seventh Form: Honoikazuchi no Kami managing to slash Muzan but the attack was more shallow than expected. Inosuke keeps attacking Muzan with his techniques forcing the Demon King to employ its shockwave once more. Before he can attack Inosuke, Tanjiro recovers and unleashes successive Sun Breathing techniques realizing Muzan needs to recharge before using his shockwave attack. Tanjiro weakens after using the Sun Breathing: Sun Halo Dragon Head Dance, giving Muzan an opening, but has his tubes sliced by Inosuke. Zenitsu tries to join the fight but is unable to muster enough speed to use his techniques. Muzan swathes Inosuke away to a building and Tanjiro loses footing, but Zenitsu manages to recover enough to use one last attack, but is himself injured by Muzan. Tanjiro seizes the chance and stabs Muzan pinning him to a building, unable to use any more techniques as he gambles it all in keeping Muzan in place. Muzan tries to kill Tanjiro but a recovered Kanroji entagles herself to his tentacles while ripping his left arm tearfully yelling him to stop, while Muzan's right arm and tentacles are sliced by Sanemi. Left with little choice, a bifurcation appears in Muzan's front, revealing an enormous bestial mouth trying to eat Tanjiro who cannot do anything but remain in place. To protect him, Obanai puts himself in harm's way as he is mauled by Muzan, as dawn is breaking. Muzan panics at the sight of the sun and desperately unleashes a powerful shockwave, catapulting his attackers away except for Tanjiro who loses his left arm but firmly stays in place trying to turn his blade bright red, when Giyu appears to aid him and together the blade changes injuring Muzan. In response to the sun's menace Muzan proceeds to enlarge himself, adopting a large demonic baby form and absorbing Tanjiro in the process. As Muzan tries to get into shade, hordes of Demon Slayers block his path by tossing bookshelves and ramming vehicles on him, as he fights back for a way through. He is soon blocked by another group of Demon Slayers pushing a bus on him to prevent his escape. Muzan soon begins burning from the sun forcing him to fight for his life. Before he can overwhelm the lower ranked Slayers, Sanemi appears and slices his right arm, cursing the demon's persistence and demanding him to die. As he tries to climb over the bus blockade, he has a chain tied to his neck by Gyomei, aided by multiple Slayers who pull together to bring Muzan down. As he burns further Muzan resorts too digging as an escape maneuver forcing Giyu, Sanemi and Obanai to attack him to deplete his stamina. Soon the chains breaks in what appears to be a hopeless moment, but Tanjiro who remains within Muzan is able to ignite his blade and injure him from the inside causing Muzan to flinch from the pain as he begins disintegrating from the sun's light. As his body fully burns into ash, the once invincible Demon King who ruled the shadows of Japan, spreading misery and suffering for a millennia, finally laid in defeat, ending the seemingly eternal war with the Demon Slayers' victory. Legacy. Muzan's defeat, while significant, would prove to be a costly victory for the Demon Slayers, leaving scores of members deceased, dozens mauled and heavily injured, and many on the verge of death. Additionally, despite Muzan's death, with his last breaths, he managed to turn Tanjiro into a demon. As Muzan transfers his blood and memories into Tanjiro's dying body, he is able to successfully revive him as a demon, deeming him the King of Demons he influences Tanjiro into conquering the sunlight and achieving his dream to end the Demon Slayer Corps. Tanjiro's poisoned eye is restored along with regenerating his left arm, as the young Slayer rampages in a feral state against the rest of the Demon Slayers and successfully overcomes the sun. Although the new Demon King was fundamentally invincible, Tanjiro's consciousness would fight back for control with the help of Nezuko and Kanao, the latter who used the humanizing drug as a conduit for everyone's pleas to reach Tanjiro. The reminder of Muzan's will resorted to deception and psychological torture in order to convince Tanjiro to embrace his new demon heritage, but in absolute contrast to all the Demon King ever stood for, Tanjiro rejects the immortality and powers of demonhood in favor of living the few years he has left in peace as a human with everyone's company, leaving Muzan's spirit behind putting both a definitive end to his reign of terror once and for all, avenging their tragic victim's deaths and to atone his sins for eternity in Avici; the worst and the most torturous region of all hells.

Nagakura is a Demon Slayer from the Demon Slayer Corps. Appearance. Nagakura is a male with trimmed hair and a noticeably round nose. Personality. Not much is known about his personality, but he is impressed by the Hashira's skills. History. At a point in his life, Nagakura joined the Demon Slayer Corps. Synopsis. Hashira Training Arc. Nagakura is seen eating and conversing with Murata. Sunrise Countdown Arc. Nagakura is shown killed by Muzan's attacks while protecting Tanjiro Kamado from the Demon Lord. Abilities. Nagakura is presumed to have average Demon Slayer abilities, surviving the initial raid of the Infinity Castle, but still perished at the hands of Muzan.

Naho Takada is a servant of the Butterfly Mansion. Appearance. Naho is a light-skinned, young girl with black button-like eyes. Her hair is parted in the middle with two braided twin tails tied with green butterfly clips. She wears a long-sleeved nurse uniform with a green wrap tied into a bow around her waist and white socks and shoes. Personality. Naho is bright, cheery, and helpful, readily willing to help others. History. After her family had been attacked by demons, Naho was taken in by the Butterfly Mansion by Shinobu and Kanae Kocho, along with Kiyo Terauchi and Sumi Nakahara. When Kanae was killed by a demon, she mourned her death with the rest of her adoptive family. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. Naho, along with Kiyo and Sumi, aided in rehabilitating Tanjiro Kamado, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira after becoming wounded during their battles on Mount Natagumo. The girls were responsible for stretching their bodies to become more limber, following their long stays in bed while in recovery. Later, seeing Tanjiro grow frustrated at his lack of progress during rehabilitation against Kanao Tsuyuri, the three offered him advice regarding Total Concentration Constant, the key to the Hashira's and Kanao's superior abilities. They later informed Tanjiro that Kanao trains with special gourds to increase lung power, which he takes on enthusiastically. He later tasks them with beating him awake with carpet beaters should he stop using Total Concentration while sleeping, which they do with glee. Eventually, Tanjiro improves his strength and speed, to the point where he can now contend with Kanao and destroy a small gourd. After Zenitsu and Inosuke follow Tanjiro's lead and all three succeed in mastering Total Concentration, Constant, they soon depart for their mission to assist the Flame Hashira. Naho and the girls see them off, tearfully telling them to be careful, though when Zenitsu asks if they are upset to see him leave, they deny it. Entertainment District Arc. Naho and Aoi were both abducted by Tengen Uzui, who needed female Demon Slayers to infiltrate Tokyo's Yoshiwara. Kanao, Kiyo, and Sumi tried to stop the Hashira from doing so but they could not free them from the much bigger Demon Slayer. Tanjiro had interrupted when he heard the commotion and asked Tengen to release the girls, to which Tengen responded that he needs a female Demon Slayer to come with him for his mission and had planned for them to come. One of the little girls said that Naho doesn't even have the demon slayer uniform on, prompting him to throw her off, with Tanjiro catching her. Abilities. As an ordinary human, Naho does not possess any additional powers or abilities. However, being one of the staff at the hospital ward of the Butterfly Mansion, she possesses a fair amount of knowledge. Notably, she helped teach Tanjiro the essential path to becoming stronger.

Nakime is a recurring character and a supporting antagonist in the Infinity Castle Arc of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She is a demon who owns and controls the Infinity Castle and serves directly under Muzan Kibutsuji. Some time after Hantengu's death during the battle in the Swordsmith Village, Nakime attains the position of in the Twelve Kizuki. Appearance. Nakime is a pale woman with a grayish complexion, who has sharp, blue-stained nails and notably red lips which sharply contrasted the tone of her skin. She has shiny, hip-length hair of a dark brown color, which she wore falling down her back in slight waves that cut off sharply at the ends, with two chin-length strands left to frame her face and long bangs that obscured her large eye set in between them, swept to either side of her nose. Nakime dons a plain black kimono with a muted white lining, secured with a striped pale brown-striped obi, white socks and no shoes or clogs. She was always seen holding a four-stringed wooden with a large . Since becoming an Upper Rank, Nakime took to wearing her bangs as to not obscure her face, showing that she possessed a single large, pink-colored eye with the for engraved into its iris. The upper portion of her face was also revealed, and appeared to be a darker gray color than the rest of her pale skin with prominent veins surrounding her one eye. Personality. Nakime is aloof and taciturn, almost never speaking and displaying little to no emotion or will outside of obeying orders. She was extremely loyal to Muzan, listening and following his every order faultlessly, something he appreciated; in fact, her unwavering loyalty to him is one of the very few instances Muzan ever complimented an individual, though it seemed more likely that he was satisfied to have a powerful tool to use at his disposal. Despite this outwardly one-sided relationship, Nakime graciously accepted his words and told her master she was honored to be of great use to him. She showed little interaction with other demons and seems to be mostly disinterested in their presence. During the Lower Ranks Meeting, she calmly sat by and observed with the same stone-faced expression as the demons were all ruthlessly killed, almost paying them no attention and simply waiting for Muzan to give her another order. Similarly, in the Upper Ranks Meeting later on, she only speaks during two instances; answering Akaza's queries and rejecting Doma's invitation to be at his temple. Despite this, in her battle against Obanai Iguro and Mitsuri Kanroji, Nakime appeared to be very confident in her powers and did not regard the threat the two posed on her, remaining unmoving as the Hashira launched numerous attacks against her that would prove futile due to her vast and highly unorthodox powers. History. In the past, Nakime was an obscure amateur biwa musician struggling to make ends meet. The man she married to was hopelessly addicted to gambling who squandered her earnings and savings while contributing nothing to improve their lives. One night, she was scheduled to play her biwa at a particular stage but discovered that her husband stole her only kimono that she used for biwa performances and gambled it away. Enraged, Nakime murdered her husband using a hammer. Shortly after she killed her husband, Nakime realized that the appointed time to play was fast approaching, and she was forced to wear a worn-out, tattered kimono. The crowd did not appreciate her shabby looks and gave her disapproving looks. With the traumatic sensation of committing the murder for the first time still fresh in her mind, her hands shook in nervousness as she played her biwa. But surprisingly, the sound coming from biwa as Nakime played with utmost tension, was so beautiful that her audience loved her performance and shouted for encore. Both her customers and the stage owner were pleased with the unexpected outcome and Nakime was paid handsomely. Since then, Nakime developed a disturbing habit of killing people before performing for large audiences. Every time the sound of her biwa was highly commended and her performance would receive extraordinarily positive feedback. During a fateful day, when she had a routine appointment to perform at stage again, she randomly chose a new person to kill and the target happens to be Muzan. She tried to kill him but failed. Muzan was impressed with Nakime's searching skills and pleased with what she did, so he spared her life and offered to make her a demon. Nakime accepted his offer, became a demon and climbed the ranks quicky and became one of Muzan's top servants. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. Following the death of Lower Rank Five Rui, Nakime was ordered by Muzan to summon the remaining members to the Infinity Castle.She summons them in order: Enmu was the first to be transported to her space, followed by Rokuro, Wakuraba, Mukago, and finally Kamanue. Once all members were present, she takes them all to a platform that stood before her and a disguised Muzan. Nakime sat and silently observed as Muzan proceeded to admonish and kill each member of the Lower Ranks. After he spares Enmu and gives him his blood, while providing a chance at receiving more, Nakime shortly after transported Muzan to the top of the castle near the surface, while manipulating Enmu's position to take him to an undisclosed town through supernatural doors. Swordsmith Village Arc. Nakime once again plays her biwa to summon the Upper Ranks to a meeting after Daki and Gyutaro's deaths.When Akaza asks her where Muzan is, she replies straightforwardly that he has not yet arrived. She is also questioned as to where Upper Rank One is, to which she replies that he has always been inside the castle, as Kokushibo was the first to arrive.During the meeting, she once again sat quietly as Muzan berated the Upper Ranks for their continual failures to find the Blue Spider Lily and kill the Ubuyashikis. After he gives the Upper Ranks final instructions to push themselves harder, Nakime summons doors to close off Muzan's presence, ending the meeting. After a short confrontation between Akaza and Kokushibo ends with both demons leaving on their own accord, Nakime plays her biwa again to transport Gyokko and Hantengu to their assigned mission. When Doma is left last and attempts to invite her back to his residence, she bluntly refuses Doma's offer and immediately sends him back to his temple. Hashira Training Arc. Nakime, now the new Upper Rank Four replacing Hantengu, is shown to be with Muzan. Using small eyeball familiars, she has been tracking down the Demon Slayers and determining their locations and hideout. Expressing her honor at Muzan's compliment for her rapid growth, she uses her technique to locate Kagaya Ubuyashiki. Infinity Castle Arc. When the Demon Slayer Corps arrive at the Ubuyashiki mansion to try and stop Muzan, they are all transported into the Infinity Castle and separated from one another by Nakime. Obanai Iguro and Mitsuri Kanroji are the first to encounter her, but find it extremely difficult to land blows on her due to her control over the environment.Later on, after Kokushibo's death, Nakime becomes the only remaining Upper Rank and the final member of the Twelve Kizuki. During the beginning of Tanjiro and Giyu's fight with Muzan, the latter reveals to the Demon Slayers that Nakime has successfully defeated both Obanai and Mitsuri by crushing them both to death using the rooms of her castle. However, he is taken by surprise when the supposedly dead Hashiras launch a surprise attack on him, still very much alive, and angrily asks Nakime what she is doing. Muzan is shocked upon learning that Yushiro has completely taken control over Nakime's vision, and with it, the Infinity Castle, which he begins to use against the Demon King as revenge for his killing of Tamayo. Muzan immediately begins countering Yushiro, using his own mental powers in order to take back his final Upper Rank, which kicks off a fierce battle of wills between the two demons. This mental fight causes the castle to completely spiral out of control as both wrestle for dominance, and, just as Muzan appears to have taken the upper hand, Obanai and Giyu launch an attack on the Demon lord. He has no choice but to counter, which causes his hold on Nakime to slip as he tries to defend himself and ward the Hashiras off with his own attacks. Yushiro quickly begins to fight back while Muzan is distracted and manages to have Nakime change the battlefield again, leaving Muzan and the Hashira falling. Soon realizing that he can't take back Nakime and fight the Demon Slayers at the same time, Muzan uses his powers to kill his final Upper Rank by crushing her head, which prevents Yushiro from using the castle against him and allows him to fully focus on killing the remaining Hashiras and Tanjiro. As Nakime doesn't immediately disintegrate, Yushiro manages to use her body to push the castle above ground in an attempt to protect the Demon Slayers. Abilities. Overall Abilities. Despite not displaying much in terms of fighting ability, as the holder of the fourth highest position in the Twelve Kizuki, Nakime is nonetheless an extremely powerful demon. She was capable of using her unorthodox Blood Demon Art to thwart the efforts of Obanai and Mitsuri at beheading her and stall the two Hashira for most of their battle, with neither of the two skilled combatants being able to so much as scratch her. Talented Biwa Player: Nakime was an expert at playing the biwa, garnering attention from others when she performed while she was still a human girl. Demon Abilities. Eye Detachment: Later, upon obtaining the rank of Upper Rank Four and presumably receiving more blood from Muzan, she displayed the new ability to create and detach several eyeballs from her body. This allowed her to spy on others from a long range. With this new ability, she was able to successfully find and locate the positions of nearly all members of the Demon Slayer Corps as well as the hidden mansion of Kagaya Ubuyashiki, who had gone to extreme lengths to hide its location from even the highest-ranking members of the Demon Slayer Corps. Physical Abilities. Immense Speed & Reflexes: Nakime was shown to possess a level of speed comparable to the Hashira, namely of Obanai and Mitsuri, reacting to and successfully evading the former's Venom Fangs of the Narrow Head technique and the latter's attacks. Fighting Style. Blood Demon Art. Infinity Castle Manipulation: Nakime's Blood Demon Art takes the form of an extra-dimensional space that houses a fortress of immense scale. As its owner, Nakime possesses absolute dominion over the space, being able to manipulate and alter it at will by simply strumming her biwa. In her fortress, there are countless rooms with seemingly endless variety, like an open room filled with giant pillars where the fight against Kokushibo took place; a small garden where the fight against Doma took place; a corridor leading to several other rooms where the fight against Akaza took place. Nakime sits at the center of the Infinity Castle, with the entire space being distorted around her. Nakime has also displayed the ability to use her unorthodox Blood Demon Art for offensive purposes. She achieves this by shaping rooms into gigantic pillars and ramming it into her enemies to crush them. By binding and rooting her hair to a nearby wall inside the castle, she could control the castle's positioning as she likes: shifting and changing the positioning of various rooms and walls as if they were her own limbs. However, doing so presumably renders her immobile. Equipment. Biwa: Nakime is always seen carrying a four-stringed wooden on her lap. A biwa is a short-necked lute which Nakime used in performances when she was a human, being particularly talented in playing it as well. Her biwa is used as a medium for her Blood Demon Art, as she is required to strum to instrument using a single large pick to use it. As a demon, it's possible that her Biwa and Bachi are fashioned from her flesh and blood, similar to other tools and weapons used by demons.
