Shinobu Kocho/Relationships Relationships. Giyu Tomioka. Giyu and Shinobu are both Hashiras of the Demon Slayer Corps and they are usually assigned on missions together. They have opposite personalities and initially seem to be at odds with each other, as Shinobu appears to be under the impression that Giyu is an airhead and a klutz, assuming he is spacing out in front of a Demon as she is trying to save him. After he deflects her attack, she is angry at him for getting in the way and proceeds to remark that people dislike him as a result. However, Shinobu does wish Giyu would talk more while Giyu compliments her work ethic and hints at concern for her physical wellbeing in the second fanbook. Furthermore, Gyomei notes that the two enjoy talking with each other. Later on, both her and Giyu come to care about the Kamado siblings and are visibly upset by the hostile treatment of the other Hashiras towards them. When Giyu later hears about Shinobu's death, he suddenly recalls her smiling face and is visibly shocked at the news. Tanjiro Kamado. Shinobu first meets Tanjiro after she attempts to kill Nezuko, and tells him it is dangerous to be so close to a Demon. Later on, during the Hashira's trial, she is the only one trying to hear Tanjiro's side of the story, and has a sad expression on her face as Tanjiro desperately tries to explain that Nezuko has not and will not hurt anybody. She comes to care about both Tanjiro and Nezuko and is visibly concerned about them, even letting them rest at her estate so they are able to recover from their injuries. Tanjiro is visibly sad when he hears about Shinobu's death. Zenitsu Agatsuma. Shinobu meets Zenitsu during the Natagumo Mountain incident, and treats his wounds after he has slain one of the spider demons. Shinobu also tries to motivate Zenitsu by cheering him. Inosuke Hashibira. Inosuke meets Shinobu while recovering at the Butterfly Estate. To motivate him to continue his recovery training, Shinobu condescendingly mocks his inability to do simple things, prompting Inosuke to angrily train harder. As time passed, Inosuke saw Shinobu as a surrogate mother due to her kindness. After knowing that Doma killed Shinobu, Inosuke becomes further enraged at the Demon and joins Kanao in her battle to defeat him. Nezuko Kamado. Shinobu initially assumes that since Nezuko was a demon she was a threat to others, though she decides to make her death swift and painless when she realizes that Tanjiro was her brother. She leaps out from afar and attempts to stab the demon girl with her sword, only to be blocked by Giyu. However, at the Hashira Meeting, she doesn't object to the master's descision to accept the the her into the Corp. When Nezuko is turning back into a human by Tamayo's medicine, she remembers when Shinobu showed her goldfish to her. Murata. Murata first meets Shinobu at Natagumo Mountain when she rescues him from the Older Sister Spider. As she has seen Murata naked, he's been avoiding her since then. Kanao Tsuyuri. Although Shinobu was the one to impulsively buy her adoptive sister Kanao out of slavery, she quickly became frustrated when Kanao could not make her own decisions, declaring that she was dangerous to herself and others. However, Shinobu soon warmed up to her and developed a strong, sisterly bond. During Kanae’s funeral, Shinobu comforted Kanao and was understanding of her inability to cry. Shinobu eventually made Kanao her chosen Tsuguko (successor) due to her considerable talent and exceptional skills as a Demon Slayer. Shinobu instructed Kanao to cut off a demon’s head without thinking, though she was worried whether or not Kanao was truly following her own will. But when Kanao begins opening up and expresses her wish to train beside her specifically, Shinobu is very happy. Shinobu holds great trust in Kanao, as she entrusted her with avenging Kanae’s death while using herself as a sacrifice. She is also noted to be protective towards Kanao; Inosuke mentions that Shinobu gets “really mad” when Kanao gets hurt, and Shinobu expresses her worry about Kanao using the Flower Breath’s Final Form and thus possibly losing her sight, even when she was the one losing her life. When Shinobu dies at Doma’s hand, Kanao successfully avenges her with the help of Inosuke. In the aftermath, Shinobu and Kanae later give their blessings to their younger sister before departing to the afterlife. This causes Kanao to break down in tears for the first time. Kanao also keeps both Shinobu and Kanae's butterfly hair accessories as mementos of their lives, and continues holding both of them in high regard. Kanae Kocho. Shinobu was noted to have a very close and loving sisterly relationship with her biological older sister, Kanae having been seen to be very close to each other since early childhood and having spent their childhoods happily together with their parents. The sister's bond was incredibly deep and caring, as seen where the two of them both took an oath to protect others from demons and ensure no one else goes through their tragedy upon the two of them surviving the Demon attack that killed their parents. During this time the sisters developed a unique familial dynamic, where Kanae would frequently make lighthearted, whimsical decisions without thinking first, which then causes Shinobu great expiration and worry due to her elder sister's behavior. But Shinobu is still shown to trust her sister deeply and support her sister's decision despite not initially agreeing with her at first, as seen when the two adopted and made off with their adoptive little sister Kanao Tsuyuri. Later, Kanae's deep love for her sister was truly shown during her last moments after fighting Doma, where Kanae begged Shinobu to leave the Demon Slayer Corps and simply live her life free and happy, stating that the only thing that would make her happy is knowing that Shinobu would be able to live a full happy life and die peacefully as an old woman, showing just how much she loved her younger sister. Shinobu in turn showed her own immense love for her elder sister by swearing that she couldn't possibly live like that and begged her sister to tell her which demon killed her, swearing eternal vengeance against whoever killed her sister. Mitsuri Kanroji. Shinobu and Mitsuri are good friends. However, Shinobu has expressed jealousy towards Mitsuri's strong body before. Nevertheless, they remain on good terms. Tamayo. Although initially Shinobu harbored little trust in her due to her status as a Demon, Shinobu gradually began developing a sense of respect for Tamayo as they began working together on a drug that can finally destroy Muzan, as seen where Shinobu was genuinely impressed at Tamayo skill as a doctor and fellow poisoner and was truly appreciative of her skills due to them making it possible to successfully create their Anti-Kibitsuji Drug that successfully weakened Muzan enough to death. Tamayo herself was even willing to assist Shinobu in her quest for vengeance by helping her modify her body to be saturated in Wisteria Poison for the battle against the Upper Rank 2, showing that by that time, Shinobu had already seen past Tamayo's status as a demon and had truly come to trust and admire her as a fellow doctor. Doma. Shinobu holds a strong resentment and hatred for Doma, due to him killing her older sister, Kanae. This hatred and disgust becomes even stronger when she actually meets him and comes to understand and see first-hand his twisted personality and ideas about giving his disciples "salvation" by killing and eating them. Later, during their battle, she continuously curses him due to him not being affected by her poisons and sword techniques again and again, until she is defeated and devoured by him. However, thanks to Shinobu's body being heavily saturated with poison, Doma is severely weakened and is eventually successfully slain by Kanao and Inosuke. Inside of Limbo, Doma, having heard and been touched by Shinobu's strong faith and belief in her comrades and fellow Demon Slayers' ability to defeat the demons and slay Muzan, seemingly begins to develop genuine feelings of romantic attraction towards Shinobu. He begins to doubt his initial belief that neither heaven or hell or paradise exist, and happily asks her if she wanted to go to hell with him for a date, to which she responds with sharp rejection while having the usual kind and calm smile on her face as a final act of spite towards the Demon.

Shinobu Kocho/Synopsis History. Past. Shinobu was born as the youngest daughter within the Kocho household, living alongside her mother, father, and older sister Kanae Kocho. She was raised in a loving and caring household, until her parents were slaughtered by demons right before her and her sister's eyes. Just when the demon was about to take the lives of her and her sister as well, they were saved by the Hashira, Gyomei Himejima, who slayed the demon. Now more determined as a result of the pain and suffering they endured, Shinobu and Kanae both promised to become Demon Slayers to protect each other, as well as prevent other people from enduring the same losses they had to experience. Shinobu later states that if a demon is slain, tens of lives would be saved. She mentioned that defeating an Upper Rank will save hundreds of lives. Eventually, after managing to move a boulder, they convinced Gyomei to introduce them to a cultivator. Later in her life, while accompanying her sister Kanae on a trip, the sisters encountered a young girl being led away as a slave on a bridge. Intrigued by her, Kanae took an interest and decided to take the girl back to the Butterfly Estate, against Shinobu's initial wishes. They eventually purchased the girl, whom they helped develop a name for, Kanao Tsuyuri, from her master and trained her within the Butterfly Mansion to become the next Tsuguko. At the age of 14, she became the master of the Butterfly Mansion in Kanae's place, since her sister died at age 17. Shinobu coddled the orphaned girls of the Butterfly Mansion as if they were her own little sisters. They included one teenager, and 3 prepubescent girls. In addition to Kanao, she had at least 3 other girls train as her Tsuguko. However, all were killed by demons, further adding onto her intense hatred of demons and intense anger which she belied with a cheerful persona that she adopted following Kanae's death. Upon becoming Hashira, she frequently spoke with the stoic and introverted Water Hashira, Giyu Tomioka, whom she liked to tease. She accompanied Giyu on a mission where they went on a search for another demon in the snow mountains that reportedly killed multiple people. Shinobu arrived first and made small-talk with the locals, where she was informed of a man eating bear, much to her intrigue. They then encountered an irritable young woman named Yae, a matagi out for revenge against the aforementioned bear who had supposedly killed her father and his matagi friend. Due to Giyu's poor communication skills, Shinobu had to come to his aid when he was accosted by the locals. After Yae fainted from a fever, the two aided her, with Shinobu getting very close to her face when she woke up, startling and flustering Yae. Shinobu then gave the woman some tea, and revealed the existence of demons and the Demon Slayer Corps, inquiring information about the bear the attacked her home to confirm that it indeed was a bear and not a demon. When Yae asked if they killed all demons, she responded claiming that they only kill the bad ones, and that if a demon chose to die of starvation, she'd care for it till the very end. She offered to help Yae kill the bear, but she angrily rejected her offer and stormed off into the mountains once again. Afterwards, Shinobu changed into her Hashira attire and confided with Giyu that Yae was in trouble. The bear turned out to have been a fabricated story by Yae, and the only casualty was her matagi friend, who was killed by her father, Matazo, who transformed into a demon. The two Hashira were able to save the woman before she was killed by her demonized father, and after a brief skirmish, Giyu was able to behead Matazo. Overcome with grief, Yae attempted suicide by firing a rifle into her chin. Shinobu attempted to intervene but noted that she wouldn't reach in time. Fortunately, the rifle jammed and Shinobu tackled Yae to the ground. Shinobu then gave the woman words of comfort and told her to be strong the way they once were, before silently departing. The Hashira then made a rendezvous at a noodle shop, where she claimed that Giyu had changed and was less cold than before. After Giyu is served salmon and radish, he begins to smile, much to her discomfort. Mount Natagumo Arc. Shinobu is present when Kagaya Ubuyashiki receives news of the situation unfolding at Mount Natagumo, and is given the order to travel there and assist the lower-ranked swordsmen. Acknowledging this, she states that it would be great if everyone could get along, regardless if they are human or demon, and asks Giyu if he agrees. On Mount Natagumo, Shinobu appears before a heavily injured Zenitsu Agatsuma, greeting and asking him if he is alright. She then suddenly appears behind the daughter member of Rui's Spider Family, inquiring if the strings came out of her palms, wishing the creature a good evening, and commenting on the beauty of the moon that night. Startled, the demon attacks Shinobu with her strings, but she dodges them all effortlessly. Drawing her sword, Shinobu dryly comments that this attack means that the demon doesn't want to get along with her. The daughter demon quickly begs Shinobu for mercy, stating that she would be killed if she disobeyed Rui. Shinobu, sympathizing with the creature's plight, says that she will cooperate with the demon if she answers a few of Shinobu's questions, the first of which being how many people she had killed. The demon's answer is five, but Shinobu assures her that she doesn't have to lie, complimenting her string technique from earlier, and the demon corrects her answer to eighty humans. Despite the creature's stubborn denial, the swordswoman notes that both of them came from the west side of the mountain, and, on that side, she had found forty of the demon's cocoons. Shinobu adds that she isn't angry, but only trying to be as accurate as possible. When asked what the point of checking this information is, Shinobu tells the elder daughter demon that in order for them to be friends and to satisfy those who have died, she will have to endure punishment, explaining in gruesome detail what she had in mind for this, and adding that the creature won't die from it, so there will be no aftereffects. Enraged, the demon attacks Shinobu again, but the Demon Slayer quickly bypasses her, simultaneously landing her Insect Breathing, Butterfly Dance: Caprice attack on the creature. She laments the demon's poor choice, turning and subsequently watching as the creature collapses. Shinobu tells the creature not to let her guard down just because she can't cut the demon's head off since, she explains, that she utilizes poison as her weapon instead. Shinobu then introduces herself as the Insect Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps, stating that, although she may be the only one among her order to not possess the ability to cut off a demon's head, poison that can kill the creatures is still a potent tool. She then apologizes, realizing that the daughter demon is already dead and could not hear her explanation. Shinobu then proceeds to cut open the demon's silk cocoon, freeing Murata. She asks him if he is alright, and he asks what happened to the older sister demon, to which she answers that she had killed the demon with poison from wisteria, commenting afterwards on how lucky he is for only having his clothes melted off by the creature's attack. She later attempts to attack Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado, but her attack is deflected by Giyu. She questions his interference, noting that if he continues this course of action, everyone would hate him. The Insect Hashira asks her fellow Demon Slayer to get out of the way, apologizing to him when he replies that he isn't hated. She then turns her attention to Tanjiro, telling him that he is protecting a demon and that he should get away from her. The young Demon Slayer exclaims that Nezuko is his sister, causing Shinobu to take pity on her and plan to kill her with a toxin that inflicts no pain. Giyu then instructs Tanjiro to run, which Shinobu notes to be a violation of Demon Slayer's conduct. Later, while being restrained by Giyu's arm, she laments that she had been in the right to come kill Ddemons and therefore had broken no rules, but noted that Giyu had, asking him what his intent was. Her fellow Hashira remains quiet, prompting her to angrily ask him to say something. Giyu replies that it had all started two years ago, causing Shinobu to note that the length of time was a problem and wonder if he was holding a grudge because she had said he was hated. She then extends a blade from her right shoe and prepares to attack Giyu, only to be stopped by an important message from a crow which said that Tanjiro and Nezuko are to be restrained and brought headquarters. Later, at the headquarters of her order, the Demon Slayer stood alongside her fellow Hashira in front of a restrained Tanjiro. Rehabilitation Training Arc. She quickly informs the confused youth where he is and that he is on trial for violation of Demon Slayer conduct. When Obanai Iguro points out that Giyu Tomioka had also committed this crime and asks how they are going to deal with him, Shinobu tells him that they will think of a punishment for him later, since she is more interested in hearing Tanjiro's story. She gives the youth some water with a painkiller mixed in and asks for his story, warning him not to strain himself on account of his injuries. She then listens quietly as Tanjiro explains his sister's circumstances. Shinobu continues to listen to Tanjiro's story, but his dialogue is interrupted by the sudden appearance of Sanemi Shinazugawa, who grabs Nezuko's box. She warns her fellow Hashira not to act on his own, but he ignores her warning, stabbing the trapped Demon with his sword, much to her displeasure. She then watches as an enraged Tanjiro charge the Wind Hashira, and afterwards looked at an apologetic Mitsuri Kanroji. Shinobu's leader, Kagaya Ubuyashiki, then arrived, causing her and her fellow Hashira to bow in respect. Kagaya then asked for them all to accept Tanjiro and Nezuko, surprising Shinobu, who remained silent as her fellows argued over the decision, and as Kagaya's assistant read Sakonji Urokodaki's letter. Shinobu continues her silence through even more arguments, but is shocked as her leader revealed that Tanjiro had come into contact with Muzan Kibutsuji. She and her fellow Hashira are then halted from even more debating by a simple gesture from their leader, with the Insect Hashira remaining silent as Kagaya explains more of his reasoning for pardoning Tanjiro and Nezuko. Shinobu then cautions Tanjiro from using any of his breath techniques while pinned by Obanai, as his lungs might explode from the pressure. She calls out his name in alarm as he ignores her advice and tries anyways. After the incident with Sanemi and Nezuko is resolved, she listens quietly as Kagaya explained the dedication of the Hashira to Tanjiro. With everything resolved, Shinobu suggests they take care of Tanjiro over at her place, instructing the Kakushi to do this, and then waits for Kagaya to start the Hashira meeting. After the meeting has ended, she visits Tanjiro and his friends at the Butterfly Estate, asking them how they are doing and instructing them to begin their Rehabilitation training. Mugen Train Arc. Shinobu and Kanao were informed by a Kasugai Crow of the death of Kyojuro Rengoku. Like all the Hashira, Shinobu was fond of Kyojuro and as such was troubled by his death. Hashira Training Arc. After Kanao came back from a mission, she was greeted by Shinobu who informed her of Tanjiro's mission in the Swordsmith Village, as well as Nezuko gaining immunity to the sunlight. She then attends a meeting of Hashira in the Ubuyashiki Mansion attended by Amane Ubuyashiki, who was filling in for her husband due to Kagaya's familiar curse leaving him bed-ridden. She listened as Amane informed them of the Demon Slayer Marks. After the meeting concluded, Giyu attempted to immediately dismiss himself, much to the ire of Sanemi and Obanai. In response, Shinobu, uncharacteristically stern, asked Giyu to explain himself, causing him to respond like he wasn't like the rest of them. Before the situation could escalate any further, Gyomei made a powerful clap to cow them into silence, and proclaimed he had a proposition. The plan was to, instead of soley training their Tsugukos, a mass Hashira Training program would be exercised in order to both improve all Demon Slayers' physical abilities and overall health, bolstering the members of the Demon Slayer Corps significantly, and to improve the individual strength of each Hashira as well as practice coordinating their attacks together. Sometime during this meeting, the topic of Hashira bodyguards for Kagaya was raised, but was quickly shut down, due to Gyomei pointing out that Kagaya refused to have the Hashira serve as bodyguards, claiming they were to precious to expend on him alone. Shinobu pointed out that the Ubuyashikis haven't had bodyguards for generations. Like Giyu, Shinobu did not participate in Hashira Training, although unlike Giyu, she made it clear that she was in full support of the proposition. Instead she was tasked with collaborating with a demon doctor named Tamayo to come up with a plan to defeat Muzan Kibutsuji by Kagaya. Due to her extreme hatred of demons she was rather hesitant and mistrustful about it and asked her late sister for help to suppress her emotions. She is later approached by Kanao who announces that she is leaving to go train with the Wind Hashira before asking if she could train her after completing her section with the Stone Hashira. Shinobu responds that she's not participating in the training, and when Kanao asks why, Shinobu invites her in for a private conversation. Kanao meekly admits her desire to train with her older adopted sister, causing Shinobu to smile warmly and express happiness that Kanao is learning to speak what's on her mind more clearly. She then decides that now is the right time to reveal the demon that killed Kanae and how to defeat it. When Tamayo and her demon assistant Yushiro arrived, relations were tense. Shinobu was highly paranoid and inwardly hostile to the demons, and the notoriously overprotective Yushiro could sense it, causing him to be on edge, much to Tamayo's unease. However, they learned to work past their differences and created an Anti-Kibutsuji Drug. When she was alerted by a Kasugai Crow that an intruder had trespassed into the Ubuyashiki Mansion, she ran to the aid of her master and his family as fast as she could, alongside her fellow Hashira. However, before they could arrive, Kagaya detonated a large amount of explosives, not only decimating the Ubuyashiki Mansion, but killing both himself, and his wife and two elder daughters, who all refused to leave his side. Shinobu looked on in horror but pressed forward, where she encountered Gyomei fighting a shirtless, black-haired demon. Gyomei quickly announced that the demon was Muzan Kibutsuji himself, whilst also revealing that would not die if beheaded. After getting over the initial shock of finally encountering the King of Demons in person, Shinobu quickly sprung to action and was about to use Butterfly Dance, but before she could swing her sword, Muzan opened the Infinity Castle, forcing Shinobu and the rest of the Hashira and Tanjiro to plummet inside. Infinity Castle Arc. Inside the Infinity Castle that Muzan Kibutsuji had created after Kagaya's suicidal move, Shinobu enters a room and discovers Doma eating a group of his own female disciples. When he finally notices her, Doma reacts with delight at having another meal walk right into his room, and thanks Nakime. One of his disciples, still alive, begs Shinobu to save her, and Doma, irritated by this, attempts to finish her off, only for Shinobu to jump in and save her. She asks the young woman if she is alright, but before she can answer Shinobu's question, the young woman explodes and dies right in front of her eyes. Angered by this, and Doma's insistence that he saved the girl by killing her, Shinobu notices a pair of sharp fans that Doma uses as his main weapon, and angrily inquires if he remembers the haori that originally belonged to her elder sister. Doma finally remembers her by the butterfly wing design haori that Kanae once wore, and playfully expresses his disappointment at not being able to eat Kanae due to the sun rising, which further angers Shinobu. The Insect Hashira swiftly launches an attack at him using her Insect Breathing, Dance of the Bee Sting: True Flutter to inflict a powerful stab directly in Doma's right eyeball, which impresses him since he couldn't block it. Although he is initially dismissive of her, since he correctly guessed that she lacks the physical strength to cut off a Demon's head, he becomes excited upon learning that Shinobu's true strength lies in poisoning her opponents. Shinobu hopes that the poison will be effective enough to kill him, but then learns, much to her disappointment, that Doma had already received information regarding her poison from her battle against the Spider Family of Lower Rank 5. Doma manages to break down and render her poison non-lethal, healing himself from her attack. She is further backed into a corner due to Doma now rapidly developing antibodies and adjusting his body against her poison so that, after a mere five slashes and injections of poison, he is now entirely resistant to it. Also, due his Blood Demon Art of frozen mist, it is becoming increasingly difficult for Shinobu to breathe. Now hedging her bets on injecting a large dose to kill him by using a six stab attack, Shinobu strikes him using Insect Breathing, Dance of the Dragonfly: Compound Eye Hexagon and successfully hits him. However, as she attacks him, he simultaneously attacks her, cutting both her collarbone and ribs and puncturing one of her lungs. Finally near her wits' end and almost losing any hope of victory, Shinobu attempts to draw strength from replaying her older sister's words of encouragement in her head. Shinobu then prepares to strike at Doma again, despite her serious injuries and the immense pain she was in, and attacks him using Insect Breathing, Dance of the Centipede: Hundred-Legged Zigzag, to confuse him. She strikes Doma directly through his neck, impaling him and sending him flying towards the ceiling. Exhausted and wounded, Shinobu is triumphant upon seeing Doma being poisoned and seemingly dying from her attack. However, Doma recovers almost instantly from her attack, by which Shinobu is further enraged. Now exhausted, fatally injured, and dangerously near death, Shinobu is caught by Doma as they fell down from the ceiling. He embraces her in a bear hug and begins mocking her and calling her entire attempt to defeat him a waste of effort, assuring her she will live peacefully as a part of him. He playfully asks for her last words, and she spitefully curses him. As her disciple Kanao arrives, Shinobu passes her knowledge of Doma's abilities on through hand signals, but the demon notices and crushes her spine, killing her. Her death causes Kanao to go berserk, but she is repelled by an irritated Doma, who tells her not to interfere when he's in the middle of devouring someone. He successfully absorbs Shinobu's body into himself, leaving only her butterfly-shaped hair piece and sword behind. Shinobu's death was reported to Tanjiro and Giyu by a Kasugai Crow, with both being very shaken up by the news. After Kanao, later joined by Inosuke Hashibira, fight to avenge Shinobu's death, it turns out that she anticipated the possibility she would lose and be consumed by Doma. Thus, she had been taking and absorbing wisteria poison regularly for over a year, with Tamayo helping the process along during the Hashira training, in the hopes that if Doma consumed her, he would also devour thirty-seven kilograms worth of wisteria poison, nearly seven-hundred times the lethal dose for a normal demon. She hoped this would be enough to kill the Upper Rank or at least weaken him enough that her allies could slay him later. Ultimately, Shinobu's plan works out, as Kanao and Inosuke manage to sever Doma's disfigured head from his body, fulfilling her revenge at last. In the afterlife, Shinobu and Doma converse with each other, with Doma finally showing emotion by saying he has fallen for Shinobu. He proposes that they go to hell together, but Shinobu vulgarly declines with a smile on her face. Shinobu is last seen with her sister, Kanae, giving their blessings to Kanao, before happily reuniting with their parents in the afterlife. Legacy. When Tanjiro was turned into a demon after the defeat of the Demon King, Muzan Kibutsuji, she was among the many hands to pushed him back towards being a human alongside many of her colleagues whom had also fallen in battle, when the spirit of Muzan attempted to sabotage the serum administered to cure Tanjiro's condition. In the modern era, Shinobu reincarnates with her sister Kanae as high school girls, both of whom are seen attending an all girl's school.

Shinobu Kocho vs Doma Shinobu Kocho vs Doma was a battle that took place in the Infinity Castle. It focuses on the battle between Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho against Upper Rank Two Doma. Prologue. As he is consuming a group of his female disciples inside Nakime's Infinity Castle, Doma notices Shinobu at the entrance to his room. He reacts with delight at having another meal walk right into his room, and thanks Nakime. One of his disciples, still alive, begs Shinobu to save her, and Doma, irritated by this, attempts to finish her off, only for Shinobu to jump in and save her. She asks the young woman if she is alright, but before she can answer Shinobu's question, the young woman falls to pieces and dies right in front of her eyes. Angered by this, and Doma's insistence that he saved the girl by killing her, Shinobu notices a pair of sharp fans that Doma uses as his main weapon, and angrily inquires if he remembers the haori that originally belonged to her elder sister. Doma finally remembers her by the butterfly wing design haori that Kanae once wore, and playfully expresses his disappointment at not being able to eat Kanae due to the sun rising, which further angers Shinobu. Battle. The Insect Hashira swiftly launches an attack at him using her Insect Breathing, Dance of the Bee Sting: True Flutter to inflict a powerful stab directly in Doma's right eyeball, which impresses him since he states he was unable to block it with his hand in time. He then unleashes his Blood Demon Art: Frozen Lotus towards Shinobu with her backflipping away from his attack. Although he is initially dismissive of her, since he correctly guessed that she lacks the physical strength to cut off a demon's head, he becomes excited upon learning that Shinobu's true strength lies in poisoning her opponents. Shinobu hopes that the poison will be effective enough to kill him, but then learns, much to her disappointment, that Doma had already received information regarding her poison from her battle against the Daughter of the Spider Family. Doma manages to break down and render her poison non-lethal, healing himself from her attack. She is further backed into a corner due to Doma now rapidly developing antibodies and adjusting his body against her poison so that, after a mere five slashes and injections of poison, he is now resistant to it entirely. Additionally, due his Blood Demon Art of frozen mist, it is becoming increasingly difficult for Shinobu to breathe. Now hedging her bets on injecting a large dose to kill him by using a six stab attack, Shinobu strikes him using her Insect Breathing, Dance of the Dragonfly: Compound Eye Hexagon and successfully hits him. However, as she attacks him, he simultaneously attacks her, cutting both her collarbone and ribs and puncturing one of her lungs. Finally near her wits' end and almost losing any hope of victory, Shinobu attempts to draw strength from replaying her older sister's words of encouragement in her head. Doma, seeing the injured young woman barely able to stand, is convinced she can no longer attack and plans to behead her to finish her suffering. Shinobu then prepares to strike at Doma once more, despite her serious injuries and the immense pain she was in, and attacks him using her Insect Breathing, Dance of the Centipede: Hundred-Legged Zigzag to confuse him. Shocked by the attack, Upper Rank Two is unable to hit his opponent and barely grazes her haori. She strikes Doma directly through his neck, impaling him and sending him flying towards the ceiling. Exhausted and wounded, Shinobu is triumphant upon seeing Doma being poisoned and seemingly dying from her attack. However, Doma recovers almost instantly from her attack, by which Shinobu is further enraged. Now exhausted, fatally injured and dangerously near death, Shinobu is caught by Doma as they were about to fall down from the ceiling. He embraces her in a bear hug, and begins mocking her and calling her entire attempt to defeat him a waste of effort, assuring her she will live peacefully as a part of him, and mockingly asking her for her last words. She spitefully curses him as he begins to kill her. Aftermath. Doma breaks Shinobu's back and begins to absorb her, just as her disciple Kanao Tsuyuri arrives at the scene. In the Hashira's final moments, she manages to signal to her Tsuguko with her hand. Her death causes Kanao to go berserk with anger and she attacks the Upper Rank with her Flower Breathing, Fourth Form: Crimson Hanagoromo, only to be repelled by an irritated Doma, who tells her not to interfere when he is in the middle of absorbing someone. He successfully absorbs Shinobu's entire body until her butterfly-shaped hair piece is the only thing left of her.

Shinobu Kocho vs Spider Demon (Daughter) Shinobu Kocho vs Spider Demon (Daughter) was a battle that took place on Mount Natagumo. It focuses on the battle between the Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho against Daughter of the Spider Family. Prologue. As Daughter runs away from the fight between Tanjiro Kamado and Rui, she reminisces on the events that have led to this moment, recalling when Rui first met her, everything that happened throughout her time in the Spider Family, informing Rui of the deaths of her "Mother" and "Brother" and his wrath upon realizing they have never lived to his expectations. Soon after, she runs into Murata, much to his surprise. She immediately discerns that he is a Demon Slayer and captures him with an acidic cocoon, her own Blood Demon Art. He quickly attempts to stab and slash open the cocoon to escape but it backfires. Daughter then comments that it is futile to escape due to the cocoon being incredibly durable despite its softness. Inside, Murata sees thick lime-green liquid oozing out of the threads, slowly filling up the cocoon. The Spider Demon sadistically explains that the liquid will first erode his uniform, then his body, before she will devour his remains. Suddenly, Shinobu Kocho appears right behind the demon and inquisitively wonders if the threads come out from her palms, along with wishing her a good evening and commenting about the beauty of the moon as well. Battle. Startled, Daughter quickly steps away from Shinobu. She attempts to capture her with her acidic cocoon, but Shinobu gracefully dodges all of her silk and approaches her, closing the distance. Upon getting within range, she repeatedly kicks Daughter to the ground, pinning her down. Shinobu reflects that the Spider Demon doesn't want to become her "friend", to which the demon quickly begs for mercy. Daughter claims that she is being threatened by someone and will be killed for any defiance, causing Shinobu to appear concerned. Shinobu states that she will be willing to spare her, to Daughter's great surprise, but adds that she must asks a few questions beforehand. Coldly staring at the demon, the Insect Hashira asks how many people she has killed. Scared, Daughter quiet answers that she's killed five, as she begins to tear up. She repeats that she had no choice and was ordered to do so but Shinobu brushes aside her words and asks that she do not lie. The demon maintains that she has only killed five but Shinobu informs her of finding hordes of cocoons and at least eighty dead human captives just from the direction she came through in the forest. Seeing the frightened demon staying silent, Shinobu mentions she is not angry and simply trying to get an accurate toll. When Daughter asks about the importance of knowing how many she has killed, Shinobu responds that she needs to receive the proper punishment in order for them both to be friends. Shinobu states that she could either gouge out her eyes, slash her stomach to rip out her insides, and torture her for each of her victims. Daughter begins to panic at her impending fate, while a sly Shinobu adds that she will not die from her torture because she can heal. Disturbed and fearful of her future torture, the Spider Demon engages at Shinobu and attempts to capture her again, only for Shinobu to quickly evade it again, while lamenting the demon's poor decision. Seeing that they can never be friends, she unsheathes her sword. When the demon tries to fire her silk again, she is unable to spot the Hashira. Looking up, she sees Shinobu leaping high into the air before lunging towards her with numerous butterflies behind her. She suddenly finds herself surrounded as dozens of butterflies fly pass her, with a single one landing on her finger. When she moves in for a closer look, the butterfly begins to bleed. causing blood to drip from her finger and her body to change. In actuality, Shinobu uses her Insect Breathing, Butterfly Dance: Caprice on the Spider Demon. Daughter immediately touches her neck to see if she was beheaded, to which she realizes she was not. She questions as to how and why the Insect Hashira didn't behead her, to which she concludes that Shinobu doesn't have the necessary strength in order to behead a demon. This greatly boosts the Spider Demon's confidence in defeating her, but as she is about to attack Shinobu, she is hit by a wave of pain and sees her blood vessel changing. As her wounds begin bleeding, internal bleeding appears throughout her body, and her condition rapidly deteriorates. Daughter lets out one final scream of agony before slumping to the ground, the last of the Spider Family defeated. Shinobu happily mentions that she shouldn't feel safe if she has not been beheaded, as there are Demon Slayers like her who wield poison instead. Aftermath. After confirming that Daughter is indeed dead, Shinobu quickly frees Murata from his cocoon prison. Upon seeing the demon on the ground, he wonders if she should finish it off, only for the Hashira to state that she is already dead from the poison she used. As an embarrassed and nude Murata slinks away, Shinobu turns her attention to the demon Daughter had said has been ordering her, wondering if the demon has been reached by her partner Giyu Tomioka already.

Shizu Shinazugawa was the mother of Sanemi and Genya Shinazugawa. Appearance. Shizu was a petite woman with a small and dainty frame Her black hair was fastened in a low bun with her bangs clipped back on the crown of her head. She also had a very small face with large blue round eyes. Shizu wore a white underneath her horizontally stripped yellow kimono, and had a black obi tied around her waist. As a demon, she possessed noticeable fangs and sharpened nails, but otherwise appeared the same as whilst she was human. Personality. Shizu was described as a hard worker who would work from "morning until night" and hardly slept. Despite being in an abusive marriage, and having a small frame, she would always shield her children from her husband Kyogo's abuse and was considered a "hero" to them. In the afterlife, even when she was unable to control herself as a demon, Shizu could not stand to be with the children she unwillingly killed and reserved herself to her fate in Hell, though she seemed appreciative when Sanemi did not hesitate to go with her. History. At some point, Shizu had married Kyogo and had a total of seven children: Sanemi, Genya, Hiroshi, Sumi, Teiko, Shuya, and Koto. However it was an incredibly abusive marriage, where Kyogo would often beat her as well as her kids. Despite her much smaller size, she never failed to protect them from his outbursts. In time, he was eventually killed in a grudge, freeing Shizu and her children from his abuse. One night, Shizu was transformed into a demon by Muzan and did not return home. Her oldest son Sanemi decided to look for her and Genya stayed behind to watch his siblings, during which Hiroshi, Sumi, Teiko, and Shuya would wake up as well. As the night dragged on, Sumi expressed concern as Shizu had never been so late, dawn was close by. Eventually, Shizu returned home and banged on the door. Shuya realized it was her and was joined by Hiroshi, Sumi, and Teiko in running to the door to greet their mother. Despite Genya's warning against opening it, Shizu burst through the door with incredible speed, killing the four children almost instantly, before she lunged at Genya and Koto, scarring Genya's face and slitting Koto's throat. As she leapt to the ceiling to stalk him, Genya was unable to see his assailant and believed her to be a wolf. She leapt down and lunged at him, only to be tackled by Sanemi out of the house. When Shizu began to attack Sanemi instead, his wounds began to bleed heavily and she unexpected began to slow down, allowing him to incapacitate her. Losing consciousness, Shizu lay on the ground and began to fade due to the rising sun's light. Genya would then see her burning body and, in his grief, denounce Sanemi as a murderer. Synopsis. Swordsmith Village Arc. During his battle against Hantengu, Genya attempted to cut his neck but was shocked when his blade shattered upon making contact. In disbelief, he sensed that the demon's manifestation of anger was behind him and prepared to deliver an unavoidable blow. Realizing his life was coming to an end, his life flashed before his eyes and he reminisces on his past, his mother, and the circumstances of her death. Final Battle Arc. As Sanemi lingers between life and death, he calls out to Shizu and asks her to accompany him to heaven. However she tearfully declines his offer, stating that she cannot go to heaven after having killed her children. Sanemi understands his mother's anguish and agrees to carry her to hell and accompany her, but before he can join her, Kyogo interrupts angrily demanding to let go of her. He declares that she will be accompanying him and throws Sanemi as Shizu tearfully reaches out to her son, presuming that Shizu will be accompanied by her husband in hell, leaving Sanemi to regain his consciousness. Abilities. Overall Abilities: As a demon, Shizu became very fast and strong, far beyond what was physically possible for a human. However, due to her recent transformation and Sanemi's Marechi blood, she was incapacitated reasonably quickly and was left to burn in the sun, though she would still leave him with lasting scars. Moreover, due to her very recent transformation, she had no control of herself and hunted impulsively and in an animalistic manner.

Shoichi is a young boy saved by Tanjiro Kamado and Zenitsu Agatsuma when they approached him to help his older brother, Kiyoshi, escape from the Drum House. He also has a younger sister, Teruko. Appearance. Shoichi is a short young boy of around 8-10, with black spiky hair and hazel eyes with a thick black border. Shoichi wears a blue over a light green with a white juban under it. Personality. While his personality is not fully elaborated on, one can assume he is a loyal brother as he decides to follow his older brother to rescue him after he was kidnapped by a demon. He has also shown a protective side while interacting with his younger sister. It can be surmised that Shoichi is braver than average, as he decides to follow the two Demon Slayers, Tanjiro and Zenitsu, into the Drum House. Even when separated from the others with Zenitsu, he shows more courage than the Thunder Breathing user. History. While not much is known about his personal history, Shoichi came from a family of presumably three kids, with him being the middle child. Synopsis. Tsuzumi Mansion Arc. Shoichi, along with his sister Teruko, meet Tanjiro and Zenitsu at the entrance of the Drum House, searching for their kidnapped older brother. Abilities. As an ordinary human, he doesn't possess any additional powers or abilities.

Shuka Matsuda is a Japanese writer and the author of several of the "Kimetsu no Yaiba" novelized light novels.

Shuya Shinazugawa was a younger brother of Sanemi and Genya Shinazugawa. Appearance. Shuya was a young boy of small stature and fair skin tone. His dark hair was shaved down and he had large purple almond-shaped eyes. He bore a resemblance with his two oldest brothers Sanemi and Genya. Shuya wore a tan colored kimono with a two-tone black and light brown obi. Personality. Shuya, like his siblings, was a warm and caring child. He loved his mother dearly, who, in return, would often protect him from his father's abuse on multiple occasions. When he awoke to find she had not come home late at night, he waited til she came home and eagerly ran to greet her at the door when Shizu did arrive, though it would sadly cost his life. History. Shuya was born to Shizu and Kyogo Shinazugawa and was raised with 6 other siblings. His abusive father would often beat his family, though he was constantly protected by his mother from his outbursts. Eventually, Kyogo would die to a vengeful stabbing and the family would be at peace. One night, as Shuya, Sumi, Teiko, Hiroshi, and Koto slept, Sanemi and Genya were concerned that their mother had not come home yet. As Sanemi ventured out to find her and Genya stayed behind, Shuya awoke with the rest of his siblings. The children became concerned over Shizu's lateness, even as Genya attempted to get them to go back to sleep to ease their concerns. Eventually, a loud knock rang from the door, leading Shuya to call out to his siblings that their mother had come home. Despite Genya's warning, Shuya, Teiko, Sumi, and Hiroshi ran to greet her and open it. The door burst open and Shizu, who had transformed into a demon, entered the house in a blur, killing Shuya instantly. Synopsis. Swordsmith Village Arc. During his fight against Hantengu, Genya discovered the small demon controlling the emotion manifestations but failed to cut through his neck. The demon's manifestation of anger appeared behind him and prepared to deliver an unavoidable blow. Realizing he will die, Genya reminisced on his past, including the deaths of his siblings and mother. Sunrise Countdown Arc. After the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, Sanemi, who had sustained several severe wounds, lost consciousness and found himself in the afterlife, where he saw Shuya and his other fallen siblings in heaven.

Slasher was the nickname given to a demon that appeared during the investigation of the Mugen Train and was responsible for a number of human attacks. He was defeated by Kyojuro Rengoku. Appearance. Slasher was a bald middle-aged man of a fairly muscular build and very pale skin. His eyes had a lime green iris, a black sclera and vertical slits for pupils, and he had sharp pointed nails that are dark blue in color and several prominent fangs in his mouth. Most prominently, Slasher's whole body was covered in dark blue tattoos, running across various places on his face, limbs and torso. These tattoos light up and glow blue when he uses his Blood Demon Art. He also wore a sleeveless blue shirt and black leggings complete with and a pair of with blue straps. Slasher was usually seen with a maniacal expression on his face. Personality. Like most demons, Slasher was a ruthless individual that only seems to care about murdering and eating humans, He also was shown having a sadistic and malicious side, off-handedly mentioning he slashed a woman till he became bored and when he dug his claws into a young boy. He was also shown to be quite arrogant at times, looking down on the Flame Hashira, Kyojuro Rengoku and boasting his speed in front of him as well as challenging him to a duel twice. However, Slasher was not above using underhanded tactics like taking a hostage to win against Kyojuro. Slasher was also rather petty, trying to find whatever means to provoke Kyojuro and growing further frustrated and more aggressive when the young man both held his ground, retorted back and even stopped his murders. Synopsis. Mugen Train Arc. Slasher encountered and terrorized a village in search of prey. He found a young woman roaming around at night but thought she didn't seem worth eating. Instead, he horrifically clawed her body till he became bored and left her to die. The next night, he boarded a train but found it empty, apart from one hapless train conductor. He quickly killed him but found him not worthy to devour too and left his body to be discovered. The news of his actions frightened the village and people feared leaving their houses after dark, causing business usually active at night to halt. The Demon Slayer Corps subsequently sent Kyojuro Rengoku to investigate. Slasher happened upon a maintenance facility for trains in search of prey. Unbeknownst to him, the facility held the Mugen Train, which was assumed to hold a demon likely responsible for numerous disappearances reported. He found a young worker and grabbed him in his claws. The scene drew the attention of Kyojuro, investigating the Mugen Train, and Slasher was confronted by the Hashira. While facing him, he wretches suddenly, before stepping on a bento box and claiming that human food is disgusting to him now as a demon. He taunted Kyojuro into attacking him, using his Blood Demon Art to rush around the Hashira and goad him into attacking, warning him that the young boy will be dead if he directly tried to attack. Kyojuro acknowledges his speed but tells him not to get cocky. Slasher then mentioned how he injured a woman the previous night but was told by Kyojuro that she will recover completely. Angered, he noticed the stepped bento box and Kyojuro's angered expression, before realizing the box likely came from a nearby station. Deciding he will kill the vendors to spite Kyojuro, he first tried to kill the boy he was holding but has both of his hands cut off. He retreated and steps outside the facility to regrow both his hands, before smelling the air for the bento vendors' scent and following the tracks, using his Blood Demon Art to cross the great distance in minutes. He arrived at the station and entered, seeing the young girl setting up her bento stand. As she staggered in fear of seeing him, Slasher moved forward to kill her but was hit by a bento box from behind, thrown by her grandmother. Momentarily distracted by the smell, he soon caught up to her outside and tried to crush her throat. Kyojuro thwarts his attack and slices his left achilles, saving her. Slasher then turned his attention to her grandmother instead but was confronted by Kyojuro once more. Wondering aloud how he manage to catch up to him so quickly, Kyojuro repeated his earlier words not to get cocky facing him. Slasher decided to make a contest for the two to determine who is faster, if Kyojuro can kill him before he kill the girl's grandmother. To this, Kyojuro mocked him for being slow and rushed forward, decapitating Slasher before he was able to react, ending his short spree of terror. Abilities. Overall Abilities. Slasher was a decently powerful demon, as evidenced by developing a Blood Demon Art and displaying skill in utilizing it for combat. He proved mildly troublesome for even a Hashira to handle, albeit most of it attributed to his penchant to use human shields. In terms of direct combat however, Slasher proved no match for the Flame Hashira. Demon Abilities. Regeneration: Like all demons, Slasher possesses enhanced regeneration. He was able to grow both his hands back in moments after having them cut, as well as healing his sliced Achilles tendon just as quickly. Fighting Style. Blood Demon Art. Speed Augmentation: Slasher's Blood Demon Art enables him to greatly augment his own speed, allowing him to traverse great distances in a short amount of time. This technique is activated whenever his dark blue tattoo glows. The speed at which he moves is such that his entire figure is covered in a blue light.

Sound Breathing is a Breathing Style derived from Thunder Breathing. Overview. Sound Breathing is a Breathing Style that mimics sound, specifically its disorientating loudness, and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. Most, if not all, known techniques and forms utilize explosives to deal massive amounts of damage while making use of extremely fast movements similar to how fast sound travels as well as the user's sense of hearing. Users of Sound Breathing also visualize themselves seemingly generating and manipulating loud sounds and explosives when unleashing its techniques. The only known user, Tengen Uzui uses a technique developed using his superhuman sense of hearing called, which involves Tengen reading his opponents movements and deconstructing them into sound by analyzing the rhythm of their movements. Through this, he is able to take advantage of their openings to much greater effect by striking in a way similar to making the beat to a song. In conjunction with this, he uses small but powerful anti-demon bombs that are capable of damaging the bodies of Upper Rank demons. Since this combat style was presumably created by Tengen, it can only be used with a specific set of weaponry, which is two gigantic -like Nichirin Cleavers, which each have a notch in the sharp ends of their blades and are held together at the hilt by a metal chain. His swords are said to have large amounts of explosive power, and it is stated that, until Tengen's fight with Upper Rank Six, no demon had ever survived a blow from them. Known Techniques. Sound Breathing has 5 techniques and forms at minimum, with 3 known techniques. Demonstrations. <tabber> </tabber>

Special One-Shot , also known as, is a one-shot about the Flame Hashira, Kyojuro Rengoku, that was written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotoge prior to the release of . The story takes place during Kyojuro's first mission. It was later compiled into the series' 2nd Fanbook. Summary. Kyojuro Rengoku goes on his first mission to kill a demon, known for destroying others with his flute. He battles him, reflecting on decisions, and risks. He ultimately defeats the demon, making his first mission a victory, and gaining the confidence he needs to continue his demon slaying journey.

Spider Demon (Daughter) The was a supporting antagonist in the Mount Natagumo Arc of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". She was a member of the Spider Family. Appearance. Daughter's physical features are very similar to that of her "younger brother," Rui. She has the looks of a girl in her early teens with a pale, milky-white skin complexion, snow white hair, and pure white eyes with only her silvery pupils separating them from her sclera. She also possesses several red, dot-like patterns on her face similar to her "family". Daughter's clothing consisted of a long white kimono and a hexagon-patterned juban underneath. She wore ribbons in her hair that were decorated with a large blue bead, and unlike her other "family members", who were barefoot, she wore black slippers. Daughter's original appearance as a demon was completely different than her current, having morphed and changed her features due to being forced by Rui as a condition to be accepted into his family. Her original appearance was that of a teen demon with black hair, slitted cat-like eyes and pale grayish skin. Personality. Daughter is shown to be the most cautious within her "family," having instead opted to observe and stand back rather than jump right into the battle against Demon Slayers. She is also shown to be very cowardly, both with battling against the Demon Slayer Corps and dealing with her family's internal conflict. When her "mother" was being violently abused and reprimanded by Rui and her "father," she stood back and gave her the same severe glare due to her weakness instead of helping her. She again shows her cowardice by trying to convince Rui to run instead to fight after most of their family was defeated, which enrages him and leads him to wound her. In truth, Daughter loathes and hates her "family" and began to think that she would have likely done better on her own. She believes that the rest of her family are fools for playing along with Rui, despite him not having any real emotional attachment or care for any of them, though she seems aware that not going along with Rui's desire's is dangerous. Whatever the case, Daughter did make a point of staying in Rui's good books, even going so far as to deliberately set up another 'Sister' of the Spider Family. She even went as far as attempting to use sympathy and pity on Shinobu Kocho, knowing that she was a Demon Slayer, by pleading that she was forced into her situation by Rui. However, this contradicts her actions as she went through various lengths to stay with him and his family, revealing that she only does what is convenient for her own survival, and took clear enjoyment out of killing humans. History. Daughter was originally a lone demon who lived on Mount Natagumo. She found herself being pursued by several Demon Slayers and was cornered at an abandoned house in a field. When her assailants were nearly on top of her, they were interrupted by the arrival of Rui, Lower Five of the Twelve Kizuki. He offered a chance to live by asking for her to be a member of his "family" to which she graciously accepted. Rui then quickly dispatched the Demon Slayers and she soon found herself introduced to several spider-like demons living in the house. Rui took her hand and she was accepted as a new sister. Inside with Rui, she was presented by her new older sister with a beverage to drink, containing a drop of Rui's blood. Immediately after taking it, she found herself in intense pain as the drop of Muzan's blood began to physically change her. Rui then added the "finishing touches" and ripped off her face to make her appear more like him, as she screamed in agony. After her ordeal, she was congratulated for being a true part of the family now. Though she was initially happy to be safe from Demon Slayers, she came to understand that Rui's view of a family was twisted and strewn with his cruelty. She was told by her sister that they were all strangers who came to Rui for protection, only for him to abuse their need for survival with his own ambitions at making a family. They witness their "mother" being tortured by Rui and Daughter is offered a chance at escaping their situation. The next day, she and her older sister attempt to descend the mountain but found their path blocked by Rui himself. Daughter, knowing the consequences, quickly re-joined his side and later watched as Rui tortured his sibling and left her to die. Despite going with her plan to escape together, Daughter looks at the horrifically wounded body of her former sibling and walks away without a second thought. Now more fearful of Rui than ever before, Daughter did her best to live to his expectations and be a "good sister". Knowing that escape was futile and she would be killed for attempting to do so, she became more withdrawn and aloof. During one occasion, she saw her "mother" being tormented by both Rui and her "father" because she repeatedly failed to meet the expectations of her role. Watching the frightened demon beg for mercy, Daughter coldly looks at her without intervening in the situation, in order to remain safe. Synopsis. Mount Natagumo Arc. As they head deeper into the forests of the mountain, Daughter is spotted by Tanjiro Kamado and Inosuke Hashibira only after recently defeating her "mother". She screams for her father's help and runs away, leaving him to fight the two Demon Slayers on his own. She meets with Rui and tells him of their mother and and elder brother's demise, asking for his next course of action. While doing so, unbeknownst to Daughter, her eyes changes back to their original appearance and is seen by Rui, who mercilessly slashes her face in his webs, angered that she unwittingly changed her appearance. They are interrupted by the arrival of Tanjiro, having been flung away from the battle by their father. Still on the ground in pain, she hears Tanjiro confront Rui for abusing her, flatly declaring that their bond is fake. This shocks Daughter, as she has never seen anyone stand up to him, much less a human. She watches the two clash and later sees the intervention of Tanjiro's sister Nezuko, taking the hit from Rui's webs to protect him. Shocked to see her emerge from seemingly nowhere, she then looks to Rui, visibly shaking at the sight of sibling love between the two. Knowing what will happen next, she tries to draw his attention and asks he do not forget about her, only for the Lower Rank to slice her to pieces with his threads. In spite of his initial anger, Rui decides to give her a final chance at redemption, asking that she hunt down the Demon Slayers still on the mountain for him. Unwilling to anger him again, Daughter obeys his commands, picks up her severed head and runs away to heal and do as he wishes. As she regenerates from her wounds, she reminisces on when she first met Rui; how he was the one to protect from the Demon Slayers on the mountain and her initial introduction to her family. She remembers how his high expectations and abuse would cause conflict and pain towards the other members, though she denounces them all as fools for playing his game. While making her way down Mount Natagumo, she comes across Murata in her path and quickly ensnares him in a silk cocoon. She taunts him with the details of how he will die to her cocoon's acid, only to be interrupted by the Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho. Shocked at her sudden appearance, Daughter hears Shinobu greet her and comment on the full moon tonight. She tries to ensnare her as well in her silk but Shinobu proves too fast and nimble to hit; she eventually knocks the demon to the ground and questions her. Daughter quickly begs Shinobu for mercy, stating that she would be killed if she disobeyed Rui. Shinobu, seemingly sympathizing with the demon's plight, says that she will cooperate with the demon if she answers a few of Shinobu's questions, starting with the number of her victims. Trapped and scared, Daughter answers that she has killed five under orders, only for Shinobu to correct her answer by stating that from the direction she came, she counted eighty cocoons in the trees, with all human captives dead and liquified. Daughter denies killing so much but the Hashira states that in one area alone, she counted fourteen. Shinobu adds that she isn't angry, only trying to be as accurate as possible. When asked what the point of checking this information is, Shinobu tells the Spider Demon that in order for them to be friends and to satisfy those who have died, she will have to endure punishment, explaining in gruesome detail what she had in mind for this, and adding that since she won't die from it, there will be no aftereffects. Horrified and angered, Daughter tries once more to trap Shinobu in her silk, but the Insect Hashira proves too quick to hit, as she laments their inability to become friends. When she turns to fight her again, she loses sight of her assailant, before looking up and watching Shinobu lunge at her with a flutter of butterflies at her back. They fly past her but Daughter sees one land on her finger; watching with curiosity, she sees as the butterfly begins to bleed, with her own body bleeding in certain spots as well. Shinobu has used Insect Breathing, Butterfly Dance: Caprice, striking her too quickly to be noticed. Daughter quickly reaches for her head and feels her neck is still intact, before noticing that Shinobu's blade isn't built to slice off a demon's head. As she declares that Shinobu is someone she can kill, her hand begins to bleed internally and her body convulses. As she begins to vomit blood and her regeneration starts to fail, Daughter lets out one final scream of agony before slumping to the ground, dead from Shinobu's wisteria poison. Abilities. Overall Abilities: Enhanced with a drop of Muzan's blood from Rui, Daughter proved to be a decently strong demon. She was solely responsible for the greatest loss of life on the mission to Mount Natagumo, having killed at least eighty Demon Slayers through her cocoons. She was quickly able to overwhelm an experienced Demon Slayer, Murata, and would have certainly killed him if it wasn't for Shinobu's intervention. Despite her power, she still proved to be no match for the Insect Hashira. Enhanced Regeneration: Like all demons, Daughter possesses powerful regeneration, able to heal the numerous severe wounds given by Rui's steel-like threads. She was even able to survived being decapitated and sliced into several pieces by him, with only a short amount of time to heal completely. Despite this, her regeneration was overwhelmed and defeated by Shinobu's advanced wisteria poison. Fighting Style. Blood Demon Art. Silk Manipulation: Like her "mother" and Rui, Daughter can manipulate threads made from her own cells, this time in a fashion similar to silk that forms a cocoon instead of threads that resemble wires. Despite being extremely soft, her silk is stronger and more durable than metal, with even a normal Demon Slayer being unable to cut or pierce through it with a Nichirin Sword. Acid Manipulation: Daughter can manipulate and generate acid made from her own blood and flesh. The acid she creates can easily dissolve a person, though the process is somewhat slow. Spider Demon (Father) The was a supporting antagonist in the Mount Natagumo Arc of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". He was a member of the Spider Family. Appearance. Physically, Father was the most formidable of his "family", possessing great height and a powerfully built physique. His skin was dark brown with the same red, dot-like design extending from his shoulders reaching down to his arms as other members of his family. Like his "wife" and "children," Father also had white hair reminiscent of Rui, although his was much longer, reaching down across his shoulders. His most unique trait was his monstrous face; unlike his "family's" more humanoid appearance, his face was identical to that of a true spider, with several eyes and large pincers for a mouth. When he moulted, he gained green skin with blade-like protrusions sticking out of his arms and legs. He lost all his hair and obtained sharper teeth and more pronounced mandibles. He also gained five spikes going upwards on his forehead. Finally, one of the most notable changes was that the number of his eyes doubled from nine, to eighteen. Personality. Father was animalistic, aggressive and extremely bloodthirsty. He was shown to be very devoted to his "family", as when he battled Tanjiro Kamado and Inosuke Hashibira, he repeatedly told them to stay away from his family while attempting to kill the duo. He served as the main protector and was seen being on the lookout for the Demon Slayers when they came to Mount Natagumo. However, he was also shown to be very abusive towards his "wife," having repeatedly slashed and physically abused her in the past without even stating his reasons for doing so due to her being weaker than to what they originally expected of her. Father was additionally shown to have been unquestioningly loyal to Rui, having never once challenged or defied him. Synopsis. Mount Natagumo Arc. After Daughter called for him, Father landed in front of Tanjiro and Inosuke. He angrily yelled them to get away from his family, before attacking them with a fierce punch. He easily blocked Tanjiro's Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel technique, attempting to counter with another punch, only to be thwarted by Inosuke's twin swords pinning his arms down. He threw the two Demon Slayers off of him, immediately charging and attacking Tanjiro while repeating his earlier demand. Inosuke attempted to attack him from behind, only to be immediately punched. The Spider Demon continued his assault on the boar-headed Demon Hunter, only to be pinned by a tree that Tanjiro had cut. He quickly recovered from this and eventually used the tree to fling his assailant into the distance. Later, while Inosuke contemplated his next move, Father attacks him, breaking the tree he was leaning against. Surprised by his opponent's quick retreat into attack, the paternal demon blocks the strike, but has his forearm severed when Inosuke uses both of his blades. Briefly examining his stump, Father then retreated and climbed up a tree, before shedding his skin and assuming a new form. He then descended the tree, ready to resume the battle.Towering over his astounded opponent, Father punched him with great force, following through almost immediately with another blow, which Inosuke only avoided by jumping into the air. Inosuke attempted to sever the Spider Demon's neck with his Beast Breathing, Third Fang: Devour, only for his blades to shatter upon contact. Father immediately countered, sending his adversary hurtling into yet another tree before picking up the Demon Slayer up by the head. Readying another punch while simultaneously throttling his opponent, Father once again repeated his earlier demand, only to be stabbed in the throat by his resilient adversary. Unfazed, he tightened his grip on the youth's head, only to have his forearm severed once more, this time by the arrival of Giyu Tomioka. Howling in pain, Father immediately regrows it, charging at Giyu. His offense and existence are soon erased as Giyu strikes him with the Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide, severing his neck and cutting him into multiple pieces. Abilities. Overall abilities: For a demon who isn't a member of the Twelve Kizuki, Father has shown himself to be quite a powerful demon. He was easily the second strongest member of the Spider Family and was able to take the combined might of Tanjiro Kamado and Inosuke Hashibira without fail. Father was likely seen by his "family" to be the main guardian and protector, due to his role and strength; unlike the other members who mainly hid from the Demon Slayers, he was seen actively hunting on Mount Natagumo to find intruders. Despite his above-average strength for a non-Kizuki demon, he still proved no match for the Water Hashira, Giyu Tomioka. Enhanced Durability: Notably, Father displayed physical durability that is uncommon in most demons, likely due to Muzan's blood in him provided by Rui and his size. Tanjiro and Inosuke found it difficult to slash through his arms and he was able to shrug off multiple attacks. Enhanced Speed: Belying his huge size, Father was very fast, easily keeping up with the likes of Tanjiro and Inosuke. Numerous times, Father's attacks have been barely dodged by the two Demon Slayers due to his unprecedented speed and he was able to catch them off-guard similarly. Enhanced Strength: As expected for his immense size, Father possessed great physical strength. He was able to punch boulders to pieces, grab a tree trunk and swing it with great speed, fling Tanjiro away over a great distance and punch Inosuke with such force, he slammed into several trees before stopping. Metamorphosis: Father possessed the ability to shed his outer skin in order to transform into a more powerful form with increased physical power and regenerative abilities, making him even stronger and durable than in his original form.
