Prologue. After most of his family has been slain by a demon, Tanjiro Kamado discovers that his sister Nezuko is the sole survivor. He tries carrying her down the mountain to a nearby village, but she awakens and shakes them off the path. They fall into a snow-laced forest where Tanjiro discovers that Nezuko has become a demon. Nezuko tries to feed on Tanjiro but he stuffs his hatchet's handle in her mouth as she pins him to the ground. Her demon form grows in size but Tanjiro pleads with Nezuko until her humanity cries out, calming herself down as tears spill onto Tanjiro's face. Just when the skirmish appears to be over, a mysterious swordsman appears and tries to behead Nezuko with a katana. Tanjiro moves her out of the way in time and only his hair is partially sliced off. The swordsman, Giyu Tomioka, questions Tanjiro and quickly takes Nezuko hostage. He explains he is a Demon Slayer and is will now kill Nezuko. Tanjiro begs him not to, asking him not to take away the last family member he has left. Annoyed by Tanjiro's pathetic groveling, Giyu gets angry and starts to berate him; he tells Tanjiro his family was massacred because he was weak and groveling will never work with demons. In reality, he blames himself for not getting to the mountain in time to save them. Berating Tanjiro is his way to help mold his resolve and give him the drive to eventually save his sister and avenge his family. Battle. The Demon Slayer stabs his sword into Nezuko, forcing Tanjiro to act by throwing a rock his opponent, which he is forced to deflect. Tanjiro grabs his hatchet and circles his target, using the trees as cover. He throws another rock while passing by a tree but Giyu easily dodges the stone. Tanjiro charges straight for the Demon Slayer, who sees his attempt is simply a frontal assault driven purely on emotion. Disappointed, Giyu knocks out the boy using the hilt of his sword. After knocking Tanjiro down, he notices that his hatchet is missing. He looks up and is nearly hit by the weapon flying through the air, ducking out of the blade's path. Giyu figures out that Tanjiro must have launched the hatchet at the same time as when he threw the second stone. He hid his hands as he pretended to attack to fool him into thinking he was unarmed. Unlike before, the Demon Slayer is now impressed by the boy's resolve to save his sister, attempting to bring down his opponent after falling in battle. Nezuko breaks out of Giyu's hold and kicks him away. She goes over to Tanjiro, causing him to believe she'll try and devour him. However, he is shocked when Nezuko protects her brother despite becoming a demon. Giyu ponders on Nezuko's state of mind as he dodges an assault from the newly-turned demon. He keeps her back using only his hands and surmises that because she decided to protect her brother rather than eat him, despite sustaining wounds that would be healed by eating him. Knowing that demons will even feed on their family members soon after transforming, he realizes these siblings must be truly unique.Nezuko jumps off a tree and tries to attack the Demon Slayer's head. Giyu sheathes his sword and uses a strong chop to the neck to knock her unconscious. Aftermath. Tanjiro eventually wakes up to find that he and Nezuko are both unharmed. Giyu tells him to find a man named Sakonji Urokodaki who lives at the foot on Mount Sagiri, while indirectly revealing his identity. Before disappearing, Giyu tells Tanjiro to keep Nezuko out of direct sunlight.Tanjiro returns home to bury his family and says one final goodbye. Afterward, Tanjiro and Nezuko begin their long journey to return her to normal.

Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Mantis Demon was a short skirmish that occurred north north-west of the Butterfly Mansion. It concerns the Demon Slayers Tanjiro Kamado and the recognized demon Nezuko Kamado against the Mantis Demon hiding in a mountain shrine. Prologue. Following the death of Kyojuro Rengoku, Tanjiro, along with Zenitsu Agatsuma and Inosuke Hashibira became intensely motivated to train harder and become stronger than ever before. While doing chores in the Butterfly Mansion, he was tasked with killing a demon that had inhabited a mountain shrine. With Nezuko now recognized as a member of the Demon Slayer Corps, the siblings set out to their mission. Battle. Amidst pouring rain, Tanjiro arrives to the shrine where it has been reported, with Nezuko inside her box on his back. As he looks around, the demon crawls up to the ceiling unnoticed. He then detects a scent from above and looks up to see the demon descending to attack him, drawing his blade in response. It crashes to the floor and chases him, while Tanjiro sprints up a pillar. Nezuko emerges from her box and claws at the demon's legs. Together, they drive the demon out of the shrine through a wall and force it out into the open; Nezuko leaps up and tries to punch the demon, only narrowly missing. The demon flees and descends the mountain, while the siblings pursue it. Tanjiro realizes he has made a mistake when he sees the demon is heading to a village at the mountain's foot. The demon hides in a tool shed and heals its leg, while trying to understand what kind of Demon Slayer his assailant was. Tanjiro appears at the shed's entrance and asks the demon resign himself to his fate. The demon refuses and charges at him once more. As it gets close, he uses Water Breathing, Fourth Form: Striking Tide and slices off the demon's legs, before turning around and cutting through its neck to kill it. Some time later, a young boy who has heard the scuffle runs to the shed with a flashlight. He shines it around and looks for something but cannot, despite knowing he had heard something.

Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Rui Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Rui was a battle that took place on Mount Natagumo. It focuses on the battle between Demon Slayer Tanjiro Kamado, and Demon Nezuko Kamado against Lower Rank Five Rui. Prologue. Tanjiro walks into Rui abusing his older sister, using his threads to cut her face bloody; she falls to her knees, sobbing. Rui notices him and tells him to come forward. Tanjiro then says that he doesn't have a real family bond, only a fake one made out of fear, mistrust and violence, and not a bond made of love, kindness and compassion. This enrages Rui who then attempts to cut Tanjiro to pieces with his threads, Tanjiro dodges them and attempts to counter using Total Concentration: Water Breathing, First Form: Water Surface Slash but his sword is unexpectedly shattered by the threads and he sustains a cut across his face. With his sword broken Tanjiro dodges the steel-like threads to his best efforts. Rui then surrounds Tanjiro with a barrage of threads. Tanjiro closes his eyes, expecting to be cut up, but he was unharmed. Both Tanjiro and Rui are surprised, as its revealed that Nezuko was the one who protected Tanjiro from the threads, while letting her body receive the full cutting force of the threads. Tanjiro screams Nezuko's name in horror, and then he quickly carries her to safety. Rui realizes that the two are siblings. He is shocked that even though Nezuko was a demon, she still protected Tanjiro, a human. Rui realizes that their bond was genuine. He declares that he wants that bond, his eyes shining with envy. Daughter, who was listening to this, begs Rui not to abandon her, as she was his older sister. In response, Rui uses his threads to not just cut off her head but to chop off her body, telling her to shut up. He then says coldly that she and everyone else in the "family" never fulfilled their roles, not even once. He then tells her if she wanted to prove her worth to him, she should go and kill all of the Demon Slayers on Mount Natagumo. She regenerates her body and then picks up her head, leaving the scene. Rui then attempts to negotiate with Tanjiro, saying that he was really moved by Tanjiro and Nezuko's bond. Rui then says that he will let Tanjiro leave alive, but only if he lets him take Nezuko. Tanjiro immediately says no, saying that Nezuko is a living being with feelings, emotions, and a heart. Rui then says it would be alright, saying that he will forge a bond of fear between him and Nezuko. Tanjiro declares he will never hand over Nezuko, and that he will sever Rui's head. Rui compliments Tanjiro on his spirit and courage. He reveals to Tanjiro that he is actually Lower Rank 5 of the Twelve Kizuki. Rui then says he would like to see Tanjiro try to defeat him in battle. Battle. Rui uses his threads to pull Nezuko over to her side, saying now that he had his sister, Tanjiro's role was to die. Tanjiro then charges straight at Rui with his broken Nichirin Sword. Rui uses his threads to attack Tanjiro while Nezuko attempts to escape from Rui's grasp, even clawing at his face. As Tanjiro dodges Rui's attack, he notices that Rui isn't holding Nezuko anymore. Just then, a spurt of blood falls on Tanjiro's blade. He looks up and sees Nezuko strung up midair by Rui's threads, with the threads digging into her skin, badly wounding her. Rui says that the threads won't kill Nezuko, since she's a demon, but she'll have to be taught a lesson. He continues to say that if Nezuko doesn't behave, he will leave her like that until sunrise to be burned and disintegrated. Tanjiro yells at Rui, demanding that he let Nezuko go. Rui then uses his threads to trip Tanjiro and make him collapse to the ground. He then kicks Tanjiro in the stomach which sends him flying to a bush. Rui then beats up Tanjiro, and this continues until Tanjiro gets a chance to cut Rui's head off, but his blade doesn't even scratch Rui's neck. Rui declares that Tanjiro has no chance of defeating him, and then gives another kick to Tanjiro, making him crash into the mound of dirt nearby. Nezuko who was witnessing this struggles in her strung-up state, screams and attempts to break free from the threads. Rui says she's making too much noise, and then he tells her to quiet down. The threads tighten and cut deeper into Nezuko's flesh, causing her to scream in pain as she becomes even more injured. Tanjiro tells Nezuko not to get emotional, or she would be playing right into Rui's hands. Nezuko then seemingly falls into a sleep-like state. Rui notes that Nezuko has a unique aura and is different from other demons. Tanjiro tells himself to calm down and to control his breathing. He realizes that in order to defeat Rui, he must use the final form of the Water Breathing. Tanjiro uses the Total Concentration: Water Breathing, Tenth Form: Constant Flux. Rui thinks to himself that if this continued, he would be in trouble. Rui then pumps his own blood into his threads, turning them red and increasing the power to his absolute limit. Rui uses his Blood Demon Art: Cutting Thread Cage to Tanjiro which completely surrounds him. Tanjiro can tell by the scent of the threads that he cannot cut them at his current strength. Thinking that he will die from the threads, Tanjiro's life flashes before his eyes. He then remembers the Hinokami Kagura his father, Tanjuro Kamado would perform at New Year's Eve every year. He also remembers what his father said about making sure that the hanafuda earrings and the Hinokami Kagura would get passed down to Tanjiro uninterrupted. Tanjiro remembers the promise he made to his father. Then, Tanjiro switches from the Water Breathing to the Hinokami Kagura: Dance, the dragon of water gracefully turning into a burst of fire and sun. The Breathing Style that had been passed down the Kamado family for generations, was powerful enough to cut Rui's strongest threads. Rui started to panic after seeing this. He started to back away from Tanjiro while he counterattacked with more threads. The clash between threads and Hinokami continued until Tanjiro used his enhanced sense of smell to find the opening thread. Tanjiro knows, that even if he is struck down by Rui's threads after the final strike, he must defeat Rui no matter what. Meanwhile in Nezuko's consciousness, Kie Kamado appears and reaches out to her pleading that she helps her brother, or else he would die. Nezuko then wakes up, and she unlocks the ability to use Blood Demon Art: Exploding Blood. Nezuko turns the blood on Rui's threads that were entangling her into pink and crimson red flames that incinerated the threads that were about to strike Tanjiro, while also leaving a few drops of Nezuko's blood on Tanjiro's Nichirin Sword. Rui is surprised that the threads were burned by the pink flames. Tanjiro then gets his blade's range into the opening thread. Tanjiro then exclaims that the bond between him and Nezuko can never be severed by anyone. As he exclaimed this, the drops of Nezuko's blood on the broken blade turned into fire and then the heat of the fire is absorbed by the blade, allowing the color of the blade to briefly turn crimson red from black. Tanjiro then severs Rui's head from his body with his blade, which had combined the powers of Tanjiro and Nezuko as one, like how the sibling's hearts were as one. Aftermath. After the battle, Nezuko is released from Rui's entanglement. She collapses to the ground, exhausted. Tanjiro also collapses to the ground due to forcibly switching between the Water Breathing and the Hinokami Kagura. As he crawls towards Nezuko, he realizes that Rui wasn't giving off the ash-like smell when demons disintegrate. It is then revealed that Rui quickly cut his own head with his threads before Tanjiro could. Rui reattaches his head, saying that he is annoyed at how Nezuko's Blood Demon Art damaged him but not Tanjiro. Rui has now become even more angry, and he attempts to finish off Tanjiro with Blood Demon Art: Murderous Eye Basket. Just as Tanjiro was about to be cut into pieces, he is saved by the Water Hashira Giyu Tomioka. Giyu commends Tanjiro for holding his own against a Twelve Kizuki for this long. He then tells Tanjiro to rest up and protect his sister while he deals with the rest. Rui, infuriated that more Demon Slayers had shown up, prepares his most powerful attack: Blood Demon Art: Cutting Thread Rotation. Giyu uses the Total Concentration: Water Breathing, Eleventh Form: Dead Calm to block it, nullifying the attack. Rui is shocked that Giyu nullified his most powerful attack, without even trying. He tries to attack Giyu with more threads, but before he could do so, Giyu had cut Rui's head in one simple slash and flicks off the Lower Rank's blood with the process of Chiburi. Rui was shocked by this, not wanting to believe what just happened. He then disintegrates into ash as he tried to reach Tanjiro and Nezuko, with Tanjiro resting his hand onto Rui's robe after sensing the scent of grief from his body. The demon is touched by this, comparing his hand to warm sunlight.

Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Swamp Demon Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Swamp Demon focuses on the battle between the Demon Slayer Tanjiro Kamado and his accompanying demon sister Nezuko Kamado against the Swamp Demon. Prologue. Every night in the town to the northwest, a young girl disappears mysteriously without a trace. The latest victim, Satoko, is taken unexpectedly whilst she walks with her fiancé Kazumi at night. He is blamed for her sudden disappearance, despite his pleas that she had vanished with him knowing. On his first mission as an officiated member of the Demon Slayer Corps, Tanjiro Kamado travels to the town to investigate the disappearances. There, he meets a grieving Kazumi and believes his statement. Investigating from the afternoon till sunset, Kazumi tries to persuade Tanjiro to hold off and continue in the day, only for Tanjiro to note that demons are only active at night. Elsewhere, the demon uses his Blood Demon Art to drag another girl named Tokie from the village, into his swamp dimension. Its scent gets stronger, enabling Tanjiro to track it down to the exact spot where the demon is holding Tokie underground. He stabs his blade into the ground, forcing the pocket portal to open. It spews out murky water, but Tanjiro sees Tokie's kimono and is able to pull her out. A morphed demon appears from the bog and screeches at Tanjiro before disappearing again. Kazumi catches up to him and Tanjiro asks him to hold onto Tokie so he can protect them. Tanjiro examines the area and the possible places the demon could appear from. Even when submerged in its own swamp, the demon's scent isn't erased. Battle. Tanjiro sense the demon is ready to attack and prepares to use Water Breathing, Fifth Form: Blessed Rain After the Drought as a counter and rushes to the spot where the portal will appear. However, three bog puddles appear and three different demons sprawl out of the swamp. The young Demon Slayer jumps to avoid their grasp and calms himself as he switches forms. Tanjiro tries to attack all of the three demons at once and uses Water Breathing, Eight Form: Waterfall Basin. Due to switching forms mid-strike, his attack is too shallow to cause sufficient damage. He calms himself again, determined to make the demon talk about Muzan Kibutsuji. The Swamp Demon tries to go for Kazumi and Tokie, but Tanjiro protects them with Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel. Once again, Tanjiro's attack is too shallow, but he was able to save the others. He takes two more quick swings at the demon and misses, forcing the demon to retreat. The young Demon Slayer cannot chase the demon or take a full swing with Kazumi and Tokie nearby. The two-horned clone is not amused and demands the Demon Slayer back off or else Tokie will lose flavor. The three-horned clone tells his other self to calm down and claims to have eaten plenty of sixteen-year-old girls already. Kazumi demands to know what the demon did with his fiancée, only to find out that they devoured her. Enraged, Tanjiro quickly evades the three-horned clone's surprise attack. Its arm cracks the wall next to Tanjiro but he jumps above the demon and slashes its arm off. He considers this a miss and then realizes he has come too close to the wall. Tanjiro twists his body over to avoid the attack and is forced to back up by an attack from underground. The two-horned clone nearly lands a hit by appearing from behind, but Nezuko kicks out of her box and breaks the demon's neck. The Swamp Demon questions why a swordsman would be accompanying a demon. The downed two-horned clone fixes its neck and they all fade back into the bog. Under hypnotic suggestion from Sakonji Urokodaki, Nezuko sees all humans as her family, and she will fight to protect them. She rushes the demons as they appear from the swamp and tries to crush them with a fierce axe kick. The demon disappears into the bog in time to evade her attack. They try to lead her away but Tanjiro asks her to return to his side. She runs back to him and one of the demons try to grab her, but she easily flips over him to avoid it. This allows Tanjiro to realize that he can let Nezuko protect Kazumi and Tokie while he focuses on attacking. A swamp portal opens beneath them as a distraction while the two-horned clone goes after the girl. Nezuko protects Kazumi and Tokie and keeps the demon back. Tanjiro asks Nezuko to continue protecting Kazumi and Tokie while the young Demon Slayer heads on to confront the other two clones. He descends into the demon's bog dimension, where there is hardly any air and the clothes of many victims float about. The two clones inside the swamp believe it must be hard for Tanjiro to move or breathe, and that he is a fool for diving in. They swim at him at high-speed, but the young Demon Slayer declares he is not to be underestimated. On top of Mount Sagiri, where Tanjiro spent over two years training, the air too has little oxygen like the swamp. There, Tanjiro also learned that Water Breathing's forms can only be unleashed to their full potential underwater. The demons dart away at a sharp angle just as Tanjiro is about to counterattack, thought he notices that he can wait for them to get close again. They try and rush him from a different angle, but Tanjiro senses the Opening Thread. He uses a technique that can be unleashed with no sure footing, a fierce slicing vortex created by a violent twist of his upper and lower body, Water Breathing, Sixth Form: Whirlpool. The slicing whirlpool slashes apart the clones into pieces, killing them instantly. Despite his victory, Tanjiro is saddened by the number of victims that the demons have claimed. He begins to run short of breath and swims back toward the entrance to the swamp. Meanwhile, Nezuko is overpowering the last remaining demon with her bare hands. Nezuko weaves through four of the demon's strikes in a row, including a strong hammer fist that crushes the ground. She follows up with a powerful jab into the demon's gut that is strong enough to make him cough up blood. The last clone manages to evade her next punch, but he immediately gets hit by another punch and kick combo. The demon tries to slip back into the bog, but the girl acts quickly and sweep kicks so the demon can't escape. She tries to hit him with a flying kick but he's able to block it. Nezuko is too fast for the demon to dive back into the swamp, but he begins to get used to her straightforward fighting style. They exchange a few blows that they are able to either redirect or avoid until the demon narrowly blocks another strong to his head. He is able to block her next combo, confident he can regenerate from anything she throws at him. The demon rushes Nezuko and is able to block her jab, giving him an opening to slash her forehead with his claws. The Swamp Demon tries to stab his claws into Nezuko's face, but Tanjiro emerges from the portal in time to save his sister. Tanjiro cuts off the demon's arm, demanding the demon not lay a hand on his beloved sister. He follows up by slicing off the demon's other arm before it can attack again, ultimately defeating the Swamp Demon. Aftermath. The last clone of the Swamp Demon falls over and realizes its other selves have been killed. Tanjiro tells him he gives off a terrible stench and asks how many girls he's kidnapped. The demon tries to defend its actions by claiming he was killing girls so they wouldn't get old and taste bad. Irritated, Tanjiro cuts out the demon's tongue and moves on to his next question. Tanjiro presses his blade close to the demon and forces him back against a fence. He demands to know all the information the demon has on Muzan Kibutsuji. However, Tanjiro is not prepared for the crippling fear of Muzan the demon has. He cowers and trembles down to his bones, claiming he can't say anything.The scent of fear grows thick and the demon acts out of panic, recalling when Muzan once threatened him to not say anything by reminding him he sees and knows everything he does. He grows his arms back and lashes out, forcing Tanjiro to cut his head off and end him. He laments at being unable to gather any information and checks up on Nezuko. She has fallen asleep to heal her wounds, so Tanjiro promises to protect her from now on and puts her back inside her box.

Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Temple Demon Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado vs Temple Demon is a battle between siblings Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado and a demon they encounter in a mountain temple. Prologue. While traveling toward Mount Sagiri, Tanjiro passes through a small town and purchases materials to make a basket to carry Nezuko in. He leaves the town at sunset when Nezuko is able to walk beside him. The siblings eventually pass by a temple with the lights still on. Tanjiro wants to see if anyone is there, but immediately notices the scent of blood. Tanjiro rushes to the temple's entrance believing that someone might have gotten hurt along the path. He opens the door and is shocked to find a demon feeding on two dead men. Annoyed, the demon turns to the Kamado siblings and warns them about trespassing on his turf. The demon turns to face them and, as the last light withers away, he pounces on Tanjiro. Battle. Tanjiro quickly reacts by drawing his hatchet and slashes open the demon's throat. The man-eating demon stumbles back, but it only takes a few seconds before the slash is fully healed. Meanwhile, Nezuko is distracted by the bloodied victim's bodies.The Temple Demon pins down Tanjiro before he has time to react; the creature easily overpowers him in strength and speed. The demon tries to snap the boy's neck but Nezuko comes to her senses and rushes back to her brother's side. She kicks the demon's head clean off his body, freaking out Tanjiro. The headless body slowly tries to grab Tanjiro, leading to Nezuko kicking it away into a tree. The severed head and body can move individually. The body attacks first, serving to isolate Nezuko from her sibling. Tanjiro tries to help, but the head grows arms and he leaps onto Tanjiro's hatchet. The body kicks Nezuko several times before throwing her deep into the forest.Tanjiro headbutts the demon with in an attempt to stop it and it proves effective. The demon suffers two blows from Tanjiro's rock hard head before getting thrown with the hatchet into a tree, pinning him there. Tanjiro finds his sister to a cliff side where she is being kicked closer to the edge.Tanjiro tackles the demon's body over the large cliff, but Nezuko grabs him before he falls too far. The body falls to its demise, and the head is knocked unconscious as a result. Aftermath. Tanjiro prepares a knife to finish off the demon's head. He struggles to come to terms with taking another life and believes this is not the demon who attacked his family. A man in a goblin mask appears and tells Tanjiro he cannot finish a demon off using a simple knife. The masked man challenges Tanjiro to figure out another way. The boy believes crushing the demon's head with a rock will suffice and picks up one nearby, but he remains unable to bring himself to brutally end the creature. The demon awakens and curses Tanjiro until the sun rises, causing him to disintegrate into ash. The man introduces himself as Sakonji Urokodaki. He believes Tanjiro will never have the resolve to be a Demon Slayer, since he is unable to make decisions and he cannot even answer a question about the potential danger his sister presents to humans. Nonetheless, Sakonji agrees to test the boy's capabilities.

Tanjiro Kamado vs Hand Demon Tanjiro Kamado vs Hand Demon is a battle that takes place in the forests of Mount Fujikasane during Final Selection. It focuses on the battle between the prospective applicant Tanjiro Kamado and a vindictive morphed demon. Prologue. After fending off two demons at the start of Final Selection, Tanjiro notices a rotting smell and the scream of an applicant fleeing in fear. He glances over and is horrified to notice a giant, green, morphed demon, made up of hands covering its entire body. The demon swallows a dead applicant whole and grows stronger from devouring him. The Hand Demon launches its appendages at the fleeing boy and pulls him in. Before the demon eats him whole as well, Tanjiro builds up the courage to leap into action and cuts the arms off using the Water Breathing, Second Form: Water Wheel. Despite being wounded, the demon seems more pleased to see another "fox cub" and asks what the year of the Meiji era is. When Tanjiro tells him it is now the Taishō Period, the demon goes crazy and curses Sakonji Urokodaki for trapping him on the mountain for so long, a new era has passed. Tanjiro is surprised to learn the Hand Demon knows of his trainer. The demon tells him he was trapped on the mountain by Sakonji forty-seven years ago and he has been feeding on all his students as revenge. He can tell them apart from other applicant because of the warding masks he crafts for them. The demon has survived by eating over fifty applicants during the selections over the years, including thirteen of Sakonji's pupils. He recalls two pupils in particular; a young boy who he considered the most powerful of the ones he had faced and a petite girl who was extraordinarily agile. Realizing the demon is speaking about Sabito and Makomo, Tanjiro hears the demon gloat over when he told Makomo of Sakonji's foolishness in making his masks, speaking of her grief in defending Sakonji's intentions and how he had ripped her apart when she lost control. Battle. Filled with rage, Tanjiro charges head-on towards the Hand Demon and leaps for its head. However, he is punched away by an arm from the side and crashes into a tree. The boy falls injured with his mask broken and bleeding from the head.The applicant Tanjiro had saved flees the area and leaves him for dead. As the demon approaches the downed Tanjiro, a vision of his brother Shigeru begs him to wake up, causing him to dodge the demon's hands in the nick of time. Tanjiro back flips out of the way and the demon unleashes a barrage of extended arms. The swordsman in training cuts away at the arms until he is forced to retreat. The demon claims Tanjiro cannot win just by slicing away his arms, remembering that not even Sabito was able to slice his neck. Sakonji's latest student cuts off another arm and stands off with the demon. He knows he cannot lose and must bring down this morphed demon in this decisive battle. Tanjiro charges toward the demon, cutting off three more arms before noticing the demon's scent coming from below him. Four hidden arms appear from the ground but Tanjiro jumps out of the way in time, surprising his opponent. The demon tries to capitalize on this moment and attempts to grab Tanjiro whilst he is mid-air. He deflects the hand with his rock-hard head and flips onto the demon's giant outstretched arm. The Hand Demon spawns smaller arms and tries to stop Tanjiro, but he counterattacks with Total Concentration Water Breathing and swiftly slashes the arms apart as he lunges through his enemy's defenses. Tanjiro manages to get close to the demon's head with a leaping strike. The Hand Demon believes his neck is too tough for his opponent to cut and plans to crush his head after the sword fails. However, Tanjiro detects the Opening Thread and decapitates the demon with the Water Breathing, First Form: Water Surface Slash. Aftermath. The manner of the Hand Demon's defeat reminds it of the previous loss at the hands of Sakonji; he recalls feeding on several human bodies before being discovered and captured by Sakonji.After beheading the demon, Tanjiro watches as the morphed body begins to disintegrate into ash. The demon regrets that the face of a Demon Slayer will be the last thing he will ever sees, but while lamenting over his fate, he is surprised to notice Tanjiro's sad expression despite his victory. Tanjiro detects a scent of sadness being emitted from its body and prays that the demon will not be reincarnated as another again, holding onto one of his hands. The demon himself tears up as he disappears, and has a vision of himself heading towards a light in the afterlife, reincarnated as a human child asking his brother to hold his hand as they go home. At the same time, the souls of Sakonji's students waiting by the stone the demon had killed and eaten are finally able to be put to rest, waking through the mist into the afterlife.

Tanjiro Kamado vs Inosuke Hashibira Tanjiro Kamado vs Inosuke Hashibira was a small skirmish that took place outside the Tsuzumi Mansion. It focuses on the fight between Demon Slayer Tanjiro Kamado against Demon Slayer Inosuke Hashibira. Prologue. After having defeated the former Twelve Kizuki member, Kyogai, Tanjiro arrives outside with Kiyoshi on his back. To his horror, he discovers his new acquaintance, Zenitsu, bleeding on the floor as he holds onto the box containing Nezuko. The mysterious boar headed assailant, proceeds to pummel down on Zenitsu, yelling at him to get up and fight him, as he threatens to stab him along with the box. Witnessing the assault, Tanjiro becomes furious as he has a flashback from when he saw his family dead on the ground, and rushes in to attack the assailant, instigating a fight. Battle. Tanjiro rushes in to prevent the assailant from stabbing Zenitsu by punching him the stomach, knocking him backwards. The impact of the punch is so powerful, Zenitsu appears shocked after hearing the sounds of the assailant's ribs breaking. Tanjiro berates him for drawing his sword on Zenitsu and trying to fight him, despite being a fellow Corps member, as he struggles to stand up. However this does not deter the boar-headed Demon Slayer, and he instead does a kip up to get back up on his feet, and challenges Tanjiro to a fist fight. Tanjiro tries to deescalate the fight by explaining that its wrong for Corps members to fight one another, but the assailant attempts to kick Tanjiro in the face. Tanjiro realizes that the assailant is set on fighting him, and is forced to go on the defense while simultaneously trying to knock him out to cease the fighting. As they engage in a fight, Tanjiro realizes that he's remaining unusually close to the ground when he attacks, and compares him to a four legged boar. He attempts to kick his legs in order to knock him off balance, but the assailant gets below Tanjiro's leg and knocks him to the ground. The assailant displays his extreme flexibility, causing Tanjiro to scold him for straining his injuries. The assailant refuses to listen to Tanjiro and moves in to attack him yet again. However Tanjiro headbutts him out of anger, and tells him to calm down, causing the assailant's mask to fall off. Tanjiro and Zenitsu look at the boy in shock as they see his feminine face, and he proceeds to grow irritated as they stare at him. The boy yells at Tanjiro to headbutt him again so they can continue the fight, but Tanjiro refuses and tells him to sit down. The boy tells Tanjiro that his name is Inosuke Hashibira, but when asked how his name is written, he reveals that he doesn't know how to read or write.Inosuke unexpectedly stops speaking and everyone watches him to see what he'll do next. However, his eyes proceed to roll back and he falls unconscious on the ground. The group is left stunned as Tanjiro explains that Inosuke probably has a concussion from the headbutt he gave him, reassuring that he's not dead. Zenitsu looks at Tanjiro in horror as he stands unfazed from the powerful headbutt, ending the confrontation. Aftermath. Inosuke angrily awakens from being knocked out and attempts to attack Zenitsu once again, however he discovers everyone burying the bodies from the Tsuzumi Mansion. Tanjiro sees Inosuke and asks him to help them lay the bodies to rest, but he refuses and tells Tanjiro to fight him instead. He misunderstands Inosuke and tells him to rest since his wounds must be painful, and reassures him that they can continue while Inosuke takes a break. Feeling like he's being mocked, Inosuke becomes determined to show Tanjiro that he can do whatever they can do and yells out that he can bury hundreds of people, before proceeding to quickly bury the bodies. Following the burial, Inosuke accompanies the Tanjiro and Zenitsu as they follow the crows onto the next location.

Tanjiro Kamado vs Kyogai Tanjiro Kamado vs Kyogai was a battle that took place in the Tsuzumi Mansion. It focuses on the battle between Demon Slayer Tanjiro Kamado against the former Lower Rank Six, Kyogai. Prologue. Following his battle with Yahaba and Susamaru, Tanjiro is tasked by the demon Tamayo with obtaining a sample of blood from a demon within the Twelve Kizuki, the demons serving directly under Muzan Kibutsuji, in order to aid in her research to turn his sister Nezuko Kamado back into a human. Following this instruction, he is soon directed to his new mission; to investigate a woodland mansion. As he travels, he encounters and is joined by another Demon Slayer; the meek and cowardly Zenitsu Agatsuma. Though annoyed by his antics, he nonetheless takes him along to aid in his mission as extra man-power. After reaching the forest, the two meet a pair of siblings, Teruko and Shoichi. They inform Tanjiro that their older brother has been taken by a demon and is trapped in the mansion, which emits eerie drum-like noises from inside. Tanjiro and Zenitsu head in to investigate, leaving Nezuko's box with the children outside. But as they enter the rooms, the children unexpectedly join them. Before the problem can be resolved, the four become separated as pairs, Tanjiro with Teruko and Zenitsu with Shoichi. Tanjiro and Teruko then discover the strongest demon within the mansion, Kyogai. The demon begins ranting about his "ruined hunt", but when Tanjiro tries to attack him, he taps on a tsuzumi imbedded in his body, causing the room to turn sideways. Discovering that Kyogai can use a Blood Demon Art, he is soon interrupted by the appearance of a new Demon Slayer; a young man wearing a boar mask and wielding two blades. The stranger's antics ruin Tanjiro's plan of attack, and his argumentative attitude almost causes an altercation. The two quickly learn that Kyogai is also capable of creating invisible powerful slashes. Kyogai then causes the rooms to change, leading Tanjiro and Teruko to locate her oldest brother Kiyoshi. Seeing that he is holding one of Kyogai's tsuzumi, having been ripped off in a fight with another demon, Tanjiro then discovers that Kyogai is hunting him for his rare blood. Sensing that Kyogai is nearby, Tanjiro informs the siblings of his plan; when the demon emerges, he will charge towards him to leave them simultaneously as Kyoshi taps his tsuzumi. Once the rooms shift, they will be safe and Tanjiro can fight, promising to find them afterward. Battle. As Kyogai peers behind the wall at his target, Tanjiro lunges forward and gives Kyoshi the signal; he taps the tsuzumi and their room shifts, keeping them safe. The Demon Slayer charges at the Drum Demon as he taps a tsuzumi twice, flipping the room upside down. However, Tanjiro senses the change and is able to land upright. Surprised, Kyogai speeds up his tsuzumi playing, but Tanjiro is able to remember each of the different actions from the tsuzumis. As he gets close to Kyogai however, he plays the central tsuzumi on his stomach, creating a slash that nearly hits Tanjiro, forcing him to stop. Tanjiro soon realizes that his injuries from his previous battle are still hindering his movements, preventing him from staying up. Looking for a way forward, he recalls his lessons from training regarding Water Breathing's adaptability to any situation. Now regain his confidence to fight, Tanjiro prepares himself to attack Kyogai, as the demon grows angry at his defiance. Kyogai repeatedly plays his tsuzumis, causing the room to turn uncontrollably and sending numerous slashes to kill his adversary. Tanjiro becomes disoriented and is nearly hit by the slashes, barely dodging them in time. Kyogai, wanting to reclaim his place in the Twelve Kizuki, plans to wear Tanjiro down and kill him, focused on devouring Kiyoshi. Tanjiro declares that he will not hand the boy over to him, and his refusal to quit suddenly reminds the demon of moments of his past when someone had told him to quit. He speeds up his tsuzumi playing, disorienting Tanjiro even more as he struggles to keep up in time. The demon reminisces on his past as a tsuzumi player and composer, but his hobby was rebuked by others and he was insulted for being a shut-in. After one final insult, Kyogai, already a demon at that point, had killed his tormentor by slicing him apart with a slash. Reminded of the painful memories, he unleashes Rapid Drumming, playing them faster than ever and causing the room to spin so quickly, Tanjiro is trapped by the altered gravity. His slash attack becomes more dangerous, now causing five slashes instead of three. Despite his seemingly unwinnable situation, as the tsuzumi playing slows, Tanjiro realizes something he had been doing subconsciously. He had been using shallow breaths after re-injuring himself in order to not aggravate his wounds, allowing him to stay upright while maintaining strength. Kyogai shifts the room again but Tanjiro is now able to cope and stay up despite the demon's tsuzumi playing. Additionally, he notes that a mould-like scent can be detected just before the slash attack appears, enabling him to dodge them more effectively. With his new knowledge, Tanjiro is now able to evade Kyogai's attacks with minimal movement, shocking the former Kizuki. Preparing his final attack, Tanjiro breathes in to empower himself and uses Total Concentration: Water Breathing, Ninth Form: Splashing Water Flow, Turbulent. As the room shifts, he leaps up and maintains his footing as it turns upside down. Unable to react, Kyogai watches as Tanjiro closes the distance between them. Finally, he senses the Opening Thread for the slash and beheads the Drum Demon. Aftermath. After beheading Kyogai, Tanjiro accidentally takes a deep breath in a moment of forgetfulness, causing him great pain. Kyogai, having heard him acknowledge his Blood Demon Art as incredible, asks the Demon Slayer if he meant what he said. Tanjiro states that he truly believed so, but also tells him that he can't be forgiven for killing innocents. Remembering to take a sample of blood, Tanjiro jabs the demon's body with a syringe-like knife, taking a vial of blood for Tamayo's research. Kyogai, hearing Tanjiro compliment his tsuzumi playing, remembers his past memories regarding people rejecting his hobby, finally realizes it is not true. Watching the Demon Slayer pray for him before departing, he sheds tears as he fades away into ash, happy that someone has recognized his talents.

Tanjuro Kamado was the husband of Kie Kamado and the late father of Tanjiro, Nezuko, Takeo, Hanako, Shigeru, and Rokuta. Appearance. Tanjuro was a frail man with black hair tipped with red, red eyes, and a pale skin complexion. His son Tanjiro has a striking resemblance to him in hair and eye color. He suffered from an illness that made him frail and caused his skin to appear dull. He was born with a mark on his forehead. Tanjuro also wore a similar outfit to his son, sporting a black checkered that was orange instead of dark turquoise. He wore hanafuda earrings when he was alive; these were passed down from his ancestor, eventually leading Tanjiro to wear them upon his death. When performing the Kagura ritual dance, Tanjuro took the appearance of an Iwami Kagura dancer with a long sleeved dark brown dress with golden and crimson red frames with a large blindfold covering his entire face with the kanji for inscribed on it. He used a decorated wooden blade akin to a, which bore the appearance of a flaming sword, inspired by Yoriichi's Sun Breathing forms. Personality. Tanjuro was a quiet, calculating, forgiving, charismatic and loving person. He had a peaceful relationship with his family and regularly lectured Tanjiro about life. While he appeared calm on the outside, he showed a decent, noble aura with a quiet perception to his surroundings. According to his son, he did not like standing out or displaying his true abilities to others. However, if his family is in danger, he would not hesitate to protect them and shows no mercy towards the enemy. History. At some point in his life, Tanjuro married Kie and had their six children. Tanjuro seemed to have a connection with the demon-killing world but in his final years was a wise but sick and frail man. He died some time before the slaughter of his wife and youngest children but still manages to inspire his two remaining children. Synopsis. Mount Natagumo Arc. Tanjiro has to fight against Lower Rank 5, Rui, and is nearly killed by his Blood Demon Art when a flashback of his father telling him to breathe and become Hinokami resurfaces in his memories. Tanjiro remembers himself and Nezuko as children watching their father perform the Hinokami Kagura throughout the night. Tanjiro asks his mother how Tanjuro's able to perform the Hinokami Kagura throughout the freezing night, only for him to be told there is a way to breathe so that he can dance no matter the temperature. Tanjuro then tells Tanjiro to make sure the hanafuda earrings and the kagura get passed down uninterrupted, no matter what. Tanjiro then switches from the Water Breathing, Tenth Form: Constant Flux, to use the Hinokami Kagura: Dance. Mugen Train Arc. When Tanjiro realizes he was trapped in a dream-based Blood Demon Art by Enmu, Tanjuro appeared to him in a sudden gust of wind, telling his son to pick up his blade as he must slice something to awaken himself. Later, during his final clash with Enmu, as he prepared to use Hinokami Kagura: Clear Blue Sky for the killing blow, Tanjiro prayed to his father to protect him. A dream version of his father also appeared, although this illusion of Tanjuro would later berate Tanjiro for being the sole-survivor of Muzan's attach after Enmu forces Tanjiro into having a nighmare. Infinity Castle Arc. When fighting Upper Rank 3 Akaza, Tanjiro recalled his father slaying a monstrous bear 3 days before his death whilst entering the Selfless State. Tanjiro would later use this to sneak up on Akaza and behead him. Sunrise Countdown Arc. After Nezuko was administered with a drug to reverse her back into being a human, she runs away from the Demon Slayer Corps's hideout in order to come to the rescue of her brother, who she sensed was in danger. The spirit of Tanjuro appeared to give his daughter direction. Abilities. Overall Abilities. Despite not being a Demon Slayer and having a tragic disease that makes his body incredibly frail, Tanjuro was shown to be a phenomenally strong individual. He was able to slay a bear nearly nine feet tall with a single axe at speeds magnitudes faster than the blink of an eye. His mastery of Hinokami Kagura enabled him to perform a long, arduous dance in frigid conditions without tiring. Demon Slayer Abilities. Demon Slayer Mark: As a descendant of the Kamado family and being able to access the "Transparent World", Tanjuro's birthmark on his forehead is secretly a Demon Slayer Mark. This is proven by Shinjuro's explanation that all Sun Breathing users naturally have a mark on their forehead. Selfless State: Throughout his entire life, Tanjuro emanated absolutely no sense of drive, hatred, anger, fighting spirit, animosity or fear even in dire situations such as him succumbing to his death or facing against an enormous bear. Physical Abilities. Immense Stamina & Endurance: Tanjuro had immense stamina and endurance for a non-Demon Slayer thanks to his mastery of Hinokami Kagura, being able to practice the ritual dance from dusk to dawn without any rest, despite his illness, frail body and freezing surroundings. Supernatural Abilities. Extrasensory Perception: Tanjuro possesses the ability to perceive the presence and strength of humans and animals, even outside of his immediate vicinity. This is evident when there was an incident of a bear attacking and eating six people. The villagers hung ropes lined with on the mountain to alert them. When the bear appeared again and Tanjuro went to confront the bear, the animal was still on the other side of the rope. Even though the bells never rung, Tanjuro was able to sense the bear's presence and murderous intent while he was in his bed sleeping.

Taro was a Shiba Inu dog owned by Yae who travelled with her on her quest. He was killed by Matazo when they encountered him. Appearance. Taro is a dog of the genus breed. Personality. Taro's been Yae's dog since her childhood, and seems very loyal to her. Yae cares deeply about him.

Tatsu Tatsu is a minor character in in "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba". He was a train maintenance worker that was held hostage by the Slasher demon. Appearance. Tatsu is a young boy, approximately 15 years old, which is the legal age for employment in Japan. He is of average height with dark brown hair and chocolate brown eyes that appear empty, lacking visible pupils. He typically wears a brown bib-and-brace work overall over a white long-sleeve shirt, with the sleeves rolled up for practicality. History. Under the instruction of the chief train engineer, Tatsu, along with seven other train maintenance workers, was tasked with preparing the Mugen Train for service after it was brought back to the maintenance facility due to suspicions of a demon linked to numerous disappearances. Synopsis. Mugen Train Arc. In the train maintenance facility, Tatsu is resting in the office when Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku arrives in the main hall to bring the workers bento boxes with food. The chief engineer instructs a worker to deliver a box to the resting Tatsu. However, the Slasher demon has entered the building in search of new prey and finds Tatsu. The demon captures Tatsu, holding him hostage by his neck. When Kyojuro and the other workers arrive at the scene, Tatsu cries out to the chief. Seeing a Demon Slayer, the demon tortures the boy, puncturing his cheek with a clawed thumb and digging clawed fingers into his chest. Tatsu cries out in pain from the demon’s claws. The demon taunts Kyojuro, using his Blood Demon Art to dash around the Hashira while holding Tatsu, goading him into attacking. He warns Kyojuro that the boy will die if he directly attempts to strike. The workers flee in terror while Kyojuro stands his ground. The demon boasts about his speed, claiming Kyojuro cannot kill him without harming the boy. Tatsu, bleeding and terrified, begs Kyojuro to save him. Noticing the bento box and Kyojuro’s angered expression, the demon deduces that the box likely came from a nearby station and decides to kill the vendors to spite Kyojuro. Before he leaves the demon threatens to kill Tatsu in front of Kyojuro and when he attempts to do that, Kyojuro swiftly cuts off both of the demon's arms and catches the falling Tatsu. The demon retreats and, standing outside the shed, detects the scent of the nearby station and speeds off to kill the vendors. Kyojuro administers first aid to Tatsu and leaves him in the care of the arriving Demon Slayer members, who were guided to the train maintenance facility by his Kasugai Crow. Later, the medical squad will treat Tatsu’s wounds upon their arrival.

Tecchin Tecchikawahara is the chief of the Swordsmith Village and its most skilled swordsmith. Appearance. Tecchin is an elderly man who is partially bald on the crown of his head, but has white, shoulder length hair. Despite his face being obscured by a mask, he has noticeable wrinkles which can be seen from above his mask and along his neck. He is very short in stature, even admitting he is the smallest resident of the entire village. Tecchin wears a diamond patterned with a white juban underneath, and a black on top. His haori has the for on the back. Personality. Tecchin has the tendency to be very straight forward in regards to his thoughts, openly admitting to being the most esteemed person in the village and proving so when he boldly told Tanjiro to bow before him till his head touched the floor. However despite his intimidating demeanor, he still acts in a civilized manner as seen when he called Tanjiro a "nice young man" and even offered him snacks. Tecchin's authority as chief is such that he is the only one to control the hot-blooded and brash Hotaru Haganezuka, despite the village residents' general dislike of the smith for his attitude and antics. History. During some point in Hotaru Haganezuka's childhood, Tecchin took him in and raised him after his explosive temper and behavior made it difficult for his parents to raise him. Synopsis. Swordsmith Village Arc. When his swordsmith Hotaru refuses to make him a new blade, Tanjiro Kamado arrives to the Swordsmith Village and sits down to a meeting with Tecchin. Tecchin, introducing himself as chief, asks that the Demon Slayer bow to him, to which Tanjiro forcefully does so in respect. After offering him candy, Tecchin asks for his reason to be in the village and is informed by Hotaru's behavior. Noting that Hotaru had always possessed a fiery temper, Tanjiro apologizes for breaking his Nichirin Sword. However, Tecchin rejects his apology and instead states it is Hotaru who is to blame for making a weak sword. He advises Tanjiro to stay in the village to heal in its hot springs and decides that if Hotaru is not found, a new smith will be designated to Tanjiro, before bidding the young man good bye. Later, the village is besieged by Gyokko, Upper Rank Five of the Twelve Kizuki, who unleashes Blood Demon Art fish demons to destroy buildings and kill swordsmiths indiscriminately. He sends his largest demon to Tecchin's residence, where it kills the stationed Demon Slayers and grabs the chief, almost squeezing him to death. Tecchin is saved when the Love Hashira Mitsuri Kanroji arrives in the nick of time, using her Love Breathing to cut down the monster instantly and save him. As the demon burns, Tecchin nearly falls to the ground but is caught by Mitsuri. As she asks on his condition, Tecchin remarks he is feeling much better in the arms of a young woman, causing her to playfully chide him. When another injured smith asks for Mitsuri's attention, Tecchin orders him to not interrupt his moment. In the morning after the village's attack, Tecchin, supported by a swordsmith, walks around to survey the damage. He is greeted by Kozo Kanamori and Kotetsu, and with them are Tanjiro and Nezuko following their battle with Upper Rank Four. Tecchin asks Tanjiro on his condition and is relieved to hear he is relatively fine. He then notices Hotaru hiding away from them and asks Kozo about him, who states he is still likely angry at Tanjiro. When Hotaru blames his client for his sword's destruction and using an unpolished blade, Tecchin orders him to calm himself and explains Tanjiro's reason to be in the village. Eventually, Hotaru releases his anger and complies with Tecchin's orders, much to Tanjiro's gratefulness. As the Demon Slayer departs from the village, Tecchin bids him good bye. Abilities. As a normal human, Tecchin has shown to have no indication of any superior abilities or advanced powers. However, as the chief of the Swordsmith Village, he is in charge of assigning a swordsmith to each member of the Demon Slaying Corps and his authority is well respected amongst the village. Being its most skilled smith, the main objective in the event of the village being attacked is to protect Tecchin, as his skill is invaluable and his death would mean a tremendous blow to the Demon Slayer Corps. Above Average Endurance: Despite his small size and lack of physical training, Tecchin has been shown to survive getting squeezed by the largest of Gyokko's Blood Demon Art spawn with little lasting damage, immediately claiming he was okay when asked by Mitsuri, though it seemed to be more about his delight in being held by her. Master Swordsmith: Tecchin is an extremely skilled swordsmith, able to forge intricate Nichirin Swords with specialized features. He is also one of the few who is entrusted to forge the blades for the Hashira.

Teiko Shinazugawa was a younger sister of Sanemi and Genya Shinazugawa. Appearance. Teiko was a girl of average height and light skin complexion. Her black hair was tied in a bow in the back and she had large almond-shaped purple eyes. She was very similar in appearance to her brother Sanemi. She wore a mint green kimoni lined with white waving stripes and tied with a lime green obi. Personality. Teiko, like her siblings, was a caring and loving young child. She loved her mother dearly and cared for her wellbeing, shielding her eyes during one of her father's abusive outburst because she could not stand to see the violence and staying up late to wait for her to come home when she was late. When she woke up to find Sanemi and her mother was not home at night, she looked to Genya as comfort, warmly addressing her older brother. History. Teiko was born to Kyogo and Shizu Shinazugawa. She had 6 other siblings, the oldest two being Sanemi and Genya. Their abusive father frequently used his size to torment them, though her mother had never failed to protect them from him. He would eventually die from a vengeful stabbing. One night, as Teiko, Sumi, Koto, Hiroshi, and Shuya slept, their mother had not returned home, concerning Sanemi and Genya. As the oldest, Sanemi ventured out to search for her while Genya stayed at home to watch his siblings, shortly after which they would wake up as well. As dawn approached, they began to expressed worry since she had never been so late before, though Genya tried to ease their concern. When a knock rang from the door, Teiko, Sumi, Hiroshi, and Shuya ran to greet their mother. Despite Genya's warning against opening it, the door broke open and their mother, who had transformed into a demon, rushed into the home, killing Teiko instantly. Synopsis. Swordsmith Village Arc. When he fails to cut the neck of Upper Rank Four Hantengu, Genya, in his shock, realizes that the demon's manifestation of anger had appeared behind him. As the demon prepares to stab him in the head, realizing he cannot avoid the attack, his life flashed before him and he remembered his childhood, including the death of his family. Sunrise Countdown Arc. As he lay dying from his numerous severe wounds from the against Muzan Kibutsuji, Sanemi found himself in the afterlife, where he saw Teiko and their other fallen siblings in heaven.

Temple Demon The was the first demon Tanjiro Kamado encountered that has taken a human's life. Appearance. The Temple Demon was a muscular demon of average height. He had pale, ash-gray skin with two green marks around both of his upper arms and legs and shoulder-length, spiky dark-green hair parted at the middle of his forehead. He also possessed prominent fangs and sharp nails, attributes common to Demons. The Temple Demon was seen wearing a sleeveless, blue tunic with a dark-turquoise-and-white pattern outlining his exposed chest. He wore pale colored bracelets around his wrists and ankles. After getting his head kicked off by Nezuko Kamado, the demon grew two muscular arms out of the sides of his head. Personality. The Temple Demon, like most demons, was cruel and ruthless to humans, attacking Tanjiro Kamado without a moment's hesitation upon discovering he was human. He appeared to be very defensive of his territory as he was irate about Tanjiro and Nezuko intruding onto his domain. The demon also displayed a sense of superiority over Tanjiro when the two fought, boasting his quick recovery after getting hit in the chin. History. The demon had already been attacking travelers who take shelter at a small temple hut on the pathway that leads to Mount Sagiri. When Tanjiro was asking for directions, one of the villagers mentioned that it would be dangerous for him to travel at night as people had been going missing in the area. Synopsis. Final Selection Arc. Tanjiro and Nezuko pass by the temple that the demon is feeding in, and, smelling blood, the former rushes over and opens the door. He is shocked to find the demon feeding on two dead men, and, annoyed, the demon turns to the Kamado siblings and warns them about trespassing on his turf. He turns to face them and, as the last light withers away, he pounces on Tanjiro.Tanjiro quickly reacts by drawing his hatchet and slashes open the demon's throat. The demon stumbles back, but it only takes a few seconds before the slice is fully healed. The demon pins down Tanjiro before he has time to react. He easily overpowers him in strength and speed. The demon tries to snap the boy's neck but Nezuko comes to her senses and rushes back to her brother's side. She kicks the demon's head clean off his body, shocking Tanjiro. The demon's body slowly tries to grab Tanjiro so Nezuko kicks it away into a tree. The head and body can move individually. The body attacks first, serving to isolate Nezuko. Tanjiro tries to help, but the head grows arms and leaps onto Tanjiro's hatchet. The body kicks Nezuko several times before throwing her deep into the forest.Tanjiro headbutts the head with reckless abandonment and it proves effective. He suffers two blows Tanjiro's rock-hard head before getting thrown with the hatchet into a tree, pinning him there. Tanjiro tracks his sister to a cliffside where she is being kicked closer to the edge.Tanjiro tackles the body over the large cliff, but Nezuko grabs him before he falls too far. It falls to its demise, and the head is knocked unconscious as a result. Tanjiro prepares a knife to finish off the head. He struggles to come to terms with taking another life and believes this is not the demon who attacked his family. A man in a Tengu mask appears and tells Tanjiro he cannot finish a demon off using a simple knife.The masked man challenges Tanjiro to figure out another way. The boy believes crushing the head with a rock will suffice, but can't bring himself to brutally end the creature. The head awakens and curses Tanjiro until the sun rises and he disintegrates into ash. Abilities. Overall Abilities. The Temple Demon proved to be a troublesome adversary for Tanjiro and Nezuko. His inhuman physical abilities and inability to take damage from normal wounds made him extremely dangerous to any ordinary human. Tanjiro, despite his use of an axe and physical fitness, was completely overwhelmed and would have certainly been killed if it had not been for Nezuko's intervention as a demon. Even after getting decapitated, the Temple Demon's head and body remained unharmed and continued to fight back, forcing the Kamado siblings to fight him by defeat both parts separately. Demon Abilities. Flesh Manipulation: After getting his head kicked off by Nezuko, the Temple Demon was shown to grow a new pair of arms from the stump of his neck, which allowed him to move and continue fighting Tanjiro Regeneration: As a demon, the Temple Demon possessed regeneration that allows him to heal conventional wounds within seconds, easily repairing the slice from an axe on his neck without issue. Because he sustained damage not performed by a Nichirin Sword, he remained alive and kept fighting the siblings. However, he succumbed to the innate weakness of all demons, burning quickly once the sun had risen. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Speed: The Temple Demon is faster than an ordinary person can see, easily blitzing Tanjiro's perception and appearing in front of him in a blur. Tanjiro, despite looking at him the entire time, could not see him move.

Tengen Uzui is a major supporting character of "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba" and a major character in the Entertainment District Arc. He was a former member of the Demon Slayer Corps, standing as the previous . Appearance. Tengen is a very tall, broad-shouldered, and muscular man with lightly-tanned skin and white hair. His hair is of an uneven length, the longest strands reaching his shoulders, and is styled with three more notable, shorter clumps arching up to fall as bangs between his eyes and on either side of his face. He has quite thin, maroon eyes that appear to slant inwards, each with one long eyelash flowing to the far side of his face. He is considered very attractive as noted by many women and even by Zenitsu; this has led him to use his looks as a tool for his missions whenever persuasion is necessary. During his days serving the Demon Slayer Corps, Tengen wears a sleeveless and dark turquoise version of the standard Demon Slayer uniform, along with a wrap of burgundy cloth around his calves with his pants tuck in, and white-strapped . He also wears two thick, golden rings around his upper arms and what appear to be a pair of finger-less blue gloves, secured around his middle finger with a band of white and his wrists with another set of thinner gold rings, this time with two on each side. As well as this, Tengen sports a white head-wrap that covers his hair, leaving only a thin ponytail visible to fall behind his head from between its layers, which is adorned with a large headband of pale gray that's decorated by six light pink gemstones, three large and arranged in a line, and three small and arranged in a triangle to the far left. A chain of smaller, pale blue gemstones hangs from each side of this headdress, framing his face, and he also wears what looks to be red eye make-up around his left eye, consisting of alternating large and small dots that run inwards, towards his eye. After his retirement from the Demon Slayer Corps due to the injuries he has sustained during his fight with Gyutaro, Tengen changes his appearance to coordinate the loss of his left eye and hand. He now wears a long, aqua colored yukata and a black, and replaces his old head-wrap with a dark eyepatch adorned with what look to be the remaining gemstones left over from his old headdress, leaving his hair to fall loosely past his shoulders. Personality. Tengen is an eccentric and flashy individual, always wanting to be "flamboyant", possessing a need for everything to be flashy and outstanding, even proclaiming that he is the god of flashiness and festivals. This is shown when he gets excited imagining how "flamboyant" it would be if Tanjiro Kamado's blood vessels exploded, and tries to forcefully haul Aoi Kanzaki off to the Entertainment District with him so she can unwillingly help him with a dangerous mission, even spanking her. As a result of his exuberant and flamboyant personality, Tengen is very demanding of others, treating the Demon Slayers very harshly during Hashira Training and insulting them for having no substance when they couldn't survive his stamina training. Furthermore, he also abhors the idea of unflashy things, as shown when the Hashira openly expresses his hate for plainness. He is usually seen talking boastfully, proclaiming that he is "god" in front of Tanjiro, Zenitsu and Inosuke, even calling them trash and declaring that if he tells them to become dogs, they must become dogs, and if he tells them to become monkeys, they must become monkeys. Tengen even demands for the trio to always humor and stoop down to him, imploring him for favours and always doing their best to flatter him. This was also shown in his initial encounter with Upper Rank Six, Gyutaro, proclaiming that he was in tip-top shape despite being severely poisoned. However, Tengen does possess a caring side that is masked under his flamboyant façade, one he only shows to those that are extremely close to him, most notably his three wives, Makio, Suma, and Hinatsuru, who Tengen is shown to truly care for, praising and encouraging Makio and Suma after their undercover mission and assuring Hinatsuru that she has completed her mission and telling her to get out of harm's way. Furthermore, Tengen also declares that they must value their lives above all others as they are precious to him. After the events in Yoshiwara, Tengen also becomes more friendly towards Tanjiro, Zenitsu, and Inosuke. Although he can be very boastful and expressive, Tengen also shows a side of modesty and humility. He openly denied Gyutaro's statement that he was blessed with any talent, comparing himself to the other Hashira and especially Kyojuro Rengoku. This implicates a sort of inferiority complex, further proven by the fact that he told himself that he could never become someone as great as Kyojuro. Tengen is also shown to harbor regret over the fact that he has let so many lives slip through his fingers over the years. Kagaya Ubuyashiki praised Tengen for the hard path he chose and for facing forward and fought to protect human lives despite carrying all of his conflicts and contradictions he hides behind his loud and confident façade, which caused Tengen to deeply respect Kagaya from that moment on. Despite being a shinobi that has traditionally valued completing the mission over all else, Tengen has rejected that ideology after seeing its effect on his family. He believes that his subordinates, whether they be his wives or the Demon Slayers under his command, should value their lives, and the lives of innocents, over their missions or his own. Tengen especially hated becoming like his brother or father who were apathetic towards human lives and wanted to desperately abandon what he was taught by them. Abilities. Overall Abilities. As a Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps, Tengen is a very powerful and skilled combatant. He has displayed incredible physical feats of strength and speed, being seen as the second physically strongest and the fastest runner out of the Taisho era's Hashira. He could match the combat proficiency of both Daki and Gyutaro, both Upper Rank demons that have fought and killed numerous Hashira in the past. Tengen was also able to effortlessly decapitate Daki without her realizing it, to the point that he didn't see her as an Upper Rank demon at all. Impressively, he was able to fend off the combined efforts of Daki and Gyutaro while being infected by a poison that would kill someone quickly under normal circumstances, even managing to protect bystanders in the process. Tengen has also showcased great skill and precision in using explosives, minimizing damage dealt to the surroundings and maximizing the damage dealt to his opponents. Due to his shinobi training, Tengen has greater tactical skills and sharper senses, most notably his sense of hearing, which helped him greatly during the course of his battle. Even after losing his left hand to Gyutaro, Tengen was able to fight the Upper Rank on even terms due to completing his Musical Score, allowing him to deflect Gyutaro's attacks, cut off his arm and pin him down at the cost of losing his left eye. Nonetheless, due to the poison circulating in his body, he was unable to attempt a finishing blow and needed Tanjiro to do so. Indomitable Will: Tengen possesses an undaunted spirit and immense willpower, never faltering even when faced disadvantages and difficult circumstances. Despite being poisoned in the beginning by Gyutaro, he boldly proclaimed he could fight just fine, even attacking both Daki and Gyutaro at the same time, deflecting multiple poison blood blades with a missing hand. Even when his left eye gets slashed out, he pushed through all the damage until the demons were defeated. Shinobi Training: Before joining the Demon Slayer Corps and becoming a Hashira, Tengen descended from a family of shinobi. Tengen received extremely harsh training that killed all his siblings except for his younger brother who became cold and heartless. However, as a result of his intensive shinobi training, Tengen possesses great technical skill in weaponry such as kunai and explosives. His training also made him extremely pain tolerant and poison resistant, which saved him from Gyutaro's poison and allowed him to fight despite suffering numerous injuries and losing his hand. Tactical Intellect: Due to accumulating years of experience as both a shinobi and Demon Slayer, Tengen has incredible judgement, making decisions on the fly while in battle with Upper Rank demons to protect bystanders and minimize the damage dealt to the surroundings. Even when he was held back by Gyutaro's poison, Tengen was able to properly determine the most efficient strategy to fight off the Upper Rank demons and even fooled Gyutaro into thinking he was dead by stopping his own heart to prevent himself from dying from his poison, which managed to give Tengen an edge against him. Demon Slayer Abilities. Muscle Control: Tengen can control the physiology of muscles to a great extent. During his battle with Gyutaro, Tengen used his muscles to stop his heart and temporarily prevent the poison from circulating, which also allowed him get the drop on Gyutaro, who did not pay him heed until he unexpectedly attacked the demon. Physical Abilities. Immense Speed & Reflexes: Tengen is said to be the fastest runner out of all the Hashira, and possesses tremendous levels of raw speed and reflexes, often shown when he moves so fast he appears to teleport. His speed also far surpasses that of Tanjiro, Zenitsu, and Inosuke, who were unable to keep up to, let alone perceive, the Hashira's blisteringly quick movements. Most notably, Tengen was fast enough to behead Daki, an Upper Rank demon, before she could even register what had happened. Moreover, he could fend off both Daki and the true Upper Rank Six, Gyutaro, despite being held back by a deadly poison that would've killed someone quickly under normal circumstances. Even after relinquishing his position as the Sound Hashira, Tengen's tremendous speed remained apparent. During a training exercise where he played the role of a demon stalking the trainees, his speed and reflexes gave him a handy advantage as he downed the Demon Slayers one by one without any one of them even able to see him; only Tanjiro, who has previous experience with fighting Upper Ranks, could see him moving and read his attacks to retaliate, leading to a short skirmish between them. Immense Stamina & Endurance: Due to his upbringing being raised to become a shinobi and his own father's increased attempts to revive their clan by forcing Tengen and his siblings to train even more harshly and painfully then necessary, Tengen developed inhuman resistance to pain, as seen where he bared little to no reaction at having being caught up in a hail of Kunai knives and being pierced by them without even flinching or showing any form of discomfort or pain, continuing to attack Gyutaro as if nothing had happened. Later, Tengen was also noted to have suffered other severe injuries during the battle, such as getting his eye and hand slashed off by Gyutaro, and managed to ignore the pain of such injuries as well. Immense Strength: Tengen possesses tremendous physical strength even amongst the Hashira, the strongest Demon Slayers of the Corps. He was ranked second in an arm-wrestling contest among all the Hashira, with only the hulking Gyomei Himejima surpassing him. Tengen displayed his strength numerous times, as he was shown effortlessly carrying Aoi and Naho, and soon after knocked Zenitsu and Inosuke unconscious with a single punch to the stomach. Moreover, Tengen is able to fight at blistering speeds while carrying around his giant Nichirin cleavers, swinging them incessantly to fend off his opponents without much trouble and being able to hold both his enormous cleavers at their tip with only two fingers. Furthermore, Tengen was able to match Gyutaro in strength with only one arm after his left hand was cut off. In his role in overseeing the first stage of Hashira Training, Tengen once stopped a trainee from moving by just holding his wooden blade outstretched, despite the Demon Slayer attempting to budge with all his might. He was also able to initiate an intense spar with Tanjiro, who had undergone considerable development between his mission in Yoshiwara and Hashira Training. Supernatural Abilities. Enhanced Hearing: Tengen has a heightened sense of hearing similar to Zenitsu Agatsuma. This ability allows him to easily hear noises deep underground, and he uses it to immediately discern that there are channels of underground tunnels and caves directly beneath him when he was looking for Tanjiro Kamado and Daki. He also uses his superhuman hearing the monitor all the activity in Yoshiwara in an attempt to find the location of the demons dwelling in the area. Tengen also used his hearing to discern whether people are still present on a floor in a building. Fighting Style. Master Swordsman: As a Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps, Tengen is one of the most powerful and skilled swordsman in the entire organization. Unlike most Demon Slayers, Tengen chooses to utilize a dual-wielding swordsmanship style with his Nichirin Cleavers, making use of a -esque sword wielding style. Tengen displays his unique and extraordinary swordsmanship skills during his battle with Daki and Gyutaro, able to adapt to the former's incessant obi slashes and the latter's "mantis-like" fighting style, and go toe-to-toe with him for an extended period of time despite the Upper Rank having over a century of combat experience. Tengen can also use his sword wielding expertise in conjunction with his explosive beads with great synergy, making him all the more effective at fighting demons. He also showed the ability to wield his Nichirin Cleavers with only one arm. In addition to traditional slashes and swings, Tengen has also been shown to spin his blades by their chain; the whirling motion allowing him to block blows and quickly attack in retaliation, with the blades in constant rapid motion. Equipment. Dual Nichirin Cleavers: Befitting Tengen's flamboyant personality, he carries an equally flamboyant set of weaponry, wielding two gigantic Nichirin cleavers that are amber in color. The blades each have a notch in the cutting edge and are held together by a metal chain, making it very reminiscent to . The weight of his blades enables them to generate immense explosive force, as seen when they create a blast upon making contact with Gyutaro's blood blades or when Tengen struck them on the ground to propel himself. It is stated that, until Tengen's fight with Upper Rank Six, no demon had ever survived a blow from them. The cleavers' tsubas are round with four slight indentations. They are gold in color and decorated with a maroon ring that connects to the center; it has an outer green border. The handles are dark green, wrapped with red cord and capped with an engraved gold kashira; this is also where the chains connect to the cleavers. The blades are engraved with the phrase . Due to his cleavers' large size, Tengen doesn't use a sword sheath and instead carries them on his back, having them wrapped in cloth. Explosive Beads: Tengen carries dozens of small black beads that create large explosions and detonate with the slightest amount of friction, capable of harming the bodies of Upper Rank demons. Kunai: Like his three wives, Tengen carries around dozens of standard black, which he used to threaten Omitsu's husband to reveal information about Zenko's and Hinatsuru's disappearance and to destroy the Obi sash that captured Hinatsuru.
