Tengen Uzui/Relationships Relationships. Tanjiro Kamado. Tengen first meets Tanjiro at his trial among the other Hashira. Upon hearing that he's been travelling with a Demon, Tengen initially vouches to kill him since he has disobeyed the rules and also rejects Kagaya's blessing to allow Nezuko and Tanjiro to travel together. When they meet again at the Butterfly Mansion, Tanjiro becomes angry and confronts Tengen after witnessing his attempt to kidnap Aoi and Naho. During the intense exchange, Tengen becomes fed up with Tanjiro's attitude and explodes at him for disrespecting him despite being his superior. However, the exchange eventually cools down when the boys offer to accompany Tengen on his mission instead of the girls. As they formally begin their mission, Tanjiro's naïvety pleases Tengen, seemingly melting away any tension between them. When Tanjiro struggles to restrain Nezuko following her demonization, Tengen scolds him for his lack of control over his sister and advises him to put her to sleep, instead of attacking her himself. As the two work together to take down Gyutaro, Tanjiro becomes concerned over Tengen's deteriorating health due to the poison and constantly tries to protect him from oncoming attacks. Even during situations when Tanjiro is risking his life, Tengen consistently manages to throw Tanjiro out of the way, or protect him before he can be seriously wounded. At the end of the battle, Tengen turns around to warn Tanjiro of Gyutaro's oncoming attack instead of fleeing showing his concern for him. Despite having horrible wounds himself, Tengen still shows his concern for Tanjiro's well being as he tells him to stay still, if not he would die from his injuries. Following the completion of their mission, Tengen finally acknowledges Tanjiro's abilities by telling Obanai that he "has grown to become strong enough" to fill his vacancy as he retires. Nezuko Kamado. Initially, Tengen didn't accept the Kamado siblings because Tanjiro Kamado was keeping his sister who was turned into a demon alive. Hearing that he had been traveling with a demon, Tengen vouched to kill both of them for breaking the corps rules. It is implied that Tengen was at least neutral with Nezuko living after she was tested to see if she'd attack Sanemi after he provoked her but didn't, considering he overlooked her when he went to Entertainment District with Tanjiro, Zenitsu and Inosuke. He also viewed her not attacking Sanemi as "showing off" in front of the master and was also displeased when she transformed into an advanced demonic state and began to lose control of herself, claiming she had no right nor reason to demonize so flashily. What changed Tengen's mind about Nezuko is when he was dying from Gyutaro's poison, Nezuko used her Blood Demon Art to completely burn away the poison from his entire body which at first, confused Tengen thinking if it was even possible. He eventually retires from being a Hashira due to being rendered incapable of fighting. Zenitsu Agatsuma. When the two originally meet, Zenitsu develops a disdain for Tengen after he attempted to kidnap the girls of the Butterfly Mansion, and due to his flamboyant personality, even referring to him as the "god of idiots." Tengen's frivolous attitude doesn't sit well with Zenitsu's character and often annoys him. When Tengen tells the boys of his plan to find his wives, Zenitsu becomes enraged at his womanizing antics and mocks him for claiming to have three wives, which results in him getting knocked unconscious by Tengen. Tengen's appearance also causes Zenitsu to seethe with jealousy as he appears to draw more attention from the women within the Entertainment District. Zenitsu's dislike for Tengen reaches its peak when he abandons Zenitsu at the Kyogoku House and tells the manager to have him clean the brothel, causing Zenitsu to seethe with rage as he is left to complete his mission. Inosuke Hashibira. Tengen initially finds Inosuke to be quite disturbing due to the boar's head he wears. When Tengen introduces himself to the trio of boys, Inosuke uses the opportunity to introduce himself as the "god of the mountain", however his introduction does not appeal to Tengen and he calls Inosuke "creepy." Inosuke's blunt personality also doesn't sit well with Tengen as seen when he punched Inosuke for carelessly questioning if Tengen's wives are even alive. Inosuke doesn't necessarily speak to Tengen with respect as seen when he blamed him for being reckless and allowing the obi to escape from the underground cavern. However, Inosuke does acknowledge Tengen's advanced abilities and skills to the point where he mimics Tengen's catchphrases. Obanai Iguro. Despite Tengen's victory against Upper Rank 6, Obanai downplays this significant achievement to instead emphasize the extent of his injuries. Tengen, for his part, brushes aside Obanai's concerns, insisting on retiring and disagreeing with the latter's sentiment that the Demon Slayers were going into decline. Kyojuro Rengoku. Tengen deeply admired and respected Kyojuro during their time as fellow Hashira, going so far as to say the Flame Hashira was even flashier than he was. During his battle against Daki and Gyutaro, he denies being talented and laments how many lives he's failed to save, acknowledging that Kyojuro was always ahead of him. Later, while wondering if he could handle the battle as Kyojuro would, the Flame Hashira appears before him admitting that he could never be like Tengen either, and asks him to watch over Tanjiro for him. Makio, Suma, and Hinatsuru. Tengen holds a large amount of respect for his wives and cares about them deeply. When Tengen joined the Demon Slayer Corps, he made sure to inform his wives that they needed to prioritize their lives instead of the mission, and make sure to return home to him. Tengen wanted to make clear that his wives were his top priority in regards to keeping people safe. During their stay in the Entertainment District, Tengen would often communicate with them via letters and decided to search for them once he stopped receiving them. When Inosuke questions if his wives are even alive anymore, Tengen becomes enraged and punches him unconscious, showing that he chastises any disrespect towards his wives. Later on when Tengen discovers Hinatsuru in the Kirimise, he administers medication to her and asks her if she's alright. When she starts to apologize to him for failing the mission, Tengen reassures her that she did well and embraces her tightly before instructing her to leave the district for her safety. However when Hinatsuru returns to assist in the fight against Gyutaro, she gets captured by the Demon causing Tengen to go into a panic to try to save her. Tanjiro manages to save Hinatsuru in time, allowing Tengen to express his gratitude towards him and mentioning that he "owes him one" for saving his wife. When Tengen discovers the underground cavern, he slashes the obi within the vicinity of his wives and apologizes to Suma and Makio for being late. He approaches the women and pats them on the head, reassuring them that they've lived up to his expectations as his wives, causing the two of them to tear up upon reuniting with him. Following the events of the final battle, Suma, Makio, and Hinatsuru immediately rush in to administer first aid to Tengen, but his wounds appear to be too grave for them to treat, causing them to worry. They each become concerned for his well being as Suma begins to wail, Makio begins to panic, and Hinatsuru begins to weep at the sight of his injuries. However when Nezuko manages to heal Tengen from being poisoned, the women rejoice at the fact that he's been healed, and wail as they share a relieved hug with him.

Tengen Uzui/Synopsis History. Tengen was born into a family of nine children within a clan. Three of the nine children died before they even reached 10 years old due to overzealous training. With the remaining six of his siblings, they were forced to kill each other on their father’s orders without them knowing who they fought, as their heads and faces were covered with masks. Tengen realized his father's trick only after he had killed two of his brothers. By the age of 15, seven of his siblings had already died leaving only him and his younger brother who is two years younger. As children, his father had forced them to undergo harsh and intensive training as an attempt to save the clan, and influenced them to believe that they needed to dispose innocent lives for their benefit, and solely have a wife as means for producing offspring. As his last remaining brother adopted this mindset, and did not feel bad about killing their other siblings, Tengen became appalled and decided to leave the clan permanently. He left the village with his wives without fighting his brother. The Uzui family practices polygyny, so when Tengen turned 15, he must have 3 wives, who were chosen by the head of the clan. After leaving the village with his wives, he would later teach them to value themselves before the mission, going against their teachings as . For a while after he had left the clan, it became habit for him to say he was going to hell, but he stopped after Makio got angry with him, Hinatsuru cried, and Suma bit him. He anguished over whether he should have exterminated the Uzui clan, but he couldn't bring himself to kill his father or brother. Following the departure from his clan, Tengen and his family searched for Kagaya Ubuyashiki to help fight for the Demon Slayers, and he formally joined. Tengen would later go on to climb the ranks of the Corps and become the Sound Hashira before Sanemi Shinazugawa became a Hashira, and when Kanae Kocho was a member.Notably, Kagaya empathized with Tengen and could only imagine how difficult it had to have been for him to abandon everything about his past to take on a new path and this was this empathy that caused Tengen to become deeply devoted to the Oyakata. During Sanemi's first time at a Hashira meeting, he insulted Kagaya after falsely believing he would willingly send Demon Slayers to their deaths, earning Tengen and Gyomei's ire. After said incident was resolved by Kanae and Kagaya, Tengen berated the newly appointed Hashira and told him his behavior during his first meeting was unacceptable. Synopsis. Rehabilitation Training Arc. Tengen was present as a member of the Hashira when Tanjiro Kamado was put on trial. Upon initially meeting Nezuko and Tanjiro, he openly expresses his distaste at the idea of them travelling together, even claiming that he will "cut off his head with style." When Tanjiro explains his reasoning for travelling with a Demon, the Sound Hashira becomes intrigued and even requests to see their interaction. However when the leader of the Demon Slayer Corps informs the Hashira of his acceptance of the siblings, Tengen openly rejects the idea of allowing Tanjiro to remain with Nezuko. Mugen Train Arc. Although Tengen did not participate in any major battles during the arc, he receives news of Kyojuro's death from a crow and expresses his concern that even he had lost his life to one of the Upper Ranks. Entertainment District Arc. At the beginning of the arc, Tengen enters Butterfly Mansion and attempts to kidnap Naho and Aoi to assist him on his mission. However he is forced to change tactics when the three boys —Tanjiro, Zenitsu and Inosuke Hashibira— rescue the girls, and force him to take them along on his mission. On their way to the site, Tengen reveals that they are going to investigate the disappearance of his wives within the Entertainment District. In order to do so, he explains that each boy will be sent to one of the three brothels: Ogimoto House, Kyogoku House, or Tokito House to try to gather information on their whereabouts. Once they arrive at the district, Tengen disguises the boys as girls ands drops them off at each house to begin their investigation. Tengen proceeds to lie low as the boys gather information within each house, and monitors for any unusual activity within the district. After Zenitsu goes missing, Tengen senses the immediate danger and tells the other two boys to abandon the mission and let him complete it for their safety. He reaches the Kyogoku House and holds the brothel manager hostage demanding to know where Zenitsu and Hinatsuru had disappeared to. Upon learning that Hinatsuru had been sent to the Kirimise, Tengen presses the manager for more information and he reveals that Warabihime had been causing the disappearances. When Tengen arrives at the Kirimise, he discovers Hinatsuru had been held prisoner by Daki's obi and defeats it, before tending to his wife. Once he administers medication to her and checks that she's okay, Tengen instructs Hinatsuru to leave the district and run for safety before continuing his search for his other wives and Zenitsu. When he arrives back in the district, Tengen hears the sounds from the underground cavern, and enters it to discover his wives —Makio and Suma— inside fighting the obi. After freeing them, the obi manages to escape and Tengen scrambles after it, with Inosuke and Zenitsu trailing behind him. Tengen on the scene to discover Tanjiro struggling to control his sister, and quickly decapitates Daki unable to believe that she is the Upper Rank they have been searching for. Upon discovering the truth behind Daki and Gyutaro's presence, the Hashira engages in fierce combat with the Demons. Gyutaro manages to poison Tengen during the fight, preventing him from decapitating the Demon. After they finally manage to bring down the Demon siblings, Tengen ends up losing his left hand and eye in the process. By the end of the battle, Gyutaro's poison has spread throughout Tengen's body resulting in his inability to speak. As he lays dying from the poison, Nezuko Kamado intervenes and uses her her Blood Demon Art to burn the poison out of his system, allowing him to rejoice with his wives. Once Obanai arrives to the scene, he tells him that he is officially retiring from the Demon Slayer Corps and assures him that the trainee he "hates so much" has grown strong enough to fill the void his absence will leave, alluding to Tanjiro. As the Kakushi rush in to clean up the scene, Tengen is then supported by his wives as he walks away to begin his retirement. Hashira Training Arc. Despite officially retiring, Tengen assists in Hashira Training along with his wives. He oversaw the first level, which is basic stamina training. He proved to be rather strict and demanding to the trainees, causing Hinatsuru to gently reprimand him for being so tough on them. When he encounters Tanjiro however, he showed a more amicable side towards him and congratulates him when he completes his stamina training. Infinity Castle Arc. Tengen and Shinjuro Rengoku were located in another section of the Ubuyashiki estate when it was taken into Muzan Kibutsuji's Infinity Castle. They stand guard outside of the room Kiriya, Kanata, and Kuina Ubuyashiki are located in as the surviving Ubuyashikis map out the fortress and give instructions to the Demon Slayers.

Tenma Uzui is the descendant of Tengen Uzui. He is a professional gymnast who won the gold medal in gymnastics for Japan during the recent Olympics. He has seven siblings. Appearance. Tenma is a very good-looking person. He bears a striking resemblance to his flamboyant predecessor: having the same white hair, the same eye shape, the same eye color, and even the same receding eyebrows! Also, his skin shade is slightly tanned due to his participation in the Olympics. Personality. Tenma seems to be a playful attention-seeking person. In the news picture about his gold medal win, he is seen doing an (an eyelid pull) accompanied by sticking his tongue out, while holding his medal towards the camera. He is also noted to be rude, often flashing his middle finger and choking reporters. Synopsis. As the Agatsuma siblings make their way to school, Toko Agatsuma looks at a news article on her phone, which shows that Tenma had just won a gold medal in gymnastics for Japan. Toko is totally smitten by Tenma, but her brother Yoshiteru Agatsuma says that Tenma was rude and gives examples of his behaviour. Toko defends Tenma and he wondered aloud if one can get away with anything just because he was good looking.

Teruko is a young girl, accompanied by her brother Shoichi, who approaches Tanjiro Kamado and Zenitsu Agatsuma to help save her older brother from the Tsuzumi Mansion. Appearance. Teruko has shoulder-length black hair parted back into two low pigtails tied with red bobble hair ties. Like her older brothers, she has amber/brown eyes with fair skin. Throughout her appearance, Teruko wears a pale-pink kimono and a purple obi with square patterns. History. Teruko lived with her two brothers, Kiyoshi and Shoichi along with their family. When out walking during the night with her brothers, Kiyoshi was kidnapped by Kyogai. Her and Shoichi followed the trail of blood left by Kiyoshi due to him sustaining a wound on his leg. They eventually ended up at the Tsuzumi Mansion where they waited in shock, unsure of what to do.

Tetsuido was a swordsmith affiliated with the Demon Slayer Corps. He was responsible for Muichiro Tokito's swords until he died from a heart attack. Appearance. Tetsuido is an elderly man, evident by the wrinkles on his skin and skinny frame. He has long white hair that reaches past his neck. As a resident of the Swordsmith Village, he wears a Hyottoko mask to hide his face. He wore a long dark green haori, baggy black pants tied around above his ankles, white socks, and light gray slippers. He is commonly seen smoking. Personality. Tetsuido was a gentle, keen, and understanding man, being one of the few people including Kagaya Ubuyashiki to see past the stoic façade Muichiro Tokito put on. He knew his client was hiding his problems behind the brave face he was showing and urged him to prevent making his issues his alone to burden. He was proud to be the Mist Hashira's swordsmith and mentioned that he tears up seeing his blade being used. History. Tetsuido was delegated as the first swordsmith for the Mist Hashira Muichiro Tokito. Despite Muichiro's quiet and blunt demeanour, Tetsuido sensed that he was hiding something and urged the young boy to speak to someone, in the hope his problems and burdens didn't weigh on him alone. Shortly before his death, Tetsuido spoke to Muichiro one last time, expressing his worry that no one could help understand the problems and hardship the young Hashira faced in his life if he didn't speak to anyone about them. Stating that at his age, he does not worry about his own death, Tetsuido instead commented that he cannot seem to stop worrying about Muichiro. Synopsis. Swordsmith Village Arc. During his battle with Gyokko, Muichiro receives his new Nichirin sword from the swordsmith Kozo Kanamori, using it to slice the octopus tentacles holding him. Thanking him for his newly forged blade, Kozo notes that he had only followed the guide to make it laid out by Tetsuido, his previous smith. As he prepares to face Gyokko once more, Muichiro recalls a meeting he had with Tetsuido before his death, apologizing for causing him to worry but claiming he is now alright. Abilities and Powers. As an ordinary human, Tetsuido does not possesses special physical abilities. However, as a swordsmith entrusted to forge the blade of the Mist Hashira, it can be assumed that he was an incredibly skilled swordsmith.

Thunder Breathing is one of the five main Breathing Styles directly derived from Sun Breathing. Overview. Thunder Breathing is a Breathing Style that mimics lightning, specifically swift strikes and movements akin to lightning ripping through the sky, and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. Most, if not all, known techniques and forms involve utilizing blinding speeds and immensely fast attacks to overwhelm the enemy in an instant. Users of Thunder Breathing also visualize themselves seemingly creating and manipulating lightning and electricity when unleashing its techniques. It has been remarked by Zenitsu Agatsuma that this Breathing Style focuses on channeling strength into the user's legs, and maximizing the output of every single muscle and blood vessel in them. Users also mimic lightning to such high fidelity that they cause the air to vibrate when poised to unleash a technique and create immensely loud sounds akin to thunder with their mere footsteps. This Breathing Style is also very reminiscent of a swordsmanship style practiced and utilized in real life known as, a famous quick-draw sword technique. This Breathing Style was created from one of Yoriichi Tsugikuni's students who attempted to learn Sun Breathing, but due to not being as innately powerful as Yoriichi, they were instead taught an alternated personalized Breathing Style that focused on their individual strengths and weaknesses, which eventually evolved into Thunder Breathing. A known cultivator of Thunder Breathing in the Demon Slayer Corps is the former Thunder Hashira, Jigoro Kuwajima. Known Techniques. Thunder Breathing has 6 standard forms in total, with the first form said to be the foundation for all the other forms. However, Zenitsu Agatsuma developed a Seventh Form in order to stand on equal ground with Kaigaku, his former senior disciple under Jigoro who had become the Upper Rank Six of the Twelve Kizuki. Note: The second to sixth forms of Thunder Breathing have only been displayed by Kaigaku, who uses actual lightning in conjunction with his swordsmanship. While the forms are "presumably" still similar to the original style, it is currently unknown how a normal swordsman would perform these techniques, or if mastery of the first form would alter how the others are executed. Tojuro Rengoku is the descendant of Senjuro Rengoku. He is a teenage student currently going to the same school as the Kamado and Agatsuma descendants. Appearance. Tojuro shares a striking resemblance with his ancestor, Senjuro and his brother Kyojuro. Like them, he also has golden shoulder length hair with red tips, black forked eyebrows and gold eyes with red irises. Personality. Like Kyojuro, Tojuro has an air of great optimism, is extremely positive and often have an enthusiastic smile plastered on his face. He says thanks, even when insulted. He has a very strong heart. He has a passion for, often forgetting about everything else when he's training and participating in the kendō club at school. Synopsis. On his way to school, Tojuro sees his friend Sumihiko Kamado running and catches up to him. Greeting him, Sumihiko remarks that it is unusual for Tojuro to be late. Tojuro explains that he had woken up at 4 in the morning, but had gotten absorbed into his training. He says that he couldn't hear anything until his father whacked him. Suddenly a police car with two police officers, Sanehiro Shinazugawa and the reincarnation of Genya Shinazugawa, in it draws nearer to the boys, asking them to stop. but Tojuro ignores them and continues the conversation, telling Sumihiko that he should join a sports club at school. Sumihiko replies that it'd cut into his sleep, and Tojuro laughs and says that he should at least try something because he'd be awesome at it. Sumihiko says he could never hold a candle to Tojuro in terms of sport. The two continue to run the rest of the way together, with the police officers continue shouting at the pair to stop. They arrive at their high school where the principal, Murata's descendant, asks for the gate to be closed as soon as he sees Sumihiko and Tojuro arriving. The person at the gate says that there are still three minutes until it should close but the principal insists, saying that Sumihiko was a habitual offender. As the gate begins to shut, Sumihiko says he believes they will make it and Tojuro agrees. Both of them somersault over the gate and land inside the school, making it just on time.

Tokie is a resident of Northwest Town where the Swamp Demon attacked and his final target. Appearance. Tokie is a young girl with fair skin and a small, petite build. She has long straight black hair with thin strands over her forehead and long bangs framing her face. Tokie, at the night of her kidnapping, wore a lime-green kimono with a blue obi. Over this, she wore a long dark red . Personality. Tokie is shown to be a very obedient girl as when she was asked to stay home at night by a family member of hers, she does listen and decides to rest indoors. She is also kind and caring as shown when she wonders about whereabouts of the missing girls kidnapped by the Swamp Demon and hopes that they are alright. Synopsis. Kidnapper's Bog Arc. Tokie is first seen leaving her family members to go to sleep, having just been told to stay indoors due to the disappearances that had been happening during the night. She obeys and sadly thinks about the girls who had already been kidnapped, hoping that no other girl would be taken as she gets into bed. As she's falling asleep, the Swamp Demon creates a swamp pool under her futon and pulls her under, much to her horror. She is defenseless to escape his grasp despite her struggling and is successfully knocked out and dragged into the depths. She is later saved from the demon by Tanjiro Kamado and Kazumi, and it can be assumed that she managed to return safely home. Abilities and Powers. As an ordinary human, she doesn't possess any supernatural powers or abilities.

Tokito House The is a traditional Japanese brothel located in the Entertainment District of Tokyo, Japan. History. It is not known when the Tokito House was established in the Entertainment District. However, when Tengen Uzui was investigating the report of a demon within the district, he sends his wife, Suma, to infiltrate the Tokito House to try and gather information. After he loses contact with his wife, Tengen travels to the Entertainment District with the Demon Slayers to try to infiltrate a second time.

Toko Agatsuma is the great-granddaughter of Zenitsu Agatsuma and Nezuko Kamado. She is also the older sister of Yoshiteru Agatsuma. Appearance. Toko bears a great resemblance to her ancestor, Nezuko Kamado, having the same waist-length black hair parted to the left side of her forehead, though her hair tips are much darker than her ancestor's and are closer to an actual red color than Nezuko's orange. She has round, pink eyes with prominent eyelashes and thin eyebrows. Toko wears her school's standard uniform, consisting of a light blue long-sleeved shirt, black skirt, black ribbon necktie, and white vest. She also sports her uniform's black knee-socks and brown loafers. Personality. Towards her brother, Toko shows great aggravation and animosity, often berating him for his antics and telling him off for not studying. At times, she resorts to physically attacking Yoshiteru, such as kicking his back or tugging on his ear. Such irritable behavior is similar to her great-grandfather. According to Yoshiteru, the females in their family were kind and gentle, with Toko being an exception. Toko's harsh and violent actions show that she cares deeply about her younger brother's academic success and wants to see him grow up to be a mature and responsible individual. Through her efforts, Yoshiteru was able to improve his grades and gain admission to high school. However, when Toko is with Kanata Kamado, she instantly loses her angry demeanor and instead becomes much more jubilant, especially if Kanata compliments her. She is still easily annoyed by her brother if he interrupts her and Kanata's activities. Toko's personality shows that she doesn't believe in "superstitious" things, such as Zenitsu's journal about their journey to fight back against the demon race. Synopsis. When Yoshiteru was reading Zenitsu's memoir, Toko appeared from behind with a kick to his back, scolding him for reading Zenitsu's fabricated memoir. She then scolds Yoshiteru for his lack of studying, partly due to his recent low grades. Although Yoshiteru defended himself by saying how his great-grandfather risked his life to fight, Toko pinched his ear and forced him to study properly so as not to dishonor his great-grandfather. On the way to school, Yoshiteru, with an extremely annoyed attitude when he was scolded and beaten by his sister, thinks that Toko is different from all the women in the family because of her hot temper. Yoshiteru then asked Toko if she believed in reincarnation, but as someone who was not superstitious, Toko scolded Yoshiteru immediately. After apologizing to her, he expressed his thoughts that those who fell to fight the demons have now been reincarnated and will live happier lives than before. Toko immediately ignored him and opened her phone to see a notification, which informed her of the latest news about an athlete named Tenma Uzui, who won a gold medal in gymnastics. Despite being criticized by Yoshiteru as a thug and rude, Toko defended Tenma. Toko was then snatched by her brother to see a news item about a botanist named Aoba Hashibira. Seeing her younger brother praising Aoba as a beauty, Toko immediately called him a boy and mocked Yoshiteru for being lustful like their father. While crossing the street, Toko and her younger brother met a pair of twins who looked like Yuichiro Tokito and Muichiro Tokito. Due to discovering her brother had evil intentions, Toko immediately told him he was disgusting. With that same displeasure, she continued to look at Yoshiteru as he watched two female students who looked like Kanae Kocho and Shinobu Kocho from Sekirei Academy. At that moment, Toko spotted Kanata Kamado, her cousin, and said good morning with an extremely amused expression on her face. After receiving compliments from Kanata, Toko's personality changed, she became softer and seemed quite shy around Kanata. Later, Toko invited Kanata to go to a restaurant of a couple who looked quite similar to Mitsuri Kanroji and Obanai Iguro, but after hearing Kanata's story and discovered that her younger brother was who made Toko and Kanata unable to go to that restaurant, she turned around, with a very angry expression, and looked at Yoshiteru. Relationships. Yoshiteru Agatsuma. As an older sister, Toko is always telling off him to focus on his studies, especially when Yoshiteru was reading Zenitsu's book. Although she was always angry at him, both Yoshiteru and Toko care for each other, showing they have a good relationship. Kanata Kamado. Kanata is Toko's second cousin. When around him, she often switches to a happier personality instead of her angry demeanor, and they often compliment each other. Toko appears to enjoy holding his hand. Abilities. As an ordinary human, Toko does not hold any special abilities or powers.

Tomi was a bento vendor for a train station supporting the Mugen Train, and the grandmother of Fuku. Appearance. Tomi was an old woman of short stature with long white hair worn in a bun down her back. She had dark purple eyes that fade into a violet color lower down, their irises white and vertically rectangular. Tomi wore a brown kimono and a red, as well as large round glasses. Personality. Tomi was seen to be a polite and kind woman, evident when she defended Kyojuro Rengoku after her granddaughter became suspicious of him when he had asked her about demons. She cares for her greatly and tried many times to reassure her when she was upset about the poor sales of her bentos at night. Unlike most humans, she has known about the existence of demons for a long time, owing to her own life almost ending to an attack years ago, which was the reasoning for her cautioning Fuku not to stay out at night, in spite of the girl's skepticism. She also was shown to be very brave, attacking the Slasher when he tried to attack her granddaughter. History. Twenty years before meeting Kyojuro Rengoku, Tomi and her young daughter were attacked by a demon. In the nick of time, they were saved by the Flame Hashira of then, Shinjuro Rengoku. Rescued and safe from the threat, she never forgot his appearance and ritualistic way of sheathing his Nichirin sword. Synopsis. Mugen Train Arc. At the station, Tomi listens as her granddaughter Fuku laments to her about the poor sales of their bento boxes. Kyojuro Rengoku appears, and Fuku becomes wary of him, which Tomi tries to pacify. After he buys their bento boxes and leaves, the two close up the shop together. Tomi and Fuku are attending the shop again the next day when they're approached by a demon, Slasher, who almost strangles Fuku. Kyojuro appears and is able to save her, defeating the demon, to which the two express their thanks by offering the Hashira a bento box. Tomi reminisces about the time she herself was saved by a Flame Hashira, along with Fuku's mother, which Kyojuro recognizes as his father. Fuku apologizes to her grandmother about her disregard for demons but Kyojuro cheerfully responds that not believing in them may be for the better. Before Kyojuro boards the Mugen Train for his investigation, Tomi and her granddaughter provided him with beef bentos as a token of appreciation for saving their lives, which he happily accepted and enjoyed. Abilities. As an ordinary human, she doesn't possess any additional powers or abilities.

Tongue Demon The was a demon that lived in the Tsuzumi Mansion. Appearance. The Tongue Demon was a muscular man with gray skin and very dark blue hair, set noticeably far back on his head to make room for the two small horns that protruded from either side of his forehead. He had two pairs of eyes, one large and cat-like of a green color and the other more squinted and set above the first, their irises red. His most notable features were his extremely long tongue and the navy blue arrows that patterned his nose and forearms, a large blotch of a similar color on each temple. The Tongue Demon wore nothing above his waist, under which he sported only the bottom half of a patterned knee-length yukata. Personality. The Tongue Demon, as with many others of his kind, was a ruthless being who seemed only to care about eating any and all humans that crossed his path. He appeared to be somewhat unintelligent, as he often talked to himself and repeated words when speaking as well as slithered around on the floor rather than walking. History. Before Tanjiro Kamado and Zenitsu Agatsuma entered the mansion, the Tongue Demon discovered the manor's demon Kyogai had found a boy, Kiyoshi, which he had intended to devour for his Marechi blood. They were joined by a third demon and the three fought over who had the right to devour the boy. In the argument, the Horned Demon ripped off a tsuzumi from Kyogai's back, which Kiyoshi grabbed and used to transport himself away from them, leaving the three demons to look for him inside the mansion. Synopsis. Tsuzumi Mansion Arc. While crawling around the Tsuzumi mansion, the Tongue Demon happened upon Zenitsu, a member of the Demon Slayer Corps, and Shoichi, the younger brother of his desired prey Kiyoshi. He startled the two with his unusual appearance and long tongue, before chasing them into an empty room. Overwhelmed by the creature's grotesque appearance and his fear of demons, Zenitsu suddenly lost consciousness, to the Tongue Demon's confusion. He attempts to grab Shoichi with his tongue but unexpectedly has the tip of it sliced off, which the demon fails to see. Zenitsu suddenly arose and began to breathe, which confuses and scares the Tongue Demon, who notes that his aura has changed. In an instant, the Demon Slayer beheads the demon with his Thunder Breathing, First Form: Thunderclap and Flash. The demon's head rolls next to Zenitsu, who becomes startled by the demon's unexpected death upon snapping awake. Abilities. Demon Abilities. Flesh Manipulation: This demon has displayed the ability to manipulate the length, speed and sharpness of his tongue, being able to slice a vase with ease.
